More than 2,500 Afghans gathered in Herat city, capital of Hirat District and Herat Province, on December 8, 2017, to protest the US decision to recognize Jerusalem as the capital of Israel.

Hundreds of people gathered in Lashkargah city to protest US recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel, as reported on December 12, 2017. They also called for the Afghan government to cut ties with the US.

Taliban fighters attacked the convoy of an American company called 'Supreme' in Bagram District, Parwan Province, on the morning of December 20, 2017. 12 staff of the company were either killed or injured (unclear if American or Afghan citizens; half coded as fatalities).

A Taliban-controlled mine explosion targeted US NATO soldiers near Forward Operating Base Fenty/Jalalabad Airport on the afternoon of December 21, 2017. 2 US soldiers were killed and 3 others injured.
The Taliban claimed that a 'tactical' explosion in Herat City on December 27, 2017, targeted US NATO soldiers belonging to a US intelligence organization. 2 soldiers were killed and 4 were injured.

Taliban fighters attacked US NATO forces stationed at Jalalabad airbase on the night of December 30, 2017, with missiles. They reported 'heavy casualties' to US soldiers, but no independent confirmation.

properties.notes: 1 US NATO soldier was killed and 4 others wounded in a combat engagement in Achin District, Nangarhar Province, on January 1, 2018.

On 3 January 2018, Taliban fired rockets on Bagram airbase, the largest US airbase in Afghanistan shared with Afghan forces, in Bagram city, Parwan. They claimed 'heavy casualties,' but it is unclear if anyone was killed (so fatalities coded as 0).

On 11 January 2018, members of a local militia attacked US NATO forces, their interpreter, as their own local militia leader in Achin District, Nangarhar Province [coded to Sra Kala]. The US NATO serviceman and interpreter were wounded while the militia leader was killed. The Taliban claimed the attack was carried out by two 'insurgents' disguised as local militiamen who had infiltrated the local forces months earlier. The Taliban reported that these 2 infiltrators were killed by the US forces, and the attack had killed or wounded 16 US soldiers. Some sources mentioned the local militia as ALP forces.

IS claimed responsibility for an attack early on the morning of January 29, 2018, in which 5 armed men attacked the army unit guarding a military university in the Qarghah area outside of Kabul city. 11 ANA soldiers were killed and 16 wounded; 4 of the attackers were also killed--2 via suicide bombing and 2 by security forces--and a 5th was detained. Afghan forces seized a rocket, some rifles, and a suicide vest from the assailants. IS claimed that the attack also targeted a US military base next to the Afghan military academy and that over 100 people had been killed and injured. 15 total fatalities (including attackers).

Islamic State sources reported that on February 19th IS militants fired a rocket at the US air force base at the Jalalabad airport in Nangarhar province. No casualties were reported, however rescue planes were reported to have rushed to the scene of the explosion.

Taliban sources reported that on March 10th, 4 Afghan military Special Forces, 1 Taliban militant, and 1 civilian were killed after Taliban militants attacked a joint party of US soldiers and Afghan Special Forces while they were raiding a house in the Gholam Dag area of Chaparhar district, Nangarhar.

As reported on March 31st, at least 4 unidentified militants, including 2 from the Chinese Islamist group Turkistan Islamic Party, were killed, and 13 wounded, during clashes with security forces in Jurm district of Badakshan province. It is unclear whether this battle is the same in which 4 civilians were reportedly killed on the 29th.
Taliban sources reported that on April 8th, Taliban militants hit a US air base near Jalalabad city with a rocket attack and inflicted unknown casualties.

On 26 December 2022, residents of Berxulla protested in Tirana in front of the US embassy demanding more transparency on a road construction project funded by the US in their area, claiming it affects their private property.
On 15 December 2020, pro-Polisario Saharawi refugees from the 'Smara' camp held a protest sit-in in Tidouf (Tindouf) to denounce the US recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara.
Police forced back some 40 Algerian parliamentary deputies who were marching towards the US embassy to protest the war in Iraq.

Elements from the Gendarmerie - who are entrusted with providing security for the Chinese company CITIC-CRCC, in charge of building El-Adjiba road, east of Bouira - were targeted by a militant group. One militant was killed by his own explosion

Algerians protested in Bouira province to denounce the US decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israels capital.
Inhabitants of Mascara protested against the recent US decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israels capital. The protest was organised by the MSP.

On 10 June 2018, a Chinese citizen was robbed and killed by criminal Algerians in broad daylight in the region of Dalbeda in Algiers. The Chinese ambassador pointed out that attacks against Chinese companies and personnel have increased significantly and issued a statement, alerting Chinese citizens in Algeria to take further safety precautions.
On 2 December 2018, unemployed workers from the Algerian-chinese factory Daphine d'Or, closed for two months, protested and called for the reopening of the factory.
On 04 January 2020, workers employed at a Chinese factory in Bechloul protested against 'deplorable' working conditions.
A Chinese citizen was killed and two Angolan citizens were seriously injured when the Chinese man allegedly tried to smash an explosive device he had collected from the bush

Cabinda separatists attacked a military vehicle tasked with guarding Chinese miners in northern Angola this week, resulting in the deaths of between two and 12 people, government and separatist sources said Friday.

On 12 February 2022, hundreds of Afghan refugees demonstrated in the Emirates Humanitarian City where they are housed in Abu Dhabi (Abu Dhabi) for the third consecutive day to denounce the failure of the UAE and US governments to relocate them to the US or other countries for six months as well as 'prison-like conditions' in the facility.

On 23 May 2023, in Lomas de Zamora (Buenos Aires), a group of workers at a Chinese store on Laprida 100 Avenue held a demonstration outside the premises of the store to demand better labor conditions.

On 2 November 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), thousands of people from the LGBTQ+ community and various social organizations, including the Evita Movement, Mothers of Plaza de Mayo, Grandmothers of Plaza de Mayo, and the group Hijos e Hijas por la Identidad y la Justicia contra el Olvido y el Silencio (HIJOS), participated in the 33rd edition of the LGBTQ+ Pride March, which started from Mayo Square and ended at the Congress Square. The protesters advocated for their rights, condemned violence against the community, and criticized the policies of President Javier Milei's government, demanding the enactment of a comprehensive trans law and an anti-discrimination law. The march included representatives from the City and Province governments, United Nations programs, and embassies of the United States, Germany, and France.

On 15 November 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 14 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), members of the Argentine Committee of Solidarity with the Palestinian People, integrated by Arab, Palestinian, and Jewish organizations, as well as human rights, social, and political organizations, protested in front of the United States Embassy to reject the shipment of weapons to Israel used in operations in the Gaza Strip. The protesters, who called for an end to apartheid against Palestinians and the prosecution of those responsible, condemned the invasion of Lebanon and the bombings of Syria, Yemen, and Iran carried out by Israel.

On 25 November 2024, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), women, students, members of the LGBTIQ+ community, a local legislator (FIT), and members of social, union, and political organizations marched from the intersection of Avenida de Mayo and 9 de Julio to Mayo Square against sexist violence, public policies promoted by President Javier Milei's government, Israel's military actions in Palestine, and the support provided by the United States to that conflict. The demonstrators also asserted their rights and expressed support for public education, Comprehensive Sexual Education (ESI), the separation of Church and State, and the right to abortion. They demanded justice and support for victims of violence. The mobilization was part of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

On 25 August 2020, in Buenos Aires (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), around 20 organizations, including environmentalists, gathered in Mayo Square to demand protection for the wetlands and question the agro-industrial businesses and the agreement between China and Argentina about the pork production. The police arrested three women, two of them were released.

On 25 September 2020, in San Carlos de Bariloche (Rio Negro), PO (Workers' Party) members and environmentalists of different associations gathered in the Civic Center to join the global movement Friday for Future, led by activist Greta Thunberg, to demand measures to the climate change crisis. The group also repudiated the pork production agreement with China, besides demanding the sanction and appliance of the Wetlands and the Forest Laws.

On 27 September 2020, in Santa Rosa (La Pampa), students gathered in the Civic Center to join the global movement Friday for Future, led by activist Greta Thunberg, to demand measures to the climate change crisis and repudiate the pork production agreement with China. The global movement took place on 25 September 2020, but in Santa Rosa it was postponed to 27 September due to bad weather.

On 11 October 2020, in Santa Rosa (La Pampa), environmentalists associated to La Pampa for the Environment group, gathered in a roundabout and protested to repudiate the pork production agreement with China, claiming that it would pollute the environment and waste water.

On 9 November 2020, in Santa Rosa (La Pampa), environmentalists associated to La Pampa for the Environment group gathered in a roundabout in the Civic Center and protested to repudiate the pork production agreement with China. The group handed the Governor a petition and also addressed other complaints.

Property destruction: On 23 October 2018, in Santa Fe (Santa Fe), a Chinese-owned supermarket was set on fire after unidentified individuals threw Molotov bombs in the establishment in the Presidente Roca y Arijon avenue. According to residents, the attack could have been motivated by a robbery attempt or connected to the Chinese mafia.

On 29 November 2018, in Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires, Buenos Aires, people gathered in front of the Chinese Embassy to protest against the G-20 Summit and to report persecution of the Falun Dafa group in China. At least four protesters were arrested by police forces.
On 23 August 2019, unidentified armed men attacked a group of Chinese migrants in the bus terminal in Cordoba, Cordoba. Two women were reported killed and one man injured.

Around 24 March 2021 (as reported), in El Espinillo (Chaco), residents protested with roadblocks against the installation project of Chinese mega pig farms in the area. Protesters expressed their concern, claiming that big amounts of soybeans, corn and millions of litres of water would be needed to feed the animals. In addition, protesters asked for piped water to be provided from the government.

On 25 August 2021, in San Fernando del Valle de Catamarca (Catamarca), members of the Workers' Socialist Movement (MST) and other left-wing organizations marched to repudiate President Alberto Fernandez (Justicialist Party)'s visit to the province, complaining about his support to the mining project and the pork production agreement with China, both eco-unfriendly activities. The protest took place during a general dissatisfaction with the government, weeks after became public a picture of the First Lady's birthday celebration inside the Presidential House during the period of social isolation.

On 25 August 2021, in Buenos Aires - Buenos Aires (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), environmentalists, members of the Workers' Socialist Movement (MST) and Workers' Left Front (FIT) gathered in front of China's Embassy to repudiate the pork production agreement with China, claiming that it would pollute the environment, waste water and that it is an extractive policy that hinders the country's food sovereignty.

On 24 September 2021, in Rosario (Santa Fe), a group that included students, Barrios de Pie, the Workers' Left Front (FIT), and the Workers' Party (PO) marched from San Martin square towards the Monument to the Flag to demand the approval of the wetlands law and measures to contain the climate change crisis, convened by Fridays for Future (FFF). The group was also against mining and repudiated the pork production agreement with China, claiming that it would pollute the environment and waste water.

The group was also against mining and repudiated the pork production agreement with China, claiming that it would pollute the environment and waste water. On 24 September 2021, in La Plata (Buenos Aires), a group, which included members of Youth for Climate (YFC), marched from Moreno towards San Martin square to demand measures to contain the climate change crisis, convened by Fridays for Future (FFF). The group was also against mining and repudiated the pork production agreement with China, claiming that it would pollute the environment and waste water.

The group was also against mining and repudiated the pork production agreement with China, claiming that it would pollute the environment and waste water.

On 24 September 2021, in Resistencia (Chaco), a group marched to demand measures to contain the climate change crisis, convened by Fridays for Future (FFF). The group was also against mining and repudiated the pork production agreement with China, claiming that it would pollute the environment and waste water.

On 24 September 2021, in Cordoba province, a group marched to demand the approval of the wetlands law and measures to contain the climate change crisis, convened by Fridays for Future (FFF). The group was also against mining and repudiated the pork production agreement with China, claiming that it would pollute the environment and waste water.

On 24 September 2021, in Buenos Aires (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), hundreds of people, including members of Youth for Climate (YFC), gathered in Mayo square to demand measures to contain the climate change crisis, convened by Fridays for Future (FFF). The group was also against mining and repudiated the pork production agreement with China, claiming that it would pollute the environment and waste water.

On 24 September 2021, in San Carlos de Bariloche (Rio Negro), many people, including members of Youth for Climate (YFC), gathered in the Civic Center's square to demand measures to contain the climate change crisis, convened by Fridays for Future (FFF). The group was also against mining and repudiated the pork production agreement with China, claiming that it would pollute the environment and waste water.

On 22 October 2021, in La Plata (Buenos Aires), environmentalists marched from Moreno square towards San Martin square demanding the government to act against the environmental destruction, request the approval of the wetlands law, and repudiate the pork production agreement with China.

As reported on 31 October 2019, in Santa Rosa (La Pampa), workers of the Chinese supermarket Super Peron gathered in demonstration against the job insecurity workers face. Participants set tires on fire in demonstration.

On 4 June 2020, a group of people organized a protest in front of the embassy of US in Yerevan (Yerevan, Armenia) against the racism and in support of the Black Lives Matter demonstrations in US started after the murder of George Floyd.

On 14 June 2020, members of Adekvat held a protest in front of the embassy of US in Yerevan (Yerevan, Armenia) and claimed that the embassy is not responding to the political persecutions in the country. The police detained the protestors for the violation of social distancing rules due to covid-19 pandemic.

On 19 January 2022, winners of the Green Card Lottery protested near the US Embassy in Yerevan, Armenia, as it has been months that they are not able to attend their Green Card interviews due to the bureaucratic processes.

On 9 April 2022, a group of people protested near the US Embassy in Yerevan, Armenia calling against the Western biological laboratories that allegedly operate in Armenia. The information about these laboratories was spread by Russia.

On 3 March 2025, supporters of Vardan Ghukasyan, who has been detained by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and is facing deportation, protested in front of the US Embassy in Yerevan, Armenia, calling the US government not to deport him.

On 22 March 2025, a group of people protested in front of the US Embassy in Yerevan, Armenia, calling against the US's silence on police brutality and violation of human rights in Armenia and support of questionable biomedical laboratories.

On 24 June 2022, protesters demonstrated with signs and interrupted a speech by the Chinese Ambassador at the University of Technology Sydney in Sydney - Eastern (New South Wales) to call for freedom in Tibet and express concern over the treatment of Uyghurs.

On 23 June 2022, protesters gathered outside the Prime Minister's electorate office in the Marrickville neighborhood of Sydney - Eastern (New South Wales) to call on the Prime Minister apply pressure to the US and UK to free Julian Assange.

On 27 June 2022, hundreds-about 400 of protesters gathered outside the US consulate in Perth - Central (Western Australia) to oppose the US Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe Vs Wade, a historical landmark abortion ruling. Protesters also called for a change in state laws. Western Australia is the only state with laws that determine under what circumstances an abortion can take place. US citizens in Australia and female students stood in solidarity with the protesters.

On 27 June 2022, protesters from March4JusticeAU gathered outside the US consulate in Melbourne - Central (Western Australia) to oppose the US Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe Vs Wade, a historical landmark abortion ruling.

On 1 July 2022, nearly 1,000-more than 2,000 protesters gathered at King George Square in Brisbane - Central (Queensland) to oppose the US Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe Vs Wade, a historical landmark abortion ruling, and stand in solidarity with women in the US. Labor group representatives, an ALP MP, a Greens MP, and a member of the Socialist Alliance spoke at the protest. The protest was supported by Children by Choice, Cheek Media, One Woman Project, and March4Justice.

On 1 July 2022, around 5,000 protesters marched through Adelaide (South Australia) before gathering in front of the state parliament to oppose the US Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe Vs Wade, a historical landmark abortion ruling, and stand in solidarity with women in the US. Prominent students, lawyers and a local Greens councilor spoke at the protest.

On 30 June 2022, hundreds of protesters gathered in Newcastle (New South Wales) to oppose the US Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe Vs Wade, a historical landmark abortion ruling, and stand in solidarity with women in the US. Two state ALP MPs and city councilors from the ALP and Greens spoke at the protest.

On 28 November 2022, about 200 demonstrators including members of the greater Chinese community and supporters gathered at the Melbourne State Library in Melbourne - Central (Victoria) to rally in support of the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China and to rally against Chinese President Xi Jinping. Students were among those present.

On 23 December 2022, demonstrators including Latinx American-Australians and others gathered outside the Peruvian Consulate in Sydney - Eastern (New South Wales) to rally in support of ongoing protests following the ousting of the president of Peru after he attempted to dissolve Congress when faced with impeachment proceedings due to alleged corruption charges. They called for the Australian government to intervene and for the US government to cease its support of the current Peruvian government.

On 22 February 2021, around 100 people gathered in Yorkeys Knob (Queensland) to protest a mooted Chinese wellness center, labelling it 'ghastly' and 'gross'. The protesters stated that the site is an inappropriate location for any type of development, especially for a large-scale wellness center.
On 3 June 2023, volunteers of the Australia-Cuba Friendship Society gathered at the Botanical Gardens in Brisbane - Central (Queensland), calling for an end to the US blockade of Cuba.

On 11 September 2023, activists protested and held banners outside the US Consulate building in Melbourne - Central (Western Australia). They criticized the US involvement in Chile during the 1970s coup against the socialist government. They also denounced the ongoing US interference in Latin America, including its economic war against Cuba and Venezuela.

On 29 October 2023, 50,000 people, including union members, such as a person with the New South Wales Nurses and Midwives' Association (also a midwife), Palestinian people, and Muslim Australians, marched from Hyde Park to Belmore Park in Sydney - Eastern, New South Wales, calling for the freedom of Palestine and a ceasefire of the armed conflict between Hamas and Israel. They also accused the Primer Minister, Israel, and the US of supporting Israeli military actions in Gaza. The Palestinian Action Group organized the event.

On 10 November 2023, about 200 pro-Palestinian protesters, including a Jewish person, gathered outside the Israeli and U.S. embassies in Canberra, Australian Capital Territory against the Israeli attack on Gaza. They called for an immediate ceasefire of the armed conflict and the freedom of Palestine. Members of the Palestine Action Group and Canberra Muslims for Palestine were present in the protest.

On 19 November 2023, tens of thousands of pro-Palestinian demonstrators gathered at Hyde Park in Sydney - Central (New South Wales) to demand a ceasefire and to condemn the Australian and the US governments for supporting Israel in what demonstrators call a 'genocide.'

On 10 December 2023, thousands of people, including an MP from the Australian Greens and a MEAA member, marched to Adelaide Street in Brisbane - Central, Queensland, to criticize the Prime Minister for his stance to support the U.S. and Israel. They also called for an immediate and permanent ceasefire in the armed conflict and the freedom of Palestine. They opposed the Israeli attack on Gaza.

On 13 March 2024, a dozen members of the CFMEU protested at the western approach to the Centenary Bridge in Jindalee (Brisbane - Western, Queensland) against the suspected use of Chinese steel in a vital bridge duplication.

On 20 March 2024, people protested in front of the Chinese embassy and the parliament in Canberra, Australian Capital Territory, to call for democracy in China. On the same day, the Chinese Foreign Minister arrived in Australia.

On 26 August 2021, about 120 fishers, surfers, environmental activists and other residents of King Island gathered in Currie (Tasmania) to oppose seismic testing by a US oil and gas company off the coast of the island. About 100 gathered on the wharf itself while about 20 gathered on boats and dinghies on the water.

On 16 June 2024, anti-China government protesters, including the president of the East Turkistan Australian Association and a Uyghur advocate, chanted 'Uyghur lives matter' and 'Human lives over profit' near Adelaide Zoo in Adelaide, South Australia. This demonstration was in response to China's Premier Li Qiang's visit to Australia and China's gift of two pandas to the zoo. The protesters waved flags representing Uyghur, Tibetan, Hong Kong, Australia, and East Turkistan, and called on the Australian government not to be swayed by 'panda propaganda.' They encountered pro-China government groups holding flags and chanted 'Shame on China' and 'Shame on you' at them.

On 18 June 2024, people protested in Perth, Western Australia, against the China's human rights abuses against Muslim Uyghur minority groups in Xinjiang, oppression in Tibet, and Beijing's crackdown on dissent in Hong Kong. The protest was a response to China's Premier Li Qiang's visit to Australia.

On 17 June 2024, about 500 anti-China government people, including Tibetans, Uighurs, members of the Hong Kong pro-democracy movement, and advocates for Tibet and Uyghur human rights, along with a journalist, demonstrated in front of the Parliament in Canberra, Australian Capital Territory, to call for free speech. They waved Tibet's flags. Simultaneously, about 500 pro-China people demonstrated, holding both Chinese and Australian flags. The demonstrators from both sides clashed. One demonstrator was arrested. The event was in response to China's Premier Li Qiang's visit to Australia. On the same day, both pro and anti-China government demonstrators gathered outside the Premier's hotel and lined the streets where his motorcade would travel to Parliament.

On 31 May 2024, about 100 pro-Palestinian people gathered in front of the Victorian Investment Centre on Collins St and marched to Collins Square in Melbourne - Central, Victoria, against a state government-backed defense forum taking place in the center. Some staged a die-in. During the event, a man threw coffee at a participant, who then hit him over the head with a megaphone and scratched his face. On the same day, pro-Palestinian rioters smashed the windows at the US Consulate General on St Kilda Rd, Melbourne - Central, Victoria, and splashed paint on the walls with 'Free Gaza' graffiti. The events were part of a national day of action, featuring occupations at ALP MP offices across the country.

On 4 July 2024, about 100 people, including members from Anakbayan Melbourne, SA, Australia-Cuba Friendship Society said the US, Latin American Solidarity Network, Free Palestine Coalition, and Venezuela Solidarity Campaign, protested outside the US Consulate in Melbourne - Central, Victoria, against the US's perceived role in causing global conflict and devastation. Participants waved Palestinian flags and criticized the US for supporting what they described as Israel's 'genocide.' They also denounced Australia for its support of US military presence, including bases, troops, and aircraft stationed in the country. Additionally, the protesters opposed what they viewed as US preparations for conflict with China and criticized US accusations against Cuba while supporting Israeli actions against Palestinians.

On 26 October 2024, around 40 members of a neo-Nazi group gathered outside the Chinese consulate in Toorak, Melbourne - Southeastern, Victoria, demanding China extradite the man accused of throwing hot coffee on a baby in Brisbane in August. The group used offensive language and displayed a banner reading, 'Yellow grubs hand over the baby mutilator.'
On 27 November 2024, Palestine supporters rallied outside the US consulate in Melbourne - Central, Victoria, in response to the US vetoing a Gaza ceasefire in the UN Security Council.

On 7 February 2025, about 200 people, including members of Friends of Palestine WA and members of SA: Socialist Alliance gathered to protest with placards and banners at the US consulate in Perth (Western Australia). They showed solidarity with the Palestinian people, opposed Donald Trump's recent announcement of a potential Gaza takeover by the US, and demanded that the Australian government cut ties with Israel.

On 22 February 2025, anti-war protesters gathered outside the Garden Island Naval Base at Potts Point (Sydney - Eastern, New South Wales) as part of the global day of action against military bases. They held banners with messages such as 'No nuclear marines, No war on China,' 'Stop Pine Gap targeting Palestinians in Gaza,' and 'Scrap AUKUS now.'

On 16 May 2021, members of the Kurdish community and supporters protested in front of City Hall in Sydney - Eastern (New South Wales) demanding that the US stop supporting Turkey's actions towards Kurds.

On 30 March 2021, hundreds of people from Uyghur community group gathered in Adelaide (South Australia) to protest the opening of the new Chinese consulate. The demonstrators were later joined by people from the Tibetan community who compared the consulate being built with China's takeover of Tibet.
On 31 January 2022, 5 Tibetan monks departed Newcastle (New South Wales) on a march to Sydney to protest human rights abuses in China and their treatment of the Tibetan community.

On 12 March 2022, over 150 Tibetans and supporters of the Tibetan community protested with banners in the city center of Canberra (Australian Capital Territory) to mark the 63rd anniversary of Tibetan National Uprising Day. The protesters highlighted the repressive policies of the CCP and demanded justice for Tibetans in Tibet. A separate group also gathered outside the Chinese Embassy.
On 18 July 2021, people from the Australia-Cuba Friendship Society including Cubans held a car convoy protest in Brisbane (Queensland) to call for an end to the US blockade on Cuba.

On 5 June 2020, around 8,000 people protested in Vienna - Alsergrund in front of the US embassy against police violence under the motto 'Black Lives Matter'. The protest was sparked by the murder of George Floyd by the police in the US.

On 12 September 2023, people protested in front of the US embassy in Vienna - Alsergrund (Wien 9-Alsergrund, Wien) for the freedom of the indigenous political prisoner Leonard Peltier who has been imprisoned in the USA since 1976 due to his actions as a member of the American Indian Movement (A.I.M.).

On 15 March 2024, 3 Last Generation activists gathered outside the Federal Chancellery in Ballhausplatz in Wien - Inner City (Wien), expressing their discontent regarding the visit of US Secretary of State Antony Blinken. They aimed to highlight the responsibility of the US and Europe as major contributors to the climate crisis, urging for more action to safeguard the future of civilization.

On 6 January 2020, hundreds of people, including Iranians, peacefully commemorated the death of Iranian General Soleimani on a square in Vienna - Inner City (Wien), at Stock-im-Eisen-Platz (next to Stephansplatz), while the organizer also criticised the role of Germany and accused the US of supporting terrorism. A small counterprotest took place, which denounced the fascist and national socialist Iranian regime.

On 24 October 2021, 28 people protested in front of the Ministry of Sport (BMKOS) in Vienna - Inner City to call for a diplomatic boycott of the 2022 Beijing Olympics, citing the 'genocide' of Uyghurs by China.

On 15 August 2018, in Baku, several dozen of people held a demonstration in support of Turkey outside the Turkish embassy in Baku. They were protesting against the US policies and sanctions imposed on Ankara. The picket chanted slogans, including 'Long live Turkey, Long live Erdogan', 'Down with dollars'.
On 27 February 2021, around 100 people staged a protest at the Chinese embassy in Brussels - Woluwe-Saint-Pierre to denounce the treatment of the Uighur population in China.
On 11 March 2021, several dozen people staged a protest at the Chinese embassy in Brussels - Woluwe-Saint-Pierre to denounce the treatment of the Uighur population in China.

On 11 January 2020, around 30 people staged a protest action in front of the US Embassy in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to demand the closure of Guantanamo Prison. Several organizations were present, including Comite Free Assange Belgium, Collectif de Lutte Anti-Carcerale (CLAC), Be. One party and Bruxelles Pantheres.

On 5 April 2021, around 30 people of Iranian descent staged a protest at the Iranian embassy in Brussels - Woluwe-Saint-Pierre to denounce the recent trade agreement between China and Iran, claiming Iran sells out its national wealth.

On 12 January 2020, around 350 people gathered at Brussels Central Station in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to protest against the Chinese oppression of its Uighur population. Uighur and Turkish flags were widely present.

On 14 June 2021, an unknown number of Amnesty International activists staged a protest at the American Embassy in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to demand the closure of the US Guantanamo Bay prison, in the context of the state visit of US President Biden to Belgium.
On 27 June 2021, an unknown number of Greenpeace activists staged a protest in Tongeren against the imminent arrival of the Chinese company Alibaba to the Liege Bierset Airport.
On 24 November 2021, around 50 people staged a protest at Kouter square in Gent to denounce the US boycott of Cuba.

On 2 June 2022, an unknown number of Amnesty International activists staged a protest at the Chinese embassy in Brussels - Woluwe-Saint-Pierre to commemorate the 33rd birthday of the Tiananmen massacre and denounce the Chinese crackdown on political opponents in Hong Kong.
On 30 June 2022, several hundred people staged a protest at the American embassy in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to denounce the rollback of the federal right for abortion in the US.

On 26 October 2022, around 120 people staged a protest outside the Central Station in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles to denounce the continuing US blockade of Cuba. Members of ABVV-FGTB, ACV-CSC, PVDA-PTB and Vooruit were present.

On 17 January 2020, an unkown number of people staged a protest action on Place Saint-Lambert in Liege against the coming of the Chinese company Alibaba to Liege Airport, allegedly causing considerable environmental damage.

On 22 April 2023, at the call of action group CPLBCC - Coordination Lifting the Blockade against Cuba, an unknown number of people protested in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles, to demand that U.S. president Biden normalize relations with Cuba and lift the U.S.'s economic blockade of the country.

On 18 June 2020, at least 4 activists of Amnesty International staged a protest action at the Chinese embassy in Brussels - Woluwe-Saint-Pierre by shouting the names of the people who signed their petition against the new Chinese security law regarding Hong Kong.

On 20 November 2023, an unknown number of Amnesty International activists staged a protest in front of the US Embassy in Brussels (Brussels) by laying 200 white sheets symbolizing the victims of the war in Gaza. They demanded US support for a cease fire.

On 20 February 2024, 200 people gathered in front of the US Embassy in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to ask for the acquittal and immediate release of Julian Assange. On 14 May 2022, about 100 people held a rally in downtown Vancouver (British Columbia) for abortion rights after a leaked U.S. Supreme Court draft revealed that it could change the landmark Roe V. Wade decision that legalized abortion.

On 15 May 2022, around 200 people gathered at Olympic Plaza in downtown Calgary (Alberta) for abortion rights after a leaked U.S. Supreme Court draft revealed that it could change the landmark Roe V. Wade decision that legalized abortion.

On 13 May 2022, a group of protesters who staged a rally in Queen's Park in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to demonstrate against access to abortion met with a group of pro-choice counter-protesters after a leaked U.S. Supreme Court draft revealed that it could change the landmark Roe V. Wade decision that legalized abortion.

On 28 May 2022, about twenty women staged a rally in front of the American consulate in Quebec City (Quebec) for access to abortion after a leaked U.S. Supreme Court draft revealed that it could overturn the landmark Roe V. Wade decision that legalized abortion.

On 2 October 2021, dozens of people protested at Highway 99 in Vancouver (British Columbia) to call for the federal government to repatriate Canadians detained in China. This event was sparked the return of Michael Sparvor and Korvig to Canada on October 1.

On 2 October 2021, around 40 people protested in front of the US consulate in Vancouver (British Columbia) in solidarity with Texan protesters against the abortion ban. The protest was organized by Options for Sexual Health.

On 9 November 2022, local residents, including women groups, staged a 'pro-choice' rally in front of the Saskatchewan Legislature in Regina (Saskatchewan) in solidarity with Americans for reproductive rights to call for better access to abortion.

On 27 November 2022, local residents, including Chinese community members, staged a protest outside the Chinese consulate in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to show solidarity with ongoing protests against anti-lockdown demonstrations in China and to demonstrate against the Chinese Communist Party due to the deaths of at least ten people in an apartment fire in the Xinjiang region.

On 27 November 2022, hundreds of people, including Chinese community members, staged a protest outside the Art Gallery in Vancouver (British Columbia) to show solidarity with ongoing protests against the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China and to demonstrate against the Chinese Communist Party due to the deaths of at least ten people in an apartment fire in the Xinjiang region.
On 16 March 2023, workers of Windsor Salt, including Unifor members, staged a rally in Windsor (Ontario) to demand a fair contract from the U.S. holding company.

On 10 March 2023, protesters, including Tibetan community members, rallied outside City Hill in Calgary (Alberta) to protest against the Chinese government and mark the anniversary of the Tibetan uprising.

On 24 March 2023, a few dozen local residents, including Haitian community members, held a rally in front of the United States Consulate General in Montreal - Center East (Quebec) to protest against US interference in the internal affairs of Haiti.

On 12 April 2023, workers of Windsor Salt, including Unifor Locals 1959 and 240 members, staged a rally in Windsor (Ontario) to demand job security and to protest against the company's American owners for contracting out their jobs. NDP leader Jagmeet Singh joined to support their strike.

On 17 July 2021, several people, including Cuban Canadians, gathered outside the US Consulate in Montreal - Center East (Quebec) to demand the removal of the US embargo against Cuba. The protest was organized by Table de concertation de solidarite Quebec-Cuba.

On 9 July 2023, protesters, including Uyghur and Muslim communities, held a march from Dorchester Square to Place des Arts in Montreal - Center East (Quebec) to protest against the systematic harassment of Uyghurs and ethnic Muslim minorities by the Chinese government in Xinjiang and to commemorate the 14th anniversary of the July 2009 riots in the City of Urumqi. International Support for Uyghurs (ISU) organized the march.

On 20 October 2023, more than a hundred people, including members of the Palestinian community, held a pro-Palestinian and anti-Israel rally outside the U.S. consulate and in front of Premier Minister Francois Legault's office in Montreal - Center East (Quebec) after a projectile exploded at the al-Ahli Arab Hospital in Gaza on 17 October, to support Palestinian civilians and to denounce Israeli airstrikes and ground operations against Gaza. The Palestinian Youth Movement organized the rally. Members of Solidarity for Palestinian Human Rights McGill and Independent Jewish Voices were also present. This demonstration took place in the wake of renewed fighting between Israel and Hamas.

On 17 October 2023, more than 1000 pro-Palestinian people, including members of the Palestinian community, rallied outside the U.S. consulate in Montreal - Center East and then walked to the Israeli consulate in Westmount Square in Montreal - Center West (Quebec) after a projectile exploded at the al-Ahli Arab Hospital in Gaza on 17 October, to call the U.S. to denounce the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and to stop sending financial support to the Israeli military. Demonstrators also condemned the loss of Palestinian civilian life and attacks by Israel. Members of the Palestinian Youth Movement organized the protest. This demonstration took place in the wake of renewed fighting between Israel and Hamas.

On 21 October 2023, thousands of people held a pro-Palestinian rally outside the U.S. Consulate and marched south along University Avenue and then reached Lake Shore Boulevard West and York Street, steps away from the Gardiner Expressway in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to support Palestinian civilians and to call for a ceasefire in the Israel and Hamas war. Protesters stopped and chanted 'Free, Free Palestine' outside Cafe Landwer - a Jewish-owned cafe at University Avenue and Adelaide Street. This demonstration took place in the wake of renewed fighting between Israel and Hamas.

On 4 November 2023, thousands of people held a pro-Palestinian rally and sit-in in front of the U.S. Consulate General and blocked downtown streets in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to support Palestinian civilians, to condemn Israeli military action, to call for Canada to condemn Israeli military action, and to call for a ceasefire in the Israel and Hamas war. The Palestinian Youth Movement organized the rally. Members of the Jews Say No to Genocide group attended the rally. This demonstration took place in the wake of renewed fighting between Israel and Hamas.

On 18 November 2023, thousands of people held a pro-Palestinian rally outside U.S. Consulate General along University Avenue in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to support Palestinian civilians and to call for a ceasefire in the Israel and Hamas war. Demonstrators also condemned the state of Israel. Members of Independent Jewish Voices and Palestinian Youth Movement were present at the rally. Demonstrators also set off smoke bombs and fireworks during the march. This demonstration took place in the wake of renewed fighting between Israel and Hamas.

On 22 February 2021, a group of people, including Uyghur, gathered on Parliament Hill in Ottawa (Ontario) to protest against the Chinese government's treatment of the Uyghur minority in China. During the protest, the House of Commons accused the Chinese government of carrying out a campaign of genocide against Uyghurs and other Turkic Muslims.

On 9 December 2023, people, including members of the Palestinian community, held a pro-Palestinian rally at the Human Rights Monument on Elgin Street and marched toward the US embassy in Ottawa (Ontario) to call for a permanent ceasefire in the Israel-Hamas war and to denounce Israeli airstrikes and ground operations against Gaza. The Palestinian Youth Movement organized the rally. This demonstration took place amid the Israel-Hamas war which began in October 2023. On 10 December 2023, thousands of people, including members of the Palestinian community, held a pro-Palestinian rally outside TPS 52 Division and the US Consulate in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to call for a ceasefire and to denounce Israeli military action. Police arrested a protester for assaulting a police officer. According to organizers and police, a police officer on his bike clipped a demonstrator on his bike, causing the demonstrator to fall. In response, another demonstrator pushed the police officer to the ground. According to demonstrators, when police officers arrested the individual who pushed the officer, they punched him several times in the head and placed a knee on his neck. The Palestinian Youth Movement organized the rally. There was also a separate rally of about 500 people in support of Palestine at the Yonge and Dundas area. This demonstration took place amid the Israel-Hamas war which began in October 2023.

On 16 December 2023, people, including members of the Palestinian community, held a pro-Palestinian rally outside the US Consulate, and some protesters staged a sit-in at Eaton Centre in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) in support of health care workers in Gaza, to call for a ceasefire in the Israel and Hamas war. The Palestinian Youth Movement organized the rally. This demonstration took place amid the Israel-Hamas war which began in October 2023.
On 23 February 2021, Chinese community staged a car rally in Burlington (Ontario) against Communist Party of China.

On 12 February 2024, hundreds of people held a pro-Palestinian rally outside of the Mount Sinai Hospital, after which they marched to the U.S. consulate and the Israeli consulate in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to call for a permanent ceasefire in the Israel-Hamas war and a weapons embargo on Israel. This demonstration took place amid the Israel-Hamas war, which began in October 2023. Mount Sinai Hospital was founded as a Jewish hospital. The groups Jews Say No To Genocide, Palestinian Youth Movement and Toronto4Palestine, who organized this demonstration, denied any antisemitism and claimed the hospital was merely located along the protest route.

On 6 April 2024, thousands of pro-Palestinian demonstrators marched outside the U.S. Consulate General on University Avenue and then toward the south of Dundas Street in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) in support of Palestine and waving the Palestinian flag. Roughly a half-dozen counter-protesters rallied at the same location in support of Israel. Toronto police arrested a counter-protester for breach of peace. This demonstration took place amid the Israel-Hamas war, which began in October 2023.

On 2 May 2024, perhaps 400 pro-Palestinian students from Concordia University and McGill University staged a rally and maintained their encampment at McGill University's campus in Montreal - Center East (Quebec) in support of Palestine to demand that their university divest from Israeli companies and an academic boycott of Israeli universities. The Solidarity for Palestinian Human Rights McGill, Solidarity for Palestinian Human Rights Concordia, Independent Jewish Voices McGill and Independent Jewish Voices Concordia organized the rally. A handful of Orthodox Jews and MNA Haroun Bouazzi (QS) were also present. Hundreds of pro-Israeli counter-protesters, including Jews, rallied in front of the McGill encampment in support of Israel. The counter-protest was organized by The Stand With Us Canada group. Police officers on horseback and bicycles kept a distance between protesters and counter-protesters. This was the sixth day of a campus demonstration after the arrest of student demonstrators at Columbia University in New York on 18 April. This demonstration was held amid the Israel-Hamas war, which began in October 2023.

On 24 May 2024, over a dozen local residents of Lewisville held a rally in Moncton (New Brunswick) to protest against an American Iron & Metal scrapyard near their homes. Moncton city councilors Monique LeBlanc, Charles Leger, Shawn Crossman, deputy mayor Paulette Theriault, and MLA Daniel Allain (PC) were present.

On 25 May 2024, around 30 local residents of Lewisville held a rally for the second day in a row in Moncton (New Brunswick) to protest against the American Iron & Metal (AIM) recycling operation near their homes and to show their concern about environmental and noise pollution.

On 10 March 2021, at least 100 local residents from Tibetan community held a march from city hall to the Chinese consulate in Calgary (Alberta) to mark Tibetan Uprising Day over the Chinese occupation of Tibet.

On 8 June 2024, pro-Palestinian protesters held a march outside the U.S. consulate on University Avenue and held up a large flag of Palestine in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) in support of Palestine, to demand a weapons embargo on Israel. Demonstrators also held a flag to obscure other demonstrators graffitiing a building. When police officers tried to confiscate the flag, some protestors resisted the arrest by pushing and shoving police officers. At least one demonstrator was punched in the face by a police officer. The police arrested 4 demonstrators for mischief and obstructing a police officer. This demonstration took place amid the Israel-Hamas war, which began in October 2023.
On 5 September 2021, around 150 people protested outside Parliament Hill in Ottawa (Ontario) to demand for the release of two Canadian men from Chinese prisons.

On 7 October 2024, hundreds of pro-Palestinian protesters held a rally at the Vancouver Art Gallery in Vancouver (British Columbia) as part of an International Day of Action for Palestine to mark the first anniversary of the Israel-Hamas war. They called for an immediate and permanent ceasefire in Gaza and condemned the Israeli military strikes in Gaza and Lebanon. The Samidoun Network (a Palestinian group; sanctioned due to its links with the PFLP by multiple international governments) organized the rally. A masked speaker addressed the crowd, declaring, 'We are Hezbollah, and we are Hamas,' and led chants of 'Death to Canada, death to the United States, and death to Israel.' Both Hamas and Hezbollah are designated as terrorist organizations by Public Safety Canada. This demonstration occurred amid the ongoing Israel-Hamas war, which began in October 2023.

On 8 February 2025, around 50 protesters staged a rally outside the U.S. consulate in Vancouver (British Columbia) to protest against the U.S. tariffs on Canadian exports and rejected President Donald Trump's suggestion that Canada should become the 51st state. They aimed to protect Canadian sovereignty and freedom.

On 17 February 2025, about three dozen protesters staged a rally outside the U.S. embassy in Ottawa (Ontario) to protest against Elon Musk, the U.S. tariffs on Canadian exports and rejected President Donald Trump's suggestion that Canada should become the 51st state. They aimed to protect Canadian sovereignty and freedom.

Property destruction: On 5 March 2025, a masked individual vandalized a home in High River (Alberta), targeting a U.S. flag displayed outside while also damaging two vehicles. The perpetrator(s) also threw a concrete block through the front window of the home. The homeowners, one of whom is a Trump supporter, believe the incident was politically motivated. However, the High River RCMP has launched an investigation and has not confirmed the suspect's motive.

On 1 March 2025, almost 30 protesters from the Buffalo People Arts Institute, held a rally outside of the Regina German Club in Regina (Saskatchewan) to demand that the Buffalo Party stop using the word 'buffalo' in their name and emphasized the cultural and historical significance of the buffalo to Indigenous communities. They also protested the Buffalo Party's event discussing Canada becoming the 51st state, condemning USA and Trump.

On 3 March 2025, hundreds of people, including the Ukrainian community, held a rally following a verbal confrontation between Trump and Zelenskyy at the White House near Yonge and Dundas streets, then headed to the U.S. consulate in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to demand continued international support, including aid, amidst Russia's ongoing invasion. Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow (NDP), Deputy Mayor Mike Colle (i) and City Councillor Dianne Saxe were present.

On 4 March 2025, hundreds of protesters, including American citizens, staged an anti-tariff rally outside the U.S. embassy in Ottawa (Ontario) to protest against the U.S. tariffs on Canadian exports and rejected President Donald Trump's suggestion that Canada should become the 51st state. They aimed to protect Canadian sovereignty and freedom. During the protest, some demonstrators waved Ukrainian flags to support Ukrainians, following a verbal confrontation between Trump and Zelenskyy at the White House.
On 14 March 2025, around 15 people staged an anti-tariff rally in the Village of Elbow (Saskatchewan) to support Canadian sovereignty in response to U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs and threats.

On 8 March 2025, hundreds of people, including members of Meres au Front, rallied on International Women's Day on Ste-Catherine Street outside the U.S. Consulate in Montreal - Center East (Quebec) to protest against U.S. policies on women's rights and to support Canadian sovereignty. Protesters denounced Donald Trump's policies and his administration and against Elon Musk, associating him with regressive policies. The rally also showed solidarity with women in the United States, the LGBTQ+ community, as well as Ukrainian and Palestinian people amid the Israel-Hamas war which began in October 2023.

On 9 March 2025, a few dozen protesters rallied outside the RBC Place during Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre's speech in London (Ontario) to protest against Poilievre and Donald Trump, with some holding signs critical of both Poilievre and Trump. Demonstrators were also in support of the LGBTQ+ community.

On 9 March 2025, around 1000 people staged an anti-tariff rally on Parliament Hill in Ottawa (Ontario) to support Canadian sovereignty and to protest against the U.S. tariffs on Canadian exports and rejected President Donald Trump's suggestion that Canada should become the 51st state. Ottawa Mayor Mark Sutcliffe and MP Yasir Naqvi (LPC) attended the rally.

Property destruction: On 20 March 2025, an unidentified group set fire to two Tesla superchargers located in the Woodgrove Centre parking lot in Nanaimo (British Columbia). The perpetrator also used an unidentified blunt weapon to damage the rest of the Tesla superchargers. The RCMP believe that this is a part of actions against Elon Musk and his political role in the United States. No private vehicles were damaged during the event.

On 15 March 2025, approximately 100 people rallied in front of the Stablex factory in Blainville (Quebec) to protest against the Legault government's bill that would allow Stablex to expand its landfill for hazardous waste. They demanded that the toxic waste coming from the USA stop being deposited in their area. Members of the Blainville Citizens' Coalition Against Stablex Unit 6 and the party leader of Climat Quebec Martine Ouellet were present.

On 15 March 2025, a handful of protesters staged a rally outside the Tesla showroom at Lime Ridge Mall in Hamilton (Ontario) against Elon Musk, to call for a boycott of Tesla, due to his support of Donald Trump and his controversial statements. They also supported Canadian sovereignty in response to U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs and threats.

On 16 March 2025, about two dozen protesters staged a rally of 'Elbows up Canada' outside the Tesla dealership in Surrey (British Columbia) against Elon Musk, to call for boycotting Tesla due to his support of Donald Trump and his controversial statements. They also supported Canadian sovereignty in response to U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs and threats.

On 15 March 2025, dozens of protesters staged a rally of 'Elbows up Canada' outside the Tesla showroom on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver (British Columbia) to demonstrate against Elon Musk, Tesla, and the Trump administration and criticized Musk for his financial and political support of Trump. They also supported Canadian sovereignty in response to U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs and threats.

On 22 March 2025, about 40 to 50 protesters staged a rally in front of a Tesla dealership on Carling Avenue in Ottawa (Ontario) against Elon Musk, to call for a boycott of Tesla, due to his support of Donald Trump and his controversial statements. They also supported Canadian sovereignty in response to U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs and threats. A driver taking a shortcut through the parking lot hit a demonstrator. The demonstrator was not injured and the police issued the driver a ticket.

On 22 March 2025, dozens of protesters staged a rally at the Peace Arch monument in Surrey (British Columbia) to protest against the U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his recent suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state, and in support of Canadian sovereignty. American members of Raging Grannies participated. Mary Lou Steward, mayor of Blaine, Washington also attended.

On 22 March 2025, hundreds of protesters staged a rally of 'Elbows up Canada' at Nathan Phillips Square in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to protest against the U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his recent suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state, and in support of Canadian sovereignty.

On 24 March 2025, dozens of protesters staged a rally of 'Elbows up Canada' outside the U.S. consulate in Vancouver (British Columbia) to protest against the U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his recent suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state, and in support of Canadian sovereignty. There was one counter-demonstrator in support of President Trump. The police escorted him away from the demonstration.

On 22 March 2025, hundreds of protesters staged a rally at the riverfront in Windsor (Ontario) to protest against the U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his recent suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state, and in support of Canadian sovereignty. The rally aimed to highlight the strong ties between Canadians and Americans and to reject Trump's divisive approach. The rally was organized by Detroit-based 'We the People Dissent.'
18 March. Protesters organised by ODS leader, Lilian Koulou Engoulou, demonstrate in Yaounde of Mfoundi against the US intervention in Cameroon internal affairs.

properties.actor: Boko Haram - Jamaatu Ahli is-Sunnah lid-Dawati wal-Jihad
properties.notes: A Cameroonian soldier was killed during the military's response to a raid by Boko Haram on a Chinese construction company and their kidnapped 10 Chinese nationals

Around 20 August 2020 (as reported), youths demonstrated in front of the US Embassy in Yaounde city (Mfoundi, Centre), calling on the US government to arrest and deport Cameroonians living in the US and 'fanning terrorism' in Cameroon.

Around 9 February 2021 (as reported), residents burnt a truck and houses of workers of a Chinese gold mining company in Kambele 2 village, Batouri subdivision (Kadey, Est), after the truck killed a local gold miner in an accident. The gendarmerie forces reportedly made use of live ammunition to disperse the demonstrators, injuring several. Several others were arrested.

On 15 November 2017, an altercation occurred between villagers and a Chinese worker, who took a homemade gun and shot a villager dead. The local population reacted with pebbles, pickaxes, and clubs to fight the Chinese man who was also killed. The anger of local populations did not stop at the death of the Chinese, they also administered a caning to all Chinese nationals of the yard.
On 9 April 2019, in Abidjan, in front of the US embassy, a group of private security workers from G4S staged a protest to demand better salaries.

On 22 December 2019, the populations of Yakasse-Feyasse town, in Abengourou subdivision (Indenie-Djuablin, Comoe) erected roadblocks as they were protesting against the installation of Chinese illegal gold diggers in their area.
Around 2 November 2020 (as reported), residents burnt 5 cars belonging to the Chinese CHICO company in Danane town (Tonkpi, Montagnes), after one of the cars killed a resident in a road accident.
Protest at US embassy over comments made by ambassador

On 12 January 2024, over 300 youths beat security guards and damaged material at a mining site in Kafine (Niakaramandougou, Hambol, Vallee du Bandama) accusing the Chinese mining company of polluting the nearby water dam.
04 October. An angry crowd in Sosso Nakombo killed three Chinese nationals and injured at least one other. The attack followed the drowning of a local youth leader who worked for the foreigners.

On 30 August 2020, a group of local armed people clashed with FOCA soldiers and private security guards in a mining site in Gaga village, located 70 Km from Yaloke (Yaloke, Ombella M'Poko). The state forces were forced to retreat, allowing the locals to loot the office of the Chinese mining company which runs the site, including the robbery of Chinese workers. The clash was triggered by an incident in which 1 local was shot and injured by the soldiers. No fatalities and/or injuries reported.

Non-violent transfer of territory: On 16 December 2020, anti-Balaka fighters from Bossangoa and Bozoum occupied the city of Yaloke (Yaloke, Ombella M'Poko) on the second day for a total of 48 hours, impounding vehicles of the Chinese company constructing the road connecting Bossembele to Bossangoa.
On 10 September 2021, a group gathered in front of the US embassy in Bangui (Bangui, Bangui) in a demonstration to demand the lifting of the country's arms embargo.

Looting: Around 18 November 2021 (week of), Russian mercenaries from Wagner Group looted two mining excavators, belonging to a Chinese private mining company and to a Central African miner, in Yidere village, 40km from Abba (Nana-Mambere).

Around 25 November 2021 (week of), Russian mercenaries from Wagner Group abducted around 10 miners, who worked for a Chinese mining company, in Lamy-Pont mining site near Abba (Nana-Mambere). The victims were then released after a few days and after the Chinese company paid a ransom of 60 millions francs. There were no fatalities nor injuries.

properties.actor: CPC: Coalition of Patriots for Change
properties.notes: On 13 October 2022, CPC militants attacked and fought with FACA at a mining site in Ndiba Mole at about 35 kilometers of Gallo (Baboua, Nana-Mambere). Two soldiers were killed, one Chinese civilian injured and another soldier held hostage.

properties.actor: CPC: Coalition of Patriots for Change
properties.notes: On 28 November 2022, suspected CPC fighters clashed with FACA soldiers along the Niem-Yelewa Road, coded to Niem (Niem-Yelewa, Bouar, Nana-Mambere) leading to 1 soldier killed. 1 Chinese national working for a road reconstruction company was abducted. The victims were traveling with another FACA soldier and an interpret who managed to escape.

properties.actor: CPC: Coalition of Patriots for Change
properties.notes: On 13 March 2023, suspected CPC fighter abducted 3 Chinese nationals near Gbembo, 25 kilometers from Abba (Abba, Abba, Nana-Mambere). They were transferred to an unknown location. The reason for their abduction is not known.

On 19 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked Chinese miners at the Chimbolo gold mining site in Chimbolo, coded to Bambari (Bambari, Bambari, Ouaka). 9 Chinese miners were killed and 2 were seriously injured. The attackers had overpowered the site guards. The identity and the reason for the attack are not known. CPC released a statement denying their involvement and blaming the Wagner mercenaries.

properties.actor: CPC: Coalition of Patriots for Change
properties.notes: On 3 July 2023, suspected CPC militants clashed with the FACA soldiers escorting Chinese miners between Ndiba-Mole and Gobolo, coded to Gobolo (Abba, Abba, Nana-Mambere). At least 4 FACA soldiers and 1 civilian were killed. 5 Chinese were wounded. Local sources say 5 Chinese mining workers were also abducted.

On 18 November 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with FACA forces at the Zongo mine site, a few kilometers from the village of Lami, coded to Abba (Abba, Abba, Nana-Mambere). Casualties unknown. At least 4 were injured; including a soldier who was seriously injured, 5 Chinese miners were abducted after the FACA retreated and left them behind. The motives of the abduction are not yet known.

On 24 January 2024, 150 youths protested against the suspected arrival of the American private military company Bancroft in front of the American embassy in Bangui (Bangui, Bangui, Bangui). It is suspected that the Wagner mercenaries organized the protests through misinformation.

Around 5 March 2024 (as reported), an unidentified armed group clashed with FACA forces who were escorting Chinese workers in Gbimo, 15 kilometres from Yaloke (Yaloke, Yaloke, Ombella-M'Poko) to a mining site. 1 soldier and 1 civilian commercial bike rider were killed. 2 suspects were arrested.

On 5 May 2024, Wagner mercenaries arrested an unspecified number of Chinese miners at Gofo mining site, along the Dimbi - Mingala road, coded to Dimbi (Kembe, Kembe, Basse-Kotto). The mercenaries also confiscated their vehicles. The reason for the arrests is not known.

On 8 July 2024, an unidentified armed group ambushed and clashed with FACA forces between Alim and Douagouzou, coded to Alim (Kounde, Baboua, Nana-Mambere). There were no fatalities. 2 FACA soldiers were injured but escaped. The attackers abducted 2 Chinese nationals. The reason for the abduction is not known.

properties.actor: CPC: Coalition of Patriots for Change
properties.notes: On 8 July 2024, militiamen (belonging to the 3R group, member of the Coalition of Patriots for Change) abducted 2 Chinese men working in the mines in Beloko (Baboua, Nana-Mambere).

Around 1 August 2024 (as reported), around 400 people gathered to protest in Bangui - 5 (Arrondissement 5, Bangui, Bangui) against what they perceived as the destabilizing role of the United States in the country and Africa. The protest came after an American citizen was arrested on suspicion of being a spy.

On 31 October 2024, an unidentified armed group clashed with FACA forces near Alim (Kounde, Baboua, Nana-Mambere). 2 FACA soldiers were killed, and their vehicle burnt. The FACA forces were traveling with a woman and a Chinese national returning from the Mbali mining site. The 3R militants were accused of the ambush but denied their involvement. The woman and the Chinese national were abducted but released the next day.

On 22 March 2022, former Tchad- Cameroun constructor company workers gathered in front of the company siege in NDjamena (NDjamena, NDjamena) to call for the application of a justice decision condemning US oil company Exxon to financially compensate them.
Unidentified armed men kidnap a Chinese worker and are most likely holding him near Tine, a border area shared with Sudan. A joint Chadian-Sudanese search party was mounted.

On 16 March 2025, at the call of the Committee of Solidarity with the Ukrainian People, around 100 Ukrainian nationals gathered outside the Russian mission in Geneva (Geneve) to express solidarity with the Ukrainian people and protest against U.S. President Donald Trump's decision to strike a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom they labeled an 'assassin'.

On 15 July 2021, dozens of demonstrators, including members of the Cuban community, gathered at the Nations square in Geneva. They denounced the political regime in Cuba and called for the removal of the American economic embargo on the island.

On 13 May 2022, hundreds members of Uyghur community demonstrated in front of United Nations High Commissioner office in Geneva to call for the release of a report denouncing crimes against humanity committed by the Chinese government against their community.

On 1 July 2022, at the call of feminist associations (JS, Feminist Strike and EKDM) and the Socialist Party Women section, around 500 people demonstrated in Bern to denounce the US supreme court decision ending the constitutional right to abortion.

On 1 June 2020, more than 1000 people, including elected officials and BLM activists, demonstrated in Zurich to denounce racism, police brutality, and lack of justice in Switzerland and the rest of the world. They also paid tribute to a African-American man killed by the police in Minneapolis on 25 May 2020.
On 9 November 2024, around 150 people gathered in Bern (Bern) to protest the election of Donald Trump as President of the United States and to voice opposition to fascism.

On 8 February 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of the 'Geneva Pride' association, a few hundred people, including members of the LGBTQ+ community, gathered on Nations Square in Geneva (Geneve) to protest against the regression of the rights and freedoms of minorities, in the United States and elsewhere.

On 31 October 2023, in Concepcion (Biobio), leaders of the Huachipato steel mill's 2 unions protested outside the Municipal Library with a banner to demand measures to protect the Chilean steel industry against cheaper Chinese imports. The protesters, who briefly conversed with President Boric (who was on an official visit to the region), feared the loss of over 20,000 jobs.

On 23 November 2023, in Concepcion (Los Rios), representatives of 31 trade unions and federations, including fishers, metallurgy workers (FESTRAMET, ASIMET), exporters (ASEXMA), CUT, UPC, shipyard workers (Asmar), small- and medium-sized business unions (UNAPYME, Pymead) and a Huachipato steelworks union, protested outside the cathedral to call on authorities to protect employment in the region, to express support for workers at Huachipato and to demand that the Antidistortion Commission swiftly introduce higher import duties on foreign steel. The Chilean steel industry was struggling to compete against cheaper Chinese imports and Huachipato had suffered steep year-on-year losses; workers feared the wide-ranging implications of its potential closure.

On 21 December 2023, in Concepcion (Biobio), hundreds of unionized workers at the Huachipato steel mill, supporters of the Huachipato football club and members of other trade unions in the area (CUT; unions at several other companies; unions for forestry workers, fishers and stevedores) marched through the city to demand measures to prevent the closure of the business. Protesters, who wanted to show just how many local workers would be affected if the mill closed, were joined by the city's mayor (PDC) and demanded that the Commission against Market Distortions place a tariff on Chinese steel due to unfair competition.

On 27 February 2024, in Santiago (Metropolitana), union leaders at the Huachipato ironworks (located in the Biobio region), alongside a senator (PS), a congressman (DC) and the governor of the Biobio region (Ind.), protested outside the Moneda presidential palace to demand that the government introduce 25% tariffs on steel imported from China via the Anti-distortion Commission to protect national jobs and especially those at the Huachipato works. The protesters delivered a letter to the President ahead of the Commission's decision to impose temporary protectionist measures.

On 22 March 2024, in Talcahuano (Biobio), over 100 workers at the Huachipato steelworks, as well as relatives and neighbors, marched along Colon avenue to protest against its scheduled closure due to competition with Chinese imports. Protesters demanded sustainable support for the national steel industry and highlighted that the government should take measures to prevent the loss of thousands of local jobs. Steelworkers also protested on-site by making noise with their tools (cacerolazo).

On 30 March 2024, in Concepcion (Biobio), players belonging to the Huachipato soccer team protested alongside workers from the steelworks (in Talcahuano) of the same name on the pitch ahead of a match. The steelworks was set to close due to competition from Chinese imports.

On 4 April 2024, in Santiago (Metropolitana), representatives of the Huachipato steelworkers held a peaceful march towards the La Moneda Palace to meet with ministers of President Gabriel Boric. They demand open dialogue with the government to avoid the planned plant closure due to the managing CAP company's inability to compete with imported Chinese steel.

On 1 April 2024, in Talcahuano (Biobio), workers at the Huachipato steelworks set tires on fire near its entrance to demonstrate against its planned closure due to the managing CAP company's inability to compete with imported Chinese steel. Demonstrators, who waved black and Chilean flags, called on CAP to resubmit a request for higher tariffs on Chinese steel to the Anti-market Distortions Commission. On 4 April 2024, in Talcahuano (Biobio), around 60 workers at the Huachipato steelworks set tires on fire near its entrance to demonstrate against its planned closure due to the managing CAP company's inability to compete with imported Chinese steel. Five demonstrators were arrested for blocking traffic.

On 9 April 2024, in Santiago (Metropolitana), over 400 unionized workers at the Huachipato steelworks, alongside the Governor (Ind.) of the Biobio region and the mayor (UDI) of Talcahuano (where the plant is located), marched from the Metropolitan Cathedral to the Moneda presidential palace to demand that the government increase tariffs against Chinese steel imports. Managing company CAP was unable to compete against Chinese competition and had announced the steelworks' closure. Protesters, who accused China of dumping, stated this would endanger around 22,000 jobs and hoped CAP's appeal with the Anti-market distortions Commission would be favorable.

On 13 April 2024, in Talcahuano (Biobio), dozens of unionized workers at the Huachipato steelworks, members of its management, and community members protested at the Tortoise Coliseum stadium to express support for the Chilean steel industry and demonstrate their unity. Managing company CAP had announced the closure of the steelworks due to unfair competition from Chinese imports but had submitted another request to the Anti-Market Distortions Commission to increase tariffs on these. The result was due to be published on 16 April.

On 19 April 2024, in Concepcion (Biobio), workers at the Huachipato steelworks (in Talcahuano), their relatives, workers subcontracted by the plant and union leaders marched from Espana square to the city's cathedral to demand that the government save it from closure and that the Anti-Market Distortions Commission swiftly reveal the decisions reached during its session on 16 April. Managing company CAP had scheduled the steelworks' closure due to potentially unfair Chinese competition and had requested higher tariffs on imports of Chinese steel.

On 14 November 2019, in Canete, Biobio, around 250 people participated in a recalling the first anniversary of the death of a Mapuche leader by police. Some demonstrators erected barricades and attacked the house of the president of the Biobio Regional Council, shattering some windows. Around 50 people looted a Chinese store. One girl was wounded by a stone.

On 7 June 2021, a citizen group protested at the US Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against US interference in Chinese political affairs, claiming that the June Fourth incident was a lie manufactured by the US to topple the Chinese government.

On 18 June 2021, many groups of citizens rallied at the US and UK Consulate General offices in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against foreign interference in Chinese political affairs, referring to the US and UK governments' support for now-prosecuted pro-democracy news outlet Apple Daily.

On 20 July 2021, several pro-establishment citizen groups carrying placards gathered outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau at Chater Garden in Central (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They protested the U.S.'s recent warnings for companies about the risks of doing business in Hong Kong, claiming that the U.S. intervened in China's domestic affairs and defamed the National Security Law. Participating groups included 'DQ Action Group', Shatin District Council Observers, and Chinese-HK Hearts.

On 19 July 2021, pro-establishment citizen group 'Protect Hong Kong' and members of the public carrying China's flags gathered outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau at Chater Garden in Central (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western). They protested the U.S.'s recent warnings for companies about the risks of doing business in Hong Kong, claiming that the U.S. intervened in China's domestic affairs and damaged 'One County, Two System.'

On 25 October 2021, New Millenarian members protested at Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau at Chater Garden in Central (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against the perceived U.S.'s political intervention in Hong Kong affairs, including condemnation of disqualification of pro-democracy lawmakers in the city.

On 10 December 2021, people protested at the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau at Chater Garden in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against the virtual Summit for Democracy held in Washington, accusing the U.S. of intervening Hong Kong affairs. They also condemned 'fugitive' ex-lawmaker Nathan Law, who would speak at the Summit.

On 6 April 2023, eight representatives of the Defend Hong Kong Campaign held placards and banners, and chanted slogans outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Hong Kong - Central and Western to protest against US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy's visit to Taiwan, which they said was a disrespect of the One China Policy and was secessionist.

On 13 February 2024, representatives of the Hong Kong Federation of Trade Unions and Love Hong Kong Alliance, including Legislative Council members, held banners and defaced the American flag outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They demanded that the United States stop demonstrating its support for 'people who creates chaos for Hong Kong'. The demonstration came after Daniel Kritenbrink, the Assistant Secretary of State for East Asian and Pacific Affairs of the United States, had a meeting with four political activists who were wanted by the Hong Kong government for violating the national security law.

On 15 April 2024, 10 representatives of the Defend Hong Kong Campaign chanted slogans, and held placards and banners outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They demanded that the US government stops tarnishing Hong Kong's reputation, after it warned American tourists to exercise 'increased caution' when coming to Hong Kong in their latest travel advisory.

On 30 October 2024, 20 representatives of the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment of Hong Kong, including lawmakers, held placards and banners outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They demanded that the US Treasury stop its policy which restricts US businesses from investing in microelectronics, semiconductors, artificial intelligence and quantum computing in China, including Hong Kong and Macau. They said the measure would destabilize international trade.
