On 20 November 2024, around 10 representatives of the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong, including lawmakers, gathered to demonstrate with placards and banners outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They demanded that the politicians United States stop interfering with judicial independence in Hong Kong, after the United States government reprimanded China for clamping down on democracy and human rights in Hong Kong, and indicated that they would restrict visa applications against officials involved with the enactment of the National Security Law. On 19 November, Hong Kong courts convicted jail sentences, ranging from four years and two months up to 10 years, against 45 out of 47 pro-democracy activists charged with subversion under the national security law, having participated in pre-election primaries and advocated using their veto power of the government budget as a bargaining chip for the government to fulfil the Five Demands. The guilty verdicts had been seen as the largest crackdown on the pro-democracy and Five Demands Movement in Hong Kong.

On 27 November 2024, 13 people chanted slogans and defaced the United States flag outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Hong Kong - Central and Western. They demanded that the politicians in the United States stop interfering with internal affairs in Hong Kong, after the United States government tightened their financial policies against Hong Kong.

On 23 March 2025, five representatives of the HK Anti-war Mobilization held placards and gathered to demonstrate outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Hong Kong - Central and Western to demand that the US government stop suppressing the pro-Palestinian movement in university campuses.

On 3 December 2019, almost 50 to around 100 people attended a rally at Chater Garden in Central and Western district (Hong Kong) to protest against the US interfering in the domestic affairs of Hong Kong. They opposed the passing of the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act. They held banners and sang the Chinese national anthem and marched towards the US Consulate in Central.

On 28 March 2020, about 20 members of a pro-establishment group held a march from Chater Garden to the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Central and Western District (Hong Kong), in protest against the alleged slander of China by American officials over the coronavirus outbreak. The group criticised the U.S. president for repeatedly using the term 'Chinese virus' in public to refer to the coronavirus, stating that it had caused discrimination against Chinese people. One of the members also claimed that the virus should be called 'American Novel Coronavirus' given that the United States currently have the most number of cases. Demonstrators held a Donald Trump paper doll and also burned posters of Donald Trump outside the office of the Consulate General.

On 12 June 2019, more than 30 people from pro-Beijing organisations, including The Hong Kong Southern District Community Association, DAB, HKFTU, New Territories Association of Societies, Central and Western Concern Group, Kowloon Federation of Associations, Fujian CPPCC Committee Friendship Association, petitioned at the US Consulate in Central (Central and Western district, Hong Kong) to condemn the US government's interference in Hong Kong's internal affairs and to show support for the legislation of the extradition bill amendments. They shouted slogans and held placards.

On 16 June 2019, around 40 members of some pro-government groups including Alliance for Peace and Economy Hong Kong and HKFTU marched to the US Consulate in Central (Central and Western district, Hong Kong) to demand the US government not to interfere in Hong Kong affairs.

On 6 March 2019, about 15 members of the youth faction of the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong (Young DAB) protested at the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Central and Western District (Hong Kong) to condemn recent comments made by the US Consul General in Hong Kong regarding the 'one country, two systems' policy, which they believed went against standards of international law and meddled with China's internal affairs. Protesters carried banners, shouted slogans, and submitted a petition.

On 28 May 2020, members of the DHKC held a protest march from Chater Garden to the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Central and Western District (Hong Kong), to express their dissatisfaction with the strong opposition from the US government against the enactment of the contentious national security law in Hong Kong. They held banners and placards, stating that the national security law is necessary for the protection of national security, and that the United States had no rights to interfere.

On 23 July 2020, two citizen groups of four ('Anti-Foreign Interference Alliance' and 'China-HK Youth China and International Relations Research Group') marched to and petitioned at the US Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) against American foreign interference in Chinese domestic affairs, and against the US government's recent shuttering of the Chinese consulate in Houston, Texas. One of the groups demanded for the US to close its consulate in Hong Kong as well and leave within 72 hours. They held large banners and shouted slogans.

On 4 August 2020, at least four members of two pro-establishment, anti-independence citizen groups ('Tung Sum Wu Gong' and 'Anti-Black Money, Anti-HK Independence Concern Group') staged separate protests at the US Consulate-General in Admiralty, Central district (Hong Kong) against the United States for its opposing statement on the postponement of local LegCo elections. The government had imposed a two-person size limit on public gatherings at the time.

On 17 September 2020, at least four members of a citizen group ('Anti-Black Money, Anti-HK Independence Concern Group') protested at the US Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) against US interference in domestic affairs, including the arrest of 12 Hong Kong citizens who were caught in mainland Chinese waters on a boat bound for Taiwan. They held up placards, a flag and a banner.

On 29 October 2020, a Confucianism interest group protested at the US Consulate-General in Admiralty, Central district (Hong Kong) against the US Secretary of State's announcement to designate Confucius Institutes as 'foreign missions,' and to have all the Institutes closed by the end of the year. They held up a banner, shouted slogans and read a news release.

On 8 June 2018, more than 20 Mainland Chinese women wore face masks, carried banners and protested over the shortage of cancer-preventing HPV vaccine at the office of US drug company Merck in Causeway Bay, in the Wan Chai District of Hong Kong. They urged the firm to increase its supply of the human papillomavirus vaccine. It was reported that around 500 people had spent at least 6000 HKD for a course of treatment requiring three injections. However, they were only given one or two jabs because of the vaccine shortage.

On 6 March 2020, about 25 people of the group 'Justice Alliance' held a demonstration outside the Next Digital Building in Tseung Kwan O, Sai Kung District (Hong Kong), to support the recent arrest of the founder of Next Digital. They raised banners and held slogans condemning the founder, and protested US support for him and US involvement in Hong Kong affairs.

On 28 August 2018, around 20 members of the Hong Kong and State Affairs Concern Group staged a protest in front of the University of Hong Kong in Southern District (Hong Kong) to demand the university to fire the Director of the Public Opinion Programme because they believe that the Director was sponsored by American National Democratic Institute to conduct biased public opinion survey and influence the Hong Kong society. The protesters held banners and handed a petition letter to a representative from the university.

On 2 March 2020, members of the Defend Hong Kong Campaign marched from Chater Garden to the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Central and Western District (Hong Kong) in protest of the involvement in Hong Kong affairs by US politicians in their support of the founder of Next Digital who had been recently arrested.

On 3 August 2019, a few hundred people and several groups rallied outside the US Consulate in Central in Central and Western district (Hong Kong) to demand the US to immediately stop intervening in Hong Kong's and China's internal affairs. They shouted slogans, held placards and submitted a petition letter to the Consulate.

On 10 August 2019, many pro-government civil groups including Safeguard Hong Kong, Defend Hong Kong Campaign and Patriot Alliance protested at the US consulate in Central against the United States' intervention in Hong Kong affairs and recent comments on the protests in Hong Kong. Protesters held flags and shouted slogans.

On 3 March 2021, DHKC representatives petitioned and demonstrated at the US Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) to condemn the US State Department's 'interfering remarks' about the ongoing court trials involving 47 pro-democracy politicians and activists charged with conspiracy to commit subversion. They held up placards and a banner to express their demands.

On 15 March 2021, DAB representatives demonstrated at the US-Consulate in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) for the implementation of coronavirus prevention policies without exceptions, in relation to two US consular staff refusing to enter quarantine citing diplomatic immunity.

Around 15 March 2021 (as reported), a citizen group ('United China Force') rallied at the US Consulate in Admiralty, Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) to protest against the US government's interference in Chinese domestic affairs, referring to the recent reforms to Hong Kong's electoral system. They held up flags, placards, and set up a stand with slogans.

On 4 April 2021, several groups and citizens petitioned and protested at the US Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against the US government's interference in Chinese domestic political affairs, particularly their stance on the Hong Kong electoral reforms.

On 19 April 2021, at least 12 people - citizens and those from business groups like Taxi Drivers & Operators Association, Hong Kong Overseas Chinese and Chinese Chamber of Commerce - petitioned and demonstrated at the US and UK Consulate-Generals in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against UK and US interference in domestic affairs, referring to both governments' supportive remarks to several activists and veterans handed prison sentences last week for illegal assembly during the anti-ELAB demonstrations. They chanted slogans, and held up banners and Hong Kong flags.

On 23 April 2021, at least three people from the pro-establishment group Politihk Social Strategic organised a rally outside the US Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) in support of 'patriots ruling Hong Kong' - alluding to the recent Hong Kong electoral reform - and cotton sourced from Xinjiang. They wore t-shirts with slogans, held up placards, and played a clip showing their supporters.

On 1 May 2021, the DHKC rallied at the US Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against US interference in domestic affairs, referring to the US government's condemnation of the recent Immigration Bill Amendment. They held up banners and waved national flags to express their demands.

On 14 May 2021, at least four people and four groups (DHKC, Politihk Social Strategic, 'Dqaction', '23 Alliance') demonstrated at the US Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) against US government interference in domestic affairs, referring to the U.S. State Department's annual report on religious freedom, which featured accusations against China. They chanted slogans and pointed out racial and human rights issues in the United States.

On 29 May 2021, DHKC protested at the US Consulate-General in Central district (Hong Kong) (coded as Hong Kong - Central and Western) for the US Secretary of State to respect Chinese sovereignty and rule, and opposed his remarks on the recent round of electoral reform in Hong Kong.

On 18 February 2025, over 400 demonstrators staged a protest led by the Opposition MP (Member of Parliament) and Cook Islands Party in Avarua (Southern) to oppose Prime Minister Mark Brown's recent partnership agreement with China. Protesters said they were concerned about the lack of transparency and consultation regarding the partnership, which they believed could threaten Cook Islands' sovereignty and affect its relationship with New Zealand. A co-leader of Te Pati Maori also joined the protest.
A group of citizens protested in front of the American embassy in Bogota on February 7th, 2019. The group demonstrated against the intervention of the United States in the Venezuelan conflict.

On 14 October 2023, in Bogota - Teusaquillo (Bogota, D.C.), dozens of citizens demonstrated in front of the Embassy of Palestine in support of Palestine and against the attacks on the Gaza Strip amid the recent conflict escalation between Israel and Hamas. The demonstrators also burned flags from Israel and the United States of America.

On 23 January 2024, in Mondomo (Cauca), unidentified armed individuals kidnapped a Mexican-American citizen. The victim was rescued by authorities on 25 January. There is presence of armed groups in the area.

On 7 October 2024, in Bogota - Teusaquillo (Bogota, D.C.), more than 200 pro-Palestine demonstrators marched past the Lebanese and Palestinian embassies before vandalizing storefronts, breaking down barricades, and burning an American flag outside the U.S. embassy during a rally to demand a ceasefire in the Middle East. UNDMO police officers intervened to prevent the rioters from forcibly entering the embassy and a clash with demonstrators broke out. There were no fatalities.

On 19 February 2025, in Chirivico (Santander de Quilichao, Cauca), four unidentified individuals armed with rifles abducted a Chinese businessman while he was in front of his workplace. The area is known for the presence of FARC dissident groups. The victim's whereabouts are unknown.
2 soldiers were killed in a clash with Ninjas militiamen in the Mangola area of Pool as they were guarding a Chinese road construction site.

Around 18 June 2020, in San Jose (San Jose), members of the Revolutionary Workers' Party protested against United States President Donald Trump and against racial discrimination in soldiartity with the American BLM movement.

On 3 May 2024, in Camaguey, Camaguey, students demonstrated at the University of Medical Sciences of Camaguey to show their support for the Palestinian people and denounce what they consider a genocide being carried out with the complicity of the US government. The protest called by the University Federation (FEU) also supported the pro-Palestinian student demonstrations in the United States. Similar protests were held in other parts of the country (coded separately).

On 20 December 2024, in Habana, La Habana, thousands of pro-government citizens (between 30,000 to 50,000), led by President Diaz-Canel and former leader Raul Castro, held a protest, the so-called 'March of the Combatant People, to decry the US trade embargo. Protesters held a sit-in protest in front of the US Embassy. The mobilization was called by the national regime.

On 17 November 2023, on the 50th anniversary of the 1973 Athens Polytechnic student uprising against the 1967-1974 military dictatorship in Greece, which led to the invasion of Cyprus and the division of the island, dozens of students marched to the United States embassy in Nicosia shouting the original slogans such as 'Bread - Education - Freedom' and 'NATO, CIA, Betrayal' blaming NATO and the US for supporting the junta, but also contemporary slogans of solidarity with Palestine. Police diverted the march away from their regular route, which would have passed near the Israeli embassy. The protesters hang the Cypriot, Greek and Palestinian flags on the United States embassy fence. The protesters accused Israel of murdering civilians and children in Gaza and NATO/US of endorsing this. Representatives of DISY, EDON, AKEL held speeches.

On 3 December 2023, over 1,000 demonstrators from across Cyprus rallied in Nicosia in solidarity with the Palestinians. The protesters marched holding signs reading 'Hydrocarbons and blood' referring to the agreement between Cyprus, Greece, Israel, and the US on energy exploitation. The organizers, totalling 38 Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot organizations, demanded an immediate ceasefire in Gaza and the provision of humanitarian aid among other issues. Members of the women's movement POGO unfurled a banner outside the Israeli embassy reading 'How many more dead children?' The head of the Pancyprian Peace Council, the leader of AKEL, the ambassador of Palestine in Cyprus, the leader of the Cyprus Green Party held speeches or made statements. The demonstrators chanted slogans against Israel, against the United States, and against the President of Cyprus, accusing him of supporting genocide.

On 14 January 2024, pro-Palestinian activists rallied at the gates of RAF Akrotiri carrying flags and banners, protesting that it was used as a launch pad for strikes against the Houthi militia in Yemen, saying the British bases are a destabilizing force in the region. The rally had been organized by the Cyprus Peace Council before the U.S. and British strikes on Yemen took place and was supported by AKEL, United for Palestine and other leftist groups, protesting that the base was being used to offer logistical support to Israel. The protesters denounced the presence of 3,000 U.S. soldiers in Akrotiri and demanded the closure of both British bases on the island. Messages from the World Peace Council, the British Peace Assembly and the Palestinian Embassy in Cyprus were read out, in addition to a speech by a Palestinian who lost most of his family members in Israel's bombing of Rafah. Dozens of police were present.

On 30 May 2024, around 50 people gathered outside the US embassy in Nicosia to protest Israel's ongoing military operation in the Gaza strip. Organized by United for Palestine, they held placards and shouted slogans against Israel, the United States and Biden. Speakers included members of EDEK's youth wing EDON.

On 9 August 2024, protesters, including AKEL, rallied in Limassol after the US amphibious assault ship, USS Wasp, docked in Limassol the previous day. They chanted 'No harbor to genocide' opposing 'the continuing build-up of US military forces' on the island, both inside and outside British bases, and accused the government of servicing ships supplying the state of Israel the means to commit genocide against the Palestinian people. The government said this was part of the island's humanitarian role in light of developments in the region and the US ambassador to Cyprus said this was part of a 'long-planned' partnership activity between the 2 countries.

On 7 October 2024, approximately 250 protesters organized by United for Palestine and other organizations, marched in Nicosia holding banners with slogans in support of Palestine's right to its own state and against the Western powers, the US and the EU, including the Republic of Cyprus, for their 'complicity in providing political, diplomatic, economic and military support to Israel'. They held speeches. The protest was held in coordination with the police and was peaceful.

On 18 November 2024, on the occasion of the 51st anniversary of the 1973 Athens Polytechnic student uprising against the 1967-1974 military dictatorship in Greece, school and university students marched to the US embassy in Nicosia, carrying flags of Greece, Cyprus and Palestine and chanting 'Bread Education Freedom' and slogans against fascism and in solidarity with the Palestinian people, and some anti-American slogans. They were closely observed by strong police forces. The students submitted a voting to a representative of the US embassy and they placed red carnations on the fence.

On 24 November 2024, more than 500 demonstrators marched to the US-sponsored security training facility CyCLOPS in Larnaca to protest against 'the transformation of Cyprus into a base for war', carrying banners with slogans including 'Neither the USA nor NATO, Cyprus is not a protectorate' and 'United for Palestine'. The protesters, who were organized by the Cyprus Peace Council, demanded the immediate withdrawal of US troops from Cyprus and an end to the military cooperation between US and Cyprus. They expressed their solidarity with the people of Lebanon and Palestine. The mayor of Larnaca was present. The leader of AKEL held a speech. The protesters were carrying flags of AKEL, PEO, EDON, POGO, and Palestinian flags. Police were stationed outside the training center observing the peaceful protest.

On 20 January 2025, on the day of the inauguration of Donald Trump as the 47th President of the United States, supporters of Palestinians, organized by 'United for Palestine Nicosia', rallied outside the US embassy carrying banners against US foreign policies in the Middle East and their implications for Cyprus.

On 11 February 2025, unidentified assailants (likely far-right) set fire to the residence of a 6-member Chinese family in Pafos, while the children, parents and grandparents were sleeping. The fire started at the veranda and spread to the rest of the house. They were all taken to hospital with respiratory problems and burns. The grandfather, who jumped from the first floor to escape, and the grandson, who had more serious respiratory problems, remained hospitalized. On 18 February, police arrested a man attempting to cross to the north via the Ledra Palace checkpoint in Nicosia.

On 24 February 2025, protesters organized by United for Palestine (UfP) rallied in Nicosia, demanding a permanent ceasefire in Palestine, among other issues. The protesters, carrying banners in Greek and in English, demanded an end to the Israeli occupation and protested against US President Trump over his statements about Gaza.

On 23 June 2021, after the General Assembly of the United Nations voted for the 29th consecutive year in favor of a resolution to demand the end of the US economic blockade on Cuba, supporters of Cuba rallied outside the United States embassy in Nicosia to protest for lifting the US embargo.

On 23 May 2023, activists, including members of the Communist Party, gathered for a rally in Prague, protesting against a new mutual defence treaty of the Czech Republic and the United States. At least some declared support to Moscow's activities in Ukraine and blamed the US for starting the war.

On 30 May 2023, the Communist Party activists and their supporters gathered for a rally near the Parliament building in Prague, protesting against a new mutual defence treaty signed between Czechia and the United States. At least some also brought Russian flags and blamed the US for the war in Ukraine. Another group of activists gathered nearby, supporting the treaty and criticizing Vladimir Putin. Minor verbal skirmishes were reported.

On 19 July 2023, activists gathered for a rally in Prague, protesting against a newly signed defense treaty between the US and Czech Republic. Representatives of the SPD party were present and delivered speeches. At least some participants expressed their anti-American and pro-Russian standing towards the war in Ukraine.

On 13 June 2020, about 300 Czech and international activists affiliated to the Socialist Solidarity movement gathered in Prague, protesting against racism and police violence in the US and in the world, within the framework of the BLM campaign. The protest was sparked by the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.
On 4 January 2024, activists gathered near the US embassy in Prague, protesting against what they see as a 'colour revolution' being organized by the White House in Serbia.

On 8 March 2024, about 200 mostly female activists gathered for a rally in Plzen, calling for peace in Ukraine. At least some of the speakers declared their support to the Russian cause and condemned the alleged harmful influence of the US over the country.

On 28 May 2024, activists gathered for a rally in Plzen, protesting against a planned establishment of a logistical centre for NATO forces in the nearby Line. Speakers blamed the US and NATO for at least contributing to the outbreak of the war in Ukraine.
On 23 June 2024, activists gathered for an anti-war rally in Prague, protesting against what they see as an imperialist involvement of the US in the current world conflicts.

On 8 July 2024, activists gathered for a rally in Prague, demanding immediate ceasefire in Ukraine and criticizing the US and NATO for alleged contribution to this conflict and many more other around the world.
On 19 July 2024, activists gathered for a rally near the embassy of People's Republic of China in Prague, protesting against long-lasting political pressure against the Falun Gong movement.

On 1 September 2024, activists gathered for a rally in Prague, demanding end of all wars around the world, including the conflicts in Ukraine and Gaza, Yemen and others. They mostly blamed the US for fuelling global conflicts and supported Russian narratives.
On 21 February 2025, LGBTQ+ activists gathered for a rally in front of the US embassy in Prague, protesting against what they see as homophobic activities of the current US president and his allies.

On 20 January 2021, about 40 activists gathered for a rally in Prague, protesting against coronavirus-related restrictions and declaring their support to the previous president of the US Donald Trump.
On 13 January 2020, about 60 activists gathered near the US embassy in Prague, protesting against a potential war with Iran. The rally was organized by the movement Socialist Solidarity.

On 17 November 2021, thousands activists affiliated with the movement Million Moments for Democracy gathered for a rally in Prague. They were celebrating the anniversary of the Velvet Revolution and protesting against the current scandals of the government, including corruption or orientation towards Russia and China.

On 23 January 2022, activists affiliated with the Kaputin group gathered for a rally in Prague, demanding a boycott of the 2022 Olympics in China over violation of human rights of Uyghurs and other ethnic groups in the country.
On 4 February 2022, activists gathered near the Chinese embassy in Prague, protesting against the ongoing Olympic games in China due to the violations of human rights there.

On 20 February 2022, about 50 activists, including members of the Communist party, gathered for a rally in Prague near the US embassy, protesting against a transfer of NATO/US military convoy through Czechia and against alleged American military adventures.
On 2 June 2020, about 300 activists gathered in Prague, protesting against the politics of the current president, especially related to China.

On 4 June 2020, about 50 activists, including several foreigners, gathered near the embassy of China in Prague, commemorating the events of 1989 and protesting against violations of human rights in China.

On 6 June 2020, Czech and foreign activists gathered near the US embassy in Prague, protesting against police violence against civilians, especially Afro-American ones. The protest was sparked by the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.
On 25 January 2020, about 15 activists affiliated to the Kaputin movement gathered in Prague near the embassy of China, demanding freedom for Tibet and Hong-Kong.

On 26 November 2022, several hundred activists gathered for a rally in Prague, protesting against the government. They were criticizing alleged meddling of the US to the Czech domestic politics, extensive support of Ukraine and overall worsening economic condition of the country.
On 9 March 2020, members of The Left protested in Zittau under the motto 'Peace instead of war' against the US Defender Europe 2020 (movement of US personnel and equipment from the US to Europe).
On 10 March 2020, around 50 people protested in Potsdam against the US Defender Europe 2020 (movement of US personnel and equipment from US to Europe). The protest was organised by The Left.

On 22 March 2022, 5 people demonstrated and blocked highway A10 near Berlin - Pankow (Berlin), against the opening of a plant for the American company Tesla. 3 demonstrators were temporarily arrested.

On 19 March 2022, around 700 people, including Nabu, Greenpeace, and BUND members, demonstrated in Uberherrn against the planned construction of a Chinese battery manufacturer (SVolt). Demonstrators called for the protection of the environment and nature conservation.

On 28 June 2022, around a dozen climate activists demonstrated in Munchen against the American investment management company Blackrock amid the G7 Summit and for debt relief for poorer countries. Demonstrators also gathered to call for climate protection as they called it a 'Climate Demo'.

On 12 July 2022, around 200 people demonstrated in Uberherrn to denounce the planned settlement of the Chinese battery manufacturer SVolt in the area while a council meeting was taking place to address the topic.

On 6 August 2022, people, including Catholic and Protestant representatives, demonstrated in Gottingen against the war in Ukraine, for peace, and the withdrawal of American nuclear weapons from Germany. They were also against its acquisition of new nuclear bombers and for a world free of nuclear weapons. They had gathered on the occasion of the 77th anniversary of the Hiroshima and Nagasaki nuclear bombings in Japan.

On 28 August 2022, around 2,500 people demonstrated in Plauen, at the call of the 'Forum for Democracy and Freedom', for the end of sanctions against Russia, a dissolution of the German Bundestag and a withdrawal of American troops from Germany.

On 11 September 2022, around 5,500 people demonstrated in Plauen, at the call of the 'Forum for Democracy and Freedom', for the end of sanctions against Russia, a dissolution of the German Bundestag and a withdrawal of American troops from Germany.

On 25 September 2022, approximately 4,250 people demonstrated in Plauen against Germany's policy in the wake of the energy crisis due to the war in Ukraine and denounced the presence of US troops in Germany. There were flags of the Free Saxons party waving during the protest.
On 12 November 2022, Chinese students demonstrated in Berlin - Mitte against the Chinese government.

On 26 November 2022, between 900 and 1,200 (according to the police) people, including far-right affiliates, a former AfD politician, and the editorial officer of Compact Magazine, demonstrated in Leipzig, in front of the Federal Administrative Court, against the presence of the United States of America in Germany. Demonstrators called on the US government to withdraw its troops and nuclear weapons from Germany under the slogan 'Ami go home'. More than 1,200 people gathered for a counter-demonstration and tried to stop the participants with sit-in blockades of around 500 people. Pyrotechnics were set off at both demonstrations. According to initial findings, one person was injured. Several police officers were slightly injured in the operation but were able to continue their service.

On 3 December 2022, around 200 people, including an elected official (The Greens), and BUND members, demonstrated on the market square in Grunheide (Mark) against the expansion of the Tesla factory as environmental requirements are not met. They called for a citizens' consultation on the further development of the US company.

On 3 November 2022, people, including members of the Tibetan community, staged a rally on Cathedral Square in Munster to denounce the Chinese occupation of Tibet. The event was organized on the occasion of the G7 Foreign Ministers Summit hosted by the city on 3 and 4 November 2022.

On 10 December 2022, around 900 people demonstrated in Berlin - Mitte, from the Berlin Cathedral to the Brandenburg Gate through Potsdamer Platz, to condemn human rights violations in various other states (Iran, Belarus, and China). Demonstrators showed solidarity with the protest movement in Iran, following the death of Mahsa Amini, denounced the suffering of political prisoners in Belarus, and excessive coronavirus-related measures causing repression in China. They had gathered on the occasion of International Human Rights Day.

On 3 January 2023, around 45 environmental activists demonstrated in Hooksiel against the delivery of natural gas from the US to the city, claiming the gas was extracted using harmful fracking methods. They also opposed the discharging of chlorine and bromine into the ocean and the dependency on Russian gas amid the war in Ukraine.

On 24 December 2022, about 900 people and members of the far-right demonstrated outside the Federal Administrative Court in Leipzig to demand the U.S. to withdraw its troops and nuclear weapons from Germany. Among the demonstrators were speakers of a far right wing extremist magazine and a former AfD politician. A counter demonstration of about 500 people took place to stop the right-wing demonstration. There were reports of physical attacks against law enforcement officers resulting in the injury of one individual. It remains unclear which group perpetrated the attacks.

On 26 February 2023, around 2,500 people from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, including Reich Citizens, Querdenken affiliates, and supporters of the Russian government, demonstrated in front of Ramstein air base in Ramstein-Miesenbach against arms delivery to Ukraine from NATO. They also opposed the presence of U.S. troops in Germany. Demonstrators shouted the slogan: 'Yank go home'.

On 10 April 2023, around 290 people staged a protest march at the air force base with US nuclear warheads in Buchel, to protest for peace and call for negotiations between Russia and Ukraine. The protest was part of a series of traditional protests during the easter holiday.

On 10 May 2023, several groups of activists interrupted the convention of VW corporation in Berlin. Among them, environmental activists demanding more responsible climate policy - someone pelted a cake on the company representatives. Other activists protested against the company's ignorance of human rights violations in China, especially related to Uyghur forced labor. They were removed from the premises by the police. Another group of activists, including ALG, gathered outside the location with pickets.

On 6 May 2023, around 40 anti-NATO, -USA, and -EU activists took part in a motorcade from Fredersdorf-Vogelsdorf to Strausberg, opposing the supply of weapons to Ukraine, and denouncing US and EU policies.

On 20 June 2023, Tibetan refugees and supporters demonstrated in front of the Bank of China in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), to protest against human rights violations and oppression of Tibetans in China. The protesters staged a mock torture session.

On 24 June 2023, around 900 people camped and demonstrated in front of the US Air Base in Ramstein-Miesenbach to denounce NATO as warmongers. They demanded immediate peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine. Around 20 people gathered for a counter-demonstration.

Around 10 November 2023 (as reported), around 2,000 Airbus Helicopters employees demonstrated in Donauworth (Bayern) against the Bundeswehr's purchasing policy. They expressed concerns about their jobs if orders from the Bundeswehr's special funds went primarily to American companies. They called for the special fund to go to European and German industries.

On 9 November 2023, at the call of Ver.di, around 60 striking German civilian employees of the US Army demonstrated in Katterbach (Ansbach) to call for fair contractual conditions in the renegotiation of their collective labor agreement.

On 13 November 2023, at the call of IGM, around 200 striking people from Hensoldt and Airbus gathered in front of the Airbus Defense and Space headquarters in Immenstaad am Bodensee (Baden-Wurttemberg, Bodenseekreis) against the Bundeswehr's purchasing policy, accusing orders from the German armed forces' special funds to go primarily to American companies.

On 30 May 2020, around 2,000 people protested in Berlin - Mitte in front of the US embassy against racism and police violence in view of the death of a black man in the United States at the hands of police officers.

On 15 February 2024, a group of about 10 pro-Palestinian protesters demonstrated against and interrupted a lecture by Safra Catz, CEO of the US software manufacturer Oracle, at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) in Munchen (Bayern). Reasons stated were about the situation in Gaza. The demonstrators were taken out by security forces.
On 18 January 2020, people protested in Munchen against the action of US President Trump in Iran.

On 2 March 2024, a good 400 people participated in a protest in Uberherrn (Saarland) against the planned location of a battery factory of the Chinese manufacturer SVolt on Linslerfeld, citing environmental reasons. The protesters criticized the factory's environmental and hazardous substance pollution, as well as the number and type of jobs announced.

On 16 May 2024, around 50 environmental activists, including 'Citizen initiative Grunheide' (Burgerinitiative Grunheide) and 'Turning off the Tap on Tesla' (Tesla den Hahn abdrehen) and 'Green League' (Grune Liga), staged a protest in Grunheide (Mark) (Brandenburg) in the context of the vote of the city council and called on representatives to vote against the expansion plans of the US car manufacturer Tesla.

On 18 January 2020, about 30 people, including women and Democrats Abroad - suspected to be both US American and German - protested in Munchen in support of women and for equal rights of women in the US.

On 13 June 2024, people, including Last Generation and Extinction Rebellion activists, staged a protest in Karlsruhe (Baden-Wurttemberg) against the Landesbank Baden-Wurttemberg's and EnBW AG's financing and import of environmentally harmful US fracking gas.

On 2 August 2024, at the call of The Left, people gathered for a peace demonstration in Pirna (Sachsen), calling for disarmament instead of rearmament. The protest aimed to oppose the planned stationing of US intermediate-range missiles in Germany starting in 2026 and to demand a reduction in military arms.

On 3 October 2024, at least 10,000 people gathered for a protest organized by the alliance 'War Never Again' in Berlin - Mitte(Berlin). The protest aimed at opposing the deployment of US missiles in Germany, the war in Ukraine and the Middle East, and Germany's arms supplies to Ukraine and Israel. Key speakers included Sahra Wagenknecht (BSW), Ralf Stegner (SPD), and Gesine Lotzsch (Linke). A variety of groups joined the protest, including a protest bloc of pro-Palestine protesters. In contrast, several counter-protests occurred nearby, such as one organized by the German Peace Community (DFG-VK), with a smaller group of activists dressed in black and wearing skull masks, who protested in front of the Russian embassy earlier in the day. They criticized the main protest for including far-rights elements, with messages like 'Russia is waging a war of aggression.' Additionally, several hundred participants, including members of the SPD and the group 'Vitsche - Activists Empowering Ukraine,' advocated for support of Ukraine and condemned Russia's actions. These counter-protests emphasized their stance against what they labeled 'pseudo pacifism' of the main protest.

On 18 October 2024, at 5 pm, around 500 people gathered for a pro-Palestine demonstration titled 'Joe Biden Is Not Welcome', at Alexanderplatz in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), opposing both the war in the Middle East and criticizing US President Joe Biden's support for Israel, as he was visiting Berlin. The march, which was planned to proceed from Dircksenstrase to Alexanderufer, was interrupted multiple times by the police due to the chanting of slogans considered unconstitutional by authorities. Simultaneously, a small counter-protest of around 20 pro-Israel supporters took place near the Museumsinsel subway station nearby. Police intervened to keep both groups apart, and several arrests were made throughout the evening.

On 17 October 2024, people gathered for a protest, organized by FRIKO, the Berlin Peace Coordination, at Brandenburger Tor in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) directed against the planned deployment of US medium-range missiles and the storage of nuclear weapons in Germany, as well as against the US's foreign policy towards Russia and in the Middle East.

On 18 October 2024, around 700 people gathered at a parking area near the L46 highway and marched toward the main entrance of the US Air Base in Spangdahlem (Rheinland-Pfalz) for a protest, organized under the slogan 'Justice for Micha,' following the acquittal of a US soldier by a military court after a fatal stabbing at the Wittlich fair in August 2023, which led to the death of a 28-year-old German man. Protesters expressed their outrage at the verdict, which they felt denied justice for the victim. When one participant approached the base gate, there was a brief standoff with the police, but the situation remained peaceful and quickly de-escalated.

On 4 January 2020, at least 100 supporters of the Iranian regime, Iraqis and Iranians, protested in Berlin - Steglitz-Zehlendorf in front of the Iranian embassy against the killing of Soleimani and against the US military.

On 24 November 2024, around 100 to 200 people protested outside the Spangdahlem Air Base (Rheinland-Pfalz) against the acquittal of US soldier Michael Ovsjannikov by a US military court. Ovsjannikov had been charged with the fatal stabbing of a 28-year-old man at the Saubrennerkirmes fair in Wittlich (August 2023). Protesters demanded justice and a review of the NATO Status of Forces Agreement, which transferred the case to US jurisdiction.

On 23 November 2024, at the call of the group 'Hand in Hand for Our Country' (Hand in Hand fur unser Land), around 1,000 people, including farmers with around 23 tractors and numerous cars, staged a protest at the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), demanding 'speech rights' in the Bundestag. The protesters protested for energy security and agricultural policies, and expressed opposition to the SPD-FDP-Green coalition government, with demonstrators waving German and peace flags. While the demonstration initially aimed to address agricultural policies, it quickly expanded to a broad range of grievances, including opposition to the war in Ukraine, coronavirus measures, and Donald Trump. The protest was also marked by a diverse set of political views, with some speakers expressing far-right ideologies, while others focused on agricultural issues like EU trade deals.

On 29 November 2024, at the call of Ver.di, several hundred German Amazon employees, alongside colleagues from the USA, Sweden, the UK, and Italy, gathered in Bad Hersfeld (Hessen) for a protest. The protest, part of the global campaign #MakeAmazonPayDay, aimed to highlight what they called unfair working conditions and the lack of a collective bargaining agreement at Amazon.

On 9 December 2024, on the occasion of the 43rd anniversary of Mumia Abu-Jamal's imprisonment, around 30 people gathered in front of the US Embassy in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), demanding his release and the abolition of the death penalty. The protest featured speeches on racial injustice, mass incarceration, and prison abolition, with participants writing solidarity postcards and chanting slogans.

On 20 January 2025, people gathered near the People-to-People store and the MLPD district office in Gelsenkirchen (Nordrhein-Westfalen) to protest against Donald Trump's inauguration. The protesters voiced concerns over what they called his misogynistic policies, links to far-right leaders, and plans for deportations, with many calling for a ban on the AfD.

On 4 July 2020, around 100 to 300 people protested in Berlin - Mitte in front of the US embassy inder the motto 'Black Lives Matter' for the release of Mumia Abu-Jamal, a black man who is accused of killing a white police officer in the United States.
On 16 July 2020, 14 activists from Germany, the Netherlands, and the United States protested against nuclear weapons by blocking the US military airport in Buchel.
On 5 August 2020, 6 Greenpeace activists protested in Buchel against US nuclear weapons with a hot air balloon.

On 1 September 2020, people from Hong Kong protested in Berlin - Mitte outside the Federal Ministry for Foreign Affairs, demanding sanctions against China. The reason for the protest was a visit by the Chinese Foreign Minister in Berlin.

On 12 September 2020, more than 600 people - predominantly from the far left - protested in Leipzig under the motto 'Storm the fortress - break all borders!' against the European Union's refugee policy, human rights violations by China, racism, capitalism, and police violence. The protest was organised by NIKA.
On 28 January 2020, about 70 people protested in Berlin - Mitte against US President Trump's Middle East plan.
On 31 January 2020, about 80 Palestinians protested in Dusseldorf against Israel and US President Trump.
On 31 January 2020, at a memorial of the liberation of Brandenburg from the NS, about 20 people protested in Kienitz against the upcoming US military exercise 'Defender Europe 2020'.
On 1 February 2020, about 100 peace activists protested at the US airfield in Wiesbaden against the upcoming military exercise 'Defender Europe 20'.

On 6 January 2020, about 100 people, including MLPD supporters, women and students, protested in Darmstadt for more peace, against the Turkish military offensive in Rojava, and against the US military strategy in the Middle East.

On 23 January 2021, around 20 people protested in Berlin - Mitte outside the Chinese Embassy against the suppression of the Uighur minority in China. The protest was organized by a former CDU politician.

Property destruction: On 9 March 2021, an unknown perpetrator threw several incendiary devices at the Chinese embassy in Berlin - Mitte. The incendiary devices landed on the ground outside the embassy building. Employees of the embassy extinguished the fire before it could damage the building. No one was reported injured. Private security forces detained the perpetrator, who was then arrested by police. The motive is not yet clear.
On 8 February 2020, about 1700 people protested in Hamburg (Hamburg) against the oppression of the Uyghurs in China. The protest was organized by the banned organization Hizb ut-Tahrir.
On 5 April 2021, around 90 people protested in Buchel for the removal of US nuclear weapons, which are suspected to be stored in Buchel.
On 9 January 2020, about 100 people of the peace movement protested in Bremen against the US military action in the Middle East and the failure of the German government to oppose US President Trump.
On 1 May 2021, people protested in Frankenberg/Sachsen outside a military barracks for the withdrawal of the US army and nuclear weapons from Germany.
On 17 May 2021, people protested in Leipzig in solidarity with 'emancipatory fights' in China by Uighurs and Hong Kong activists.

On 9 June 2021, four unknown men racially and xenophobically insulted and physically attacked a South Korean man at Rathaus Schoneberg in Berlin - Tempelhof-Schoneberg. Before kicking and punching the South Korean man, they had asked him whether he was from China. The South Korean sustained minor injuries on his face and leg.
On 3 July 2021, people, including representatives of Christian groups, protested in Buchel against nuclear weapons and the storage of nuclear weapons at the US military base in Buchel.

On 9 July 2021, around 50 activists protested in Buchel against the nuclear weapons stored at the US military base in Buchel. 15 of the activists blocked three gates to the US military airfield and were later carried away by police. The protesters demanded the withdrawal of US nuclear weapons from Germany.
On 10 July 2021, around 200 people protested at the US Air Base Ramstein in Ramstein-Miesenbach against the Air Base.
On 20 February 2020, Greenpeace activists protested in Bremerhaven against the NATO exercise Defender 2000 and the arrival of a US cargo ship loaded with military vehicles.

Around 17 November 2021 (as reported), people, including the Uyghur community, JL, JU members, Falun Gong believers, and Tibetan activists, protested in Gottingen to call for the closure of the Gottingen Confucius Institute co-financed by Chinese authorities. Protesters denounced Chinese politics against the Uyghur Ethnic Group such as detaining people in camps.

On 26 November 2021, members of Extinction Rebellion protested and blocked the entrance of a company in Bad Hersfeld against an American multinational technology company (Amazon). Protesters wanted to draw attention to the company's high CO2 emissions and the negative consequences of mass consumption with the 'Black Friday'.

On 11 January 2020, about 2000 people protested in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), through the St. Georg district and the city center, against the oppression of Uyghurs in China. The protest was organized by the Islamist group Hizb ut-Tahrir.

On 20 December 2019, residents of a locality in Lac Assal from the Afar ethnic group clashed with Chinese workers at a salt factory in Lac Assa area situated in Tadjourah region, accusing them of having sexually assaulted girls of their village. Several injuries were reported on both sides.
Around 16 August 2020 (as reported), dozens of citizens held a demonstration and burned tires in Obock (Obock) to denounce illegal fishing practiced by Chinese travelers.

On 16 October 2024, in Canefield, Saint Paul, in the morning, truckers affiliated to the Tipper Truckers Association held a protest demanding better wages, and more work on government projects. They decried the allocation of projects to Chinese truckers and not to local ones. The truckers parked their vehicles near the Canefield Industrial Park, blocking traffic. Police forces fired tear gas against them. A woman and her children not taking part in the mobilization were affected as canisters of teargas fell in her yard. One officer was seen kicking a protester. Another one was arrested and later released. According to police, rioters threw stones and bottles against them, but several sources stated that the mobilization was peaceful, except for a scuffle, and that the police intervention was unjustified. Another source identified the rioters as angry bystanders throwing firebombs at the truckers to force them clear the road. Non-members of the Tipper Truckers Association and operatives of the United Workers Party (UWP) participated in the mobilization.
On 29 June 2021, demonstrators gathered in front of an American manufacturer company's office in Brondby demanding they stop supplying construction equipment to Israeli companies in the Gaza Strip.
On 14 November 2021, people demonstrated in front of the US Embassy in Copenhagen to oppose the US trade embargo and sanctions against Cuba.

On 19 February 2022, people gathered in Ronne to oppose the governments plans to allow US soldiers and military equipment on Danish soil as part of a new bilateral agreement to facilitate the troops' movement in Europe. Members of the Red-Green Alliance took part in the event. A smaller counter-demonstration took place at the same place.
On 25 June 2022, people demonstrated in front of the US Embassy in Copenhagen to denounce the US Supreme Court's decision to overturn the abortion legislation in the United States.

On 26 August 2022, around 100 people demonstrated in front of the US Embassy in Copenhagen to denounce the US Supreme Court's decision to overturn the abortion-related Roe v Wade in the United States and in support of reproduction rights. Amnesty International and 3F trade union activists participated in the event, among others.

On 31 May 2020, at least 2,000 people gathered by the US Embassy in Osterbro, Copenhagen, for a Black Lives Matter protest, demonstrating against racism and discrimination. The protest ended by the Christiansborg parliament buildings. It was organized by Black Lives Matter Denmark. The coronavirus assembly ban does not apply to demonstrations.
On 28 October 2022, football fans gathered in Brondby (Hovedstaden) to oppose the decision of the local football club's board to sell most of the club's shares to the US investment group company.
On 7 June 2020, over 15,000 people gathered for a Black Lives Matter solidarity protest in Copenhagen. The protest moved from the US embassy to Christiansborg. Politicians took part.

On 22 July 2020, approximately 300 to 400 protesters gathered in front of the US embassy in Copenhagen to demonstrate against racism, on the occasion of US Secretary of State, Mike Pompeo, visiting Denmark. The demonstration was organized by Black Lives Matter. Protesters from the Afro Danish Collective took part.

On 22 July 2020, an unknown number of protesters including Palestinians in Denmark demonstrated during an official visit by the US Secretary of State in Copenhagen, calling for a boycott of Israeli products.

On 26 January 2025, around 200 to 300 people demonstrated in Copenhagen to oppose the Danish government's proposal to allow permanent US military bases on Danish soil. Activists from Demos, Global Action (GA), the Communist Party (KP), and the United Federation of Danish Workers (3F) participated in the event, among others.
On 8 February 2025, peace activists staged a protest performance in Roskilde, Sjaelland, to oppose the Danish government's proposal to allow permanent US military bases on Danish soil.

On 22 March 2025, people demonstrated in Aarhus, Midtjylland, to oppose US President Donald Trump's attempt to assert control over Greenland, to oppose US military bases on Danish soil, and to call for increased welfare spending over military investments. Among other things, participants also voiced concerns about Trump's administration on climate policies, the treatment of LGBT rights, the perceived undermining of international agreements, and the situation in the West Bank.
On 30 January 2020, demonstrators including Palestinians, gathered in front of the US Embassy in Copenhagen to oppose the US actions in the Middle East and demanding to boycott Israel.

On 20 January 2021, Amnesty International activists gathered in front the US Embassy in Copenhagen over the inauguration of Joe Biden as the new president of the United States. The activists expressed hope for an improvement in the human rights area and, among other things, the closure of the Guantanamo base.

On 10 March 2020, ethnic Tibetan staged a march and a demonstration in front of the Embassy of People's Republic of China in Copenhagen to accuse the Chinese government of human rights violations and to call on it to recognise Tibet as a free state.
02 January. Mayi Mayi Fimbo na Fimbo Bitonto ambushed a company convoy near Mulange village. One person was killed and others were injured, including a Chinese employee of the company.

properties.actor: Unidentified Armed Group (Democratic Republic of Congo)
properties.notes: On 17 March 2019, an unidentified armed group of approximately 40 militia members attacked the Kimya gold mine, at the Muchacha mining site and near Epulu village (Mambasa, Ituri). The assailants killed two Chinese workers and one Congolese. They also looted 50,000 USD and 50 grams of gold.

properties.actor: Unidentified Armed Group (Democratic Republic of Congo)
properties.notes: On 17 June 2019, near Blukwa, an unidentified armed group attacked a convoy of Chinese mine workers and FARDC soldiers, who were accompanying the party. In the ensued firefight 1 FARDC soldier and 1 Chinese national were killed. On 20 June, a provincial deputy has been arrested, together with other 14 people, and accused of organizing the attack.

On 28 October 2019, civil society activists reportedly held a march from Kitutu to Kitumba in Sud-Kivu, Mwenga territory, in Beni city of Nord-Kivu (coded to Kitutu), to protest against the illicit exploitation of local minerals by Chinese companies in the area.

properties.actor: Unidentified Armed Group (Democratic Republic of Congo)
properties.notes: On 21 November 2019, unidentified persons abducted 3 Chinese workers of a mine company in Kitumba, Matebo, groupement Bingilibazala, chefferie de Wamuzimu, Mwenga. 2 FARDC soldiers and another civilian were injured.

On 19 March 2020, Mimbulu market sellers set tires and barricades on fire in demonstration in the neighbourhood of Upemba, in Lubumbashi (Haut-Katanga), against the municipality's decision to sell part of the market. Rioters attacked a Chinese passer-by, who was saved by police officers before the latter started shooting in the air to disperse rioters.

properties.actor: CODECO: Cooperative for Development of Congo
properties.notes: Between 4 and 5 April 2020, an armed clash ensued between CODECO militiamen and FARDC forces in a mining area in Sumbabho, near Mwanga (Ituri). The clash resulted in three Chinese civilians and a FARDC official dead. It was reported the Chinese were mining gold and the Congolese military was committed to protect them. The perpetrators stole gold before escaping.

properties.actor: Unidentified Armed Group (Democratic Republic of Congo)
properties.notes: On 11 August 2020, 7 unidentified armed men clashed with private security guards at a mining site in Kakula (Kolwezi, Lualaba) following an incursion by these 7 attackers. 1 Chinese national of the company Zijin Mining Group Co, which runs the mine, was killed in the attack and 1 Congolese national was also shot and injured.
On 24 October 2020, a group of construction workers of a Chinese company demonstrated in Tshikapa (Kamonia, Kasai) to demand their unpaid salaries for the last 4 months.

properties.actor: Military Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (2019-)
properties.notes: On 30 November 2020, Mayi-Mayi rebel combatants (unidentified group) clashed with the FARDC in an unspecified goldmine in Mambasa territory (Mambasa, Ituri), following an incursion by these rebels. 2 rebels were killed and 1 civilian was shot dead by a stray bullet. The Mayi-Mayi, who managed to loot this goldmine run by Chinese nationals, abducted 7 civilians (5 of them women), and forced them to carry the loot.

properties.actor: Unidentified Armed Group (Democratic Republic of Congo)
properties.notes: On 2 December 2020, unidentified militiamen ambushed and killed 1 Chinese civilian with machetes in Basimbi village, near Kitumba (Mwenga, Sud-Kivu). The victim was a worker of the Chinese company Bluent Mineral Mining, which operates in the area.

On 28 January 2021, a group of residents barricaded the main road near a mining site (Gecamines Kapata) 15 km from Kolwezi town (Kolwezi, Lualaba). They showed their outrage for the death of a Congolese worker the previous day and accused Chinese workers of being the perpetrators (unconfirmed). The police intervened and dispersed the crowd.
On 1 February 2021, workers of the Chinese mining company Lualaba Cooper Smelter marched in Kolwezi (Kolwezi, Lualaba) to demand better working conditions and wages.

Around 7 February 2021, members of the Mayi Mayi militia raided a hotel in the TP 32 suburb of Mambasa's trading center (Mambasa, Ituri), which allegedly serves as the headquarters of a Chinese mining company. According to reports, the militiamen killed one or two civilians and wounded one or two others. Subsequent to this event, members of the Congolese military forces, the FARDC, detained 6 Mayi Mayi militia men.

On 20 March 2021, a group of people marched in Ingende (Ingende, Equateur) to protest against Chinese business owners who cut timber in their territory, demanding business compliance to logging protocols.

On 10 June 2021, a group of artisanal gold miners gathered in the streets of Badengaido (Mambasa, Ituri) to demand the eviction of Chinese expatriates, whom they say are looting the area and eroding the river ecosystem with the use of chemicals.

Around 18 June 2021, a group of people, including Lamuka activists, gathered in front of the American Embassy in the city of Kinshasa - Gombe (Kinshasa, Kinshasa) to protest against American support for the country's current administration, which they say is illegitimate. They also protested against a new law governing the country's National Independent Electoral Commission (CENI), which they say will give an unfair advantage to the President's political party and his predecessor's during the 2023 elections. The PNC intervened in the event, dispersing the protesters. 8 people were detained and later released.

properties.actor: Military Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (2019-)
properties.notes: On 20 July 2021, two elements of the FARDC whipped and tortured 2 miners at the Camus mining site located in the outskirts of Musonoie town (Mutshatsha, Lualaba). Other sources suggest the incident took place in Kolwezi. The soldiers were sentenced to 2 years and 18 months of prison time, respectively, on 23 July. Two Chinese men, who reportedly ordered the FARDC soldiers to attack the miners, were also detained by the military court.

On 30 August 2021, a group of people marched in the village of Kenge, located in Wamuzima chiefdom (Mwenga, Sud-Kivu) [coded as Kabikokole], to protest against the Governor's decision to suspend the mining activities of 6 companies in this part of the province. They also protested against what they say is the illegal exploitation of minerals by Chinese companies in the south of Mwenga.

properties.actor: Military Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (2019-)
properties.notes: Around 13 August 2021 (between 12 August - 15 August), the FARDC clashed against the CODECO-URDPC near Kilo (Djugu, Ituri), either in Lisey or Itendey/Itendeyi. The clashes were triggered after the armed group abducted 3 Chinese nationals (who were extracting gold in a mining site), looted goods and burnt down houses, including a hospital. While some sources suggest that one of the Chinese nationals was killed, others point out that three bodies (presumed to be of the victims) were found dead, while other sources suggest the fatality number is still unknown. Community displacements were triggered.

properties.actor: Military Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (2019-)
properties.notes: On 5 September 2021, a FARDC soldier killed the administrator of a mining site held by the Chinese called 'Sun City', in the locality of Biondo, located 40 km of Mambasa (Mambasa, Ituri). The soldier was killed the next day by rioters in reprisal of the attack (coded as another event). Sources suggest the soldier was given the order to kill over a land conflict.

On 13 September 2021, several hundred local residents barricaded streets (through unspecified means) and burnt tires in Kitutu (Mwenga, Sud-Kivu), to demand that a Chinese mining company cease what they say is the illegal exploitation of resources. The PNC/FARDC fired shots in the air to disperse the demonstrators.

On 14 November 2021, a Mayi Mayi militia of ethnic Batwa clashed against the FARDC in the village of Mutuka (Kabambare, Maniema). 1 FARDC soldier was killed and 4 people (including a Chinese man) were wounded. 100 people were displaced. A mining site was looted.

properties.actor: FPDC: Popular Front for Democracy in Congo
properties.notes: On 20 November 2021, the Mayi Mayi FPDC clashed with police and military forces during an attack on a Chinese mining camp, 4 km away from Mukera or in Mukera (Mutambala, Fizi, Sud-Kivu). The armed men abducted 5 to 8 Chinese citizens following a fire exchange against 11 police officers. 1 police officer or FARDC soldier was killed and another security officer was injured. The abducted Chinese miners were released on 6 June 2022.
