On 17 July 2022, hundreds of members of the French Tibetan community demonstrated in Fecamp to pay tribute to a Tibetan worker killed by his Chinese employers and call for justice. The victim who worked in a restaurant was stabbed to death by three of his employers in a restaurant in Saint-Leonard on 11 July.

On 27 July 2022, striking NP workers gathered outside their factory in Dole to denounce that they were not informed about the acquisition of their firm by an American company. The acquisition came in the context of their demands to raise their salaries and to have better work conditions.

On 1 June 2020, people demonstrated in Amiens to denounce systemic racism, police brutality, and lack of justice in France and the rest of the world. They also paid tribute to a African-American man killed by the police in Minneapolis on 25 May 2020.

On 17 July 2022, hundreds of or several thousand members of the Tibetan communities of France and other European countries (Spain, Belgium, Switzerland) demonstrated in La Bastille square in Paris to pay tribute to a Tibetan worker allegedly killed by his Chinese employers and call for justice. The victim who worked in a restaurant was presumedly stabbed to death by three of his employers in a restaurant in Saint-Leonard on 11 July 2022.

On 3 December 2022, hundreds of people, including members of the Chinese community, gathered at the Place de la Nation in Paris, to demonstrate against the Chinese government and denounce the treatment of the Uyghur Muslim minority in Xinjiang.

On 23 June 2022, at the call of MFPF, the Feministes revolutionnaires Nantes collective, and the NOSIG LGBTQ+ association, people demonstrated in Nantes to defend the right to abortion, ahead of the US Supreme Court's decision on Roe v. Wade.

On 22 April 2023, several hundred people, including members of the Tibetan community and teachers, gathered in Paris in support of the Dalai Lama and denouncing the 'use of Chinese propaganda' by French journalists and the media over a recent, controversial video of the Dalai Lama. The event was called for by six Tibet-affiliated associations.
On 25 July 2020, around 100 persons demonstrated near the Embassy of China in Paris. They protested in support to Ouighours.

On 6 May 2024, at the call of LDH and AI, around 20 people demonstrated in Toulouse (Occitanie) to protest against what they deemed a 'genocide' of the Ouighour population by Chinese authorities. The protest happened during Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to France.

On 17 July 2024, about 40 Gaussin company employees gathered outside the commercial court of Dijon (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte) to protest against the planned buyout of a subsidiary (Metalliance) of their company by a French-American company, claiming this would be detrimental to their professional future.

On 15 July 2024, FaC affiliates gathered for a press conference in Lucciana (Corse) to protest against the sale of Rubis Terminal to the American I Square Capital pension fund, which they considered potentially conducive to an increase in gas prices.

On 4 May 2024, several thousand members of the Tibetan community gathered on Republic Square in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against the state visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping, whom they deemed a 'dictator', to France.

On 17 September 2024, at the call of UGVC - General Union of Cognac Winegrowers (Union Generale des Viticulteurs pour l'AOC Cognac), between 800 and 1,000 farmers, winegrowers, and salespeople, drove 120 tractors at a slow pace to protest from several localities in the area and gathered outside the Sub-Prefecture in Cognac (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against Chinese authorities' decision to impose import taxes on French Cognac, threatening the revenues of the Cognac industry. The protesters urged the European Union (EU) to financially support them and advocated for a cancellation of the Chinese taxes. On 9 October 2024, at the call of FNSEA and JA, around 30 farmers with 10 tractors gathered outside the Sub-Prefecture and dumped grapes in Cognac (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against Chinese authorities' decision to impose import taxes on French Cognac, threatening the revenues of the Cognac industry. The protesters urged the European Union (EU) to financially support them and advocated for a cancellation of the Chinese taxes.

On 9 October 2024, at the call of FNSEA and JA, around 30 farmers with 10 tractors gathered outside the Sub-Prefecture and dumped grapes in Cognac (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against Chinese authorities' decision to impose import taxes on French Cognac, threatening the revenues of the Cognac industry. The protesters urged the European Union (EU) to financially support them and advocated for a cancellation of the Chinese taxes.

On 17 October 2024, at the call of CGT and CFDT, around 40 striking Sanofi employees staged a picket line at the Doliprane production site in Lisieux (Normandie) to demonstrate against Sanofi's decision to sell its consumer healthcare branch, Opella, to an American pension fund.

On 17 October 2024, over 200 people gathered in front of the prefecture in Nantes (Pays de la Loire) to demonstrate against job cuts announced by General Electric Vernova, an American wind turbine manufacturer. At the time of reporting, the company planned to eliminate 360 jobs across its facilities in Montoir-de-Bretagne and Saint-Herblain, with 140 positions cut from the wind turbine assembly plant in Montoir-de-Bretagne and 220 jobs at the Saint-Herblain site.

On 20 October 2024, protesters gathered outside the US embassy in Paris (Ile-de-France) to condemn ongoing US support for Israel amid the Israeli military's offensive on Gaza and express solidarity with the Palestinian people.

On 19 November 2024, at the call of FO, striking Hennessy employees gathered for a picket line in Cognac (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against the relocation of the packaging unit to China, citing fears of downsizing and decreasing product quality.

On 28 November 2024, in the morning, at the call of CGT, FO, and CFTC, over 500 people, including employees of Hennessy and other local businesses, staged a protest in Cognac (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to demonstrate against the potential outsourcing of bottling to China. The protesters demanded that bottling remain within the designated region to protect the AOC Cognac standards.

On 8 February 2025, at the call of AFPS, CGT, the Gaza Health Collective (Collectif Gaza Sante), LE, FSU, GES, LFI, JC, MP, MRAP, NPA, PCF, PS, SUD, the Jewish collective 'Tsedek', the Libertarian Communist Union (Union Communiste Libertaire - UCL), UDB, UEP - European Peace University (Universite Europeenne pour la Paix), the French Jewish Union for Peace (Union Juive Francaise pour la Paix - UJFP), the student union Union Pirate (Pirate Union) and 4ACG - Association of Former Conscripts in Algeria (Association des Anciens Appeles en Algerie), around 100 people, including national deputy (LFI) Pierre-Yves Cadalen, gathered in De La Liberte Square in Brest (Bretagne) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people and demand an end to the killing of Palestinian civilians in the Gaza Strip by the Israeli army. The protest also condemned Donald Trump Jr.'s plans to buy the Gaza Strip.

On 8 February 2025, PCF members gathered in Perpignan (Occitanie) to protest against Donald Trump's proposal to turn Gaza into the 'Cote d'Azur of the Middle East' and more broadly against his ideology.

On 23 February 2025, around 200 people, including members of the association Children of Ukraine (Enfants de l'Ukraine) and the national deputies Arthur Delaporte (PS), Bertrand Bouyx (Horizons), and Christophe Blanchet (MoDem), gathered on Theater Square in Caen (Normandie) to condemn Donald Trump's recent remarks on the war betwen Ukraine and Russia. The event was held to mark the third anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the ongoing war that followed.

Property destruction: On 2 March 2025, overnight, an unidentified group set fire to 12 Tesla cars at a dealership in Plaisance-du-Touch (Occitanie), destroying eight vehicles and partially damaging four others. The attack was claimed online by an unnamed antifascist group in a statement published on the Iaata website, in which the perpetrators stated they acted to denounce racism, neo-colonialism, and far-right ideology. They specifically referenced the rise of neo-Nazism and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, who appeared to perform a Nazi salute during Donald J. Trump's inauguration on 20 January 2025. The statement framed the act as part of a broader struggle against white supremacy, patriarchy, and economic exploitation.

On 7 March 2025, several hundred researchers, professors, scholars, and PhD candidates gathered on the Machines of the Isle of Nantes Square in Nantes (Pays de la Loire) to demonstrate. The event was part of a broader international mobilization, called 'Stand Up for Science', to express outrage against budget cuts and censorship imposed by US President Donald Trump and to demand more funding and support for public research and academic freedom.

Around 8 March 2025 (as reported), striking Keraglass workers began maintaining a continuous picket outside their workplace in Bagneaux-sur-Loing (Ile-de-France) to protest against a planned downsizing that would potentially result in the loss of 77 jobs. The protest, ongoing as of 24 March 2025, was led by CGT representatives who denounced the measure as unjust and profit-driven, highlighting the group's financial performance and the impact of unfair competition from China.

On 20 November 2020, around 50 delivery riders of an American company (Uber Eats) and CGT union members protested in Agen to denounce their working conditions. They protested a reduction in their pay and no minimum wage. They called for their employer to listen and answer their demands.

On 28 November 2020, people, including unions (CGT, FSU, CP), political party members (PCF, LFI, EELV), yellow vests demonstrators, and Attac activists, protested in Annemasse against the establishment of an American multinational technology company (Amazon) in France. They denounced the harmful consequences that the company could have on the local economy and the environment.
On 21 February 2021, around 300 people, including employees of Amazon, protested in Briec against the expansion of an American multinational technology company (Amazon) in the city.

On 7 January 2020, several dozen people, including railway workers, CGT union, employees, teachers, demonstrated in Paris against pension reform. They broke into the office of an American global investment management corporation (BlackRock), symbol - according to them - of those who are gaining wealth from the pension reform that they are asking to be withdrawn.

On 16 March 2021, around 50 employees of Altuglas and union members (CGC, CFTC, FO, SUD) blocked the entrance of the company in Saint-Avold to protest against the sale of the company to an American group (Trinseo). They demanded a bonus if the sale goes through.
On 13 March 2021, members of an association for the defense of Tibet demonstrated at the Francois-Rude square in Dijon. They called for an urgent action to protect the Uyghur community in China.

On 20 March 2021, nearly 1000 environmental activists, including students and Extinction Rebellion activists, protested in Caen to call on the government to implement concrete measures to tackle climate change. They also protested against the expansion of an American multinational technology company (Amazon) in Moult. Protesters denounced cutting down trees for a business project, the health consequences of climate change, as well as the precariousness that affects employees of the entertainment and cultural industries. A few Extinction Rebellion activists blocked temporarily and peacefully the entrance of a store at the end of the day.

On 28 March 2021, between 200 and 250 people protested in Briec to call on the government to implement concrete measures to tackle climate change. Protesters also demonstrated against the expansion of an American multinational technology company (Amazon) in the city. The event was part of a national day of protest called by Greenpeace, Friends of the Earth, International Movement ATD Fourth World, Attac, CARE, CCFD-Terre Solidaire (Catholic Committee against hunger and for development), XR, L214, FAGE, France Nature Environnement (French Nature Environment), Generations Futures (Future Generations), LDH, LPO - Ligue pour la protection des oiseaux (League for the Protection of Birds), Notre affaire a tous (Everyone's Business), OXFAM, SDN, EELV, Generation Ecologie (Ecology Generation), CFDT, and PS, before consideration by parliament of the government's climate and resilience bill, which they criticized.

On 7 April 2021, people, Friends of the Earth members, small business owners, and LFI members, protested in Paris against the expansion of an American multinational technology company (Amazon) in France. They denounced the harmful consequences that the company could have on the local economy and the environment as well as how it influences the climate change bill. They called on the government to implement concrete measures to tackle climate change and denounced that the climate change bill isn't enough. They brought hundreds of Amazon packages in front of the National Assembly.

On 18 March 2021, around 130 people protested in Strasbourg against the establishment of the company Huawei and the Chinese Communist Party. Protesters denounced alleged persecutions committed in China against minorities.

On 22 May 2021, between 480 (according to the police) and 500 pro-Palestine protesters, including activists (LDH, AFPS), demonstrated in Mulhouse to denounce escalation of violence in Palestine as a deliberate Israeli and American policy.
On 15 May 2021, around 60 people protested in Strasbourg to support the population in Tibet and call on China to release the 11th Panchen Lama.
On 13 June 2020, Gambians demonstrated before the Embassy of the US in Banjul city (Banjul) to denounce police brutality and racism against black people.
On 27 June 2020, Black Lives Matter activists demonstrated in front of the US Embassy in Banjul city (Banjul, Banjul) against injustice and racism.

On 22 March 2018, hundreds of Gambian environmental activists staged a protest and dug up pipes dumping waste from a Chinese animal feed factory directly into the sea in Gunjur (an hour south of Banjul). The activists had complained for months that it was a health hazard.

On 4 July 2020, three members of the Menwith Hill Accountability Campaign (MHAC) staged a protest outside of the US military base in Menwith Hill to call for transparency and accountability for what goes on at the base. 40 further campaigners took part via a webinar.

On 21 July 2020, a demonstration took place outside of the Old Bailey courthouse in Smithfield, London - City of London, against the plans to extradite Julian Assange to the US for prosecution, which the protesters deem to be an issue of press freedom.

On 6 September 2020, Stand Up To Racism campaigners held a Refugees Welcome and Black Lives Matter protest in Glasgow coinciding with the start of the US trial of the four police officers involved in the killing of George Floyd.

On 15 March 2021, residents demonstrated in Sanyang town (Brikama, Kombo South) after a Senegalese stabbed a Gambian to death over a private dispute. They erected barricades, burnt tires on roads, and set fire to a Chinese fishmeal factory where both were employed. Locals also attacked the properties of Senegalese civilians during demonstrations.The police forces intervened and fired tear gas at the demonstrators who burnt the local police station down in return. One person was arrested. The army was later deployed to settle the situation.

On 25 September 2020, campaign group Save British Farming held a tractor demonstration in Northallerton against post-Brexit trade deals that could open the door for American imported food with lower standards than British produce. A member of Green Party also attended the rally.
On 8 September 2020, at least 6 residents protested outside the Chinese consulate in Belfast - South after the erection of a boundary wall built without planning permission.

On 5 January 2020, the family and friends of a slain motorcyclist staged a protest at the spot he was hit by a car in Brackley, demanding justice. The driver returned to the US with no trial, claiming diplomatic immunity.
On 1 October 2020, Chinese protesters burned Chinese flags and chanted for Hong Kong independence outside the Chinese embassy in London - Westminster.

On 23 October 2020, farmers drove a convoy-rally through Marlborough (Wiltshire) to protest a proposed US-UK trade deal that protesters claim would lower food safety standards that foods imported from the US would be held to including chlorinated chicken and beef that has been produced using growth hormones.
On 3 February 2020, three unidentified men targeted a Chinese student in Cross Farm Road, Harborne, where they punched and kicked him, accusing him of having coronavirus.
On 4 February 2020, two international students were pelted by eggs in a racial attack on The Square in Market Harborough, which was prompted by the scare surrounding the coronavirus in China.

Around 5 February 2020 (as reported), a Chinese female student wearing a face mask was pushed and verbally threatened in Sheffield, by three people in what was considered as 'xenophobic and racist' attack during coronavirus pandemic.
On 6 January 2020, more than 100 members of Stop the War Coalition protested at Buchanan Street in Glasgow City centre to call on the British government to oppose any US war actions directed at Iran.

On 7 May 2021, at least 26 people protested outside Menwith Hill in Harrogate, calling for the closure of the US military base concerning its purpose of military, political and economic information data collection. Menwith Hill Accountability Campaign and Yorkshire CND organized the event.

On 22 May 2021, Black Lives Matter supporters gathered outside the US Embassy in London - Lambeth to hold a vigil marking the first anniversary of the murder of George Floyd which sparked an international protest movement. Also in attendance were supporters of SUTR: Stand Up To Racism and Unison.

On 25 April 2021, a female Chinese student was knocked to the ground in a violent attack by a group of people on Fargate in Sheffield due to coronavirus fears and lockdown rules. The victim was hospitalized for eye injuries. Police classified the incident as a hate crime.
On 16 February 2020, two Chinese women were punched in the head and stomach by a group of youths in Runcorn, who blamed them of spreading coronavirus. One of the women needed stitches in her head.

Around 15 August 2021 (weekend of), UK Drone Watch campaigners gathered outside the Royal Air Force Station in Waddington to oppose experimental US drone flights from the airbase over the UK. They highlighted that the planned flights scheduled for this summer might breach safety regulations due to the airbase's proximity to houses, schools, and businesses.

On 4 November 2021, Extinction Rebellion campaigners blockaded Schlumberger Gould Research Centre in Madingley to protest the American oilfield services company's research into fossil fuel extraction. Some locked themselves to a pink boat blocking the front entrance, while others blocked the delivery entrance and camped in tents surrounding the center's roads.

On 21 November 2021, thousands of Ethiopians and their supporters marched to the American Embassy in London - Westminster to protest against the US government's alleged support for the Tigray People's Liberation Front. This was the second day of demonstrations.

On 4 February 2022, on the eve of the Winter Olympics opening ceremony in Beijing, hundreds of Uyghurs, Tibetans, Hong Kongers and British politicians rallied outside the Chinese embassy before marching to Piccadilly Circus in London - Westminster. They condemned China's human rights record and the International Olympic Committee's decision to award the country a second Olympics in just over a decade. The founder of the Stop Uyghur Genocide campaign, a leader of Tibetan Community UK, a member of Free Tibet, and the director of Hong Kong Watch (also a human rights lawyer) participated in the rally.

On 4 March 2020, a Chinese university student was assaulted and threatened with a knife by four unknown white men on Castle Street in Exeter, as they accused him of having coronavirus. The attackers punched, kicked and spit at the teenager.

On 14 May 2022, pro-choice campaigners gathered outside the US Consulate in Edinburgh to protest against the erosion of the right to an abortion in the US following the Supreme Court's ruling to strike down the court's precedent in protecting the right to an abortion in the Roe vs. Wade. Green Party and Labour Party MSPs were present and addressed the crowd.

On 21 May 2022, hundreds of anti-nuclear activists gathered outside an RAF base in Lakenheath to demand that nuclear weapons owned by the US military, which uses the base, be stored in underground bunkers on the site. Activists from the CND were present.

On 25 May 2022, around 50 Black Lives Matter demonstrators gathered for a protest organized by Stand Up To Racism in front of the US Embassy in London - Westminster, against racism, and in remembrance of George Floyd.
On 5 March 2020, a Chinese student had clothes torn by three people shouting 'coronavirus' on Dumbarton Road in Glasgow's area of Scotstoun.

On 24 June 2022, an unknown number of people gathered for a protest outside the US consulate in Edinburgh, against the US Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, and in support of abortion rights. An unknown number of anti-abortion demonstrators were also present in support of the court's decision.
On 12 June 2022, people marched in Nottingham to protest the city's sister-city relationship with Ningbo, a city in China. The rally was organized by Nottingham Stands with Hong Kong.

On 17 March 2020, four Chinese students wearing medical face masks were attacked on Vincent's Walk in Southampton by 'a group' in a racially motivated attack related to the coronavirus. No injuries were reported.

On 19 November 2022, residents gathered at RAF Lakenheath in Lakenheath against the planned roll-out of American nuclear bombs to the airbase. The protest was organized by the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament.

On 16 October 2022, Hong Kong pro-democracy protesters gathered outside the Chinese Consulate in Manchester in response to the 20th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party being held in China. A diplomat and staff from the Consulate clashed with protestors, ripped down pro-democracy posters, dragged a protestor inside the consulate, and beat him. Police forces intervened and rescued the protestor.

On 9 December 2022, activists from Palestine Action broke into the American-owned weapons plant, Teledyne Labtech Ltd site in Presteigne, to denounce Labtech's involvement in supplying military hardware to Israel. Demonstrators smashed windows, threw red paint over the buildings, and destroyed several computers.
Property destruction: On 15 April 2020, the walls of a Chinese takeaway were spray-painted graffiti by racist vandals in Quarry Bank amid the coronavirus outbreak. Police said it was a hate crime.
On 20 May 2023, campaigners for CND and other local groups staged a protest outside RAF Lakenheath in Lakenheath against the planned roll-out of American nuclear bombs to the airbase.

On 28 May 2020, more than 20 people staged a protest in front of the US Embassy in Battersea, London - Wandsworth, in response to the death of George Floyd, a black man in the United States at the hands of police officers.

On 4 November 2023, pro-Palestinian protesters marched from the Queen's University to the US Consulate offices in Belfast - South (Northern Ireland) in solidarity with Palestinians and to demand a ceasefire between Israel and Palestine. Protesters condemned Israel's actions in Gaza and the US's support for Israel.

On 4 February 2024, pro-Palestinian supporters, including UCU Ulster and UCU at QUB members, gathered for a rally at Queen's University Belfast and headed toward the US Consulate in Belfast - North (Northern Ireland), calling for an end to the Israeli military campaign in the Gaza Strip, while expressing solidarity with Palestinians. The event was organized by the Ireland Palestine Solidarity Campaign (Belfast).
On 2 April 2024, campaigners from The Lakenheath Alliance for Peace group staged a protest in Lakenheath (England) against the return of US nuclear weapons to the RAF base in the area.

On 11 May 2024, CND campaigners gathered outside the US Embassy in London - Wandsworth (England) to protest against the return of American nuclear weapons in Britain. The event was part of the National Day of Action.

On 2 November 2024, at the call of PSC and on the occasion of Balfour Day, tens of thousands of pro-Palestine protesters, including independent politician and MP Jeremy Corbyn, held a march from Whitehall in London - Westminster to the US Embassy in London - Wandsworth (England) to protest US support for Israel amid ongoing conflicts in Palestine and Lebanon. Protesters carried Palestinian and Lebanese flags, with signs reading 'Free Palestine' and 'End Israeli apartheid.' Meanwhile, a small pro-Israel counter-protest took place nearby, with demonstrators holding British and Israeli flags and calling for the release of Israeli hostages held in Gaza. The Metropolitan Police reported arrests related to 'suspected support for proscribed organizations' among pro-Palestinian demonstrators.

On 6 November 2024, dozens of people and SUTR activists gathered outside Lime Street Station in Liverpool (England) to express their opposition to the recent election of Donald Trump as the 47th US president, denouncing 'racism, misogyny, and bigotry'. This protest followed Trump's victory over Democratic candidate Kamala Harris in the 2024 US presidential race.

On 20 January 2025, anti-Trump campaigners from SUTR, CND, StWC, pro-life and climate groups gathered in the city center in London - Westminster (England) for a Together Against Trump rally and his 'reactionary and far-right agenda' after he was sworn in as US president.

On 18 January 2025, at the call of the UK Women's March, up to 3,000 women marched from Waterloo to Old Palace Yard in London - Westminster (England) as part of a nationwide Women's March protesting increasing reports of violence against women. The protest occurred just days before Donald Trump's inauguration as President of the United States and featured signs condemning his presidency, the pro-life movement, and transphobia. Labour MP Bell Ribeiro-Addy also addressed the crowd.

On 18 January 2025, the Sudanese community living in the UK gathered outside the Embassy of Sudan in London - Westminster (England) to celebrate recent victories and express their solidarity with the Sudanese armed forces, joint forces, and their allies. Protesters called on international actors, including the UAE, to respect Sudan's sovereignty and refrain from interference. Sudanese protesters also denounced the U.S. Treasury's sanctions against Sudan's military leadership. Sudan's Minister of Culture and Information, Professor Khalid Al-Aiser, addressed the crowd.

On 5 February 2025, people protested outside the US Consulate in Belfast - South (Northern Ireland) to denounce Donald Trump's actions during the early days of his second term as US president. The protesters criticized what they described as 'anti-democratic, draconian, and dangerous' measures, joining a broader wave of protests taking place across the US and internationally.

On 8 February 2025, more than 1,000 people, including members of the Chinese, Tibetan, and Uyghur communities, gathered outside the historic former site of the Royal Mint in Tower Hill, London - Tower Hamlets (England), to protest against the proposed Chinese 'mega-embassy' in the city. Demonstrators waved flags and carried placards denouncing the project, citing concerns over security threats and transnational oppression by the Chinese Communist Party. There were scuffles - shoves and pushes - between demonstrators and the police, after which two individuals were arrested for breaching public order conditions.

On 15 February 2025, at the call of PSC, tens of thousands of pro-Palestine protesters held a march from Whitehall to the US Embassy in London - Wandsworth (England) to protest the proposal by President Donald Trump for the United States to consider taking ownership of the Gaza Strip and redevelop the territory into the 'Riviera of the Middle East'. Protesters carried banners and signs that read 'Hands off Gaza', 'Stand up to Trump', and 'Mr. Trump, Canada is not your 51st state. Gaza is not your 52nd'. Various campaign groups, including the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, Stop the War Coalition, and a Jewish community also attended the march. Independent MP Jeremy Corbyn also attended the march and spoke to the crowd. A pro-Israeli counter-protest by Stop the Hate group also took place along the route of the march at the junction of Grosvenor Road and Vauxhall Bridge. The two groups were separated, and the protests remained peaceful. However, police forces arrested eight individuals, but it is unclear from what side.

On 1 March 2025, pro-Palestine protesters, as well as an AI representative, held a march and gathered for a rally outside the US Consulate in Belfast - South (Northern Ireland), opposing America's support for Israel's actions in Gaza.

On 5 March 2025, at the call of the Ukraine Solidarity Campaign, hundreds of pro-Ukraine protesters gathered outside the US Embassy in London - Wandsworth (England) against Donald Trump and his policy toward Ukraine, while calling for the cancellation of his state visit to the UK. Protesters waved Ukrainian flags and held signs that read 'turncoat Trump. Now we must rejoin the EU', 'TrumPutin what an ugly cowardly team' and 'occupation is not peace. Justice for Ukraine'. Independent MP John McDonnell spoke at the rally.

Property destruction: On 8 March 2025, overnight, PA activists vandalized US President Donald Trump's Turnberry golf resort in Turnberry (Scotland) to condemn the US administration's stance on Gaza. Activists damaged greens, sprayed blood-red paint over the clubhouse, and wrote 'GAZA IS NOT 4 SALE' in large white letters on the lawn. The group described the action as a 'direct response to the US administration's stated intent to ethnically cleanse Gaza.' Police in Scotland were investigating the incident at the time of reporting.

Property destruction: On 17 March 2025, unknown individuals vandalized a Tesla car dealership on Boucher Road in Belfast - South (Northern Ireland), damaging at least 20 vehicles by breaking wing mirrors, smashing windows, and denting bodywork. The incident occurred amid a broader wave of demonstrations in the United States and Europe targeting Elon Musk and the Trump administration. Police had opened an investigation into the vandalism at the time of reporting.

On 7 June 2020, thousands of people gathered at the US embassy in the Nine Elms area of London - Wandsworth for a Black Lives Matter protest, demonstrating against police brutality after the killing of George Floyd, an unarmed black man, by a police officer in the United States.
On 12 September 2019, Alliance of Patriots organized a protest in Tbilisi. They demanded that the former US assistant state secretary David Kramer was declared persona non grata in Georgia.
On 15 September 2019, Alliance of Patriots organized a protest at the US Embassy in Tbilisi against Matthew Bryza and David Kramer. They also said the US should not support Saakashvili and his team.
On 12 November 2019, employees of a Georgian-US oil company organized a protest in front of US Embassy in Tbilisi. They demanded salaries that had not been paid to them for 10 months.

On 6 January 2020, up to 70 Iranians organized a vigil in relation to the death of Qasem Soleimani at the Embassy of Iran in Tbilisi. Placards condemning US actions in Iran and death of Soleimani were present.

On 26 January 2020, Alliance of Patriots organized a protest in front of the US Embassy in Tbilisi. They demanded that two US organizations - NDI and IRI stop their operation in Georgia. The protests were related to the public opinion polls that are periodically released by these organizations. The Alliance of Patriots claimed that the survey results of the latest polls are falsified in favor of the United National Movement.

On 18 February 2020, former employees of a US oil company organized a protest in Dedoplistkaro, demanding their unpaid salaries. The protesters claimed they would not allow the company to transport oil until their demands are met.

On 4 June 2020, a protest was organized in Tbilisi in relation to the death of George Floyd. The protesters condemned systemic racism in USA, supporting Balck Lives Matter movement. Two individuals arrived at the rally to declare the opposite and claimed that there is no racism in USA. US citizens were among the protesters.

On 12 August 2020, workers of an American oil company Frontera organized a protest in Dedoplis Tskaro. The protesters claimed that the company owes them salaries for months. Similar protests had been organized multiple times in the past.
On 4 January 2021, employees of an American company organized a protest in Dedoplis Tskaro and demanded belated salaries.
On 26 January 2021, up to 40 employees of an American oil company organized a protest in Dedoplis Tskaro and demanded indebted salaries.

On 9 January 2023, members of the Nottingham Stands with Hong Kong group staged a protest outside the Council House in Nottingham to call for Nottingham to end its twinning arrangement with the city of Ningbo in China considering the Chinese covernment's political repression in Hong Kong.
On 12 June 2019, dozens of protesters demonstrated in front of the US Embassy in Tbilisi demanding that the US stops supporting LGBT groups.
On 21 January 2018, people in Kaspi protested against hiring Chinese workers at the Heidelberg Cement factory and demanded that the company hire local workers.

On 19 August 2021, youths suspected to be illegal miners set ablaze an excavator belonging to a local mining firm at Adubiaho Mining site in Adubia town (Amansie West, Ashanti). Private security guarding the mining firm is alleged to have shot sporadically into the group, killing one person, and a Chinese national sustained serious injuries.

Construction work on the Sofoline Interchange at Kwadaso in Kumasi has come to a standstill as workers of the Chinese Geo Corporation (CGC) working on the interchange have decided to lay down their tools and protest their pay.

On 4 May 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the NDC party branch chairman for Dunkwa-Kadadwen Nkansah Daaho 'B' on the Tweapiase-Obuase road in Akrofuom (Obuasi, Ashanti). He was shot in the head, dying instantly while the other passengers escaped. The chairman was driving two Chinese gold dealers when the attackers' fired shots at the vehicle. The attackers stole gold and money.

Around 29 June 2023, youth protested in Hiawa (Prestea-Huni Valley, Western) against the killing of a suspected thief by security official of Chinese illegal miners. The suspect was at the premises of the Chinese miners when the security officers shot him.

On 20 October 2020, an unidentified armed group shot a Chinese national in Kumasi (Kumasi, Ashanti). There were no fatalities. The victim was taken to the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital for medical attention.
Around 6 September 2024 (as reported), suspected Galamseyers shot and killed a Chinese national (miner) in Watereso coded to Adubia (Amansie West; Ashanti). The suspected were later apprehended.

On 18 October 2024, a mob fight erupted between local youth and Chinese miners at a Galamsey (illegal mining) site in Sekyere Krobo, also called Krobo, coded to district capital Nsuta (Sekyere Central, Ashanti). The confrontation began when Chinese operators allegedly refused to cease their mining activities as demanded by local youth. The situation escalated to an exchange of gunfire, resulting in two people being shot and injured.

On 14 October 2024, a group of residents attacked and injured Chinese contractors at the Buduburam stretch of the Accra-Winneba Highway in Kasoa (Gomoa East, Central). The mob violence occurred after a rock blasted into the area, killing at least four people.
On 28 October 2024, fans of an American rapper recently arrested in Miami held a protest in Kumasi (Kumasi, Ashanti) to call for his release.

On 1 April 2021, a group of youth almost lynched their chief (Nana Owusu Acheaw Brempong II.) in Donkro-Nkwanta coded to (Nkoranza, Bono East). They accused the chief of releasing hectares of land to Chinese expatriates for illegal mining activities
Workers of the China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC), the company undertaking the Tema Port Expansion Project, protested against what they described as poor working conditions
Around 27 March 2019, Employees of a Chinese construction company staged a demonstration in Accra to protest their treatment.

On 9 April 2020, youths from Kwahu Praso (Kwahu West, Eastern) attacked a mining company in the area, mounted road blocks and fired gunshots to demonstrate against the mining activities in the community. Police forces rescued Chinese staff members of the company.

On 23 January 2025, around 100 women from various villages stormed the heavy sand exploration mine in Varela (Sao Domingos, Cacheu) to protest against the heavy sand mining activities in Nhiquin, which resumed last week. The protesters also invaded the facilities of the Chinese company 'GMG International (FZC) SA' which is responsible for the exploitation of the mineral, and claimed that the process was damaging their land.

On 14 May 2018, the Communist Party of Greece (KKE), affiliated labour unions and campaign groups demonstrated outside the Israeli embassy in Athens against U.S policy in the Middle East after dozens of Palestinian protesters were killed and over 2,000 were injured in clashes with Israeli soldiers along the border of Gaza following the transfer of the U.S. embassy to Jerusalem.

On 11 January 2020, there were two anti-war rallies and marches in Thessaloniki. The first was organised by members of PAME, the Committee for International Peace and the Federation of Greek Women and the second by LAE, ANTARSYA, KKE (m-l) and OKDE. The protesters shouted slogans against military interventions in the Middle East and when they reached the United States Consulate they burned an American flag.

On 31 January 2020, hundreds to 7,000 protesters rallied at Syntagma square in Athens while the Greek Parliament approved an updated defense agreement with the United States, allowing the use of Greek military facilities. The protest was organized by communist, left-wing, anti-war demonstrators, student associations and labor unions, who believe that NATO and U.S. bases are targets for reprisals.

On 16 April 2020, youth of Nsuem Number Two in Bosome Freho District (coded to Asiwa, Ashanti Region) attacked Chinese owners of a gold mine over a recent accident on the site. 1 Chinese person died and 2 were injured.

On 12 June 2018, in the afternoon, a group of ten people targeted the offices of the Hellenic American Union (HAU) in Athens - Central Athens smashing a window. The group also threw flyers before fleeing the scene. The embassy of the United States condemned the attack and a similar one at the HAU offices in Thessaloniki. Two members of anti-establishment groups Revolutionary Struggle and Conspiracy of Cells of Fire were identified by police using CCTV footage. They were both detained and charged.

properties.actor: Police Forces of Greece (2019-) CT Unit
properties.notes: On 29 January 2020, police disrupted a plot to commit a string of attacks. In North Athens, a counter-terrorist unit arrested a member of Conspiracy of the Cells of Fire, known as the 'Syntagma Archer', along with two women - one affiliated with Revolutionary Struggle. Police found a Kalashnikov rifle, a submachine gun, a handgun, stolen license plates, and a draft of a manifesto taking responsibility of planned attacks at the Association of Shipowners and the Chinese company that owns Piraeus port.

On 2 June 2020, about 300 members of KKE (m-l), ANTARSYA and KEERFA marched in Thessaloniki to express their solidarity with the Black Lives Matter demonstrations in the United States over the death of George Floyd in police custody and to protest against racism among other issues. The protesters burnt a US flag in front of the United States consulate.

On 28 September 2020, members of KKE and left-wing groups marched to the United States embassy in Athens-Central Athens with the main slogan 'Pompeo go home' during the visit of the US Secretary of State in Thessaloniki, demanding that US and NATO bases leave Greece and that Greece does not participate in any NATO military operations. Some of the demonstrators clashed with police, which used tear gas.

On 17 September 2021, members of labor associations, the Hellenic Committee for International Disarmament and Peace (EEDYE), student associations, associations of the self-employed, OGE and members of KKE marched to the United States embassy in Athens - Central Athens to protest during a meeting of NATO's military committee in Athens against the Mutual Defense Cooperation Agreement (MDCA) between Greece and the United States and the use of further locations in Greece by U.S. military forces.

On 30 December 2020, members of PENEN protested in Piraeus against the government and the Chinese company that owns Piraeus port over their plans for Piraeus port, which, according to the protesters, compromise the environment and workers' rights.

On 18 October 2021, 3 Tibetan activists (likely United States nationals) protested during the flame-lighting ceremony in ancient Olympia (Archaia Olympia) for boycotting the Beijing 2022 Olympics over China's human rights record. The protesters unfurled a banner reading 'No Genocide Games' and a Tibetan flag meters away from where the torch was lit and close to Greece's President and other officials. Security led them away. Police also detained another 4 protesters outside the stadium 1 hour before the start of the ceremony.

Combination of two related events. On 13 April 2022, container workers at Piraeus port, represented by the Piraeus Port Dock Containers Workers Union ENEDEP, staged a job walkout demanding that the Chinese shipping group COSCO, which is the majority owner of Piraeus port, pays the surcharges for night work, as well as Saturdays, Sundays and holidays. The protesters also demanded part-time workers' contracts change to full-time. On 14 April 2022, during a 24-hour strike, container workers at Piraeus port, represented by the Piraeus Port Dock Containers Workers Union ENEDEP, protested a financial proposal included in their collective labor agreement tabled by COSCO, and demanded that the Chinese shipping group, which is the majority owner of Piraeus port, pays the surcharges for night work, as well as Saturdays, Sundays and holidays. The protesters also demanded part-time workers' contracts change to full-time.

On 21 February 2023, hundreds of demonstrators held rallies in Athens - Central Athens during the two-day visit of US Secretary of State Antony Blinken. Members of KNE and PAME rallied outside the United States embassy shouting slogans and raising banners against US policies and against NATO bases in Greece. Students, leftist organizations and members of DiEM25 rallied in central Athens and marched to the embassy of the United States separately.

On 9 August 2023, on the occasion of the 77th anniversary since the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki on 6 and 9 August, members of the Thessaloniki Committee for International Disarmament and Peace (EDYETH) marched in central Thessaloniki 'against the imperialist designs of the U.S.A - NATO - EU.

On 17 November 2023, on the 50th anniversary of the 1973 Athens Polytechnic student uprising against the 1967-1974 military dictatorship, about 25,000 protesters, including students, political parties of the extra-parliamentary left and anti-authoritarian space, trade unions, KKE, SYRIZA, DiEM25, PASOK - KINAL, marched separately to the United States embassy and then to the Israeli embassy. (The United States is widely accused of supporting the junta during the Cold War years). The Association of Jailed & Exiled Anti-Junta Fighters holding a banner saying 'Resistance against fascism forever' headed the main march. PASP students carried the blood-stained Greek flag of the university students killed during the junta's attack at the university. Palestinians and members of anarchist collectives protested for a Free Palestine and against the war in Gaza. Smoke bombs in the colors of the Palestinian flag were thrown in front of the US embassy. The Palestinian ambassador laid a wreath at the Polytechnic memorial site. Roma demonstrators protested the fatal shooting of a Roma teenager by an OPKE police officer on 11 November.

On 13 January 2024, pro-Palestinian protesters marched in Athens - Central Athens in solidarity with the Palestinian people, following a call by the Palestinian Community of Greece and the Stop the War - Solidarity to Palestine alliance, demanding a ceasefire in Gaza and that Greece stop supporting Israel and the United States. The protesters shouted slogans and made stops at the embassies of the U.S. and Israel.

On 13 January 2024, members of the Thessaloniki Committee for International Disarmament and Peace (EDYETH) rallied at Thessaloniki port shouting slogans against the docking of U.S. warships in Thessaloniki and then marched in the city blocking traffic.

On 27 March 2024, demonstrators opposing the presence of US troops in Greece and any Greek involvement in current conflicts/missions, organized by the Communist Party of Greece-backed Peace Committee of Larissa and the Labor Center of Larissa, forced their way into a concert hall during a performance by the West Point Glee Club, a musical group of the US Military Academy, which was on tour in Greece, before they were pushed back by MAT riot police, who used tear gas and stun grenades. The demonstrators stormed inside after failed negotiations between police and the leaders of Laiki Sispirosi of Larissa and Thessaly arguing for their representatives to demonstrate in the building. US military cadets clashed with some demonstrators. There were no reports of injuries or arrests. The concert was cancelled.

On 26 April 2024, students, organized by their associations, rallied outside the United States embassy in Athens - Central Athens to express their solidarity with Palestinians and students in the US protesting against the war in Palestine. They also protested against US police and against the US government's support of Israel.

On 11 July 2024, on the occasion of 75 years since the founding of NATO, members of the Thessaloniki Committee for International Disarmament and Peace (EDYETH) and the Palestinian community of Thessaloniki marched demanding Greece's disengagement from NATO and to express their solidarity to the Palestinian people. When they reached the United States consulate they torched NATO and US flags. Anarchist collectives and members of the extra-parliamentary left rallied and marched against NATO separately.

On 7 October 2024, on the 1-year anniversary of the Hamas attack on Israel, about 2,000 demonstrators, including a large number of collectives (many of them likely far-left), marched in Athens in solidarity with the Palestinians, demanding an end to the war in Gaza and Lebanon. Police regulated traffic. The demonstrators made stops at the embassies of Israel (North Athens) and the United States (Central Athens) holding Palestinian flags, unfurling banners and chanting slogans. Many Palestinians walked with their children on their shoulders. At the end of the march, a group of rioters hurled stones and flares at MAT riot police, who responded with tear gas and stun grenades. There were 20 detentions (16 men, 4 women), 10 of which turned into arrests. There were reports of police violence chasing demonstrators in central Athens, using stun grenades next to passing drivers, choking and kicking demonstrators while they were detaining them and spraying anyone who complained about the level of violence. The Greek police violence observatory CopWatchGR released a video of 2 MAT riot police officers pushing and kicking a young woman, who confronted them verbally over the violent detentions, while a third officer attempted to stop them. There is no further information on injuries.

On 12 October 2024, KKE marched in Athens - Central Athens to mark the 80th anniversary of the liberation of Athens from Nazi occupation and denounced the current 'imperialist pursuits as seen in the competition between the United States and China, the war between NATO and Russia in Ukraine, and the latest developments in the Middle East'.

On 12 October 2024, KKE marched in Athens - Central Athens to mark the 80th anniversary of the liberation of Athens from Nazi occupation and denounced the current 'imperialist pursuits as seen in the competition between the United States and China, the war between NATO and Russia in Ukraine, and the latest developments in the Middle East'.

On 17 November 2024, on the 51st anniversary of the 1973 Athens Polytechnic student uprising against the 1967-1974 military dictatorship, thousands of protesters, including students, political parties (headed by their leaders) SYRIZA, PASOK-KINAL, Course of Freedom, Nea Aristera, KKE, DiEM25 and political parties of the extra-parliamentary left, the civil servants union (ADEDY), labor unions and anti-establishment collectives, marched separately to the United States and Israeli embassies. Student associations carrying a large Palestinian flag held a pre-rally before following the main march, which was led by The Association of Imprisoned and Exiled Resistance Fighters (1967-1974) carrying a banner reading 'Resistance to Fascism'. PASP students carried the blood-stained Greek flag of the university students killed during the junta's attack at the university. KKE and KNE protesters shouted anti-American slogans at the US embassy. ANTARSYA students had a brief confrontation (pushing and headlock of an elderly man) with supporters of ousted SYRIZA leader Kasselakis in the sidelines. More than 5,700 police (MAT, DRASI, OPKE, DIAS, Security police and Traffic police), a helicopter and drones were deployed. There were extensive traffic restrictions. Security was heightened at key locations, including the US and Israeli embassies, synagogues and Israeli-linked businesses. Before the march, police detained 150 people for identity checks and made 7 arrests.

On 17 November 2024, on the 51st anniversary of the 1973 Athens Polytechnic student uprising against the 1967-1974 military dictatorship, citizens of all ages, political parties, labor unions and the Labor Center of Thessaloniki, civil society organizations, student associations and the academic community rallied at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki to mark the occasion before setting off for a march in the city. The demonstrators were carrying tens of banners. The main slogan was 'Bread Education Freedom'. They also shouted slogans for education and demanded the end of the war in Gaza. Police regulated traffic. The Association of Imprisoned and Exiled Resistance Fighters (1967-1974) headed the march. Demonstrators (likely far-left) lit torches when the march stopped at the US consulate, and they burned the US and Israeli flags. The march split in 2 directions and a group of rioters with covered faces hurled 7-8 petrol bombs and stones at a riot police roadblock. They responded with tear gas and stun grenades, followed by a police chase in the back streets. There were 40 detentions (46 throughout the day and 7 arrests).

On 9 February 2025, a large demonstration, organized by the Thessaloniki Committee for International Disarmament and Peace (EDYETH), was staged outside the Thessaloniki port, where Greek, Turkish, Italian and French vessels were docked. The protesters, carrying a large banner, marched to the main entrance of the port and tried to block it. They burned NATO and United States flags and shouted anti-NATO slogans. They protested against Greece's participation in the NATO naval exercise Steadfast Dart 2025, requesting the closure of Thessaloniki port for military ships, and demanded that Greece stay out of the war in Ukraine.

On 14 April 2018, an estimated 6,000 people turned up at a march in central Athens organized by the Communist Party to protest the US-led airstrikes against Syria. The protesters gathered at Syntagma Square before marching to the U.S. Embassy, chanting anti-US slogans and carrying banners. Some wrote on the pavement in red paint: 'Americans, murderers of people.' Police vehicles barricaded access to the embassy and protesters left peacefully.

On 16 April 2018, around 700 people were demonstrating in the capital Athens - Central Athens as part of a wave of demonstrations against this weekend's aerial bombing campaign in Syria by the United States, France and Britain. During the demonstration, a group of Greek communist students attempted to topple a statue of former US president Harry S Truman using a chainsaw and ropes. Riot police fired tear gas to prevent the students from bringing down the bronze statue using a chainsaw and ropes. At least two people were injured.

On 5 October 2019, during the visit of the US Secretary of State, a demonstration in central Athens organised by KKE, PAME, ANTARSYA and other far left groups against the renewal of a Greece-US defence cooperation agreement turned violent. Demonstrators burned flags and threw red paint at Truman's statue; riot police responded with the use of tear gas before members of PAME retaliated physically fighting with riot police officers.

On 20 November 2023, in Saint George's, Saint George, a group of people, called by the Grenadians for Justice organization, held a pro-Palestine march demanding a ceasefire in the Gaza Strip (Palestine). Protesters stood outside the US Embassy and tried to submit a letter to its diplomats, although they refused to take it. The protest was attended by several legislators at the Parliament and a former senator. It was held as ongoing war between the Palestinian Hamas armed group and Israel caused many civilian casualties since 7 October.

On 15 March 2025, up to 1000 people demonstrated in Nuuk to protest against US President Donald Trump and his remarks about gaining control over Greenland, including possible annexation of Greenland by the United States. The Prime Minister of Greenland, Mute B. Egede (IA) and the chairman of the Demokraatit party Jens Frederik Nielsen participated in the event, among others.
On 21 June 2018, a group of people led by the civil organization Usac marched to the USA Embassy in Guatemala City to protest against the separation of Guatemalan families at the US border.

On 3 June 2020, in Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni (Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni), protesters gathered for a Black Lives Matter protest in solidarity with the protests taking place in the United States. Protesters burned American flags during the protest.

On 4 January 2019, Dozens demonstrate in Conakry outside the American embassy demanding the release of Mohamed Toure, son of former Guinean President Sekou Toure and his wife, who are in jail in the USA for forced labour and illegal accommodation charges.

On 5 February 2021, around 30 demonstrators gathered in Narsarsuaq to oppose possible open-pit uranium coal exploration on Greenland soil, citing environmental concerns as well as concerns with Chinese economic influence.

On 20 April 2020, a group of students demonstrated in front of the Chinese Embassy in Conakry city (Kaloum, Conakry), against xenophobic violence targeting African students accused of spreading coronavirus in China, and to denounce the Guinean government's inaction.

On 17 December 2021, 81 workers of a Chinese company demonstrated in Sekhoussoriya village, Madina-Oula subdivision (Madina-Oula, Kindia) against their dismissal by the company. They erected barricades on roads. The military forces intervened and fired tear gas at them, to which their replied with stones. Several demonstrators were injured.
On 2 January 2022, workers of the GGE Chinese mining company erected barricades and burnt tires on roads in Siguiri town, Siguiri-Centre subdivision (Siguiri, Kankan) to demand a salary increase.
On 5 March 2022, women labours held a protest in Kindia (Kindia Centre, Kindia) to call the mayor to cancel the tenure of a part of the market to a Chinese business person.
On 11 November 2022, a group of men and women demonstrated against illegal Chinese mining in Daabaah near Didi (Kintinian, Siguiri, Kankan). Young people barricaded the road until the night.
On 21 September 2023, women supporters of former president demonstrated in front of the US embassy in Conakry (Kaloum, Conakry) to demand his return and against the high cost of living.
On 5 April 2023, drivers of NJMC, a Chinese mining company, occupied the headquarters of their company to denounce their poor working conditions in Koundianakoro (Kondianakoro, Mandiana, Kankan).

Looting: On 12 October 2024, the military came from Kankan looted shops, stole goods and destroyed houses in Konkoye (Dialakoro, Mandiana, Kankan) after intervening in a violent demonstration against a Chinese mining company.

On 12 October 2024, for the second day, a group demonstrated in Konkoye (Dialakoro, Mandiana, Kankan) to demand the departure of a Chinese mining company that was using illegal machinery to extract gold, which was damaging the environment. They threw stones and clashed with the military (came from Kankan), who used tear gas and live ammunition. Over the two days, two people died (one shot, the other suffocated from the tear gas), four were injured and around forty were arrested. Fatalities split over two days, coded as 1.

On 11 October 2024, residents protested in Konkoye (Mandiana, Kankan) against the environmental degradation caused by a Chinese mining company's illegal gold mining activities. Police fired live ammunition at the protesters and utilized tear gas to disperse the crowd. One protester was shot and injured.

On 12 March 2025, workers employed by the Chinese company Henan Chine demonstrated along the Dalabani-Kankan road they are building, location coded to the admin center Kankan (Kankan-Centre, Kankan) to denounce the difficult working conditions, low wages and unequal treatment of the employees.

On 13 September 2024, residents and employees of a Chinese mining company blocked the road and destroyed Chinese-owned shops, taking away motorbikes and other items, in Soumbouyadi [Sombouya] (Tamita, Boffa, Boke) as they demonstrated to demand a pay rise and better working conditions from the company that employs them. Law enforcement (police and gendarmerie) dispersed them with tear gas and gunfire.

On 6 July 2023, in Georgetown, Demerara-Mahaica, scores of women from the Red Thread NGO held a protest with banners against the US ExxonMobil oil company and to demand that Guyana be protected against the perils of an oil spill. The protest was held on the occasion of a visit made by the US Secretary of State to Guyana.

On 6 September 2023, in Georgetown, Demerara-Mahaica, members of the Red Thread Women Organization held a protest outside the office of the President, at Vlissigen Road, against the US ExxonMobil oil company and to demand the protection of Guyana's environment and warn about the perils of an oil spill.

On 13 September 2023, in Providence, Demerara-Mahaica, citizens and members of the Red Thread Women Organization held a protest outside the National Stadium against the US ExxonMobil oil company and to demand the protection of Guyana's environment and warn about the perils of an oil spill, among other claims. The protest was held on the occasion of the opening game of the Guyana leg of the Caribbean Premier League.

On 4 October 2023, in Georgetown, Demerara-Mahaica, for the second consecutive day, almost 40 citizens held a protest with banners outside the office of the President, at Vlissigen Road, demanding the US ExxonMobil oil company to surrender oil blocks. Protesters asked for the 20 percent of the Stabroek Block, that is to say 120 oil blocks.

On 27 October 2023, in Georgetown, Demerara-Mahaica, over 100 Guyanese citizens held a protest in front of the President's office, on Vlissengen Road, demanding the US ExxonMobil oil company to surrender oil blocks. Protesters asked for the 20 percent of the Stabroek Block, that is to say 120 oil blocks.

On 26 March 2024, in Georgetown, Demerara-Mahaica, civil society activists held a protest outside the Arthur Chung Conference Centre (ACCC), in Liliendaal neighbourhood, to decry a visit by former US President, Bil Clinton, to Guyana. The protest was attended by members of the Red Thread and the Haiti Support Group (Guyana). Protesters claimed to opposed Clinton's role in destabilizing Haiti, among other issues.

On 5 December 2024, in San Pedro Sula, Cortes, two unidentified armed men on a motorcycle shot and killed a security guard at a Chinese restaurant on Boulevard Las Torres in the Satelite neighborhood (drive-by). The reason for the killing is unknown. 1 fatality.

On 29 January 2018, hundreds of Hondurans and Americans citizens protested in front of the US embassy in Tegucigalpa against the recognition of Juan Orlando Hernandez as new president by the US government.
On 14 May 2018, a group of people led by the former president Manuel Zelaya protested in front of the American Embassy in Tegucigalpa against the suspension of the Temporary Protection Status.

On 14 October 2021, in Roatan, Bay Islands, two unidentified armed men shot and killed an American citizen who was the manager of Infinity Bay Spa and Beach Resort - one of the most popular hotels of the area. The reason for the killing is unknown. 1 fatality.

On 22 March 2019, in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, people staged a vigil like demonstration in front of the U.S. embassy to demand the release of political prisoners and to put an end to the exploitation of natural resources and mining in the country.
Unknown gunmen shoot and kill two Chinese fishers.

On 20 October 2019, two African-American members of the US Air Force were attacked and beaten in Zadar, Croatia. The two men were attacked by a group of Croatian men after dancing, which made certain patrons of the club suspect they were gay.

On 16 December 2024, in Petion Ville - Vivy Mitchell, Ouest, unidentified armed men dressed in police uniforms and traveling in two vehicles, including a police vehicles, opened fire on a car transporting a Haitian/American man who had served as a liaison for American military contractors hired by the government to fight against gangs, and his friend. The man was abducted from the vehicle, while his friend was shot and injured but survived the attack. The abducted victim is the cousin of a police officer who had also worked with the military contractors and who had disappeared three days prior following an attack by unidentified armed men (coded separately). The whereabouts of the victim are unknown, although he was presumed dead. 1 injured.
On 20 December 2020, in Dame-Marie, Grand'Anse, several heavily armed men on horseback rode into the property of an US man and kidnapped his child at gunpoint. The child was released two days later.

On 20 January 2021, in Port-au-Prince - Tabarre, Ouest, protesters attempted to gather in front of the US embassy (Chateau Blond neighborhood) to demand that the Haitian President steps down. The protesters were appealing to US President Biden to break with outgoing US President Trump's support for the Moise administration. Only a small group of protesters managed to actually get to the embassy as police officers dispersed the protest with tear gas.

On 27 October 2019, in Cap-Haitien, Nord, there was a demonstration to demand the resignation of the president of Haiti. During the demonstration, an American flag was burned to protest against American interference.

On 22 January 2018, in Port-au-Prince - Tabarre, Ouest, thousands of people marched to the US Embassy (Chateau Blond neighborhood) after President Donald Trump called Haiti a 'Shithole country'. Security measures were implemented to protect the embassy from the protesters.

On 27 August 2021, in Croix-des-Bouquets, Ouest, unidentified armed men kidnapped a security manager of a company in front of his residence. The victim is a former US Army soldier. Perpetrators have demanded the payment of a ransom, and the victim's whereabouts are unknown.

On 26 September 2021, in Port-au-Prince - Tabarre, Ouest, people staged a protest to demonstrate against the President Biden's immigration policies in front of the U.S. Embassy (Chateau Blond neighborhood).

Around 6 November 2021 (between 6 - 7 October), in Croix-des-Bouquets, Ouest, members of the 400 Mawozo Gang shot and killed a family, killing a child and injuring an adult and another child in the attack. The dead child had the citizenship of the US, though it was not reported if the father was also an american citizen. Motivations of the attack are unknown. 1 fatality.

On 13 December 2022, in Jeremie, Grande-Anse, a few hundred residents held a demonstration against the presence of the hospital ship USNS Comfort from the US as part of their medical assistance mission in the port of the city. Demonstrators shouted anti-US and pro-Russian slogans. Reason for the demonstration were rumors about the ship being in the port to facilitate the extraction of mineral resources. According to other reports, the demonstrators called for a US military intervention instead of medical assistance. A local source described the action as a popular riot, although no destructive behavior was reported.
On 05 January 2020 in Croix-des-Bouquets, a US citizen was rescued by the police from a presumed kidnapping by two individuals who carried military badges and firearms. The two were arrested.

On 18 March 2023, in Port-au-Prince, Ouest, gang members kidnapped three American citizens of Haitian descent, a man, a woman, and another relative, during a bus ride in Martissant. Kidnappers forced them to get out of the vehicle and took them away. The gangsters demanded a ransom of 6,000 dollars as a condition for their liberation. However, after the ransom was paid, the perpetrators asked for additional 400,000 dollars and did not release the victims. The victims were liberated on 13 April, after a second ransom was paid.

On 7 October 2022, in Tabarre, Ouest, members of the Kraze Barye Gang (a.k.a. Vitelhomme Gang) attacked a couple of Haitian-American citizens at their house in Tabarre 68, shooting and killing her and kidnapping him. The man was released on 28 October, after a ransom of 300,000 USD was paid by the family to kidnappers. 1 fatality.

On 27 July 2023, in Port-au-Prince - Cite Soleil, Ouest, a group of armed men kidnapped a US woman nurse and her girl at the campus of the 'Roi Haiti Outreach International' organization. The woman was working as a missionary for this Christian humanitarian organization when the abduction took place. The kidnappers asked for a ransom of 1 million dollars as a conditions for the victims' release. The victims were released on August 9.

On 4 January 2021, in Port-au-Prince - Centre Ville, Ouest, unidentified armed men kidnapped a US citizen in Pavee Street when he was on his way to a hotel. There no information on the perpetrators, although latest reports suggest that most abductions are gang-related. The whereabouts of the victim are unknown.
On 15 February 2019, in the arrondissement of Port-au-Prince, Ouest, people took the streets to protest the US policy towards the crisis and asking the help of Vladimir Putin.

On 11 March 2021, in Port-au-Prince - Tabarre, Ouest, rioters burned tires in front of the Embassy of the United States of America (Chateau Blond neighborhood) to demonstrate against the US and the international community's support to the Government of Haiti.

On 6 November 2023, in Terrier Rouge, Nord-Est, residents and clients held a demonstration to decry the management of the National Rural Electric Cooperative Association (NRECA) US power entity. Demonstrators set up barricades of burning tires in front of the company's office and blocked the National Road 6 as they demanded the company to review its electricity distribution schedule after having changed it due to a fuel crisis.

On 18 November 2019, in Saint-Marc, Artibonite, people and government opponents held a march to demand the resignation of President Jovenel Moise. Rioters burned tires and an US flag to decry the US interference in Haiti. The demonstration was held on the occasion of the commemoration of the Vertieres Battle, and amidst a set of nationwide anti-government demonstrations.

On 28 July 2023, in Port-au-Prince - Petionville, Ouest, people took to the streets in commemoration of the U.S. occupation in Haiti. The march started at Carrefour de l'Aeroport, continued through Christ-Roi, towards Delmas where the demonstrators erected barricades (unspecified). Reports indicated the demonstrators had become violent (unspecified) in Delmas 75. The demonstration eneded in Petionville and it is unclear who intervened to disperse the demonstrators.
Around 15 June 2021 (month of), in Croix-des-Bouquets, Ouest, the 400 Mawozo Gang kidnapped two US citizens. They were released after the payment of a 25,000 dollars ransom.
Around 15 August 2023 (month of), in Croix-des-Bouquets, Ouest, the 400 Mawozo Gang kidnapped a US woman citizen. She was released after the payment of a 50,000 dollars ransom.

On 23 May 2024, in Bon Repos, Ouest, overnight, members of the Living Together gang-led initiative (a.k.a. Viv Ansanm Gang) moving in three trucks ambushed three Evangelical missionaries (a US woman, a US man, and a Haitian man) who were travelling in a vehicle with their children. The attack happened moments after the victims had left a church in the Lizon neighbourhood, in La Plaine du Cul-de-Sac area. The gang members beat up the US man and forced him to drive them to his home, where the three missionaries were killed. The property was looted and the corpse of the US missionary was found tied up and partially burned. Another version stated that the Haitian man, who was the local head of the missionary group they belonged to, was directly killed after being recognized for his work. The three used to work at the Bon Espoir orphanage. The US citizens were the daughter and son-in-law of a local politician from Missouri (US). The bodies were retrieved through the mediation of the Kraze Barye Gang (Vitelhomme Gang), which was said not to be involved in the attack. A suspect was arrested in August 2024. More than 100 gang members were thought to have participated in the attack. A person was arrested as a suspect in this case on 22 August 2024. 3 fatalities.

The clash marked the first fatal clash between both countries at the disputed border since 1975. 10 Indian soldiers held in custody were later released by the Chinese army on 18 June 2020. While it has been widely reported that between 40-45 Chinese soldiers were killed or wounded the Chinese side stated on 19 February 2021 that three Chinese soldiers were killed in combat while another was killed while crossing a river in an attempt to rescue them.
