On 11 November 2023, an unknown militant drone targeted US forces at the Harir Air Base in Erbil. Casualties unknown.
On 15 November 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched rockets targeting US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 5 November 2023, unknown militants targeted US forces with Mortar projectiles at the Ain Assad Air Base, Anbar. Casualties unknown.

On 20 November 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched ballistic missiles targeting US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Two explosions were heard at the base. Air defenses failed to intercept the incoming rockets. The attack injured 10, but there were no fatalities.
On 19 November 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq claimed to have launched a drone targeting US forces at the Harir airport in Erbil. Casualties unknown.

On 22 November 2023, the Islamic Resistance in Iraq targeted US forces with a suicide drones and rockets at the Harir Air Base in Erbil. An unknown number of US personnel were injured, but there were no fatalities.
On 23 November 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq suicide drones targeted US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 23 November 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq suicide drones targeted US forces at the Harir Air Base in Erbil. Casualties unknown.
On 26 November 2023, unknown militants launched suicide drone targeting US forces at the Harir Air Base in Erbil. The attack resulted in a fire breaking out with unknown damages. Casualties unknown.
On 3 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched a suicide drone targeting US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 3 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched a suicide drone targeting US forces at the Erbil International Airport. Casualties unknown.
On 6 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq targeted US forces with suicide drones and rockets at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 6 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq targeted US forces with a suicide drone at the Harir Air Base in Erbil. Casualties unknown.
On 8 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq militants targeted US forces with suicide drones in Harir airport, Erbil. Casualties unknown.

On 7 December 2023, unknown militants including those with 'links' to unspecified Iraqi security forces targeted the US embassy with 7 mortars or 14 rockets in the Green Zone of Baghdad - Karkh. Only material damages occurred. The strikes originated from near Abu Nawas street in Karadah. The US accused pro-Iran militias of conducting the attack. An unknown number of attackers were arrested the following week.
On 30 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq targeted US forces with an unspecified number of suicide drones at the Harir Air Base in Erbil. Casualties unknown.
On 2 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq militants launched a suicide drone targeting US forces in the Harir air base, Erbil. Casualties unknown.
On 5 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq militants targeted US forces with suicide drones at the Harir Air Base, Erbil. Casualties unknown.
On 2 January 2024, unknown militants targeted US forces with rockets at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.

On 8 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq militants targeted with two drones and two rockets US forces in the Ain Assad Air Base in Al Anbar. The attack resulted in material damage. Casualties unknown.
On 11 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq suicide drones targeted US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 15 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq suicide drones targeted US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 25 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched a suicide drone targeting US forces at the Harir air base in Erbil. The attack injured 3 US soldiers. There were no fatalities.
On 27 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq targeted US forces with a suicide drone at the Harir air base in Erbil. Casualties unknown.

On 20 December 2023, Islamic Resistance in Iraq targeted US force at the Ain Assad Air Base with a 122mm rocket in Al Anbar. There were no casualties or damages. Iraqi forces inspected the origin of the strike and discovered a truck modified to launch rockets. 4 out of 5 rockets had failed to launch.
On 7 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq targeted US forces with suicide drones at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 9 January 2024, unknown militants launched rockets targeting US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 14 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq militants targeted US forces with drones and rockets in Harir Air Base, Erbil. Casualties unknown.
On 24 January 2024, unknown militants launched suicide drones targeting US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 25 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched suicide drones targeting US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 26 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq militants launched a suicide drone targeting US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 24 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched suicide drones targeting US forces at the Harir air base in Erbil. Casualties unknown.

On 20 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched 10 missiles targeting US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. The attack resulted in 1 Iraqi army and 2 soldiers of the US forces injured. There were no fatalities.
On 22 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched rockets targeting US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 27 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq militants launched a suicide drone targeting US forces at the Ain Assad Air Base in Anbar. Casualties unknown.
On 28 January 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched a suicide drone targeting US forces at the Erbil International Airport. Casualties unknown. Other sources denied the event.
On 3 February 2024, Islamic Resistance in Iraq militants targeted US forces with drones and rockets in Harir Air Base, Erbil. Casualties unknown.

On 8 February 2024, protesters gathered in the Mashtal neighborhood of Baghdad - 9 Nissan. The protest took place at the location of the 7 February US drone strike. The protesters denounced the strike.

On 5 June 2023, workers went on strike and protested in the Bazrakan Oilfield in Maysan. The protesters are contracted by the Chinese Sinopec oil company and stated their overall numbers is more than 600. The protesters accused the company of violating their work contracts resulting in a waste of public money and loss of workers rights. The protesters added they have been complaining about the issue for months without results.

On 2 May 2024, students from Baghdad and Al-Nahrain universities protested in Jadriyah complex in Baghdad - Karadah in solidarity with the Palestinian people and to denounce 'the crimes of the Israeli aggression' in the context of the latest round of violence in Israel-Palestine. They also denounced the arrests of pro-Palestine students demonstrating in US and other Western universities.

On 20 May 2024, unknown perpetrators threw a grenade and Molotov cocktail at the home of a teacher in Al Shumukh area in the center of Nassriya city (Thi Qar), causing material damage to the house and the car of the victim. The teacher holds American citizenship. There were no casualties.

On 14 June 2024, dozens of protesters from Arab, Kurdish, and Turkman tribes, including An Nuaim tribe, protested in central Kirkuk City to call for boycotting brands that support the U.S. and Israel and in solidarity with the Palestinian people in the context of the latest rounds of violence in Israel - Palestine.

On 21 April 2024, rioters damaged the vehicles of the Chinese oil company and clashed with the police forces by throwing stones in Ghazela area of Al Musharrah district (Maysan) as a part of demonstration demanding for services and job opportunities.

On 4 June 2024, rioters demonstrated in front of the Pepsi Company headquarters in Uwayrij city (Baghdad), shouting pro-Palestinian, anti-US and anti-Israeli slogans and trying to storm the headquarters. On the same day, an unknown group of people attempted to storm Cannon dairy factory, accusing the company of supporting Israel. The Iraqi military (17th Division, 59th Brigade) arrested 7 of them and seized a vehicle belonging to the government forces. Another unknown group stormed the building of Al Marmouqa Trading Company believed to be an US company in Uwayrij Industrial Zone in Uwayrij city (Baghdad), destroying surveillance cameras. There were no casualties.

On 5 August 2024, the Islamic Resistance in Iraq - Revolutionaries targeted Ain Assad Air Base with two Katyusha-type rockets. The rockets were launched from a white Kia vehicle in the industrial area of Al Haqlaniyah city in Haditha district (Al Anbar governorate) - the car was later seized by the Iraqi security forces. It carried 8 other missiles which had not been launched. 5 American soldiers and 2 American contractors were injured (including one seriously injured). Security restrictions were imposed in the Haditha district for one day and in Ain Assad Air Base the alert was raised to the highest level. 5 people accused of targeting the base were arrested on 7 August 2024 and then released on 13 August 2024 after their tribe (Al Jughaifi) put pressure and threatened the local government. There were no fatalities.

On 10 September 2024, unknown militants launched two Katyusha-type rockets at a logistical facility (Diplomatic Support Center) belonging to the US embassy and an Iraqi base (of the Counter-Terrorism Service) in Victoria Camp at the International Airport in Baghdad (coded as Baghdad International Airport). One of the rockets landed near the logistical facility and the other one at the base, causing material damage to the buildings. No group has claimed the responsibility for the attack which took place the day before the visit of the Iranian president to Iraq, however Kataib Hezbollah distanced itself from the event. A high-level investigation committee was formed to find out who was behind the attack. There were no casualties.

On 30 September 2024, unknown militants fired at least three Katyusha rockets at the US Diplomatic Support Complex near the Victoria Base and Baghdad International Airport (coded as Baghdad International Airport, Baghdad). One of the rockets fell on the garage for the officers of the 2nd Regiment of the Counter-Terrorism Service, the other one fell in an empty yard inside the airport (near the civilian runway) and the third one near the Victoria base. Missile defense system of the base where Global Coalition forces were present was activated and it managed to intercept two missiles. The situation led to a temporary suspension of some flights from the airport. The rockets were launched from a Kia truck in Asriyah village in the area of Al Amiriyya (Baghdad) where seurity forces found other rockets that had not been launched. The Prime Minister ordered an investigation to determine the reasons for the security breach in the area from which the rockets had been launched. The commander of the force responsible for the security in the area of Al Amiriyya was arrested for negligence. No party claimed responsibility for the attack. 4 civilian vehicles were burnt. There were no casualties.

On 30 September 2024, unknown militants launched four Katyusha rockets at Victoria Base, which hosts global coalition forces (U.S.), at Baghdad International Airport (coded as Baghdad International Airport). Two rockets struck the vicinity of the base, with one landing in a storehouse used by the Iraqi Counter-Terrorism Service, causing material damage and a fire in nearby vehicles. The other rocket landed in an abandoned area of the airport. This incident coincides with heightened tensions related to the ongoing conflict in Lebanon and Palestine. No casualties were reported.

On 16 October 2024, unknown gunmen affiliates with Al Sawaed Tribal Militia (Bayt Mania) opened fire with pistols and AK-47s on an armored vehicle with two Chinese engineers in Al Msharah district of Maysan governorate (coded as Amara city, Maysan). The engineers were working for a Chinese company Maysan Oil Engineers and they were on their way back from the company's headquarters in the area of Bazrakan Oilfield (Maysan). The gunmen asked them for bribes and opened fire after refusal. The gunmen fled the scene. The engineers filed a complaint and 14 members of Bayt Mania family were arrested by the Iraqi army. There were no casualties, only material damage.

On 15 November 2024, Friday worshippers staged an impromptu protest in an unspecified location in Kufa city (Al Najaf) in solidarity with the Palestinian and Lebanese peoples, condemning Israeli atrocities in both countries, which they claim are supported by Western powers. Protesters burned the flags of the United States, the United Kingdom, and Israel, accusing these countries of supporting terrorism, massacres, and the killing of children, journalists, and hospital bombings.

Protesters took to Tahrir Square in Baghdad to express their rejection of the air strikes that took place in Syria by the US, France and the UK, in response to calls from leading Muqtada al-Sadr. The protesters held Syrian and Iraqi flags, and allegedly US flags were burned during protests, on Apr 15.

On 17 January 2016, unidentified gunmen wearing military uniforms kidnapped three Americans in the Doura district of Baghdad (Al Rashid). Some sources suggest that the unidentified gunmen were part of an Iranian-backed Shia militia but this is not confirmed. According to Iraqi News, Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi expressed doubt that the three Americans were kidnapped and denied allegations that Iran played a role in the incident.

properties.actor: Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL)
properties.notes: On 19 March 2016, an American coalition service member was killed in an indirect fire attack by Islamic State militants at the Makhmur base. 8 other American soldiers were injured in the attack.

On 12 December 2023, people gathered in front of the US embassy in Reykjavik to oppose the US foreign policy in relation to the Hamas-Israel conflict and the Israeli Defence Forces' offensive in Gaza. The activists showed their support and solidarity with the people of Palestine and condemned what they called the 'genocide' and 'occupation' of Palestine.

On 3 June 2020, between 3,500 and 5,000 people gathered for a Black Lives Matter protest by the Austurvollur parliament square in Reykjavik, showing solidarity to demonstrations in the US against police violence.

On 18 May 2021, around 60 people demonstrated during the visit of US Secretary of State Anthony Blinken in Reykjavik to show support and solidarity with Palestinians amidst escalating tensions in the Middle East between Israel and Palestine.
On 15 May 2024, people demonstrated outside of the US Embassy in Reykjavik to show support and solidarity with Palestine amid Israeli offensive in Gaza.

On 5 October 2024, people demonstrated in front of the US embassy in Reykjavik, calling on the US authorities to step up their efforts to achieve a permanent ceasefire in Gaza and stop escalation in the Middle East. During the demonstration, the embassy building was splashed with red paint. There was a minor scuffle between the demonstrators and the police, but no arrests were made. The demonstration was organized by the Iceland-Palestine Association.

On 8 February 2025, people demonstrated outside of the US Embassy in Reykjavik to protest the US government's policies regarding minority groups, including transgender people and refugees. They also condemned Donald Trump's plans for forced deportations from Gaza. The event was attended by transgender rights activists and members of No Borders Iceland movement.
On 28 January 2020, dozens of Palestinian citizens of Israel protested in Haifa city, against the US 'deal of the century' for Israel and Palestine.

On 7 December 2017, dozens of Palestinian citizens of Israel protested in Et Taiyiba city, against the US administration's recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel and moving their embassy to the city.

On 22 December 2017, hundreds of Palestinian citizens of Israel protested in Jadeidi Makr village, against the US administration's recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel and moving their embassy to the city.

On 25 June 2019, dozens of Palestinian citizens of Israel protested in Umm el Fahm city, against the 'deal of the century' announced recently by the US government. The protesters claimed it will be the end of the independent Palestinian state. The protest was organized by the National Democratic Assembly Party.

On 10 June 2024, unknown gunmen opened fire on a female engineer and her driver while they were driving a pickup truck near the gas plant in Jisr Diyala city (southeast of Baghdad city). The engineer worked for the Chinese petroleum company. Both victims were seriously injured and transferred to a hospital. 2 injured. There were no fatalities.
As reported on April 4 2019, Israeli citizens demonstrated outside the home of Education Minister Naftali Bennett in Ra'anana against the US plan which will be unveiled after Israeli elections.

On 27 October 2021, activists of Im Tirtzu organization demonstrated in Jerusalem (Jerusalem, Jerusalem) against the U.S.' decision to reopen its shattered consulate in Jerusalem for Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip. The consulate, which constitutes a de-facto U.S embassy to Palestine, was closed by the former U.S. administration, and the protestors alleged that the intention to reopen it is a violation of Israel's sovereignty.

On 12 May 2018, hundreds of left-wing Israel activists, including both Jews and Arabs, protested in Jerusalem (Judean Mountains) against the planned relocation of the US embassy to Jerusalem. Among the organizers of the protest were several organizations, including Standing Together, CFP: Combatants for Peace, Committee of Slain Palestinians' Families, and the Peace Now Movement. A Meretz MK was present at the protest.

Around 2 July 2019, around 60 demonstrators of Arab and Israeli ethnicity waved Palestinian flags and demonstrated in solidarity with Palestine outside the US Embassy in Tel Aviv. The demonstration was sponsored by Hadash.

Dozens of protesters held a rally in Jerusalem's Independence Park on Monday night, across the street from the US consulate, todemonstrateagainst US President Donald Trump during his visit toIsraelthis week.

On 4 August 2021, protestors demonstrated outside of the inauguration ceremony of an overseas campus of the Chinese University UIBE in Petah Tikva (HaMerkaz, Petah Tiqwa). The protestors renounced the establishment of the campus, a first of a kind in Israel, citing China's human rights record as the reason behind it.

On 2 May 2023, Palestinian armed groups fired rockets toward localities in southern Israel, causing sirens to sound in Niram, Erez, Ibbim, Sderot (Ashqelon, HaDarom), and other nearby towns. Between 2 to 3 May, 104 rockets were fired from Gaza toward southern Israel. At least two direct hits were reported in Sderot on 2 May, one hitting a factory and one hitting a residential area, causing damage to a vehicle. As a result of the direct hit on the factory, three workers, including a Chinese national, were injured. The Chinese worker was injured moderately and the other two were lightly injured. About nine other people required hospitalization, either due to anxiety attacks or injuries sustained while running to bomb shelters. Both the PIJ and Hamas claimed responsibility for the rocket fire, stating that it was in response to the death of a hunger-striking PIJ prisoner.

On 2 June 2020, 200 people, including Ethiopian Israelis, protested in front of the US embassy against the killing of George Floyd, the protesters called the name of Solomon Teka, a young Ethiopian Israeli who was shot and killed by police last year.

On 8 June 2020, about 200 people protested in front of the US embassy in Jerusalem, the protest was against racism in general and against the killing of unarmed civilians by police in the US and Israel, the protesters also held signs that say 'black lives matter' and 'Jewish silence is violence'.
500 demonstrators outside of the US Embassy in Tel Aviv on Saturday night. The demonstration, organized by Pantsuit NationIsrael,was part of anti-Trump marches and demonstrations across the world.
On Sunday, around 40 American and Israeli protesters gathered at Paris Square to oppose President Trump's travel ban, citing history of Jewish refugees.

Some 40 demonstrators gathered in front of the US Embassy in Tel Aviv on Sunday evening to protest President Trump's decision to put a four-month hold on refuge-seekers entering the United States and a temporary ban on travellers from Syria and six other predominantly Muslim countries.

On 23 March 2018, Israelis, Americans and Internationals gathered outside the US Embassy in Tel Aviv city on Friday afternoon to demand gun control and a ban on assault weapons in coordination with the March for Our Lives protests occurring across the United States. Among the speakers and attendees were alumni of Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, the school where the mass shooting took place that sparked the March for Our Lives protests.

On 20 March 2024, dozens of mothers of soldiers protested outside of the US embassy in Jerusalem (Judean Mountains), calling on the Biden administration to stop putting pressure on Israel, stating that US pressure is preventing Israel from defeating Hamas.

On 10 April 2024, a group of mothers of soldiers protested outside of the American consulate in Jerusalem (Judean Mountains), calling on the Biden administration to stop pressuring Israel. Protesters accused the Biden administration of hindering Israel in its efforts to fully defeat Hamas.
On 19 April 2024, dozens protested outside of the branch office of the US embassy in Tel Aviv city, demanding the US stop arming Israel and calling for an end to the war in Gaza.

On 30 April 2024, dozens protested outside of the American consulate in Tel Aviv city, calling on the US to stop putting pressure on Israel to limit military action in Gaza. Protesters called for increased military pressure on Hamas.

On 15 May 2024, dozens protested outside of the US embassy in Tel Aviv city, calling on the US government to stop pressuring Israel about its military operation in Rafah. Protesters argued that US pressure is preventing Israel from returning the hostages and eliminating Hamas.

On 12 December 2024, hundreds protested outside of the US embassy in Tel Aviv city during US National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan's visit, calling for an immediate hostage deal and a ceasefire in Gaza.

On 20 January 2025, about 20 left-wing protesters rallied outside of the US embassy branch office in Tel Aviv (Tel Aviv, Tel Aviv), protesting the inauguration of US president Donald Trump and the Israeli war in Gaza. Protesters accused Trump of enabling genocide in Gaza. MK Ofer Cassif (Hadash) spoke at the protest.

On 31 January 2025, activists from the Shift 101 women movement held a silent protest outside of the US embassy in Tel Aviv city, calling for the full implementation of the ceasefire and hostage release deal, so that all remaining hostages are released from Gaza.

On 8 February 2025, at least 2500 people, organized by the High Follow-Up Committee, demonstrated in Umm el Fahm (Hadera; Haifa), to protest against crime and violence in Arab society as well as Trump's plan to displace Palestinians from Gaza and Israel's military operations in West Bank refugee camps. Protesters raised signs accusing the Israeli police of being complicit in crime in Arab society.

On 8 March 2016, a young American citizen visiting Israel was attacked by a Palestinian in Jaffa with a knife. The American civilian was killed and 10 others, including a pregnant woman, were wounded. The attacker was killed on the scene by police.
On 6 May 2017, protests against US President Trump took place outside the US consulate in Jerusalem by Arab citizens of Israel.

On 10 September 2021, former workers of the Whirlpool Neapolitan plant, supported by the FIOM CGIL, FIM CISL and UILM (UIL) trade union branches, marched from their factory in Argine street to the Bausan gate of the port of Napoli (Napoli, Campania), briefly blocking truck transit. They protested against the US multinational company's confirmation of the liquidation of their factory, which was shut down on 1 November 2020, and call on authorities to review the decision.

On 11 September 2021, PRC activists gathered outside the US Consulate in Florence (Firenze, Toscana) to protest against the twenty years of war that followed 9/11 and demand the liberation of Julian Assange. They also asked Europe and Italy to open their borders to Afghan refugees.

On 16 September 2021, workers of the Whirlpool Neapolitan plant marched, alongside RSU, FIOM CGIL, UILM (UIL) and FIM CISL union representatives, from Termini station to the Ministry of Economic Development, where they set up a picket, in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the US multinational company's confirmation of the liquidation of their factory, which was shut down on 1 November 2020, and call on authorities to review the decision and the layoffs entailed.

On 7 August 2021, a few hundred No MUOS activists gathered by the US Naval Radio Transmitter Facility (NRTF) in Niscemi (Caltanissetta, Sicilia) to protest against the risks allegedly posed by the facility and denounce its military purpose.

On 23 September 2021, around 200 former workers of the Whirlpool Neapolitan plant, supported by the FIOM CGIL, FIM CISL and UILM (UIL) trade union branches, marched from Termini Central Station to the Ministry of Economic Development in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the US multinational company's confirmation of the liquidation of their factory, which was shut down on 1 November 2020, and call on authorities to review the decision.

On 15 October 2021, in the morning, former workers of the Whirlpool Neapolitan plant, supported by the FIOM CGIL, FIM CISL and UILM (UIL) trade union branches, gathered outside the Directional Center of the Palace of Justice of Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the US multinational company's confirmation of the liquidation of their factory, which was shut down on 1 November 2020, and call on authorities to review their appeal to the expiry of the collective dismissal procedure on 15 October 2021.

On 14 October 2021, around 200 former workers of the Whirlpool Neapolitan plant, supported by the FIOM CGIL trade union branch, gathered in a march to the Ministry of Economic Development in Rome - City Center (Roma, Lazio) to protest against the US multinational company's confirmation of the liquidation of their factory, which was shut down on 1 November 2020, and call on authorities to review the decision before the expiry of the collective dismissal procedure on 15 October 2021.

On 22 October 2021, in the morning, former workers of the Whirlpool Neapolitan plant, supported by the FIOM CGIL, FIM CISL and UILM (UIL) trade union branches, gathered, playing drums, outside the Directional Center of the Palace of Justice of Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the US multinational company's confirmation of the liquidation of their factory, which was shut down on 1 November 2020, and call on authorities to review their appeal to the expiry of the collective dismissal procedure.

On 26 October 2021, the Deputy Minister for Economic Development visited and brought the government's support to former workers of the Whirlpool Neapolitan plant, supported by union branches including FIOM CGIL and RSU, on a permanent picket at the company's factory in Napoli (Napoli, Campania). They were protesting against the US multinational company's confirmation of the liquidation of their factory, which was shut down on 1 November 2020, and calling on authorities to review their appeal to the expiry of the collective dismissal procedure.

On 29 November 2021, Tim workers gathered in Catanzaro at the call of CGIL, CISL, and UIL to protest against the uncertainty of their jobs after the possibility that the company will be bought by an American fund.

On 14 March 2020, an new Indian immigrant was attacked by unknown rioters in the town of Tiberias (Kinneret, HaZafon). Rioters assumed he was of Chinese nationality and blamed him for the coronavirus. He was then hospitalized with severe chest injuries.

Around 23 April 2022 (as reported), over 200 people, mainly far-left activists, gathered outside the Camp Darby US military base near Coltano (Pisa, Toscana) to protest against the 'militarization of the area'.

On 10 May 2022, at the call of the 'Peace and Disarmament Committee' ('Comitato Pace e Disarmo'), people, including a Catholic priest, gathered outside the town hall in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the anchoring of the US Truman nuclear-powered aircraft in the bay of Napoli, claiming it infringes the 'denuclearized status' of the city.

On 6 July 2022, the Provincial Unitary Women's Coordination organized a demonstration in front of the Prefecture in Pisa (Pisa, Toscana) following the US Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, abolishing the right to choose to have an abortion in the country. CISL and UIL delegates took part in the protest.

On 29 June 2022, numerous activists, at the call of Sos aborto Napoli, took to the streets in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to protest against the decision of the U.S. Supreme Court that denies the right to abortion and in favor of the improvement of the Law 194 in Italy.

On 7 August 2022, 300 No MUOS activists gathered in Niscemi (Caltanissetta, Sicilia) to demand the dismantling of three local antennas of the US navy's satellite transmission system. Police officers in riot gear and DIGOS officers quelled the protest with water cannons and allegedly with tear gas containing CS gas. .

On 9 September 2022, UP organized a flash mob outside the Camp Darby US military base in Coltano (Pisa, Toscana), denouncing the 'militarization of the area'. PaP, Changing Course and PRC took part in the demonstration.

On 28 May 2020, 190 dismissed workers of an American manufacturing services company staged a protest outside their plant in Marcianise (Caserta, Campania). Media reported that they have been protesting for almost a week.
On 29 May 2020, a group of people gathered (maintaining social distancing) in front of the US Embassy in Rome - City Center to protest against the death of an African-American during a police stop.

On 19 April 2022, workers at a Chinese factory in Campi Bisenzio (Firenze, Toscana), went on strike and staged a demonstration outside the factory to protest against the fact that they were fired with a WhatsApp message for having refused to work on Easter Monday. Protesters asked for 8-hour shifts and two days off per week. The COBAS took part in the demonstration. The owner of the factory physically attacked one of the demonstrators.

On 29 June 2023, at the call of CISL and UIL, about 500 Italian employees of US military bases went on strike and took to the streets of Vicenza (Veneto, Vicenza) to protest against the cut of personnel in service in Vicenza and for the stalling of the negotiations for the renewal of the national collective agreement for military base personnel.

On 29 June 2023, at the call of CISL and UIL, about 80 Italian employees of the US military base in Pisa (Toscana, Pisa) staged a picket to protest against the cut in personnel in service in Vicenza and the stalling of the negotiations for the renewal of the national collective agreement of military base personnel.

On 4 June 2020, the Italian Radicals staged a protest outside the Chinese Consulate in Milano - Municipio 8 (Milano, Lombardia) against the Chinese repressive behavior towards Hong Kong. The protest was organized on the occasion of the anniversary of the events of Tiananmen Square, which occurred in 1989.

On 11 November 2023, thousand of participants, including members of self-managed social centers, committees and young people staged a protest in the Chiaia seafront area in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to demand the immediate halt of violence against Palestinian people and peace in Gaza. Some protesters staged a flash mob to represent the killed civilians and held a Palestinian flag. Demonstrators wanted to head towards the American consulate in Repubblica square, but standing officers in riot gear standing on Gramsci street preventing them from doing so. They projected with lasers 'Assassins #FreePalestine Stop Genocide Stop Bombing Gaza' on the American consulate.

On 16 December 2023, more than 500 people, including students and workers, took to the streets from Santa Maria Novella to Ognissanti Square in Florence (Toscana) to ask for an immediate ceasefire. Protesters screamed slogans such as 'Free Palestine' and 'Gaza will win', against the Israeli ministry Netanyahu and the United States. Protesters stopped in front of the American Consulate in Florence as a protest.

On 31 December 2023, at the call of the association 'Firenze per la Palestina', about 50 pro-Palestine activists staged a picket and showed banners on Ponte Vecchio in Florence (Toscana) to protest against the conflict in Gaza and demand peace and freedom for Palestine. Protesters also criticized the Israeli and US governments.

On 20 January 2024, more than 2,000 people, including pro-Palestinian activists, took to the streets of Vicenza (Veneto) to demand peace and freedom in Gaza. Protesters criticized the Israeli government, accused of indiscriminately killing Palestinian civilians, the Italian government, NATO, and the US administration.

On 21 February 2024, at the call of the 'Free Assange Committee Naples' (Comitato Assange Libero Napoli), people demonstrated in Napoli (Campania) against the extradition of WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange to the US and in favor of freedom of information. People also exposed Palestinian flags, demanding freedom for Palestine. Members of several associations, including Article 21, AI, FFF, UdS, and Unemployed '7 November', were present.

On 24 February 2024, about 1,500 people, including pro-Palestine activists, representatives of CUB, members of the Palestinian community in Italy, and representatives of 'Young Palestinians of Italy' (Giovani Plestinesi d'Italia), took to the streets of Milano - Municipio 2 (Lombardia), from Loreto Square to Carioli Square, to demonstrate in support of Palestine and demand the end of the massacre of civilians in Gaza. In Repubblica Square, masked rioters tried to reach the US Consulate and threw eggs and cherry bombs at the police. A clash ensued, and the police pushed the rioters back. Moreover, in Princess Clotilde Square, rioters damaged the window of a supermarket and threw stones at the police, injuring an officer and damaging two cars. Rioters also exposed banners against the Israeli and Italian governments, Palestinian flags, and photos of Matteo Salvini, Giorgia Meloni, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and others covered in blood-like red paint.

On 2 March 2024, about 1,500 people marched through the city and gathered in Duca d'Aosta Square in Milano - Municipio 2 (Lombardia) to demand peace and freedom for Palestine and criticized the Israeli, Italian, and US governments.

On 29 June 2023, animal rights activists and members of META took to the streets of Napoli (Campania, Napoli) to protest against the dog meat festival, held from 21 to 30 June in Yulin, China. Demonstrators also protested against violence against animals and demanded the festival be canceled.

On 17 April 2024, approximately 500 people, including pro-Palestine activists from all over the world, including US and German citizens, and members of the 'ANGA: Art Not Genocide Alliance', demonstrated outside the Israel and United States Pavillions at the Biennial of Art in Venezia (Veneto) to protest against the massacre of Palestinian civilians and the Israeli government. In the afternoon, ANGA activists also displayed pro-Palestine banners on the Rialto Bridge.

On 13 May 2024, students pitched tents in the courtyard of the Polytechnic and in front of the entrance to the humanities faculties of Palazzo Nuovo in Torino (Piemonte) in support of Palestine. This event is part of broader demonstrations following the occupation of US universities in support of Palestine.

On 20 March 2024, at the call of Cooperative Honey (Miele in Cooperativa), more than 150 beekeepers from the Marche region staged a protest in Santi Apostoli Square in Roma - City Center (Lazio) against the unfair competition of non-EU honey, in particular Chinese honey, which, according to protesters, was not compliant with European quality and food safety standards. Several representatives of the Agriculture Commission of the Chamber of Deputies, members of PD, Lega, and representatives of consumer protection associations were present.

On 29 May 2024, as part of a national 'No Fake Italy' campaign and at the call of Coldiretti, farmers staged a demonstration at the port of Bari (Puglia)to protest against the arrival in the port of a ship with 40 containers containing tomatoes from China and against the marketing of counterfeit products.

On 2 June 2024, at the call of Young Palestinians, COBAS, and cultural association CRAC: Center for Contemporary Art and Research' (CRAC: Centro Ricerca Arte Contemporanea), people, including students, workers, and pro-Palestine activists, marched from San Marco Square to the seat of the US Consulate in Firenze (Toscana) to demonstrate against the killing of Palestinian people, the Israeli government, police repression, and the Italian government as well as the US administration. Some demonstrators dropped bricks, symbolizing the rubble in Palestine, and a bloody US flag on the ground. The demonstrators pushed forward until they reached the barriers set up in front of the consulate and threw smoke bombs at the building but the police in anti-riot gear charged them and pushed them back.

On 4 August 2024, No MUOS activists marched towards the US Navy base in Niscemi (Sicilia) to demonstrate against wars, including the Palestinian one. During the march, activists cut the networks of the military base, opening gaps of several meters along the perimeter of the base. According to rioters, the police fired tear gas canisters at eye level and used CS gas. The police and Digos tried to stop some activists, but failed, according to the report.

On 4 August 2024, a large group of No Mous activists took to the streets of Niscemi (Sicilia) and gathered outside a US military base to demonstrate against the presence of the US geo-satellite defense system (MUOS) on Italian soil and against US military occupation. Demonstrators also demanded freedom and peace for Palestine. Activists reached the MUOS station and cut the fence surrounding the base. The police intervened, using tear gas against the demonstrators.

On 5 October 2024, about 7,000 people, including students, pro-Palestine activists, members of the Palestinian community, representatives of PaP, OSA, USB, and CGIL, and members of the association 'Democratic Arab-Palestinian Union' (Unione Democratica Arabo-Palestinese), demonstrated in Roma - Ostiense (Lazio) against the Israeli government, the war in Gaza, the killing of Palestinian and Lebanese civilians, and the Italian and US governments. The demonstration, which was not authorized, started as a peaceful picket. However, a group of people gathered a few meters from the police blockade and began throwing bottles, cherry bombs, stones, and traffic signs at the police. The police pushed back, using tear gas and water cannons against the demonstrators. 30 people were injured, including demonstrators and police officers.

On 22 May 2020, Fiom CGIL, Fim CISL and Uilm (UIL) delegates gathered with dismissed workers of an American manufacturing services company in a spontaneous protest outside the workers' plant in Marcianise (Caserta, Campania).

On 5 November 2024, more than 300 people, including pro-Palestine activists, took to the streets of Vicenza (Veneto) to protest against the Israeli, US, and Italian governments and the killing of Palestinian people. When the march reached the San Pio X prison, several prisoners acted in solidarity with the demonstrators by making noise with their frying pans and setting fire to paper bags. At the end of the march, demonstrators threw firecrackers in the general direction of the Camp Ederle US military base. Representatives of the self-managed social center 'Bocciodromo', members of 'Women's Network for Palestine' (Rete Donne per la Palestina), members of the Palestinian community in Italy, and Palestinian citizens participated in the protest.

On 19 November 2024, construction workers protesting three months of unpaid wages climbed onto six cranes at the Villaggio della Pace housing complex construction site within the US military base in Vicenza (Veneto). The workers, who claimed their wages had been withheld since August 2024, ended their demonstration voluntarily after negotiations resulted in an agreement to settle the outstanding payments.
On 7 February 2025, Gurit workers staged a picket outside the factory gates in Torino (Piemonte) to protest against the management's decision to relocate production to China and fire 56 workers.

On 8 February 2025, about 700 people, including pro-Palestine activists, took to the streets in Milano (Lombardia) to protest against the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian civilians. Protesters also criticized US President Trump and his administration's stance on the war in Gaza. Students, representatives of self-managed social centers, Palestinian citizens, and members of the Palestinian community in Italy participated in the demonstration.

On 22 February 2025, people, including members of the Ukrainian community, gathered in Piacenza (Emilia-Romagna) in solidarity with Ukraine. Protesters also criticized US President Donald Trump. Representatives of the association 'Nadiya Odv' participated in the demonstration. The event was held to mark the third anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the ongoing war that followed.

On 1 March 2025, at the call of the Italy-Ukraine Maidan association, people gathered in front of the United States Consulate in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to express solidarity with Ukraine, emphasize the importance of European unity and democratic values and demand the immediate accession of Ukraine to the European Union.

On 29 May 2024, as part of a national 'No Fake Italy' campaign and at the call of Coldiretti, around 150 farmers with around 6 inflatable boats staged a demonstration at the port of Salerno (Campania) to protest against the arrival in the port of a ship with 40 containers containing tomatoes from China and against the marketing of counterfeit products.

On 3 July 2020, employees of an American multinational manufacturer and marketer of home appliances staged a protest and blocked a high-way entrance in Napoli (Napoli, Company). Protesters demonstrated against the likely closure of their plant on 31 October 2020.

On 9 July 2020, employees of an American multinational manufacturer and marketer of home appliances demonstrated in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to oppose the closure of their plant located in Ponticelli.

On 17 July 2020, employees of an American multinational manufacturer and marketer of home appliances staged a protest outside the prefecture in Ancona (Ancona, Marche). Protesters demonstrated against the company's failure to honor an agreement on the industrial plan, the destiny of the plant located in Napoli, and unclarity about the workers' future.

On 17 July 2020, hundreds of employees of an American multinational manufacturer and marketer of home appliances, together with trade unions' representatives, demonstrated in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to oppose the closure of their plant, scheduled for 31 October 2020.

On 25 January 2020, people gathered outside the US Embassy in Rome - City Center to demand freedom and Justice for an Italian national detained in the United States for murder. Protesters claimed that he was innocent.

On 23 July 2020, around 500 employees of an American multinational manufacturer and marketer of home appliances, together with Cisl Fim, Cgil Fiom, and UIl Uilm, staged a protest outside the US Consulate in Napoli (Napoli, Campania). Protesters asked the company to backtrack on its decision to shut down its branch in Napoli, to respect an agreement signed in 2018, and to ensure a future to its Italian branches.
On 2 July 2020, right-wing party Lega made a flash-mob in solidarity with Hong-Kong outside the Chinese embassy in Rome - Parioli (Roma, Lazio). The party's leader was present too.

On 26 August 2020, five protesters (as seen from a picture), including a Hong Kong pro-democracy activist, staged a protest outside Italy's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, located in Rome - Tor di Quinto (Roma, Lazio), on the occasion of a meeting between the Italian and Chinese Foreign Ministers. Protesters demonstrated against China and stood in support of Hong Kong.

On 7 September 2020, around twenty people gathered with banners in front of the US Embassy in Rome - City Center to protest against the possible extradition of the WikiLeaks founder and to demand his release. Our Voice, Amnesty International, and Article 21 participated in the demonstration.

On 13 October 2020, people gathered in Rome - City Center to demand the liberation of an Italian man arrested for murder in the US in 2000. They claim the man is innocent. The leader of Lega participated in the demonstration.

On 3 September 2020, in the morning, employees of a plant for agricultural machinery manufacturing staged a protest in Migliarina (Modena, Emilia-Romagna). On 18 September 2020, employees of a plant for agricultural machinery manufacturing staged a protest in Migliarina (Modena, Emilia-Romagna). Their company was taken over by a Chinese multinational company in 2019, and now it is at risk of closure.

As the information on the event mostly came from a fellow Chinese colleague of the victim, an investigation was launched by public authorities to obtain further information.

On 1 February 2020, several youngsters physically assaulted an Italian citizen of Filipino descent in the Pilotta district of Parma, in a reported act of anti-Chinese violence. The perpetrators reportedly assaulted the man verbally, accusing him of bringing coronavirus to Italy, before beating him. A clash reportedly ensued with the friends of the victim who were present, although no injuries were reported.

Combination of two related events. On 1 November 2024, hundreds of protesters marched after Friday prayer at Al Hashimi mosque in Irbid (Qasabat Irbid, Irbid) to condemn the role of the United States in the continued Israeli offensive on Gaza.

On 28 May 2019, hundreds of Jordanians demonstrated outside the American Embassy in Amman against the 'Deal of the century'.

Hundreds of Jordanian demonstrators denounced Trump's recognition of Jerusalem as the Israeli capital, some torched the US flag and pictures of President Donald Trump, during a protest Thursday near the American embassy in Abdoun.

On 24 November 2023, around 10 activists from Fridays For Future demonstrated in Sendai, Miyagi, to oppose consumerism and an American e-commerce company's fuel consumption and working practices.

On 4 December 2023, about 300 people, including members of the All Okinawa Council, a member of the House of Representatives from the JCP, and plaintiffs of the third Futenma 'detonating sound' lawsuit, protested in front of the Okinawa Defense Bureau in Kadena, Okinawa, in response to the U.S. Air Force Osprey crash off Yakushima Island. On 12 August 2020, 100-about 200 protesters from Stand With Hong Kong Tokyo Executive Committee Seeking A Response From The Japanese Government For Freedom And Democracy In Hong Kong gathered in front of the Diet building in Chiyoda, Tokyo, to oppose the arrest by Chinese police of a prominent Hong Kong democracy activist and a the head of a large media firm in Hong Kong that is often critical of Beijing; demanding that the Japanese government respond to these actions, and appealing for freedom and democracy to be maintained in Hong Kong. The protest was part of the Stand With Hong Kong movement, and students, teachers, the Five Demands Movement, and Hong Kong citizens participated.

On 12 August 2020, protesters gathered in Sapporo, Hokkaido, to oppose the arrest by Chinese police of a prominent Hong Kong democracy activist and a the head of a large media firm in Hong Kong that is often critical of Beijing; demanding that the Japanese government respond to these actions, and appealing for freedom and democracy to be maintained in Hong Kong. The protest was part of the Stand With Hong Kong movement.
On 17 August 2020, people protested at Motobu port in Motobu, Okinawa, against the ongoing construction of the U.S. military base in Henoko, Okinawa, demanding withdrawal of the construction.

On 12 August 2020, protesters gathered in Osaka city, Osaka, to oppose the arrest by Chinese police of a prominent Hong Kong democracy activist and a the head of a large media firm in Hong Kong that is often critical of Beijing; demanding that the Japanese government respond to these actions, and appealing for freedom and democracy to be maintained in Hong Kong. The protest was part of the Stand With Hong Kong movement.

On 15 March 2019, over 150 people protested in front of the Okinawa Defense Bureau, Nakagami District, Kadena, against the Bureau's director statement regarding the noise coming from Kadena US military base. The director declared that the effect of noise in not scientifically proven to be harmful to humans. The protesters demanded that the director withdraw his statement, apologize and resign.

On 27 August 2020, people protested in front of The House of Representatives 2nd building in Chiyoda, Tokyo, against several issues including the FTA - Trade Agreement between Japan and the United States of America, 5G, and the Plant Variety Protection and Seed Act. The protest was organized by Reject Neoliberalism! Civilian Federation.

On 13 August 2020, about 5 protesters from Niigata Volunteer Citizens That Consider Human Rights Issues In Hong Kong gathered in front of the Chinese consulate in Niigata city, Niigata, to oppose the arrest by Chinese police of a prominent Hong Kong democracy activist and a the head of a large media firm in Hong Kong that is often critical of Beijing; demanding that the Japanese government respond to these actions, and appealing for freedom and democracy to be maintained in Hong Kong. The protest was part of the Stand With Hong Kong movement.

On 19 August 2020, about 20 people protested in front of the Consulate-General of China in Fukuoka city, Fukuoka, against Chinese public vessels and fishing vessels around the Senkaku Islands where Japan and China have a territorial dispute, claiming the Islands belong to Japan. The protest was organized by Protect the Senkaku Islands! Kyushu Executive Committee.

On 29 August 2020, Uyghurs protested at Shinjuku station in Tokyo - Shinjuku, against the Chinese government over occupation of East Turkistan and the oppression of East Turkistan people and Uyghur people, demanding independence for East Turkistan. The protest was organized by East Turkistan People's Association.

On 19 March 2019, around 80-90 people protested at US Tokorozawa Transmitter Site, Tokorozawa, Saitama Prefecture, against the ongoing construction. The protest was organized by the Tokorozawa Liaison Committee that Protects the Life of the Citizens from Ospreys. The protesters displayed placards asking the authorities not to let polluted soil and sediments to be carried there.

On 5 September 2020, some 15 to 20 ethnic Mongolian people living in Japan protested in front of the Chinese embassy in Tokyo - Minato, against the Chinese government's new policy to use the Mandarin language in schools instead of the Mongol language in Inner Mongolia.

On 12 September 2020, about 100 Mongolian people living in Japan and ethnic Mongolian people from China protested in front of the Chinese embassy in Osaka city, Osaka, against the Chinese government's new policy to use the Mandarin language in schools instead of the Mongol language in Inner Mongolia. The protesters demanded rights for education in their own mother language.

On 3 October 2020, about 350 to nearly 3,000 people protested and marched around 3 areas including Tokyo - Shibuya and Tokyo - Chiyoda, against the Chinese government's oppression of minority ethnic groups such as Uyghur, Tibetan, Taiwanese, and Mongolian groups in Inner Mongolia, and oppression of people in Hong Kong, claiming the Chinese government is violating human rights. Reportedly about 600 Uyghurs, over 2,000 Hong Kongers, and over 600 Tibetans and ethnic Mongolians joined the protest, as well as supporters from Japan and other Asian nations. The protest was organized by about 20 groups in Japan which support human rights in China. The protest was held in reaction to China's recent policies including abolition of Mongolian language education in Inner Mongolia and oppression of the democratization movement in Hong Kong. Southern Mongolia Congress joined the protest.

On 31 October 2020, about 150 protesters gathered in Kanoya, Kagoshima, against the use of the Osprey military aircraft during Japan-U.S. joint military training in JMSDF Kanoya Air Base, claiming it could lead Kanoya Air Base to become a U.S. military base. The protest was organized by 5 groups including Local's Association against Having the U.S. Military in Kanoya.

On 14 June 2020, protesters marched through Chiyoda, Bunkyo and Taito districts of Tokyo, to voice discontent over the spread of the coronavirus and the perceived role of China and Chinese people in spreading the virus.

On 11 October 2020, about 120 people from Inner Mongolia living in Japan, members of the 'Executive Committee for Protecting the Mother Tongue of the Mongolian People', marched through Nagoya, Aichi, in opposition to the new language policies enforced upon the ethnic Mongolian population by the Chinese government in the Inner Mongolia province of China, describing it as cultural genocide. Besides ethnic Mongolians living in Japan, protesters from Hong Kong and Tibet also participated, and an ethnic Mongolian exchange student from China gave a speech.

On 3 June 2018, approximately 250 people gathered in Kyotango (Kyoto, Kansai) to participate in a protest march demanding the closure of the US Military Kyogamisaki Communications Site. This event was organized by Kinki Association Against US Military X-Band Radar Base and co-sponsored by Ukawa Volunteers Concerned with the Construction of US Military Bases. In attendance were members of Anti-War Committee of 1000, Japan Confederation of Rail Workers' Unions, Tajima Union, Kansai United Movement, AWC: Asian-Wide Campaign, Solidarity Labor Union and Tajima Union.

On 31 July 2018, about 40 people protested in front of the American Naval Air Facility Atsugi in Ayase, Kanagawa, calling for an investigation into the crash of an American navy helicopter and prevention of future accidents. The protest was organized by members of four anti-military base groups in Kanagawa.

On 13 January 2019, over 40 citizens protested at Tsudanuma Station (Chiba) against the presence of the US forces in Japan. The protest was held in the context of a joint military training organized by Japan and US forces in Funabashi and Yachiyo on the same day. The protest was organized by No Patriot Missile! Narashino Base Action Committee.

On 13 January 2018, about 70 protesters gathered at the gate of US military base Camp Schwab to oppose the construction of Henoko airbase. This marks the 5018th day since the sit-in began in April 2004

On 4 April 2019, a group of people protested in front of the US forces training base from Higashi, Takae, Okinawa Prefecture, against the construction of a helipad at the base. The protesters were also disturbed by the fact that the US forces decided one day before to remove placards, tents, and chairs used during the protests.

On 6 May 2018, protesters gathered outside the Iwakuni US Military Base in Iwakuni (Yamaguchi, Chugoku) to protest against plans to increase the capacity and function of the base. Protesters distributed leaflets to members of the public who were visiting the base as part of an air show and 'friendship day' event. .

On 5 April 2018, protesters gathered in front of the North Dock in Yokohama, Kanagawa, to oppose the deployment of Osprey Military Aircraft to Yokota Airbase. About 50 protesters from the 'Kanagawa Prefecture Peace Committee' participated and called for the complete removal of all US military bases.

On 12 November 2020, people, including members of the Uyghur Ethnic minority, protested in front of the Chinese Embassy in Tokyo - Minato, against the Chinese government over the oppression of East Turkistan and the Uyghur people, including forced labor and internment camps. The protest was organized on 12 November which is the founding anniversary of East Turkistan. The protest was organized by Japan Uyghur Federation.

On 10 May 2018, people gathered outside Naha Regional Courthouse in Naha (Okinawa, Kyushu) to protest against noise pollution coming from the Futenma US Military Air Base. Protesters displayed banners reading 'Withdraw Ospreys!' and 'Let's protect our children, close Futenma Base'. This event was organised by the Group for Legal Action to Stop Noise Pollution for Futenma US Air Base. .

On 26 May 2018, approximately 10,000 people gathered around the House of Representative members' building in Chiyoda (Tokyo) to protest against the continued presence of the US Military in Okinawa, the construction of a new base in Henoko and the subsequent damage to local marine life. This event was organised by Anti-War Committee of 1000 and Don't Allow War! Don't Break Article 9! Total Action Executive Committee. In attendance were Zenroren and other labour groups, the JCP, SDPJ, Christian Peace Network, Women's Democratic Club, Association to Revitalise the Constitution, Saitama Peace Centre, Shinfujin, Zenrosai, Zenrorin, Shiminrengo: Civic Alliance for Peace and Constitutionalism, Article 9 Association. On the same day, 85 people gathered outside the official residence of the prime minister in Chiyoda (Tokyo) to protest against the government's decision to build JSDF bases on Miyako-jima, Ishigaki-jima and Yonaguni-jima in Okinawa..

On 29 April 2018, people gathered in Yonashiro in Uruma (Okinawa, Kyushu) to protest against planes from nearby US Military Bases from using the airspace above Uruma. Protesters held placards that read 'US military planes, don't fly!'. This event was organised by Residents Gathering for the Banning of US Military planes using Uruma airspace. In attendance was a senior member of the JCP. .

On 14 May 2018, people gathered near the US Embassy in Tokyo in Minato (Tokyo) to protest against the US government decision to relocate their embassy in Israel to Jerusalem and show support to the cause of Palestinians.

On 18 March 2018, protesters from 'Against US-ROK Joint Military Drills - 2.18 Emergency Action Executive Committee' gathered at Sendai station in Sendai, Miyagi, to oppose join military exercises between the US and ROK. The protest was organized by the Asian Joint Action (AWC) Metropolitan Area.

On 18 April 2019, an unknown number of protesters gathered in Aoyama Park in Minato District (Tokyo) to demand the removal of the Us Military's Azabu Heliport (also known as the Akasaka Press Center).

On 7 December 2018, about 50 demonstrators from Midorigaoka Nursery School gathered in front of Ueno station in Tokyo - Taito to call for the shutdown of Futenma Airbase, one year after US helicopter crash incident happened in the area of the Nursery School. The protest was organized by the Japan Peace Committee.

On 14 October 2018, 1800 people gathered in Verny Park in Yokosuka (Kanagawa, Kanto) to protest against plans for the stationing of a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier at the nearby US Naval Base. Protesters displayed placards that read 'we don't need a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier'. The event was organised by Tear Up The US-Japan Security Treaty Central Executive Committee, Council To Abolish The US-Japan Security Treaty and Unify Kanagawa, and Miura Peninsula Liaison Committee To Stop The Re-basing Of Nuclear Carriers; and in attendance were elected members of parliament belonging to the JCP and members of Zenkenren.

On 29 October 2018, protesters from US Military X-Band Radar Base Opposition - Kyoto Liaison Committee gathered in the Tango District of Kyotango city of Kyoto Prefecture, to oppose the joint US-Japan training held at United States Forces Japan Kyogamisaki Communications Site.
On 8 December 2018, around 50 demonstrators gathered in Kochi city to oppose the resumption of US military training in the area after a US military plane crashed near the coast of Cape Muroto.

On 14 January 2018, about 40 protesters from labour unions and the city council gathered on the shoreline opposite the US naval base to oppose the deployment of the US naval ship 'Wasp', which docked in Sasebo on the same day.

On 16 September 2018, over 130 people protested in Fussa, Tokyo, against the deployment of Osprey military aircraft in Japan and demanding withdrawal of the U.S. military from Yokota base. The protest was held near the Yokota U.S. military base where a Japan-America Friendship Festival was happening at the same time. Nishitama Association against Yokota Military Base, a member of the House of Councillors from JCP, Asia Africa Latin America Solidarity Committee, Shinfujin, and Tachikawa Labour Union were all present at the protest.

On 27 April 2019, a group of approximately 23 protesters gathered at the South bus terminal of Osaka train station in Osaka (Osaka, Kansai) to voice opposition to the presence of US military bases in Okinawa. This event was organized by Osaka Action that Doesn't Allow the Construction of Military Bases at Henoko.

On 11 October 2018, about 90 people held a sitting protest in Hiroshima city, Hiroshima, against the U.S. government over a recent subcritical nuclear experiment held in the U.S., demanding abolishment of all nuclear power experiments. The protest was organized by Abolish the Nuclear Power Plant Hiroshima Peace Liaison which consists of 12 groups such as victims of nuclear power. Hiroshima Confederation of A- and H-Bomb Sufferers Organizations joined the protest.

On 10 April 2018, protesters from US Military X-Band Radar Base Opposition - Kyoto Liaison Committee gathered in front of Misaki Communication Station in the Tango District of Kyotango, Kyoto, to oppose the 2nd phase of construction on the base.

On 21 September 2018, about 70 people protested in front of the first gate of the U.S. Kadena base in Chatan, Okinawa, against parachute training in the area and a case in which a man from the U.S. military broke into a house. They demanded U.S. withdrawal from military bases in Okinawa. The protest was organized by groups such as Third Plaintiff Corps for Prohibition of Explosion Sound Suit.

On 21 July 2018, people staged a protest in front of the American army base Camp Schwab in Kadena (Okinawa) against the construction of the fence outside the base which would prevent the future sit-in protests.

On 16 November 2018, 95 people gathered in front of the Kadena Airbase 1st gate in the Sunabe district of Chatan city of Okinawa Prefecture to protest the recent string of US military helicopter accidents and the excessive noise caused by overhead flights out of Kadena Airbase.

On 16 March 2018, about 70 protesters gathered in front of the Kadena Airbase 1st gate in the Sunabe district of Chatan, Okinawa, to protest the recent string of US military helicopter accidents and the excessive noise caused by overhead flights out of Kadena Airbase, appealing for the removal of the airbase.
On 24 June 2018, about 300 people held a protest meeting in Higashi (Okinawa) against the construction of helipads in a U.S. military training area near Takae.
On 20 July 2018, about 80 people staged a protest in front of the American army Kadena Air Base in Chatan (Okinawa) against the stationing mentioning the issues of notice and smell.

On 26 August 2018, people protested and marched in Yokosuka, Kanagawa, against the installation of Osprey military aircraft in Japan and demanded withdrawal of all U.S. military stationed in Japan. The protest was organized by 'Peace Move Yokosuka.'
On 24 March 2018, nearly 100 US citizens living in Japan held a rally in Shibuya, Tokyo, to support tougher gun control measures in the US.

On 23 November 2020, people held a standing protest in Fukuoka city, Fukuoka, against the Chinese government over several issues including the Chinese government's oppression of East Turkistan and Hong-Kong, and the planned visit of General Secretary Xi Jinping to Japan. The protest was organized by Demosisto Fukuoka.

On 11 December 2020, about 50 people protested with banners in Nishinoomote city of Tanegashima, Kagoshima, against an ocean survey in advance of bringing a U.S. military training exercise and associated facilities to Mageshima, Kagoshima. The protest was organized by a local residents' group called Citizens and Organization Liaison Against Bringing the U.S. Military Facilities to Kurogeshima.

On 10 December 2020, about 30 people protested in front of the U.S. camp Zama in Zama, Kanagawa, against the harsh working conditions at the base, demanding improvement of the work environment. The protest was organized by All Japan Garrison Forces Labor Union's Kanagawa district headquarters.

On 15 December 2020, about 10 people protested near JGSDF Somagahara Airbase in Shinto village, Gunma, against the use of the Osprey military aircraft during Japan-U.S. joint military training in the base. The protest was organized by Gunma Peace Committee.

On 1 July 2018, about 100 people, including people from the Uyghur Ethnic minority, protested in Tokyo - Shinjuku against the Chinese government over the detainment and oppression of Uyghur people in China. The protest was organized by Japan Uyghur Association.

On 1 January 2021, 6 people including local residents protested in front of the U.S. military Kyogamisaki Communications Site in Kyotango, Kyoto, demanding the withdrawal of the U.S. military base for safety concerns. They also claimed public visibility into the base's operations has been reduced lately and demanded disclosure of the base's activity. A member of Kyotango city council who is also a member of the Ukawa Volunteer Association Which Are Concerned of the U.S. Military Base Construction joined the protest.

On 13 January 2021, people protested at Tsudanuma station in Narashino, Chiba, against Japan-U.S. joint military training at JGSDF Narashino Training Field over safety concerns. The protesters were also against the deployment of Osprey military aircraft in Japan. The protest was organized by Mothers Against War at Chiba and Article 9 Association/Chiba Local Councilor Network.

On 18 January 2021, 35 people held a sit-in protest at Peace Memorial Park in Hiroshima city, Hiroshima, against the U.S. government for conducting a subcritical nuclear experiment last November. The protest was organized by Abolish the Nuclear Power Plant Hiroshima Peace Liaison Conference which consists of 12 groups including Hiroshima Confederation of A- and H-Bomb Sufferers Organizations.

On 19 January 2021, about 40 people held a sit-in protest in Nagasaki city, Nagasaki, against the U.S. government for conducting a subcritical nuclear experiment last November. Peace Action Centre and Gensuikin: Japan Congress against A- and H-Bombs attended the protest. The protesters also submitted a written protest to the U.S. embassy in Japan against the experiment.

On 4 February 2021, about 60 people protested in front of Atsugi Base in Ayase, Kanagawa, against planned U.S. military Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear training in the base for safety concerns, demanding the cancellation of the training. The protest was organized by 4 local resident groups including Atsugi Base Detonation Prevention Alliance.

Combination of two related events. On 25 November 2020, around 150 to 200 people including foreign people such as Chinese, Koreans, Americans, and Polish people, protested and marched from Hibiya Park in Tokyo-Chiyoda to Ginza in Tokyo-Chuo, against the result of the U.S. presidential election, claiming there was foul play in the election process and the current president Trump won the election. Protesters were also against the Chinese government; On 29 November 2020, 650 people protested and marched starting from Hibiya Park in Tokyo-Chiyoda, against the result of the U.S. presidential election, claiming there was foul play in the election process and the current president Trump won the election.
