The protesters consisted of volunteers and foreign people such as Chinese, Koreans, Americans, Poles, and foreign people who speak Chinese joined the protest.

On 17 May 2019, 30 protesters gathered outside the City Hall in Kyotango (Kyoto, Kansai) to participate in a demonstration criticising the conduct of the Vice-Mayor asserting that delay of the public announcement of a road traffic accident involving US army personnel stationed at the nearby Kyogamisaki Communications Site contradicts promises made to residents by the local government. This event was attended by Ukawa Volunteers Concerned about the Construction of American Bases. .

On 11 April 2021, 12 people gathered in Chatan, Okinawa, to oppose the sexual violence and alleged human rights violations caused by the U.S. military in Okinawa, mourning the 2 years anniversary of a woman's killing by a U.S. marine.

On 14 April 2021, about 20 people protested in Kofu, Yamanashi, against a U.S. Marines live-fire training exercise at Kitafuji maneuvering ground, demanding a halt to training and the withdrawal of the U.S. military from the maneuvering ground. The protest was organized by Kitafuji Joint Struggle Council.

On 10 March 2021, Tibetans living in Japan protested in front of the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Tokyo - Minato, against the Chinese government's oppression of Tibetans in the Tibet Autonomous Region. The protesters also submitted a statement against the oppression. The protest was held on the 62-year anniversary of Tibetan Uprising Day. People who used to live in Hong Kong and Inner Mongolia attended the protest.

On 4 May 2021, people protested in front of the U.S. military Yokosuka Base in Yokosuka, Kanagawa, against the moving of radioactive waste from nuclear carrier Ronald Reagan for maintenance, claiming removal of radioactive matter is against the agreement between Japan and the U.S. called the 'Aid Memoir.' The protest was organized by Yokosuka Peace Ships (anti-nuclear group) and it was held on the sea as well as on land.

On 7 March 2021, about 40 women from minority groups in China such as the Uyghur ethnic people and Mongolian ethnic people who now live in Japan, and people who used to live in Hong Kong, protested in front of United Nations University in Tokyo - Shibuya, against the Chinese government's oppression of minority groups including Uyghur people. The protesters also criticized new language policies enforced upon the ethnic Mongolian population by the Chinese government in the Inner Mongolia province of China and the oppression of protests in Hong Kong. The protest was held in advance of International Women's Day which is March 8th.

On 25 April 2021, about 60 people, including Uyghur people, Tibetan people, people from Inner Mongolia and Hong Kong, and Buddhist monks protested and marched in Nagano city, Nagano, against the Chinese government's oppression of minority groups including Uyghur people and citizens of Hong Kong, demanding the protection of human rights for those people. The protest was organized by 11 groups such as Super Sangha, Students for a Free Tibet, Japan Uyghur Association, Southern Mongolia Congress, the World Mongolian Federation, Tibetan Community in Japan, Stand with Hong Kong at Japan, Hong Kong Founding of the Country Federation, Federation for a Democratic China, Asian Solidarity Council for Freedom and Democracy, and Buddhist Association for Action for Peace.

On 8 May 2021, about 600 Uyghur people, Myanmar nationals, Tibetan people, and protesters from Hong Kong, Inner Mongolia, and Cambodia who are living in Japan, protested and marched starting from in front of the United Nations University in Tokyo - Shibuya, against the Chinese government's oppression of minority groups such as Uyghur people. The protesters also criticized the coup and the Burmese military's oppression of protesters in Myanmar and demanded protection of human rights across Asia. Zainichi Myanmar Citizens' Association and Japan Uyghur Association joined the protest.

On 19 May 2021, about 300 people from Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region and from Hong Kong, joined by Myanmar nationals protested in front of the National Diet in Tokyo - Chiyoda, against the Chinese government's oppression of minority groups such as Uyghur people. The protesters also criticized the coup and the Burmese military's oppression of protesters in Myanmar and demanded protection of human rights across Asia. Japan Uyghur Association and South Mongolia Congress joined the protest.

On 11 May 2021, activists from Japan, Tibet, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Hong Kong, Myanmar and Cambodia, the Southern Mongolian Cultural Association and an LDP lawmaker protested and marched in front of the Chinese embassy in Tokyo - Minato, to support southern Mongolians against the Chinese government. On the same day, 600 people gathered to rally in Tokyo, to celebrate World Southern Mongolians Day.

On 21 February 2021, protesters, including ethnic Mongolian people, gathered in front of the Chinese embassy in Tokyo - Minato, against the language policies enforced upon the ethnic Mongolian population by the Chinese government in the Inner Mongolia province of China, supporting peoples' rights to keep their mother tongue. Protesters also demanded the right for Inner Mongolians to self-govern and the release of Inner Mongolians currently detained by the Chinese government, calling for a boycott of the Beijing 2022 Olympics unless China stops its oppression of ethnic minorities. The protest was held on International Mother Language Day.

On 21 February 2021, protesters, including ethnic Mongolian people, gathered in front of the Chinese embassy in Osaka city, Osaka, against the language policies enforced upon the ethnic Mongolian population by the Chinese government in the Inner Mongolia province of China, supporting peoples' rights to keep their mother tongue. Protesters also demanded the right for Inner Mongolians to self-govern and the release of Inner Mongolians currently detained by the Chinese government, calling for a boycott of the Beijing 2022 Olympics unless China stops its oppression of ethnic minorities. The protest was held on International Mother Language Day.

On 15 May 2021, 5 people in a car protested in Ebino, Miyazaki, against the Japan-U.S.-France joint military training conducted in Ebino, claiming military forces do not promote peace and the training should not have been held considering the ongoing coronavirus pandemic. The protest was organized by West District Labor Union Council which consists of 7 local labor groups.

On 21 February 2021, protesters, including ethnic Mongolian people, gathered in front of the Chinese embassy in Nagoya, Aichi, against the language policies enforced upon the ethnic Mongolian population by the Chinese government in the Inner Mongolia province of China, supporting peoples' rights to keep their mother tongue. Protesters also demanded the right for Inner Mongolians to self-govern and the release of Inner Mongolians currently detained by the Chinese government, calling for a boycott of the Beijing 2022 Olympics unless China stops its oppression of ethnic minorities. The protest was held on International Mother Language Day.

On 5 June 2021, people protested in Uruma, Okinawa, against the U.S. military for a helicopter's emergency landing which occurred on 2 June, criticizing the Japanese government's insufficient investigation of the landing incident. The protesters opposed nigh time flying and aircraft operations over residential areas. The protesters also opposed a planned bill called the Important Land Research Regulation Bill which is regulating the buying and selling of land near important infrastructure for national security. They also demanded the withdrawal of U.S. military bases from Okinawa. The protest was organized by Shimagurumi Conference and lawmakers from JCP, CDP, and Okinawa's Wind joined the protest.

On 24 May 2019, 10 protesters belonging to the Go away Osprey, We Don't Need You Residents Group gathered outside the city hall in Kisarazu (Chiba, Kanto) to protest against the decision to allow the preliminary stationing of the Osprey US military aircraft in the area. Protesters commented that the Osprey had caused accidents all across Japan and they are worried about such accidents reoccurring. .

On 9 May 2021, about 30 Ethnic Mongolian people from China gathered in front of the Chinese embassy in Tokyo - Minato, against the Chinese government's oppression of Mongolian people in the Inner Mongolia province of China, including the language policies enforced upon the ethnic Mongolian in Inner Mongolia, supporting their right to keep their mother tongue.

On 27 June 2021, 100 people protested in Takashima, Shiga, against Japan-U.S. joint military training at the JASDF Aibano Sub Base due to safety concerns. The protest was organized by Peace Forum Kansai Block. Peace for Aibano 2021! Kinki Network joined the protest.

On 4 June 2021, about 50 people protested in Tokyo - Chiyoda, against the Chinese government, demanding further investigation of the 1989 Tiananmen Square Protests and apologies for the victims killed or injured during the protests. The protest was organized by an executive committee which consists of groups such as a Japan branch of the Federation for a Democratic China, which was established by people who fled from China after the Tiananmen Square protests. A rally was held in Tokyo by the protesters after the protest and it gathered about 200 people. People from Hong Kong and Uyghur people also gave speeches against human rights oppression by the Chinese government at the rally. Japan Uyghur Association joined the protest.

On 15 July 2021, people protested in front of Ojojihara Maneuvering Ground in Shikama, Miyagi, to oppose live ammunition training at the ground due to safety concerns. The protesters also opposed war in general and the Security Bills and demanded withdrawal of all U.S. military bases from Japan. A former member of Sendai city council from JCP and several labor groups which are affiliated with Zenroren joined the protest.

On 21 January 2019, around 70 people protested in front of Nishinoomote City Hall (Nishinoomote, Kagoshima Prefecture) against the relocation of the US Field Carrier Landing Practice (FCLP) to Mageshima. The protesters opposed the Ministry of Defense plan of relocation, showing their support for the mayor. The protest was organized by the Tanegashima Association Against War.
On 28 May 2019, On 28 May 2019, 35 A-bomb survivors of the Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings gathered in Nagasaki city to protest against US nuclear weapon tests conducted in February.

On 28 May 2019, members of Yokosuka Peace Fleet movement staged a protest on a boat near US Yokosuka Naval Military base in Yokosuka city (Kanagawa prefecture) condemning the visit of US President Donald Trump to the base and against presence of the base in the region.

On 4 September 2021, about 30 people including mothers protested in front of Ginowan city hall in Ginowan, Okinawa, against the U.S. Marines' release of treated contaminated water containing organic fluorine compounds such as PFOS into the sewer at Futenma U.S. military air base in Ginowan, Okinawa. Protesters cited health concerns with the release, claiming that PFAS is a known toxic chemical.

On 12 June 2021, about 250 Hong Kong citizens living in Japan and Japanese people protested and marched in Tokyo - Shinjuku, against the Chinese government's oppression of citizens in Hong Kong, demanding protection of human rights.

On 21 September 2021, about 70 people protested in Yakushima, Kagoshima, against a plan to bring a U.S. military training exercise and its associated facilities to Mageshima, Kagoshima. The protesters claimed that the U.S. military may not comply with their promises, such as those about restricted times and areas for aircraft use. A lawmaker and a member of SDPJ joined the protest.

On 1 July 2021, about 60-200 protesters including people from Hong Kong, Uyghur, Tibet, Inner Mongolia, and supporters gathered in Tokyo - Shinjuku, to oppose the Chinese government's oppression of minority groups and violation of their human rights, including language policies enforced upon ethnic Mongolians in Inner Mongolia and the Chinese government's oppression of Mongolian people living in Japan. The protesters claimed that the Chinese government threatened Mongolian people not to attend this demonstration. The protest was held on the day which marked the 100th anniversary of the foundation of the Communist Party of China. Asian Solidarity Council for Freedom and Democracy and Southern Mongolia Congress joined the protest. Simultaneously, a second group of people protested against holding the first event and ten people were arrested for interrupting the event. Three of these people were released shortly after the event and criminal charges were filed against the remaining seven people.

On 14 September 2021, 10 ethnic Mongolians gathered in front of the Chinese embassy in Nagoya, Aichi, against the Chinese government's language policies enforced upon the ethnic Mongolian in Inner Mongolia province of China, supporting their right to keep their mother tongue. The protests were held in 3 places in Japan on this day.

On 10 November 2021, 15 people protested in front of the Prime Minister's Office in Tokyo - Chiyoda, against deployment of the U.S. military's missiles and ammunition into Miyakojima, Okinawa. The protesters further demanded withdrawal from the U.S. military bases in Okinawa. The protest was organized by Shimajima Standing.

On 21 November 2021, people protested and marched around the U.S. Military Yokota Air Base in Fussa, Tokyo, against deployment of Osprey military aircraft due to safety concerns. The protest was organized by Osprey Opposition Tokyo Liaison Association. Tokyo Regional Council of Trade Unions and lawmakers from JCP joined the protest. The protest was broadcast online and over 1000 people (including the audience) participated.

Combination of a series of related events. Protest against China Mines for low salaries, poor working conditions
Protest against China Mines for low salaries, poor working conditions

Around 29 July 2024 (as reported), residents held a protest in Janzur (Al Jafarah, West) to express their rejection of the decision of the GNU Prime Minister to allocate to the US embassy a 20,000 square meter plot of land in a coastal area of the town.
Libya Islamist group Ansar al-Shariah holds protest against US kidnapping of Anas al-Libi
Protesters gathered outside the old Qaddafi katiba headquarters in the Birka area to express support to the army and police and anger at the Turkish, American and British response to violence.

More than 1,000 Chinese workers were forced to flee their encampment when it was stormed with gun wielding anti-regime demonstrators. Though there were no deaths reported in this instance, there are some reports that 62 had died in the city since Sunday.

A Chinese engineer was killed in Libya 's second largest city of Benghazi. The employee of a Chinese construction company was first abducted from a work site along with two of his colleagues and was later found shot.

There were two demonstrations on 13 September, in Tobruk as well as in Zintan against the condemnation by the US and five European states of the takeover of the eastern oil terminals by the Libyan National Army (LNA). Militia leaders are now threatening to re-close the coast road in protest.

Protesters demonstrated at Tripoli's martyrs square to denounce US president Trump's decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israels capital.
On 13 June 2018, locals in Bani Walid protested against the previous U.S. strike in Wadi Lebigla affirming that three of those killed were innocent civilians with no links to terrorism.
On 2 December 2018, residents in Ubari staged a protest against a U.S. airstrike that killed a group of Tuareg youths alleged to be AQIM militants.

On 11 September 2012, militants - angered over an amateur American-made film that mocked and insulted Islams Prophet Muhammad - shot at and set fire to the US consulate in Benghazi city, killing the US ambassador to Libya and 3 staff. 8 Libyans were injured.
Libyans protested at the U.S. Consulate in Benghazi against a film trailor denouncing the Prophet Muhammad
On 24 September 2018, a group of people gathered in the airport in Saint Lucia to support the families of a Saint-Lucian killed by the US police. Also, the protester demands justice for this case

On 25 May 2021, workers of a textile factory set tires on fire and blocked roads at the Thetsane and Ha Tsolo Industrial Areas, Maseru (Maseru) in a demonstration to demand a wage increase. At night, the group vandalized Chinese and Basotho-owned stores.
On 13 March 2023, taxi operators and street vendors staged a protest in Maseru (Maseru) against Chinese vendors operating in the area, accusing them of undermining their businesses.

Around 19 December 2023 (as reported), three NSS officers severely beat a Chinese Kopano Ke Matla worker in Mphorosane near Mpharane (Leribe) following a row over the repair of a property. The other workers were ordered to watch as they would beat him. He had to be hospitalized.

On 17 May 2021, protesters gathered in front of the Chinese embassy in Vilnius with Tibetan flags to denounce reported human rights abuses in Xinjiang, Tibet and Hong Kong, also calling upon the Lithuanian government and the European Union to take more action to counter these.

On 10 March 2020, around 20 protesters demonstrated outside the Chinese embassy in Vilnius to denounce Chinese presence in Tibet. The event was organized on the anniversary of the Tibetan national uprising in 1959.

On 17 May 2023, a group of people protested in front of the Chinese Embassy in Vilnius, Lithuania, calling against the constant violations of human rights in Tibet, Hong Kong and the Xinjiang region of China and drawing attention to the situation of political prisoners in China.

On 12 December 2024, six members of the Extinction Rebellion Lithuania protested near the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Vilnius, Lithuania, calling against China's construction of the East African Crude Oil Pipeline (EACOP).

On 10 March 2025, a group of people protested in front of the Chinese Embassy in Vilnius, Lithuania, calling against the Chinese government's actions in Tibet and the human rights violations that are taking place there.

On 5 June 2020, several hundreds of people staged a protest in front of the American embassy in Luxembourg against racism and police violence in the context of worldwide Black Lives Matter protests following the death of George Floyd in the hands of police officers in Minnesota, US.
On 8 March 2024, around a dozen people protested in front of the Chinese Embassy in Vilnius, Lithuania, calling against the human rights violations in Tibet.

On 28 June 2022, at the call of Planning familial and other feminist organizations, several hundred people staged a protest in front of the US embassy in Luxembourg to denounce the rollback of the federal right for abortion in the US.
On 17 May 2024, more than 10 people protested at the Chinese Embassy in Vilnius, Lithuania, calling against the human rights violations in Tibet.

Around 16 February 2022 (as reported), an unknown number of Amnesty International activists staged a protest outside the Chinese embassy in Luxembourg to raise awareness for a persecuted Chinese journalist in China.
On 11 August 2022, former employees at the US embassy held a protest sit-in in Nouakchott (Nouakchott, Nouakchott West) to denounce their dismissal and call the embassy offer them compensations.

On 11 October 2023, the Student Initiative Against Zionist Infiltration and for the Support of Just Causes demonstrated in front of the US embassy in Nouakchott (Tevragh-Zeina, Nouakchott) to denounce US support to Israel in its military operations in Gaza and express their support to Palestinian armed groups fight against Israel.

On 20 October 2024, at the call of the Student Initiative Against Zionist Infiltration and for the Support of Just Causes, hundreds of citizens staged a protest sit-in in front of the US embassy in Nouakchott (Tevragh-Zeinah, Nouakchott) to support of Palestine and Lebanon. They also denounced Israeli military operations in both countries and the US support to Israel.

On 17 November 2024, citizens staged a protest sit-in in front of the US embassy in Nouakchott (Tevragh-Zeinah, Nouakchott) in support of Palestine. They also called for an end to Israeli military operations in Gaza and denounced the position of Arab states in the conflict.

On 19 December 2024, the Student Initiative Against Zionist Infiltration and for the Support of Just Causes held a protest outside the U.S. Embassy in Nouakchott (Tevragh-Zeina, Tevragh-Zeina), demanding an end to Israeli military operations in Gaza. The protesters blamed the US for supporting the conflict through military aid to the Israeli occupation.

On 21 February 2025, the Student Initiative Against Zionist Infiltration held a protest at the University of Nouakchott (Tevragh-Zeina, Nouakchott), against a musical performance by an American band, rejecting what they called academic normalization with supporters of Israel. The protesters chanted slogans in support of Palestine and condemning cooperation with entities linked to Israel.

On 18 March 2025, the National Ribat To Support the Palestinian People held a protest in Nouadhibou (Dakhlet Nouadhibou, Dakhlet Nouadhibou), condemning the violation of the ceasefire in Gaza by Israel. Protesters denounced the airstrikes as a violation of the ceasefire and called for global solidarity against the actions of Israel and the United States.

On 18 March 2025, at the call of the Student Initiative Against Zionist Infiltration and for the Support of Just Causes, a number of protesters, including political leaders and parliament members gathered outside the US embassy in Nouakchott (Tevragh-Zeina, Nouakchott), to condemn Israel's violation of the cease fire in Gaza. The demonstrators held the US responsible for the escalation and urged the Mauritanian government to sever ties with countries supporting Israel.
RFD members protested in the capital at the US embassy, against statements attributed to the US Embassy in Nouakchott.
Protests at the American embassy lead to heightened security.

On 24 December 2021, the Mauritanian gendarmerie opened fire with live ammunition to disperse a sit-in held by residents in Bassikounou (Bassikounou, Hodh Ech Chargi) denouncing the drilling of a well on their lands by a Chinese road construction company. 17 people were arrested and one person was injured.
Hundreds of Mauritanians protested in the capital Nouakchott against US president Trump's decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israel's capital.
Dozens of workers of the Chinese fishing company Poly Hon Done demonstrated in Nouakchott after the company arbitrarily dismissed them. Protesters calledon the authorities to intervene.
On 26 November 2019, bloggers and activists protested in front of a Chinese company shouting anti-chinese slogans and demanding more rights. .
On 10 December 2019, residents of Nouadhibou held a protest against Chinese Company 'Hong Dong' who they accuse of stealing all of the fish.
On 30 January 2020, youth protested in front of the American embassy in Nouakchott (Ouest) against the 'deal of the century.'

properties.actor: AQIM: Al Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb

On 24 December 2019, bloggers and activists protested in Nouadhibou against the Chinese fishing company, Poly Hondong.
On 07 January 2020, workers who were laid off by the Chinese fishing company, Poly Hongdong, protested against the lack of action taken by local authorities.
On 22 September 2018, an American diplomat was assassinated in a suburb of Antananarivo by unknown assailants.

29 January. An unidentified armed group and police clash in Behoririka of Antananarivo Renivohitra following assaults on Chinese citizens. One from the unidentified armed group was arrested following the clash.

On 13 March 2021, locals demonstrated against exploitation by a Chinese mining company operating in the area by throwing rocks and damaging vehicles and machines of the Chinese mining site in Talata-Ambatofahavalo (Antananarivo Atsimondrano, Analamanga). Police arrested 24 people.

On 14 April 2022, a group of people, including the presumed winner of a raffle, and his relatives, threw stones against the kiosk of the organizer of the raffle - a Chinese national - after the organizer refused to deliver the prize to the winner in Manakara (Manakara Atsimo, Vatovavy Fitovinany) arguing that the man's ticket was fake. Gendarmerie officers intervened with tear gas and evacuated the Chinese man. One woman, her baby, and 3 gendarmerie were injured.

On 2 December 2022, local residents took to the streets in Androka Ela (Androka, Ampanihy Ouest, Atsimo Andrefana) with placards, demanding the departure of the Chinese company MaproSud and calling the President for help. They accuse the company of land appropriation, destruction of coral reef and disrespect towards local customs. Androka mayor, Anselme Mahasambotse Tolojanahary, was part of the demonstration and he later declared cutting the company from its drinking water access.

On 6 March 2024, residents took to the streets with placards in Andohatapenaka, in Antananarivo - Arrondissement 1 (Antananarivo-Renivohitra, Analamanga) against the illegal land seizure by a Chinese citizen. They blocked the traffic by setting tires on fire, and police officers used tear gas to disperse the crowd. There were no casualties.

On 15 July 2024, residents took to the streets near Europe Boulevard in Ankazomanga Atsimo, in Antananarivo - Arrondissement 6 (Antananarivo-Renivohitra, Analamanga) against the illegal seizure of their 12 acres of land which was sold to a Chinese by an alleged owner. They feared the land will be fenced off and the 100 houses on it demolished.

Combination of two related events. Armed men attacked a Chinese business owner in Analamahitsy; Police chased & arrested 4 armed men in Andranobevava, suspected of attacking a Chinese business owner in Analamahitsy. 1 man escaped.
Striking SUCOMA employees attacked those attempting to continue working with stones and also damaged vehicles and property. 2 Chinese workers and a Malagasy woman were injured.

The people of Vohilava Mananjary took to the streets at the beginning of the week o protest the exploitation of a mining basin in their region. The mine is managed by a Chinese company, accused of polluting the water.
A peaceful demonstration took place in Soamahamanina as residents and the DFP handed an ultimatum over to authority over the withdrawal of Chinese workers.
In Soamahamanina, residents who were protesting against the exploitation of a Chinese firm engaged in running battles with security forces. In sum, one woman was injured and a protester arrested.

On 18 February 2022, dozens of members of the PSRM and PCRM parties, including at least four MPs, protested outside the government building in Chisinau - Buiucani against the selling of a land to the US Embassy.

On 29 May 2024, several Shor members protested in the City Gates area by blocking Dacia Boulevard in Chisinau - Botanica against the visit of the US Secretary of State Antony Blinken. The councilor of the leader (Bashkan) of Gagauzia and other representatives from Gagauzia were also present at the event. Since the protest went against the decision of the Chisinau City Hall and the requirements of the Police not to block the carriageway, some of the protesters were detained.

On 13 February 2025, several dozen supporters of the Sansa Party, linked to the illegal Shor Party, protested in front of the U.S. Embassy in Chisinau, in Chisinau - Centru. The demonstrators accused the U.S. and USAID of supporting the ruling PAS party, which they claim persecutes the opposition, and called for Donald Trump to intervene.

On 29 July 2021, PSRM and PCRM members, and one PSRM MP protested outside the Constitutional Court in Chisinau, demanding a decision cancelling an agreement on the concession of the lot of the Republican Stadium to the US Embassy in Moldova.

On 25 October 2024, youth groups held a protest walk named 'Ummah with Palestine' (Muslim protesters likely participated based on name of the protest) from the Social Centre to the Artificial Beach in Male City (Male City) against the war in Gaza, calling for the expulsion of the U.S. Embassy from the Maldives and to expedite the ban on Israeli passports and Israeli products. The walk ended with a lecture on the holy land of Palestine and the crimes committed by Israel in Palestine, and a boycott stall was set up to promote alternatives to Israeli products.

On 21 June 2022, protesters led by the University of Malawi Child Rights Legal Clinic marched to the Chinese Embassy in Lilongwe (Lilongwe City, Central) against a Chinese national accused of child abuse. Protesters demanded compensation and psychological assistance for children affected, the shutdown of Chinese websites with children's content, and the deportation of the accused to be sentenced in Malawi.
On 10 November 2020, unidentified individuals killed 2 Chinese shop owners and another person inside their shop in Karonga (Karonga, Northern). Motivation unknown.

On 23 November 2024, in Caborca, Sonora, suspected members of Grupo Delta Gang shot at two U.S. citizens who travelled in a vehicle. One of the men was injured and the other remained uninjured. One of the perpetrators was arrested around 29 May 2025. 1 injured.

On 1 February 2020, in Guadalajara, Jalisco, environmentalists from the organization Climate Save collective blocked the Macrobus lane to denounce contamination by a US meat company operating in Mexico. The protest was held in several states simultaneously.

On 8 February 2019 in Cordoba (State of Veracruz), armed attackers kidnapped a US male journalist alongside a Mexican woman who was later sexually abused by her kidnappers. The victims claimed that an organized crime group was behind the incidents. Additionally, other 12 people were allegedly kidnapped alongside the mentioned victims (10 women and 2 men). The two men were executed (tortured and burned to death), while the women were raped. 2 fatalities.

On 4 February 2020, members of a Maldivian group affiliated with the Islamic State stabbed and injured two Chinese and an Australian national in Male (Male City). One of the Chinese national was a tourist while the other two were employed in Maldives.

On 13 June 2020, in Tijuana, Baja California, about 50 people demonstrated in the Chaparral against racisms and police abuses. The protesters demanded justice for the death of two people, one African American and one Haitian, at the hands of police. The protest joined the worldwide protests against racism after the death of an African-American man in Minneapolis, USA, at the hands of the police.

On 8 July 2020, in Acapulco, Guerrero, Mexican who have returned from the United States protested outside this US consulate to demand temporary working permits for Mexicans who are working in the USA during the coronavirus pandemic.

On 8 July 2020, in Tijuana municipality, Baja California, Mexican and Central American migrants protested at the border between Tijuana and California state in the United States at the toll San Ysidro rejecting the meeting between the Mexican and the American Presidents and demanded the end of the criminalization of migrants.

On 17 July 2020, in Tecate municipality, Baja California, near the border, a group of about 40 Kumiai Indigenous people demonstrated simultaneously on the U.S. and Mexican sides to denounce that the construction of the border wall is profaning sacred soil that belongs to them.

On 2 August 2020, in Delicias, Chihuahua, a group of farmers from Chihuahua participated in a caravan of horses and hundreds of vehicles to show their opposition to the payment of a water debt to the US as part of a treaty signed with the United States in 1944.

On 30 August 2020, in Rosales, Chihuahua, around 100 farmers participated in a caravan to reject the extraction of water resources from Las Virgenes will. This takes place in the context of a bilateral water treaty between the US and Mexico, according to which the Mexican state is bound to pay its water debt to the US.

On 22 September 2020, in Cuauhtemoc area of Mexico City, a dozen people demonstrated in front of the UK and US embassies to demand the release of the founder of WikiLeaks accused of disseminating secret files and to call for his non-extradition.

Around 23 October 2020 (as reported), in Playas de Rosarito, Baja California, a man was killed and his burnt body was found. The victim is an U.S. firefighter who had been missing since August 2020. 1 fatality.

On 20 January 2018, in Cuauhtemoc, Ciudad de Mexico, at least 100 members of migrant's rights organizations protested in front of the United States Embassy against the president of the US and his policies. The protesters gathered at the Angel of Independence and marched to the Embassy.
On 18 February 2018, in Ciudad Juarez, Juarez, Chihuahua, two American citizens were abducted. Police rescued them alive on 24 February and arrested two of the kidnappers.

On 14 March 2018, in Tijuana (Baja California), around a hundred persons protested against the US President Trump plans to build a wall at the US-Mexico border. The protest took place amidst a visit from President Trump to the United States' part of the wall.

On 7 April 2018, in Ciudad de Mexico-Cuauhtemoc, Distrito Federal, hundreds of migrants from central america travelling towards the United States in the Viacruscis del Migrante caravan, staged a demonstration against Donald Trump and his administration.

On 30 April 2018, members of the organization Border Angels protested in Mexicali against the visit of the US vice-president in Calexico, USA. Protesters burnt a pinata representing Donald Trump and shouted slogans against the US migration policy.

On 10 May 2018, in Tijuana, Baja California, a group of activists from the collective Border Angels, demonstrated against U.S. President Donald Trump and American authorities over his immigration policies, and not granting asylum to Mexican and Central American migrants. .

On 28 May 2018, residents of district Miguel Hidalgo protested in Miguel Hidalgo, Ciudad de Mexico to demand a comprehensive security and road plans in Nuevo Polance before the construction of the new headquarters of the US embassy which may cause increase in the price of land in the area.

On 20 June 2018, a group of Mexican children, sons of migrant father from El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala as well as activists held a demonstration in front of the UNHCR office in Tapachula de Cordova y Ordonez against cruel and inhuman treatments and the policy of the US president against migrants.

On 13 July 2018, in Cuauhtemoc, Ciudad de Mexico, a group of people protest against Donald Trump's immigration policy outside the Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador transition house in Colonia Roma, where elected president received the US Secretary of State and other officials from that country.
On 28 October 2018, in Uribe municipality, Chihuahua, a US tourist reported missing was killed by a drug trafficker known as El Chueco in La Playita. Motive unknown. 1 fatality.

On 30 December 2020, in Cuautla, Morelos, a US citizen was kidnapped inside a grocery store by armed men in Colonia Ano de Juarez. The perpetrators asked for a ransom. He was later rescued by the police on January 13 in Colonia Ampliacion 13 de septiembre in Yautepec municipality. Three people were arrested.

On 20 March 2021, between Cancun and Puerto Morelos, Quintana Roo, a US citizen and another man were shot and killed while driving on the highway by two armed men on a motorcycle (drive-by shooting). 2 fatalities.

On 22 May 2021, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, a group of people demonstrated in front of the U.S. embassy to demand the end of the bombing of Palestinians in the Gaza Strip. The demonstrators painted a Palestinian flag and skulls with blood.

On 7 June 2021, in Tijuana, Baja California, on the occasion of the US Vice President's visit to Mexico, about 30 activists from migrant organizations demonstrated in front of the US Consulate to demand an end to mass deportations and the granting of documentation and asylum to eleven million migrants as promised by the U.S. President. The demonstrators also demanded the vaccination of migrants against the coronavirus as the shelters are full. The demonstrators burned an 'Uncle Sam' pinata to demonstrate against the racism of the American society.

On 20 July 2021, in Acapulco de Juarez, Guerrero, people protested outside the US government consulate to demand a stop to the US economical blockade against Cuba. The protesters argued that the blockage affects the health, arrival of food, and the development of the Cuban people.
On 26 July 2021, in Tijuana, Baja California, a US citizen was shot and injured by two armed men inside a motel.

On 23 July 2021, a group of people staged a protest in Male (Male City) in front of the Chinese Embassy calling for an end to violence against Uyghur Muslims in China and against China's debt on Maldives.

On 13 May 2019, an US citizen escaped from an assault in his car with a woman in Tijuana. He ran over five persons, informal shops and choked with 17 vehicles, causing the anger of local residents who tried to lynched the couple. They were rescued by the police forces.
On 27 September 2021, in Cuernavaca, Morelos, two armed individuals shot and killed a former U.S. military officer in front of a hospital in Colonia Volcanes. 1 fatality.

On 17 November 2021, in Ciudad Juarez, Chihuahua, two armed individuals opened fire and shot at two U.S. citizens who were leaving the State Attorney General's Office. Both victims were injured and transported to a hospital in El Paso, Texas. 2 injuries.
On 02 June 2019, in Acapulco de Juarez, Morena militants, students and activists protested outside of the US embassy against the tariff place on Mexican products.

On 14 March 2022, in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas, members of the CND opened fire at the U.S. Consulate. The events are related to the arrest of a high-ranking leader of a criminal organization operating in the border region. There were no casualties.

On 29 April 2022, in Tijuana, Baja California, members of migrant defense groups protested at the dividing wall between Mexico and the United States to protest against the immigration policy that was implemented by both governments in which deportations increased. The protesters set on fire two pinatas with the painted faces of former US President Donald Trump and Mexican Foreign Minister Marcelo Ebrard.

On 1 May 2022, in Orizaba, Veracruz, unionized telephonist workers held a rally against the company America Movil. The workers recalled the violations of the Collective Agreement and stated that there are job vacancies pending because the company wants them to take the positions without the benefit of retirement. The event was on the occasion of Labor Day to demand labour's rights.

On 3 May 2022, in Merida, Yucatan, retired workers of the company Petroleos de Mexico (PEMEX) demonstrated in front of the U.S. Consulate in Colonia Alcala Martin to denounce the company's failure to comply with the rights and medical services specified in their Collective Bargaining Agreement.

On 19 May 2022, in Tijuana, Baja California, around 50 migrants from several nationalities including Mexicans held a protest at the facilities of the Consulate General of the United States to demand that the US government put an end to Article 42. A program implemented by the US government that establishes a health prevention measure for asylum seekers to wait for their resolution outside the US. The protesters said that the measure is discriminatory as does not apply to all migrants.

On 17 May 2022, in Acapulco de Juarez, Guerrero, around 25 people blocked the Avenue Costera Miguel Aleman outside the U.S. Consulate to demand the removal of the U.S. blockade against Cuba. Protesters denounced the inhumane blockade imposed by the U.S. which has affected the country for more than 60 years.

On 18 June 2022, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, a group of people protested outside the embassy of the UK to demand freedom of Julian Assange and against the extradition of the journalist and founder of WikiLeaks to the U.S. Protesters demanded access to medical attention and freedom for the journalist.

On 16 June 2019, in Colonia Providencia, Guadalajara, Jalisco, an unidentified armed group attacked two American men. One man died in the attack and the other one was kidnapped. On Saturday the authorities informed that the man who was kidnapped was found.

On 29 June 2022, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, members of Amnesty International and other women's collectives protested outside the U.S. embassy to demand the right to abortion in the U.S. Protesters denounced the recently passed legislation that criminalizes abortion in several states in the U.S.

Around 29 July 2022 (as reported), in San Luis Rio Colorado, Sonora, two men were killed and their bodies were found with their feet tied. The victims were U.S. nationals and were reported missing since July 23. 2 fatalities.

On 26 July 2022, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, members of the social organizations Popular Congress of Mexico City, the Assembly of Neighborhoods and Dignified Housing Projects and the Urban Block protested outside the U.S. embassy in defense of the national sovereignty of oil, gas and electric energy.

Around 17 September 2022 (as reported), in Playa del Carmen, Quintana Roo, a man of U.S. nationality was shot dead in the area of Zona Hotelera. Two men were arrested as suspected perpetrators. 1 fatality.

On 2 November 2022, in Tapachula de Cordova y Ordonez, Chiapas, a caravan of Venezuelan migrants started their trip to the United States as a protest after the announcement of new US measures to control migration from Venezuela. The migrants demanded that the United States revoke the expansion of the law 'Title 42' which immediately expel Venezuelans who arrive by land to that country.

On 20 April 2020, in Chihuahua, a Chinese man was found dead after having been beaten. According to reports, the attack could be considered as a hate crime against the Chinese considered as people infected with the coronavirus. 1 fatality.

On 30 November 2022, in Tijuana, Baja California, a hundred people demonstrated in front of the U.S. Consulate to demand to expedite their asylum applications. The protesters were mostly people from Michoacan who sought asylum due to violence and threats from criminal groups.

On 26 July 2021, in Balancan, Tabasco, 70 construction workers held a protest against the lack of payment of their salaries by the Chinese company who hired them to work in the construction of the road for the Mayan Train.

On 9 January 2023, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, organizations supporting deported migrants gathered to held a protest around the Zocalo to call for an end to mass deportations and Title 42. Lay 42 is a U.S. law that allows federal officials to quickly deport migrants at the borders . The event was made during the visit of the President of the United States of America.

On 13 February 2023, in Oaxaca de Juarez, Oaxaca, authorities and indigenous communities of San Pedro Quitani protested to demand the President to cancel the concession and operation of a U.S. mining company and two Mexican companies. Protesters denounced the contamination caused to rivers and the destruction of several homes in the area.

On 07 July 2019, in Torreon, Coahuila, about 800 persons of the Luz del Mundo church protested to support the leader of the church arrested in the US on charges of human trafficking, child pornography and rape.

On 14 February 2023, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, around six individuals protested outside the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to denounce the sanctions imposed by the U.S. against the Syrian regime preventing the arrival of aid for those affected by the earthquake. Protesters denounced the unequal response provided to victims of the earthquake in Turkey and Syria due to the sanctions against the President of Syria.

On 7 April 2023, around Tijuana, Baja California, demonstrators marched from Friendship Park in San Diego to El Parque de la Amistad, just across the Mexican border in Tijuana (Baja California) for a Good Friday prayer service and to demonstrate against the construction of border walls, and to call for the re-opening of Friendship Park. The Friends of Friendship Park was among the groups present. A Honduran migrant to the US was a speaker at the event.

On 6 May 2023, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, a group of people demonstrated in front of the UK embassy to demand the release of the Wikileaks founder. Another group of people demonstrated in front of the U.S. embassy to demand the same and to denounce that there is no freedom of expression until this happens. The demonstrators were members of the organization #24F Life and Liberty Coalition.

On 26 May 2023, in Tijuana, Baja California, around 450 migrants protested at the U.S. consulate against the elimination of the CBP One application, which according to the US authorities encourages migrants without proper documentation to enter the U.S. Protesters denounced the planned elimination which could lead to an increase in irregular crossings.

On 21 July 2019, in Cuauhtemoc, Ciudad de Mexico, Mexico, the lawyer of the drug lord El Chapo of the Sinaloa Cartel and three persons, protested with banners in front of the office of external affairs to demand the secretary of the US to repatriate the drug lord to Mexico who was on trial in the US.

On 20 November 2022, in Ciudad de Mexico - Iztapalapa, a man was shot dead by two armed men on a motorcycle (drive-by incident) in Colonia Pueblo Aculco. The victim was a Chinese businessman. According to some reports the attack could have been due to a settling of scores. 1 fatality.

Property destruction: On 26 December 2022, in Tijuana, Baja California, armed individuals set three vehicles on fire. The vehicles were property of clients of a Chinese restaurant who parked their cars outside the business while eating. The event is related to the extortion and lack of the 'floor fee' payment. The perpetrators left a message signed by El Charco gang. There were no casualties, only property damages.

On 29 November 2022, in Tepatitlan de Morelos, Jalisco, an American citizen was kidnapped by men traveling in two vehicles. Around 16 July 2023 (as reported), she was released by their captors. Authorities have given no information on arrest made.

On 17 July 2023, in Matamoros, Tamaulipas, more than 400 workers of a US company started a strike after the directors closed the factory without paying them their salaries. The protesters gathered at the entrance of the company.
On 05 August 2019, in Cuauhtemoc, Ciudad de Mexico, DF, a group of persons protested in front of the US embassy following the El Paso shooting in Texas. A Pinata representing Donald Trump was burnt.

On 10 November 2023, in Merida, Yucatan, dozens of people, many of them of Palestinian descent and representatives of human rights organizations, protested at the doors of the United States Consulate demanding an end to the war in Gaza. The protesters accused the US for being the main sponsor of the war. They also demanded a ceasefire from the government.

On 25 June 2023, in San Francisco del Rincon, Guanajuato, almost a thousand protesters representing local businesses of shoemakers protested the influx of Chinese shoes to their areas, stating that it is affecting their sales. They called for the federal government to the ban of smuggling of Asian goods into Mexico. They started their march at Camino Viejo and walked toward the municipal palace in the city center.

On 4 February 2024, in Felipe Carrillo Puerto, Quintana Roo, a US citizen who was abducted by armed men in Los Limones town was found alive on 6 February with his hands and feet tied inside the jungle. There were no fatalities.

Around 19 February 2024 (as reported), in Gonzalez, Tamaulipas, a US man was attacked and was found with signs of torture on the Zaragoza-Gonzalez highway. The victim had injuries on his neck and face and he had signs of burning on his legs. 1 injured.

On 8 March 2024, in Zacatecas, Zacatecas, around 60 people protested in the historic city in solidarity with Palestinians and to demand a ceasefire. Protesters denounced the U.S. and England for their support of Israel.

On 14 May 2024, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, a group of around 200 students of the FNERR marched through the Paseo de la Reforma until the United States embassy near Angel de la Independencia to demand to stop the attacks on civilians in Palestine. The demonstrators called for an end to attacks against Palestine and denounced U.S. support for Israel. In front of the embassy, the protesters broke a pinata alluding to the U.S. president calling for an end to what they consider to be a genocide.
On 29 November 2023, in Huejutla de Reyes, Hidalgo, merchants held a protest against the opening of Chinese stores , which are expected to be in different locations.
On 17 June 2024, in Tlaxcoapan, Hidalgo, formal merchants demonstrated in front of the mayor's office against the arrival of two stores for the marketing of Chinese products.

On 26 July 2024, in Tepanco de Lopez, Puebla, more than 50 farmers demonstrated outside the offices of Empaque Produce Sol Dorado SA de CV to demand better working conditions because they claimed to suffer from exploitation from the Chinese owners who pay them low salaries.

On 31 July 2024, in San Francisco del Rincon, Guanajuato, nearly 2500 shoe producers protested at the main square to demand the federal government to act against Chinese footwear and avoid the bankruptcy of Mexican shoe makers.

On 18 August 2024, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, citizens staged a sit-in outside the U.S. Embassy in support of Palestine and denounced the U.S. financing of Israel and its involvement in the attacks against Palestinians.

Around 27 September 2024 (as reported), in Tijuana, Baja California, four armed men abducted an American woman for six days in a house on Lazaro Cardenas street, in Colonia Obrera. The victim managed to escape and went to a military barracks. Military officers conducted an operation and arrested the four perpetrators and seized arms and drugs.

On 7 October 2024, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, hundreds of students and members of the FNERRR protested on Paseo de la Reforma at the U.S. embassy to demand a ceasefire in Palestine and an end to the invasion by Israel in Palestine on the one year anniversary of the beginning of hostilities.

On 18 October 2024, in Altar, Sonora, according to witnesses, armed individuals on a vehicle shot at a vehicle on Caborca-Altar road, killing an American man (drive-by). The victim was an off-duty American Marine. Two other women who were in the vehicle were not injured. One of the perpetrators, a suspected member of Los Deltas armed cell of Los Mayitos Gang, was arrested in Altar on 30 October 2024. Another perpetrator was killed during an armed clash with security forces in Altar around 30 October 2024 (coded separately). A third perpetrator was arrested in Altar on 13 February 2025. 1 fatality.
On 4 November 2024, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, three residents protested at the US embassy to demand an Israeli ceasefire against Gaza and Lebanon.

On 29 November 2024, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, people marched demanding that the Mexican government break relations with Israel. The march was from the US embassy to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (SRE). The event was made in the context of the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People. The protesters also demanded that the United States stop providing further funding to the Israeli army and lift the veto it has imposed against the resolutions of the United Nations Organization that call for an unconditional ceasefire.

On 18 December 2024, in Tijuana, Baja California, around 150 migrants called by the organizations Alianza Migrante Tijuana, Angeles Sin Fronteras, and SOS Migrante marched from Juventud 2000 shelter to San Ysidro international crossing point to protest US elected president D. Trump's immigration policy and to commemorate the International Day of the Migrant.

On 19 January 2025, in Tijuana, Baja California, hundred migrants and activists held a protest in the area of the border wall, in Playas de Tijuana. The event was held prior to November 20, when the new US president Donald Trump took office. The protesters stated that he will bring many problems and will affect many families if he continues with his new laws. They also asked for a boycott against the United States.

On 20 January 2025, in Xalapa-Enriquez, Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave, a group of political activists protested in the framework of the inauguration of President Donald Trump's government and against the intervention of the President in Mexican politics.
On 23 January 2025, in Ciudad Juarez, Chihuahua, members of the association Messenger Angels protested at Santa Fe International Bridge in rejection of President Trump's migration policies.

On 20 January 2025, in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, dozens of residents demonstrated outside the US embassy and set fire to a pinata of the recently appointed President Trump and against the US administration.

On 3 February 2025, in Acapulco de Juarez, Guerrero, members of the Collective of Social and Labor Organizations in Defense of the Fourth Transformation protested in front of the U.S. Consulate against President Trump's 'interventionist' and migratory policy.

On 19 February 2025, in Uruapan, Michoacan de Ocampo, several individuals abducted an underage American boy. The victim died in an armed clash that took place during a rescue operation in Ziracuaretiro later the same day (coded separately).

Combination of two related events. On 12 August 2024, in Purisima del Rincon, Guanajuato, footwear workers from Leon and San Francisco del Rincon demonstrated against the import of Chinese shoes. The participants marched towards Leon. The participants called out on the population to buy local footwear. This event was replicated in other location (coded separately); On 12 August 2024, in San Francisco del Rincon, Guanajuato, footwear workers from Leon and San Francisco del Rincon demonstrated against the import of Chinese shoes. The participation marched towards Leon. The participants called out on the population to buy local footwear. This event was replicated in other location (coded separately).
Nearly a thousand people demonstrated against US president Trump's decision to recognize Jerusalem as the capital of Israel. Mobilization at the call of the Muslim community of the country.
On 30 January 2019, activists staged a protest in Bamako against American imperialism and in support of Venezuela.

properties.actor: JNIM: Group for Support of Islam and Muslims
properties.notes: On 18 June 2017, a group of armed men attacked the tourist resort Campement Kangaba in Yirimandio (Bamako, Bamako). At least four people were killed in the attack, including a Malian national guard, a Portuguese soldier of the EU training mission, and two civilians including a Malian and a Chinese national, a Cameroonian died from cardiac arrest. Malian and French forces intervened and killed the 4 assailants and freed 30 hostages. Fourteen people were also wounded. JNIM claimed responsibility.

properties.actor: JNIM: Group for Support of Islam and Muslims
properties.notes: On 22 March 2018, a vehicle belonging to a Chinese construction company was struck by an IED not far from Diafarabe, one Chinese worker was killed and five Malians wounded.
On 16 April 2023, a number of residents set fire to a gendarmerie post providing protection to Chinese gold miners in Balamassala (Kangaba, Koulikoro).

On 17 April 2023, a number of residents demonstrated against the presence of Chinese gold miners in Balamassala (Kangaba, Koulikoro). Clashes erupted between demonstrators and security forces (probably gendarmes) who fired gunshots and killed two demonstrators.

On 11 May 2020, a number of residents, including women, staged a demonstration in Dougabougou (Segou) against the decision by a Chinese company to relieve a factory director of his duties. The demonstrators burned tires and barricaded roads.

On 16 November 2024, at the call of Youth for Palestine, Moviment Graffitti, and representatives of the Lebanese Advocates in Malta, about 75 people, including pro-Palestine activists, members of the Palestinian and Lebanese communities, and PL affiliate Sammy Meilaq, gathered near the US Embassy in Ta' Qali Park in the municipality of Attard (Central) to protest against the US and Israeli governments and the killing of Palestinian civilians. Protesters held placards with messages such as 'Hands off Lebanon' and 'Stop genocide in Gaza,' and some raised red-painted hands symbolizing bloodshed.

On 17 July 2021, presumed Katiba Macina (JNIM) militants attacked a construction site near the village of Madina Kagoro (Nara, Koulikoro). The militants abducted three Chinese workers and two Mauritanians, destroyed vehicles and equipment, and seized other vehicles. The two Mauritanians were released on 27 July. The Chinese hostages were announced released on 1 November. Malian authorities declared they had been liberated, which JNIM denied in an audio, saying that the hostages managed to escape.
On 22 February 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked two Chinese nationals (probably miners) aboard a truck in the village of Menankote (Kenieba, Kayes). One was killed and the other wounded.

On 17 April 2020, in Ward No.1, Pakokku Town, Pakokku Township, Pakokku District, Magway Region, residents demonstrated against the hotel for hosting a Chinese national. A Chinese national was on the same flight with a COVID-19 (Coronavirus) patient. He was taken to a quarantine centre.

On 24 May 2020, in Myawaddy Town, Myawaddy Township, Myawaddy District, Kayin State, a group of drunk Chinese men with a knife who were causing a disturbance were shot by the KNU-PC. There was one fatality and three injured.

On 1 December 2020, in front of Myanmar Investment Commission's Office (Yankin Township, Yangon-East, Yangon Region), 14 factory workers demonstrated against the owner (a Chinese citizen) of the Young Clothing garment factory located in Shwelinban Industrial Zone in Hlaingthaya Township. Demonstrators demanded compensation and urged the government to take legal actions against the owner for violating the laws. The factory was shut down on 15 September and workers have not received compensation accordance in the labour law.

On 6 December 2020, at the Chinese Embassy in Dagon Township (Yangon West District, Yangon Region), about 15 people demonstrated to show that they do not want the Union Election Commission. It is not known who initiated the demonstration. Three other demonstrations took place at the same time at the US, British, and Japan embassies. 18 arrests were made at the demonstrations at the Chinese, US, and Japan embassies.

On 1 January 2021, in Hko Wein village or Muse town (Muse Township, Muse District, Shan State) (coded as Muse), an unknown assailant shot a man to death. He was identified as a Chinese national. His hands and legs were tied up. His mouth and eyes were also covered with cloth. 1 fatality coded.

On 18 November 2012, in Monywa (Monywa, Sagaing), protesters gathered in front of the office of the China-owned Wan Bao company near the Monywa copper mine site, bringing the mine operations to a halt.

On 11 February 2021, in Dagon township (Yangon-west District, Yangon Region), students, film stars and others protested in front of China Embassy against Myanmar military coup. Protesters held a placard saying 'China, supporting and helping directly or indirectly, the coup and injustices of the military do not make you a good neighbor', and 'we, the people of Myanmar have chosen our true leader by our votes. It's not you, Min Aung Hlaing', among others. On 22 February 2021, in Dagon township (Yangon-west District, Yangon Region), locals held a protest in front of the Indonesian Embassy, Chinese Embassy and Russian Embassy against the military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement, as part of the nationwide '22222' general strike.
On 1 December 2012, in Mandalay (Mandalay, Mandalay), about 100 Buddhist monks demonstrated against the Chinese mines.

On 1 December 2012, in Dagon Township, in Yangon Region, people gathered in Myaynigone for a protest against the violent suppression of Letpadaung protest camp. The protesters marched towards the Embassy of China but were blocked by the 100 police at the corner of Baho Road and Pyidaungsu Yeikthar Road near the Embassy. On 2 December 2012, in Bahan Township, in Yangon Region, more than 60 political activists staged a protest against violent crackdown of the Letpadaung protest camp. Protesters held posters saying 'Apologize the victims of the violent crackdown, abolish the Letpadaung Copper Mine project, withdraw all Chinese investment in Myanmar.' Two protesters were arrested by the police while they were marching to the Tamwe roundabout.
On 2 December 2012, in Salingyi Township (Yinmabin, Sagaing), about 500 villagers rallied in demonstration against the Chinese mines.

On 15 February 2021, in Chanmyathazi town, Chanmyathazi township (Mandalay district, Mandalay Region), youth protested in front of the Chinese Consulate-General against the Myanmar military coup and to demand the Chinese government to stop supporting the military coup.

On 16 February 2021, in Muse town (Muse Township, Muse District, Shan State), more than 1,000 locals including ethnic Shan people protested at the Myanmar-China border checkpoint against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. They held placards calling China 'not to assist the Myanmar military coup'.

On 17 February 2021, in Chanmyathazi town, Chanmyathazi township (Mandalay district, Mandalay Region), youth protested in front of the Chinese Consulate-General to demand the Chinese government to stop supporting the military coup. They also urged more workers to join the civil disobedience movement.

On 24 February 2021, in Dagon township (Yangon-west District, Yangon Region), locals including Muslims held a protest in front of the Indonesian Embassy and Thai Embassy against the military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. They held placards calling Indonesia not to support dictatorship as the military-appointed Foreign Minister was due to hold talks with the Thai and Indonesian Foreign Ministers on the same day. People also protested at the Chinese embassy.

Combination of two related events. On 14 March 2021, in Hlaingtharya town (Hlaingtharya-East Township, Yangon-North District, Yangon Region), locals held a demonstration against the military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. Military and police forces intervened and set fire to the barricades set up by demonstrators. Some demonstrators reportedly fought back with sticks and knives. They fired rubber bullets and live bullets to disperse the crowd. Security forces continued to give chase to demonstrators and fired late into the night. BBC reported that at least 40 people were killed, AAPP reported 49 killed, Khit Thit Media reported 58 killed [coded AAPP as the most recent fatality estimate]. An estimated 15 were injured. Three factories were reportedly set on fire (including two owned by Chinese nationals) but it was not confirmed who were the perpetrators. One aid worker was also killed; Property destruction: On 14 March 2021, in Insein township (Yangon (North) District, Yangon Region), a garment factory was reportedly set on fire but it was not confirmed who were the perpetrators. The incident took place on the same day as fire broke out at several factories around Yangon, including many that were owned by Chinese nationals. This happened amid rising anti-Chinese sentiments in Myanmar, leading to claims that Chinese-funded factories may have been targeted. The Chinese government has since issued a statement condemning the attacks against its factories and called on Myanmar to protect its properties and citizens.

On 18 April 2013, in Kyaukpyu Township, in Rakhine State, more than 400 residents staged a protest in front of the company office of China National Petroleum Cooperation (CNPC). Residents are protesting as the Petroleum pipeline project which is currently implementing by the company will not benefit the region. Though the police did not interfere in the protest, they monitored the protest.

On 8 April 2021, in Kyaikto town (Kyaikto Township, Thaton District, Mon State), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. They also burned China flag and pictures of Min Aung Hlaing and other Myanmar military generals during the protest.

On 8 April 2021, in Launglon town, Launglon township (Dawei district, Tanintharyi Region), locals protested against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. They also symbolically burned physical copies of the 2008 Constitution, as well as the Chinese and Russian flags during the protest.

On 8 April 2021, in Mandalay city (Mandalay Region), the Sangha Union protest column along with locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup. The protesters demanded federal democracy and the release of arrested civilians. Protesters burned pictures of the Chinese President.

On 9 April 2021, in Muse town (Muse Township, Muse District, Shan State), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. They also symbolically burned Chinese flags during the protest. On 9 April 2021, in Namhkan town, Namhkan township (Muse district, Shan state), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. They also called for people to not participate in Thingyan festival this year and symbolically burned the Chinese and Russian flags during the protest.

On 5 April 2021, in Yankin township (Yangon-East District, Yangon Region), Insein township (Yangon-North district, Yangon Region),Ahlone township (Yangon-West district, Yangon Region),  locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. Protesters also burned China's flag to condemn its position on the Myanmar military coup.

On 13 April 2021, in Hlaing township (Yangon (West) District, Yangon Region), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. They also called for people to not participate in Thingyan festival this year, held watermelon, and symbolically burned the Chinese flag during the protest.

On 18 April 2021, in Muse town (Muse Township, Muse District, Shan State), people held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. They burned Chinese flags during the protest.

On 8 April 2021, in Insein township (Yangon-North district, Yangon Region), the Myanmar military raided the neighbourhood in Hpaw Kan ward and searched people who involved in an anti-coup protest held in Insein on 6 April when protesters also burned the Chinese flag. The Myanmar military arrested 4 civilians.

On 30 April 2021, in Shwepyithar township (Yangon-north District, Yangon region), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. They also burned the pictures of military leaders and the president of China.
On 14 October 2013, in Kyauktada township, Yangon, a bomb exploded at Trader's Hotel injuring an American staying there. No fatalities.

On 2 May 2021, in Myawaddy town (Myawaddy Township, Myawaddy District, Kayin State), people protested against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the civil disobedience movement. They also called for a boycott of Chinese products.

On 17 October 2013, in Salingyi township, around 300 protesters and an equal number of armed security officers hired by China's state-owned Wanbao Mining Company confronted each other. The security officers were 'Aufully armed'Au and had used slingshots to try to chase them away, injuring at least one of the protesters.
On 23 October 2013, in Monywa township, over 150 people protested against the China-backed Letpadaung copper mine when police and security guards began bulldozing their farms.

On 22 June 2021, in Chanmyathazi township (Mandalay District, Mandalay Region), the Myanmar military invaded the Mandalay PDF bases in the city. Afterwards, both sides engaged in heavy fighting. The Kyaukse PDF aided the Mandalay PDF. The Myanmar military fired heavy weapons indiscriminately. Three Myanmar military soldiers including a Lieutenant Colonel died. The DVB and MPA reported that 2 Mandalay PDF members died, one injured and another 6 members were arrested. The Myanmar military however claimed that 8 PDF members were killed while the Irrawaddy later reported that 4 poultry farmers were also killed (including a Chinese national), quoting relatives of four civilians. The RFA also reported that some civilians were killed and 3 PDF members died. The Myanmar Now and VOA also reported that 4 PDF members died. Additionally, 8 PDF members were also arrested. Fatalities coded as 9 (2 PDF members, 4 civilians and 3 Myanmar military soldier).

On 16 August 2021, in Tigyaing township (Katha district, Sagaing region), five unknown gunmen shot and killed two factory workers from Tagaung nickel plant. Both died at the Mya Taung hospital. It was reported that the nickel plant was invested in by the Chinese government. There have been a number of attacks targeted at Chinese-linked businesses since the coup.

On 9 September 2021, in Salingyi township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), a water pipeline transporting water from the Chindwin River to the Myanmar Wanbao and Myanmar Yangtze copper mines (a joint venture between China and a Myanmar military-owned holding company) was bombed by a local PDF group. The PDF Group stated that the bomb was carried out as China had been ignoring the 'desires of Myanmar people for democracy and backing the military junta.' No damage or casualties reported.

On 26 July 2014, Salingyi Township, in Monywa District, in Sagaing Region, the villagers who were on their way to protest against the Chinese Wan Bao Company and Myanmar Economic Holdings Company Limited were blocked by the police forces. Residents were angry over the instruction issued by township administrator that residents will not be allowed to plow the lands anymore.

properties.actor: MNTJP/MNDAA: Myanmar National Truth and Justice Party/Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army
properties.notes: On 7 October 2021, in Pang Hseng town of Muse township (Muse district, Sagaing region), the MNDAA attacked a military convoy of 23 vehicles. The military based in Hpawng Hseng fired random rounds at the MNDAA positions to support their troops during the fighting. A Chinese man was injured from a heavy shell explosion.
On 7 November 2021, in Yangon city (Yangon region), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup. They also urged to reject the military regime and boycott Chinese products. .

On 27 December 2014, in Mandalay, about 500 demonstrators protesting against the death of a woman killed by police at the Letpadaung copper mine marched through the city towards the Chinese consulate where they were blocked by police.

On 29 December 2014, in Dagon township, Yangon division, demonstrators protesting the death of a woman at the Letpadaung copper mine marched through Yangon arriving in front of the Chinese embassy where they clashed with the police

Several hundred Buddhist monks, activists and farmers from nearby villages joined local protesters. Protestors requested the Myanmar government and Chinese mining firm Wanbao to follow the instructions from the Letpaduangtaung Investigation Report.

On 1 January 2015, in Dagon Township, in Yangon Region, nearly two-dozen activists gathered in front of Maha Bandoola Park before marching to the Chinese Embassy to protest in front of the building. Protestors requested the Myanmar Government and Chinese mining firm follow instructions from the Letpadaung Investigation Report.

On 25 December 2021, in Monekoe area (Muse township, Muse district, Shan State), fighting broke out between the MNDAA and the military troops. The MNDAA claimed that a Chinese female villager was killed by the military's artillery shells while Shwe Phee Myay News Agency reported that it was a Chinese man.

Around 500 local residents protested against plans by the Chinese government to build a bridge in Mankhang Township, Northern Shan State, on disputed territory claimed by both the Chinese and Burmese governments. Around 15 people and 10 armed security guards from China arrived in Kongser Village on what is believed to be the Burmese side of the China-Myanmar border and raised a Chinese flag where they wanted to build a bridge.

On 20 February 2022, in Na Nwin Taw Bo village of Natogyi township (Myingyan district, Mandalay region), the military arrested 20 more locals -16 male and 4 female - including a person who lost one leg at around 5 am after the military soldiers who were guarding the China-owned oil and gas pipeline were being attacked on February 14.

Seven people approached a vehicle carrying managers of Chinese company that they say needs to take responsibility for flooding in Salingyi township. The protesters were taken to the police station and detained for several hours. While they were being held, area villagers gathered outside the police station.

On 7 August 2015, in Insein (Yangon, Yangon), Movement for Democracy Current Force (MDCF) protested in front of Insein Prison against the amnesty given to Chinese loggers who were originally sentenced to life imprisonment by Myitkyina district court.

On 27 April 2022, in Mandalay city (Mandalay district, Mandalay region), locals held a protest against the military coup by holding banners saying 'Freedom is not free', and 'China: Respect Myanmar People's Voice, Stop Supporting Fascist Criminals'. Protestors also burned the flag of China.

On 28 April 2016, in Kamayut town, Kamayut township, Yangon (West) (Yangon Region), hundreds of protesters including a group of Myanmar nationalists, some monks from the Ma Ba Tha, staged a protest outside of the American Embassy for the use of the word Rohingya in a statement released on 20 April 2016 by the embassy.

On 28 April 2022, in Let Pa Taung area of Salingyi township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup. They also urged Chinese government, holding the banner 'China: Respect Myanmar People's Voice,' Stop Supporting Fascist Criminals.'

properties.actor: A Mi Myay Special Task Force
properties.notes: On 24 June 2022, in Salingyi township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), a combined force of A Mi Myay Special Task Force and Young People Force destroyed a transmission tower connected to a Chinese mining firm Wanbao Mining by using high explosive dynamites, causing power outage in the area. The combined force claimed that they carried out the attack to warn the company for hosting, supplying and supporting Myanmar military soldiers.

On 17 May 2016, at Ulang Pa Hka Shang, Mansi township, Kachin state, the Myanmar army used fighter jets to target KIA 27th battalion positions. Trucks carrying timber were hit, killing one Chinese national.

On 16 November 2022, near Hpayarthonesu town of Kyainseikgyi township (Kawkareik district, Kayin state), the Myanmar military forces carried out an airstrike on Mat Ka Tha No.6 Mining Site of the KNU Bridge 6 located 18 miles away from Hpayarthonesu. The airstrike was carried out at 1:45 pm. Three mining workers were killed and six others including three Chinese citizens were injured by the airstrike.

On 13 January 2023, near In Bar Par village (Mansi township, Bhamo district, Kachin state), more than 300 people including Kachin Catholic and Baptist Christian religious leaders from In Bar Par and Ding Sing Par villages held a protest against an unknown Chinese campany preparing to mine the rare-earth metals and demaded to immediately stop mining the rare-earth metals.

On 26 January 2023, in Pakokku township (Pakokku district, Magway region), five members of an unidentified armed group detained two Chinese civilians (citizens of China) from a textile factory located on the Pakokku - Yesagyo road at around 8 am for unknown reasons.
A protest was staged in Kyauktan village, Kyauktan township, Yangon, on 11 May demanding China improve the area infrastructure.

On 13 February 2023, in Salingyi township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), the National Revolutionary Guards (NRG) attacked about 15 military soldiers providing security in the Wanbao company (a Chinese mining company) at around 9 am and both sides then exchanged fire. There were 2 fatalities on the military side and a fatality on the NRG side.
More than 100 people in Muse, Shan State, protested against Chinese banks for locking them out of their accounts for nearly 10 days.

On 27 February 2023, near Aik Ma village (Indaw township, Katha district, Sagaing region), the Indaw PDF abducted seven Chinese citizens who were traveling without legal documents and a member of the Katha PDF (PaKaPha) battalion 2 who was among others transporting the Chinese citizens by three motorcycles.
On 21 March 2023, in Mansi township (Bhamo district, Kachin state), about one thousand locals from Mansi township held a protest against the Chinese rare earth mining sites.

On 8 May 2023, in Yinmarbin township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals from Yinmarbin-Salingyi held a protest against the Chinese government that supported the Myanmar military by holding banners saying ' China....Stop Killing Myanmar People by Supporting Fascist Criminals'. Separately, locals from the 'Shwe Nwe Thway' Strike, locals from the 'Kal Tin Shin Ma Shar Doh Kyay Ywar' Strike, and locals from northern Yinmarbin held protests against the Myanmar military coup. On the same day, protesters from the 'Never Turn Back Revolution' Strike set the flag of the People's Republic of China on fire and protested against the Chinese government that supported the Myanmar military.

On 16 May 2023, in Hpayarthonesu town of Kyainseikgyi township (Kawkareik district, Kayin state), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and against the Chinese government's support of the Myanmar military government.
On 7 October 2011, in Mogaung township (Mohnyin, Kachin), Burmese troops under the Mogaung (Mugang)-based Military Operation Command-3 (MOC-3), led by Brig-Gen Myat Kyaw, raped three Chinese women.
