On 11 May 2023, in Monywa town (Monywa township, Monywa district, Sagaing region), locals led by the Monywa Youth Association held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and the Chinese government at the traffic light in the center of the city, holding a banner saying, 'China...Stop Killing Myanmar People by Supporting Fascist Criminals.' They also burned the Chinese flag during the protest. Protests emerged after the Chinese Foreign Minister met with the military leader in Nay Pyi Taw on 2 May. On 11 May 2023, in Let Pa Taung area of Salingyi township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and the Chinese government, holding a banner saying, 'China...Stop Killing Myanmar People by Supporting Fascist Criminals.'

On 21 May 2023, near Shwe Si Taing (Shwe Se Taing) village (Kyaukpadaung township, Nyaung-U district, Mandalay region), the People's Defense Force - Myingyan District Battalion 2 and allies attacked a camp of about ten soldiers and policemen guarding the China Oil and Gas pipeline at 5:30 am. The fighting lasted for more than 30 minutes. The NUG reported that four policemen were killed.

On 22 May 2023, near Min Kan village (Taungtha township, Myingyan district, Mandalay region), unidentified local defense forces attacked the Myanmar military's Min Kan security checkpoint which provided security to the China-Myanmar natural gas pipeline at around 8:30 pm. The two sides then exchanged fire for around 15 minutes. Around four military soldiers were killed.

On 20 May 2023, in Let Pa Taung area of Salingyi township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and the Chinese government, holding a banner saying, 'PTT ... Stop Paying Blood Money to Junta.'

properties.actor: Military Forces of Myanmar (2021-) Border Guard Force
properties.notes: On 27 May 2023, in Laukkaing town (Laukkaing township, Kokang Self-Administered Zone, Shan-North state), the BGF members quarreled with one another and then exchanged fire at around 2 pm. Khit Thit Media and Shan Herald Agency for News reported that a BGF member was killed. Another source, Shwe Phee Myay News Agency reported that two BGF members and a Chinese businessman nearby were killed and 3 other BGF members were injured. Fatalities coded as 1 for the lowest estimates.
On 9 October 2011, in Nam Ngawn village, 6 Chinese migrant workers were interrogated and tortured by the Myanmar army.

Combination of two related events. On 14 June 2023, in Shwepyithar township (Yangon-North district, Yangon region), a 29-year-old female labour leader who had been working at the Hosheng Myanmar clothing factory owned by a Chinese national for nearly two years was arrested by the military after requesting a wage increase. She was fired by the factory on June 10 after employees led by seven labour leaders at the Hosheng Myanmar clothing factory requested a raise. She was being held at the military's interrogation center; On 16 June 2023, in Shwepyithar township (Yangon-North district, Yangon region), five labour leaders who had been working at the Hosheng Myanmar clothing factory owned by a Chinese national and two of the organizers from a labour organization were arrested by the military after requesting wage increase. The five labour leaders were fired by the factory on June 10 after employees led by seven labour leaders at the Hosheng Myanmar clothing factory requested a raise. They were being held at a police station.

On 27 June 2023, in Myitkyina township (Myitkyina district, Kachin state), an unidentified armed group opened fire at a convoy that included the Chinese consulate. The military accused the KIA of being responsible for the attack, while the KIA denied the accusation. A BGF was also accused of the attack although it denied the accusation. Casualties unknown.

On 18 July 2023, near Da Bat Yang and Sa Mar villages (coded as Da Bat Yang) (Waingmaw township, Myitkyina district, Kachin state), an unidentified armed group opened fire at a car on the Bhamo-Myitkyina road at around 12 pm. A Chinese businessperson sustained injuries in the leg, and a Myanmar national female translator sustained critical injuries around her neck and ear.

On 23 July 2023, in Kyauktaga township (Bago district, Bago-East region), an unknown resistance group destroyed No.2 transmission tower that transmits electricity to a substation in Thar Yar Kone village on Kyauktaga-Thahtaykone road with remote explosives around 11:35 pm, destroying two 230 KV power distribution towers. Locals claimed that the power distribution towers were part of the military's project to sell electricity to China and they were destroyed after the Military's artillery attack killed four civilians in Kyauktaga township (coded separately). According to Eleven Media, the Myanmar police reported that the KNLA and the PDF blew up the towers.

On 20 August 2023, in Salingyi town (Salingyi township, Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), about 150 protesters from villages in Yinmarbin-Salingyi township held a protest on the Ya Mar bridge and at a bazaar in the town against the Chinese Wan Paung company and Yang Si company which were operating a copper mine project in the Let Pa Taung area and the military-owned Moe Kyoe sulphuric acid factory. The Yinmarbin-Salingyi villages strike committee member claimed that they held a protest because the Chinese company provided a place for the military outpost, and the military committed crimes against the villagers for security reasons.

On 22 August 2023, in Yinmarbin township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals from the villages in Yinmarbin-Salingyi township held a protest against the Myanmar Wan Bao and Myanmar Yan Si Chinese companies as they supported and cooperated with the Myanmar military. Separately 'Never Turn Back Revolution' Strike and locals from 'Ahr Man Thit' strikeheld a protest against the military coup.

On 8 September 2023, in the Let Pa Taung area of Salingyi township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals held a protest against the military coup and the Chinese companies, by holding a poster saying 'Wan Bao-Yan Si, Stop Cooperating with the Fascist Army Immediately!', 'Wan Bao-Yan Si, Send back the Fascists Soldiers to Barracks', ' Stop Using Copper Mine Project as Military Base' and 'We do not want Wan Bao-Yan Si, who are cooperating with SAC'.

On 22 March 2018, in Ann township, Kyaukphyu district, Rakhine state, about 1,000 farmers protested against China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) and MOGE over the lack of compensation for damaged farmlands.

On 7 April 2018, in Ann township, Rakhine state, about a 100 farmers staged a protest and hunger strike in front of the China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) offices demanding compensation for farmlands damaged by the CNPC and MOGE oil and gas pipeline.
On 21 June 2018, in Monekoe area, Muse district, Shan state, local residents protested the road construction in Hpa Kawng village by Chinese business owners.

On 19 November 2023, in Yangon city (Yangon region), pro-military protesters including members of the Patriotic Monks Union (Yangon) and Myanmar Nationalist Organization held a protest against the Chinese government outside Yangon City Hall and the Chinese Embassy, accusing China of destroying Myanmar by selling weapons to ethnic armed organizations based near the border in northern Myanmar, and to People's Defense Forces. They marched from Yangon City Hall to the Chinese Embassy, shouting anti-China slogans including, 'China, you have been meddling in the internal affairs of Myanmar. Don't try to exploit us. We monks and people are gonna beat you up.'

On 19 November 2023, in Nay Pyi Taw city (Nay Pyi Taw district, Nay Pyi Taw region), pro-military protesters including former members of the Association for the Protection of Nationality and Religion (Ma Ba Tha) held a protest against the Chinese government on the Pyinmana-Taung Nyo road in the evening. They accused China of backing 'Operation 1027' launched by the Brotherhood Alliance.

properties.actor: KIO/KIA: Kachin Independence Organization/Kachin Independence Army
properties.notes: Combination of two related events. On 31 December 2023, in Nam Hpat Kar (Ho Pong + Pang Sa Lorp) village (Kutkai township, Muse district, Shan-North state), the KIA continued to attack the military (IB-123) base and both sides then exchanged fire for 6 days (29 - 31 and 2 - 4). Myanmar Now reported that during the rest of the fights on 31 December and 2 - 4 January, the military conducted airstrikes and fired artillery rounds on the battlefield, hitting and killing a Chinese man and a Ta'ang man. Houses in Thar Yar Kone (1) ward, Na Hpat Kar market, Kachin church, and a Pan Jar Yawt monastery were also destroyed during the six-day fight. Fatalities split across four days (31 December, 2 - 4 January), coded as 1 in this event.; On 2 January 2024, in Nam Hpat Kar (Ho Pong + Pang Sa Lorp) village (Kutkai township, Muse district, Shan-North state), the KIA continued to attack the military (IB-123) base and both sides then exchanged fire for 6 days (29 - 31 and 2 - 4). Myanmar Now reported that during the rest of the fights on 31 December and 2 - 4 January, the military conducted airstrikes and fired artillery rounds on the battlefield, hitting and killing a Chinese man and a Ta'ang man. Houses in Thar Yar Kone (1) ward, Na Hpat Kar market, Kachin church, and a Pan Jar Yawt monastery were also destroyed during the six-day fight. Fatalities split across four days (31 December, 2 - 4 January), coded as 1 in this event.

properties.actor: Military Forces of Myanmar (2021-) Border Guard Force
properties.notes: On 20 October 2023, in Kokang Self-Administered Zone (coded as Laukkaing) (Shan-North state), guards outside a Kokang Border Guard Force scam compound opened fire on Chinese telecom fraudsters who were secretly being transported back to China by major telecom fraud groups in a truck. More than 60 Chinese nationals, allegedly including undercover Chinese police, were killed and injured. Fatalities coded as 30.

properties.actor: Military Forces of Myanmar (2021-) People's Militia Force
properties.notes: On 17 February 2024, in Muse town (Muse township, Muse district, Shan-North state), two members of a People's Militia Force on a motorcycle opened fire at a man and a woman who were standing in front of the Hotel M2 at around 2:30 pm. According the DVB and the Mizzima, the man was a member of the Namhkan Myoma PMF and the woman is also related to the PMF. The man was killed by the gunshots, while the woman and a hotel staff sustained injuries. Meanwhile, the Shwe Phee Myay News Agency reported that they were Chinese people.

On 3 February 2018, in Myitkyina, Kachin state, over 200 farmers protested the confiscation of their lands in Myitkyina and Waingmaw township by Chinese businessmen to plant banana trees for tissue production.
On 12 January 2012, at Loi Leng, near Loije, Kachin state, the Myanmar army shot and killed a Chinese citizen.
On 16 January 2023, in Mansi township (Bhamo district, Kachin state), locals held a protest against the Chinese mining companies to stop mining rare-earth metals.
On 14 March 2019, in Chipwi township, Kachin state, a protest was held calling for a halt to the eight proposed damns to be built by China on the N'mai Hka and Ngaw Chang Hka rivers.

On 4 September 2024, in Yangon city (Yangon district, Yangon region), protesters from the Mayangone Democratic Front (MDF), the Owl Community, the Linn Yaung Ni Youth Organization and the Kyimyindaing Networks (KMD18) held a protest in response to a letter issued by China against the Ta'ang National Liberation Army (PSLF/TNLA), warning them to stop the conflict or face consequences. Protesters held banners saying, 'China: Back off from Myanmar', 'Revolt if being oppressed. Resist if being attacked', and 'If we burn, you burn with us'. Protesters also burned a China flag during the protest.

On 18 October 2024, in Mandalay - Chanmyathazi (Mandalay district, Mandalay region), a bomb explosion occurred at the Chinese consulate in No.1 Myothit ward at around 4:30 pm. The roof of a two-storey building at the consulate was damaged. No group claimed responsibility for the explosion. There were no casualties.

On 29 October 2024, in Hseng Taung village (coded as Hseng Taung (Ywar Haung)) (Hpakant township, Mohnyin district, Kachin state), at least 50 locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and in support of the Kachin Independence Army, the PDF, and the NUG. Protesters also demanded China and the Airbus European aerospace company to stop providing aviation support to the Myanmar military to prevent airstrikes against civilians. The Kachin Region People's Defense Force provided security to the protest.

On 26 October 2024, in Let Pa Taung area of Salingyi township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup by holding a banner saying, 'Airbus: End investment in the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC)'.

properties.actor: KIO/KIA: Kachin Independence Organization/Kachin Independence Army
properties.notes: On 3 November 2024, in Chipwi township (Myitkyina district, Kachin state), the combined troops of the Kachin Independence Army (KIO/KIA) and allies attacked and captured the Myanmar military outpost on the China - Myanmar No.16 border point around 7 am. Casualties unknown.

properties.actor: NMSP-AD/NMLA-AD: New Mon State Party - Anti-military Dictatorship/Mon National Liberation Army - Anti-military Dictatorship
properties.notes: On 6 November 2024, in Kyaik Ywea village of Mudon township (Mawlamyine district, Mon state), 20 members of the New Mon State Party - Anti-military Dictatorship fired four warning shots before capturing the factory head, a manager, and a Chinese expert from the Honda Myanmar Veneer factory. The group also seized 20 mobile phones from factory employees. The detainees were released on 8 November 2024.

On 4 September 2024, in Let Pa Taung village (Salingyi township, Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), unidentified local defense forces attacked Myanmar military security camps at the Let Pa Taung copper mining, which is operated by the military and the Chinese-owned Wanbao mining company, using bombs attached to drones for the second day. Some lounge areas of Chinese workers were damaged. There were no casualties.

On 31 March 2019, in Mogoke Township, in Mandalay Region, a fire outbreak occurred at the gemstone mining site after conflict broke out between the miners and the Chinese owned Htay Paing company. It is rumored on social media that arson attack caused the fire since the right to mine for local miners has already expired.

On 26 February 2019, in Waingmaw Township, in Kachin State, two journalists of the Myitkyina Journal were assaulted by the employees of a mining company as they reported the local residents' concerns over a controversial Chinese tissue-culture banana plantation. The employees of Tha Khin Sit Mining Import/Export company forced two reporters to go with them and then detained them separately and assaulted them.

On 27 June 2011, in Mahaaungmyay Township, in Mandalay Region, Chinese traders and Burmese traders clashed after the Burmese trader was beaten by 5 Chinese gem traders. Police dispersed the crowd, but this led to another clash between the police and the public.

On 13 December 2012, in San Chaung Township, in Yangon Region, a protest was staged to demand an investigation into the violent crackdown on the protesters of Letpadaung Copper Mine project protest camp, to apologize monks and urge the Chinese Wan Bao Company to leave Myanmar. Protesters marched from the east gate of Shwedagon and ended the protest at Koe Htat Kyi Pagoda.

On 1 February 2013, in Hlaingthayar Township, in Yangon Region, workers of Chinese owned Global Electric factory in Hlaingthayar industrial zone (2) staged a protest and demanded to substitute the foreign manager with a Myanmar national, to relax the strict rules and oppression at work.

On 1 May 2013, in Pyigyitagon Township, in Mandalay Region, more than 100 workers of Aung Sein Textile and Dyeing factory staged a protest inside the factory owned by the a Chinese to demand to close the factory on this International Labor Day as the factory ordered the workers to work overtime on May Day.

On 13 May 2013, in Hlaingthayar Township, in Yangon Region, more than 100 workers of Chinese owned Hone Sein Sack factory in Hlaingthayar Industrial Zone (2) staged a protest to demand an increase the basic salary.

On 11 June 2013, in Hlaingthayar Township, in Yangon Region, more than 1600 workers of Korean and Chinese owned Hi-Mo High-Art Wig factory staged a protest to increase the allowance. Workers had a total of 16 demands.

From 13 November to 4 December 2013,in Hlaingthayar Township, in Yangon Region, more than a thousand workers of Chinese owned East Group Garment factory located in Shwe Than Lwin industrial zone have been on protest for 22 days to call for the reinstatement of a dismissed worker and termination of 5 managers. On 4 December, the workers and owner met to discuss the workers' demands.

From 7 to 10 December 2013, in Hlaingthayar Township, in Yangon Region, more than 300 workers of Chinese owned Myanmar Soe San Win factory in Ngwe Pin Lai industrial zone staged a protest for the salary increase as equal to other departments. There were 5 departments at the factory and only one department got the salary increase.

On 25 December 2014, in Dagon Township, in Yangon Region, about 30 political activists protested and urged a stop to the Letpadaung Copper Mine Project in front of the Embassy of China. About 100 police were deployed for security at the Embassy before the protest.

On 25 September 2015, in Ann Township, in Rakhine State, about 200 residents protested to get compensation for the damage to 350 acres of lands in Taung Philar village tract. The lands were destroyed due to petroleum and gas pipeline linked from Rakhine State to China. The protesters demanded the CNPC company and the government to take responsibility for these damages.

On 4 June 2016, in Myitkyina town, Myitkyina township, Myitkyina district (Kachin State), some 40 residents protested in front of the Palm Spring Resort against the meeting between China and KSDP on negotiations about the Myitsone dam. The protest was reportedly disbanded by the police. On 5 June 2016, in Myitkyina Township (Myitkyina, Kachin), around 50 residents staged a protest against Chinese Ambassador Hong Liang over attempts to negotiate the controversial Myitsone dam project.

On 23 February 2017, in Hlaingthayar township (Yangon (North) district, Yangon Region), hundreds to some 300 Myanmar employees from Chinese-owned garment factory held 7 Chinese managers captive in a room at the factory for hours. They also broke windows, doors and equipment in the factory. The demonstration started on 1 February demanding for a sacked foreman to be re-employed and working hours be reduced.

On 18 June 2019, in Hmawbi Township, in Yangon Region, villagers staged a protest in front of Hong Yuan garment factory which is located in Phayar Lan village. The factory was built 6 months ago and is owned by a Chinese national. Villagers demanded repairs to the village road which was damaged by the factory.

On 17 October 2024, in Yinmarbin township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), joint forces of the Regional Friend Fighters, People's Defense Force - Yinmarbin (Taik Nei - 2 PaKaPha), and Black Eagle Revolution Force carried out a mine attack against about 40 trucks that carried Acid and Diluent for the Chinese Wangbao mining company and the Yang Zi mining company between No.28 Yinmarbin Police Battalion and Myauk Mayar Bridge on Pathein-Monywa Road at around 10:30 pm and 30:35 pm. Casualties unknown.

On 3 July 2019, in Yinmarbin Town, in Sagaing Region, a public consultation meeting to conduct a mining feasibility study proposed by a Chinese company was held and came to a halt when 500 locals in attendance protested, shouting that they are against the project. The locals fear that the mining project will have serious environmental and social impacts.

On 31 October 2024, in Let Pa Taung area of Salingyi township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup by holding a banner saying, 'Airbus: End investment in the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC)'.

On 3 November 2024, in Let Pa Taung area (Salingyi township, Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup. They called for an end to airstrikes on civilian homes and urban areas and demanded to stop supporting military equipment to the military junta with a banner that read 'Airbus: End investment in the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC)'.

On 3 November 2024, in Yinmarbin township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), protesters from the 'Lu Nge Ahr Man' Strike and locals from an unreported village in western Yinmarbin township held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and military's census data collection with a banner that said 'If you stay still, even the spider web will retain you. If you struggle to escape, even the iron will break'. Separately, locals from the 'Never Turn Back Revolution' Strike held a protest against the Myanmar military coup with the banner that said 'Airbus: End investment in the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC)'. On the same day, locals from the 'Aung Lan Hlwint Myi Daung Thway Ni' Strike held a protest against the Myanmar military coup.

On 12 November 2024, in Yae Kyi Pin village (Yinmarbin township, Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military coup, holding a banner that said 'Airbus: End investment in the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC)'.

On 6 November 2024, in Yangon - Hlaingtharya-East (Yangon-North district, Yangon region), around 500 laborers from the Charis Company Limited Sculpture Factory held a protest against the company as the Chinese factory director physically assaulted two female workers who refused to work overtime as the factory was unable to pay bonuses. 14 workers have been fired from the factory as they participated in the protest. The protesters made 17 demands, including dismissal of the Chinese director who physically assaulted the two female workers, reinstatement of the fired workers, and provision of workplace healthcare services.

On 13 November 2024, in Yangon - Insein (Yangon-North district, Yangon region), the Myanmar military troops in plain clothes arrested a 64-year-old Buddhist monk, who holds American citizenship and was a former political prisoner, around 4 pm near the Saw Bwar Gyi Kone area. He came to Yangon from the United States on 5 November for the religious ceremony in Nwe Khway village in Mingaladon township. Following his arrest, he was beaten during interrogation and later transferred to Insein Prison. He was charged under Section 13(1) of the Myanmar Immigration Act and Section 505(a) of the Penal Code. On 26 May 2025, the Mingaladon township court charged him 4 years prison sentence, 3 years for section 505(A) and 1 year for section 13(1) of the immigration act and a 500,000 lakhs MMK fine. He was released from Insein Prison on 29 October 2025.

On 16 November 2024, in Yinmarbin township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals from the Yinmarbin-Salingyi Multi-villages Strike held a joint protest against the Myanmar military coup. On the same day, locals from the 'Never Turn Back Revolution' Strike held a protest against the Myanmar military coup by holding a banner saying, 'Airbus: End investment in the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC)'.

On 21 November 2024, in Yinmarbin township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals from the 'Aung Lan Hlwint Myi Daung Thway Ni' Strike held a protest against the Myanmar military coup. On the same day, locals from the 'Never Turn Back Revolution' Strike held a protest against the Myanmar military coup by holding a banner saying, 'Airbus: End investment in the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC)'.

On 24 November 2024, in Salingyi township (Yinmarbin township, Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), locals from the 'Ahr Man Thit' Strike held a protest against the Myanmar military coup by holding a banner saying, 'China: Stop killing Myanmar people by supporting fascist criminals'.

On 2 December 2024, in Yangon - Shwepyithar (Yangon-North district, Yangon region), the Grand Unsung (TGU) carried out a remote mine attack on the Chinese-owned Paung Chein factory in the Tha Du Kan industrial zone. TGU claimed the attack as a warning to the factory owner for allegedly cooperating with the Myanmar military in repressing factory workers. Casualties unknown.

On 9 December 2024, in Kale town (Kale township, Kale district, Sagaing region), protesters from the 'Kale Main Strike Force' held a protest against the Myanmar military coup, holding a banner that said,' China, Stop Killing Myanmar people by supporting Fascist Criminals.'

On 25 December 2024, in Ann town of Ann township (Kyaukpyu district, Rakhine state), the Myanmar military conducted an airstrike at night, destroying buildings near the Western Regional Military Command and other infrastructures. Separately, the Myanmar military stationed at China's gas pipeline control station fired artillery in an attempt to regain the Western Regional Military Command captured by the Arakan Army (ULA/AA) on 20 December (coded separately). Casualties unknown.

properties.actor: ULA/AA: United League of Arakan/Arakan Army
properties.notes: On 6 January 2025, in Ann township (Kyaukpyu district, Rakhine state), the Arakan Army (ULA/AA) attacked and captured the Myanmar military's Taung Zauk camp which protects a Chinese gas pipeline substation located at a 20-mile distance to Ann town. Narinjara News reported that around 20 military troops were killed, and several others were forced to flee.

On 21 December 2024, in Yae Kyi Pin village (Yinmarbin township, Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), protesters from the 'Aung Lan Hlwint Myi Shwe Yae Kyi' Strike held a protest against the Myanmar military coup by holding banners saying, 'We don't want the military dictatorship', 'We don't want the Chinese government which supports the military junta', 'Establish a federal democratic union', and 'Cut off the money supplied to the military'.

On 24 December 2024, in Yae Kyi Pin village (Yinmarbin township, Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), protesters from the 'Aung Lan Hlwint Myi Shwe Yae Kyi' Strike and farmers held a protest against the Myanmar military coup by holding banners saying, 'We don't want the military dictatorship', 'We don't want the Chinese government which supports the military junta', 'Establish a federal democratic union', and 'Cut off the money supplied to the military'.

On 20 January 2025, in San Kar village (Waingmaw township, Myitkyina district, Kachin state), the Myanmar military launched drone strikes at a banana field near the Myitkyina-Bhamo road. A Myanmar citizen and a Chinese citizen were killed. 2 other Myanmar citizens were injured.

On 29 January 2025, in Yangon City (Yangon region), protesters from the Yangon Revolution Brotherhood Alliance and Sanchaung Main Strike held a protest against the Myanmar military coup and Chinese President Xi Jinping for his support of the Myanmar military.

On 21 March 2011, in Tangyan Township, in Shan State, two women were gang raped by the troops of Myanmar military LIB 291 based at Nam pong and LIB 33 from Mong Gao. One of the women who had just delivered a baby died after the gang rape. Another Chinese woman was gang raped at her home.

On 20 March 2025, in Lashio town (Lashio township, Lashio district, Shan-North state), locals held a protest against the Myanmar military leaders and the Chinese intervention in the Myanmar's politics at around 9:00 pm. The protestors demanded the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army to remain in the town.

On 6 November 2019, in Hlaingthayar Township, in Yangon Region, more than 1,000 workers of American national-owned Natural Garment factory in Shwe Lin Ban Industrial Zone staged a protest against the factory closure without notifying the workers. The protesters marched from the Industrial Zone to the township conciliation office. The organization, Action Labor Rights, assisted the protesting workers.

On 16 July 2019, in Muse Town, in northern Shan State, a 40-year-old Chinese citizen was killed by unknown gunmen. He was riding on his motorbike along the main road in Homon ward. A car followed him and two gunmen in the car shot him.

On 1 October 2019, in Hlaingthayar Township, in Yangon Region, nearly 400 workers of the Chinese-owned Unitedtex Overseas Garment factory were picketing at the factory entrance. A Chinese man drove his car into the striking workers and attempted to beat a female worker with a wooden stick. Workers have demanded 17 points, including that their rights to be respected, allowances to be paid, and factory facilities be improved.

Combination of two related events. On 14 January 2020, and until 30 January 2021, about 300 workers of Hunter Myanmar garment factory staged a sit-in protest camp in front of the factory in Hlaingthayar Township, Yangon Region, calling for the 14-point demand including the reinstatement of the dismissed workers and annual bonus. The workers also blockaded the Chinese technicians at the factory from going out of the factory. Though the dispute agreement was supposedly planned to sign on January 30, the employer failed to sign and ran away. Thus, the workers decided to continue their protest; On 26 January 2020, in Hlaingthayar Township, in Yangon Region, workers of Hunter Myanmar garment factory who were protesting at the front of the factory allowed the Chinese technicians whom were earlier blockaded to go out after authorities from Department of Labor came to the factory and negotiated with the protesting workers.

On 22 February 2018, 2018 in Montenegrin capital Podgorica a man threw a grenade at the US embassy, subsequently blowing himself up with another bomb. The attack comes after the country joined NATO. The attacker, Serbia-born Dalibor Jaukovic, connected with the conservative currents, fought in the Yugoslav Army during the NATO bombings of 1999 and reportedly expressed anti-NATO sentiments.

On 5 February 2020, in Salingyi Township, in Sagaing Region, about 300 workers of Yang Tse Copper Mine Co.,Ltd stopped work and rallied in front of the company entrance over the news about the death of a Chinese citizen at the company who came back from China. This caused worry among the workers since they assume the death may be caused by the Coronavirus. Workers also demanded the company to send the Chinese at the company to a hospital and put them under watch.

On 24 February 2020, in Myitkyina Town, in Myitkyina Township, in Kachin State, about 500 villagers from Waingmaw township staged a protest in Sein Mya Ayeyar park demanding to close the border gate with China to prevent the spread of Coronavirus.

On 31 August 2020, Inner Mongolian citizens (Chinese nationals) who live in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolian nationals and civil society organisations including 'Bosoo Khukh Mongol' NGO protested outside the Embassy of the People's Republic of China and outside the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Sukhbaatar District, Ulaanbaatar, against the Chinese government's new policy which require lessons to be taught in Mandarin rather than the Mongolian in Inner Mongolian secondary schools. The protestors held placards written in old Mongolian script and requested the Chinese Ambassador to Mongolia to convey their request to the President of the People's Republic of China.

On 3 September 2020, professors, teachers and students of History Faculty of the National University of Mongolia demonstrated outside the university (Ulaanbaatar-Su'xbaatar) calling for the authorities to save the Mongolian old script. They held placards displaying the message 'Save the Mongolian Language'. Their protest is linked to Chinese government's new policy which require lessons to be taught in Mandarin rather than the Mongolian in Inner Mongolian secondary schools.

On 7 September 2020, Inner Mongolians (Chinese nationals) who reside in Mongolia, Mongolian citizens and Mongolian non-governmental organisations protested dispaying banners and submitted a letter to the United Nations office in Mongolia (Ulaanbaatar-Su'xbaatar) demanding the UN to clarify its position regarding the rights of ethnic Monglians who live in Inner Mongolia. The protesters asked for an official UN position regarding the Chinese Government's decision to replace Mongolian with Mandarin as the language of instruction in Inner Mongolia schools.

On 15 September 2020, about 100 Mongolian citizens and local NGOs organised a peaceful demonstration 'Save the Mongolian Old Script' at the Sukhbaatar Square (Ulaanbaatar-Su'xbaatar), against the Chinese government's new policy to teach main subjects in Chinese in elementary and middle schools of Inner Mongolian Autonomous Region in China. The demonstration was organised during the visit of Chinese Foreign Minister to Mongolia. The protestors held placards written in old Mongolian script.

On 1 October 2020, dozens of people protested at the Sukhbaatar Square, the central square of the capital of Mongolia demanding the release of ethnic Mongolians arrested in China for criticizing a controversial language policy. This Chinese policy aims to teach major subjects in Mandarin in elementary and middle-schools of Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China. Some demonstrators held placards with images and words against this Bilingual Language policy.

On 29 December 2018, a special operation was conducted by police, intelligence and military forces of Mongolia in accordance with the direction given by the Prime Minister of Mongolia. It took place in Gurvan saikhan soum, Dundgovi province and terminated mining licenses of JPF LLC, a 100% Chinese invested company, for mining of Zuun (East) and Salkhit deposits from 2043 to 2047, and accusing the company for hiding of 930 million togrogs taxation.

On 23 July 2021, several non-governmental organizations including 'Save the Mongolian Language' and 'World Mongolians Federation' organized a peaceful demonstration in Sukhbaatar Square (Ulaanbaatar-Su'xbaatar) opposing the China's education policy in Inner Mongolia. The protesters also submitted a petition to the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party requesting China to respect its minority interests and rights.

On 25 August 2021, some non-governmental organizations held a press conference in Ulaanbaatar against the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics with a banner reading '160 Mongolian NGOs for a boycott the Beijing 2022!'. The protesters supported a boycott against the Chinese government's policy to conduct all pre-school programs only in Chinese. They claim that policy violates the human rights of ethnic minorities in China, including those of Inner Mongolians.

On 10 September 2021, Mongolian students, who have been unable to return to their schools in China for almost 2 years due to coronavirus travel restrictions, held a press conference with placards in Ulaanbaatar. They urged the Mongolian and Chinese governments to provide students with an opportunity to study physically in China.

On 5 July 2024, for the 39th consecutive week, Muslim worshippers staged four sit-in protest following the Friday in Casablanca, Sidi Belyout (Casablanca, Casablanca-Settat) to demonstrate their support to Palestine. They also called for an end to Israeli military operations in Gaza and Morocco's normalization deal with Israel. The protest was organized by the Moroccan Commission for the Support of the Islamic Nation Causes. During the night, hundreds of citizens and activists from PJD and MUR parties staged a protest sit-in in front of the US consulate to denounce US support to Israel and calling for an end of Israeli military operations in Gaza.
Inhabitants from Rabat, Oujda, Berkane and Nador protested to denounce US president Trump's decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israels capital.

On 15 November 2024, at the call of the Moroccan Commission for the Support of the Islamic Nation Causes, for the 58th consecutive week, dozens of Muslim worshippers including Al Adl Wa Al Ihssane activists staged a sit-in protest following the night prayer in front of the US consulate in Casablanca, Sidi Belyout (Casablanca, Casablanca-Settat) in support of Palestine. They also called for an end to Israeli military operations in Gaza and US support to Israel.

On 21 November 2024, activists staged a sit-in protest in front of the tribunal of Ain Sebaa, Ain-Sebaa (Casablanca, Casablanca-Settat) calling for the release of a BDS activist who was arrested after he participated to a gathering in front of the US consulate in Casablanca. He was denouncing the use of the Tanger Med port by a cargo ship delivering weapons to Israel.

On 26 November 2024, activists staged a protest sit-in in front of the tribunal of Ain Sebaa (Ain-Sebaa, Casablanca-Settat) calling for the liberation of a BDS activist who was arrested following a pro-Palestinian protest in front of the US consulate.

On 7 February 2025, at the call of the Moroccan Commission for the Support of the Islamic Nation Causes, dozens of people, including Al Adl Wa Al Ihssane activists, held a protest in Ouislane (Meknes, Fes-Meknes) against Israeli and US President Donald Trump's plan to displace Palestinians from Gaza. The demonstration condemned the initiative and expressed solidarity with the Palestinian people.

The protesters were demanding the Chinese Company to address their 10-point demand, including payment of the minimum wage set by the district.

On 10 March 2010, hundreds of Tibetans, including Buddhist monks and nuns, and some Westerners, demonstrated in the capital on the anniversary of an uprising against the Chinese annexation of Tibet. Several protesters were arrested.

The police on Sunday, the anniversary of 2008 riots in Lhasa, arrested 11 Tibetan exiles including three women for staging a protest and chanting anti-China slogans in the restricted zone of the Chinese consular section at Hattisar.

Police on Wednesday intervened and rounded up around three dozen cadres of CPN-Maoist from Sundhara, Kathmandu while they were staging protest seeking abrogation of the Lipulek agreement signed between India and China.

Around 22 August 2022 (as reported), hundreds of people from youth department of Rashtriya Ekta Abhiyan (National Unity Campaign), including Hindu group, held a protest rally in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district), demanding the revocation of the agreement on China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), the cancellation of the Muslim Commission, and the establishment of Nepal as a Hindu nation. The youth wing of the civil society organization accused the BRI agreement of being anti-nationalistic and the Muslim Commission of embracing and promoting 'Jihadi' ideology.

On 20 August 2022, hundreds of youths of the National Unity Campaign staged a protest rally in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district), accusing the Muslim Commission of embracing and promoting the 'Jihadi' ideology. The protesters were also demanding the revocation of the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) agreement stating it to be anti-national. The Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is a global infrastructure development strategy adopted by the Chinese government in 2013 to invest in nearly 150 countries and international organizations.

On 12 September 2022, locals, including ward chairpersons of CPN(UML), blocked the Mahendra Highway by protesting at Harakpur chowk in Gaindakot municipality (Nawalpur district). The protesters accused the Chinese contractor of being extremely negligent in the highway construction.
On 16 September 2022, National Unity Campaign staged a protest in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district) against Chinese expansionism.

Around 12 November 2022 (as reported), National Unity Campaign staged a protest in the Rajbiraj area (Saptari district), accusing President of JSPN and the Chief Minister of Madhesh province of promoting Jihadi activities in the province at the behest of China and Pakistan.

Violence and vandalism marked the second day of the Madhesi Janadhikar Forum (MJF)-imposed Madhes bandh. Bandh enforcers vandalised a Chinese Embassy vehicle in Inaruwa, where five people were also injured in a clash with police.
MCC

On 4 July 2023, members of the National Unity Campaign staged a protest at Maitighar Mandala in Kathmandu City (Kathmandu district). The protesters expressed their objection to the statement made by the Chinese Ambassador, which linked Chinese support for the construction of Pokhara International Airport to the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). The BRI is a global infrastructure development strategy initiated by the Chinese government in 2013, aiming to invest in nearly 150 countries and international organizations.

On 31 August 2023, NSU staged a protest in front of the Chinese Embassy in Kathmandu City (Kathmandu district) against China's new map for failing to incorporate Nepal's actual territories (disputed territories of Limpiyadhura, Kalapani, and Lipulekh) in its new map.

On 8 September 2023, members of the LSP staged a protest in Jaleswar municipality (Mahottari district). The protesters were against the remarks made by China's ambassador to Nepal on Nepal-India economic relations.

On 4 October 2023, people's organizations of the NCP staged a protest in Kathmandu City (Kathmandu district) against the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) agreement. The MCC agreement, which includes a $500 million infrastructure grant to Nepal by MCC, a US aid agency, was ratified in parliament on February 27, 2022.

On 17 October 2023, the CPN(RM) staged a protest in front of the Israeli embassy in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district). The protesters demanded that Israel cease its attack on Gaza and accused both Israel and America of causing fear and suffering among the Palestinian people. The protesters also called for the protection of the Palestinian people and the establishment of peace in Palestine.

On 7 September 2023, members of the National Unity Campaign demonstrated in front of the Chinese Embassy in Kathmandu City (Kathmandu district). The protesters were against China's ambassador to Nepal and accused him of interfering in Nepal's internal affairs and making controversial remarks on Nepal-India trade relations.

On 21 March 2024, ANNISU-S staged a protest in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district) against a program by the American army at Shivapuri School, opposing American imperialism and asserting national independence.

On 11 September 2023, activists, including an independent member of parliament, a doctor, an official of the National Student Council, and youths associated with the National Unity Campaign, staged a protest rally in Kathmandu City (Kathmandu district). The protesters were against the Chinese ambassador to Nepal, accusing him of interfering in Nepal's internal affairs and making controversial remarks on Nepal-India trade relations.

On 31 October 2023, locals staged a protest along the Mahendra highway in Bhedabari locality (Nawalpur district). The protesters expressed their dissatisfaction with the government for its perceived lack of concern, and with a Chinese contractor company for the delays and subpar quality of work in the completion of the Narayangadh-Butwal road expansion project.

On 29 May 2024, supporters of a cricketer, including a member of parliament elected from the RPP, staged protests at various locations in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district). The protesters were demanding that the US Embassy grant the cricketer a US visa to play in the T20 World Cup being held in the US.

On 17 March 2024, the Chure (hill range) and Forest Protection Campaign staged a protest in Birganj city (Parsa district). The protesters were against the activities of a Chinese company involved in excavating and destroying the Chure region in Siraha and Saptari districts under the guise of constructing the Mahendra Highway.

Cadres of Netra Bikram Chand led CPN Maoist torched a taxi at Sorhakhutte, Kathmandu on Friday. The CPN Maoist called a nationwide general strike against the constitution drafting process and Lipulek agreement signed between India and China on Friday.

On 5 July 2024, protesters associated with the Chure (hill range) and Forest Protection Campaign staged a protest in Amlekhgunj town (Bara district). The protesters were against a Chinese company's claimed destruction of the Chure (hill range) under the pretext of building the Mahendra Highway.

On 4 January 2025, various organizations staged a protest rally in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district), opposing the Nepal-China buffalo meat export agreement. The protesters claimed it contradicts Nepal's cultural values and demanded its cancellation.

On 18 February 2025, protesters, including a doctor who is also a medical reform activist, staged a protest near the US Embassy in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district). The protesters were demanding reconsideration of aid-cut decisions made by the Trump administration after taking office as US President.

Around 22 February 2025 (as reported), the National Student Council demonstrated by torching cycles at Laxmanawa Chowk in Birganj City (Parsa District). The demonstrators were accusing China of distributing old and substandard bicycles as aid to humiliate Madhesh students.

On 6 March 2025, the NRF staged a protest at Maitighar Mandala in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district). The protesters were against America's attempt to colonize Palestine and in solidarity with Palestinians struggling for independence.

On 8 July 2024, protesters associated with Rashtriya Ekta Abhiyan staged a protest at the gate of Pokhara Airport in Pokhara city (Kaski district), objecting to its inclusion in China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). The protesters were making various demands, including the conversion of loans into grants, environmental impact studies, and an investigation into alleged corruption during construction.

Youths and students affiliated to Nepal Peasants and Workers Party demonstrated against the murder of ousted Libya's leader Muammar Gaddhafi in Bhaktapur. Some 300 youth's chanted slogans against America and the country of its satellite citing their greed for oil ultimately led to the death of Gaddafi. The rally, initiated at Suryamadi, converged into a corner meeting at Dudhpati in the district.

On 11 August 2024, protesters led by the National Unity Campaign Nepal staged a protest in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district). The protesters demanded an end to Chinese interference in Nepal and the dismissal of the Civil Aviation Authority's Director General, among other demands.

properties.actor: JTMM-R: Democratic Terai Liberation Front-Rajan Mukti
properties.notes: A bomb exploded in front of Simyaks Meat Factory in Narsingha of Sunsari in 5 Sept. The compound walls of the factory were damaged by the blast, and it was known that the Chinese funded factory was the target of the attack. Police are further investigating. From last few months Khambhuwan Mukti Morcha (Samyukta) and Terai Janatantrik Mukti Morcha have been terrorizing Sunsari and Morang districts with such incidents.

Police detained more than 100 Tibetan exiles who were demonstrating against Chinese rule over their homeland. The Tibetan demonstrators who had gathered for a prayer meeting on the outskirts of Katmandu started chanting anti-China slogans, so the police detained the demonstrators in detention centers.

Renewed protests against China by Tibetan exiles despite a protracted crackdown by security forces became violent with angry demonstrators throwing stones at baton-wielding cops as the latter tried to pull down portraits of the Dalai Lama and banners announcing a prayer ceremony for those who had laid down their lives for religious and political freedom in Tibet. Police in Nepal are hunting for a Tibetan woman who tried to pour kerosene oil on herself and set herself on fire but was prevented by remonstrating bystanders. The attempt made police sweep down on the Samdupling Tibetan settlement in Kathmandu valley and detain 18 people found carrying cans of kerosene.

Nepalese police arrested nine Tibetan demonstrators, who waved Tibetan flags and chanted 'we want a free Tibet,' near the Chinese consular offices in Kathmandu. Four were arrested on suspicion of anti-China activity and five for carrying out anti-China demonstrations.

A group of students took out a protest in Kaliaya on Wednesday [28 October]. They protested against China's decision to support the government's policy to procure fuel from china instead of trying to end the crisis through talks with agitating Madhes-based parties.

On 20 October 2015, the police arrested three protesters on the charge of burning a Chinese flag in Birganj (Parsa, Narayani). Madhesi leaders said they had torched the flag in protest of China's support in easing the fuel crisis in Nepal.

Assumed on 31 March 2020, around 30 Chinese workers clashed with locals at Marsyangdi rural municipality's Thulobesi locality (Lamjung district). The clash occurred after two trucks laden with construction materials were brought at the Nyadi Hydropower construction site, defying the nationwide lockdown enforced by the government due to the coronavirus outbreak. Police intervened to take the situation under control.

On 30 June 2020, the civil society staged a protest against the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) agreement in Dhankuta city (Dhankuta district). The protesters claimed that the agreement is anti-national and rather an allusion for increasing US interference in Nepal and demanded that the government not proceed with the MCC compact.

On 12 May 2020, people associated with NSU and Nepal Tarun Dal protested by burning effigies of Nepali Prime Minister Oli, Indian Prime Minister Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Gorkha Municipality-12 (Gorkha district). The protesters were voicing against the encroachment of Nepali territories.
On 7 July 2020, 10 to 15 youths staged a protest in front of the Chinese Embassy in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district), against alleged interference by China in Nepal's internal affairs.

On 28 September 2020, police intervened in the protest staged by NSU in front of the Chinese Embassy in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district). The protesters were voicing against China's alleged encroachment of Nepal's territory in Humla district. Six people were arrested following the incident.

On 27 December 2020, police intervened in a protest staged by the demonstrators in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district), against the Chinese delegation's visit to Nepal. The protesters voiced against the Chinese intervention in Nepal. Police arrested 27 people following the incident.

On 24 March 2021, a clash ensued between Chinese contractors and Nepali workers at the site office of Narayanghat-Butwal Road Project in Rajahar village around Kawasoti area (Nawalpur district), over a dispute related to unpaid salaries of the workers. Six people were injured during the incident.
MCC

On 29 September 2019 in Matagalpa, on the neighborhood El Progreso, a US female citizen was shot and killed. The family of the victim accuse the paramilitary to have been the perpetrators, while the National Police states the death was caused by personal disputes. The Nicaraguan partner of the deceased woman had received threats (the wall of his house was painted with a death threat one month earlier) for protesting against the regime of Ortega.
Police arrest 26 in Kano who were on the verge of riot as they protested the visit from US President George W. Bush.

Around 22 June 2021 (as reported), locals staged a protest against the Chinese company responsible for road construction in Sindhupalchok district around Chautara area (Sindhupalchok district). The protesters blamed the company for causing environmental disaster resulting in landslides and damaging houses in the district, and demanded payment for the damages faced by them.

On 28 September 2021, about 200 NGO members and cadres of Democratic Youth Student Union, close to LSP, staged a protest in Kathmandu city (Kathmandu district), against China's alleged encroachment on Nepal's land in Humla district. The protesters also demanded the government to manage internship opportunities for the MBBS students, who had recently graduated from China.
On 6 January 2020, members of IM in Abuja demonstrated over the assassination of Iranian general Soleimani in Baghdad and burnt US flags.
On 5 February 2020, a group of supporters of the President gathered at the US embassy in Abuja (Abuja LGA, FCT) to speak out against US intervention in Nigerian affairs.
Protests against a group of Chinese construction workers in Ibadan. The protesters accused the construction workers of damaging utility and the management of insensitivity to the people's plight.
On 26 November 2019, unidentified gunmen attacked a mining site in Itagunmodi, killed a police officer on duty and abducted three Chinese workers. One worker sustained gunshot wounds.

Around 1 June 2020 (as reported), a group gathered in Lagos (Lagos Island LGA, Lagos) to demonstrate against police violence against African-Americans in the United States of America, in support of the Black Lives Matter movement.
On 21 April 2020, over 100 followers of a clergyman demonstrated at the Chinese embassy in Lagos (Lagos Island LGA, Lagos) over the ill-treatment of Nigerians in China.

On 25 April 2020, a local youth gang ambushed a Chinese mining convoy accompanied by police officers on their way from a mining site to Abakaliki (Eboyni LGA, Ebonyi). 1 Police officer was stabbed to death and his rifle stolen.
On 3 June 2020, unidentified gunmen abducted 2 Chinese miners from a mining site in Ihietutu in Ishiagu (Ivo LGA, Ebonyi)
On 22 July 2020, unidentified gunmen clashed with police officers and abducted 4 Chinese workers in Oban (Akamkpa LGA, Cross River). 1 police officer who guarded the company was killed.
Unknown Militant group kidnaps 5 Chinese Telecom Workers

On 27 November 2020, unidentified gunmen clashed with a police operative attached to a Chinese Engineer along the new Ado-Iyin Road in Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti LGA, Ekiti), and abducted the Engineer. One reported fatality and one injury. Victim was later released. Unclear whether ransom was paid.
On 14 December 2020, unidentified gunmen abducted a Chinese national at Gindin Dorowa (Wukari LGA, Taraba) but were repelled by Nigerian police operatives. One reported fatality.
Around 16 December 2020 (as reported), violence erupted between Hausa miners and Chinese expatriates at Idoko village (Obokun LGA, Osun) over access to a mining site. Two reported fatalities.

On 1 February 2021, Fulani pastoralists clashed with a police operative attached to three Chinese workers at Ifewara (Atakumosa East LGA, Osune), and abducted the workers. Militiamen demanded ransom. Victims were later released. Unclear whether ransom was paid. One reported fatality.
On 2 March 2021, unidentified gunmen abducted a Chinese construction supervisor at Igbemo-Ekiti (Irepodun/Ifelodun LGA, Ekiti). Reason for abduction unknown.
On 31 March 2021, unidentified gunmen abducted two Chinese workers at Oba (Obafemi-Owode LGA, Ogun). Gunmen demanded ransom. Kidnapped victims were later released. Unclear whether ransom was paid.

On 7 May 2021, members of the Islamic Movement of Nigeria staged demonstrations in Abuja (Abuja Municipal LGA, FCT) and burned Israeli and US flags to express solidarity with Palestine. Community sources report police forces arrested and assaulted demonstrators. Police sources on the other hand report demonstrators vandalized property, attacked residents and security operatives, and killed a policeman. 49 demonstrators were arrested.

On 5 April 2021, unidentified armed men abducted two Chinese miners at a gold mining site in Ifewara (Atakumosa East LGA, Osun). Kidnappers demanded ransom. Kidnapped victims were later released. Unclear whether ransom was paid.

On 7 April 2021, unidentified gunmen clashed with a police operative attached to three Chinese workers at a construction site in Ukum LGA (Benue) [coded to Sankera] and abducted the workers. Three reported fatalities, including one Chinese worker.
On 14 June 2021, a Taraba communal militia attacked a mining site at Arufu (Wukari LGA, Taraba), killing one and abducting two Chinese nationals. Unknown reason for attack.
An American Lutheran missionary traveling in Kano State was killed by armed robbers along a highway.

On 16 June 2021, unidentified gunmen clashed with police operatives attached to four Chinese expatriates at Adeaga/Alaagba village (Odedah LGA, Ogun) [coded to Odeda] and abducted the expatriates. One reported fatality. Kidnapped victims were later released.

On 14 June 2021, members of a militia clashed with police officers and officers of the NSCDC in the Goran Namahe / Goran Namaye ward, Maradum (Maradun LGA, Zamfara) as the group attacked a Chinese business. Six people were killed (including officers of the police and NSCDC).

On 4 January 2022, members of a Niger militia clashed with security guards escorting Chinese's nationals in in Shiroro LGA (Niger). Two guards and one Chinese national were killed and between two and four other Chinese nationals were abducted by the militiamen; the police claimed to have rescued four Chinese expatriates on 5 January.

On 8 March 2022, residents of Araromi Ajegunle community protested in Araromi (Shagamu, Ogun) over claims of forceful possession of their lands by a Chinese company. The protesters demanded for the intervention of the state government.
Around 15 December 2021 (month of), suspected militia members killed one Chinese national and abducted two others from the Zungeru Hydro power plant (Wushishi, Niger).

On 9 May 2022, cocoa farmers from Ofosu community blocked (means not specified) the Lagos/Benin Expressway in or around Ofosu (Idanre, Ondo) while protesting over claims of the sale of their farmlands to a Chinese company by the state government.
NUG protested at the entrance of the US embassy for their inclusion on the US terror watch list following the attempt made by the underwear bomber.

On 6 June 2022, a combined team of security operatives repelled an attack by Kaduna militiamen on commuters at Sabon Sara village, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna). Three abductees including a Chinese national were rescued, the militiamen fled and abandoned eight of their motorcycles. Casualties are unknown.
A civil rights leader starts a protest outside the hotel where former British PM Tony Blair and former US President Bush were staying.

On 29 June 2022, a Niger militia clashed with policemen and ambushed soldiers providing reinforcement when they attacked a mining site at Ajata-Aboki, near Galapai (Shiroro, Niger). 35 soldiers, 7 mobile policemen, and 6 civilians were killed, several persons were wounded, between 2 and 4 Chinese nationals and other workers were abducted. Seven Chinese abductees were rescued by troops of the Nigerian Air Force on 17 December.

On 7 July 2022, an unidentified armed group attacked a quarry site, killed one policeman, injured one other and abducted a Chinese citizen in Shao (Moro, Kwara). The abductee was rescued by the police after the abductors abandoned him and fled.
On 9 October 2022, an unidentified armed group on motorcycles disarmed policemen at a mining site at Iboko (Izzi, Ebonyi) and killed one Chinese expatriate whom the policemen were protecting.

On 9 October 2022, an unidentified armed group clashed with policemen when they invaded a quarry owned by Chinese nationals in Zuba (Gwagwalada, FCT). One policeman was killed, another one whom they attempted to abduct was abandoned with gunshot wounds.

On 12 October 2022, hundreds of protesters from a coalition of civil society groups protested in Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT) against the illegal slaughter of donkeys by Chinese nationals despite the ban that was placed by the government.

On 11 July 2018, gunmen, presumably a Zamfara militia, abducted a Chinese national, employee of a construction company, in Amumu, coded as Birnin Tudu (Bakura, Zamfara). There are no details about ransom demands.
On 24 November 2020, an armed group abducted a Chinese expatriate and a driver (assumed to be a local Nigerian) along the Donga-Road in Donga LGA (Taraba); there are reports about ransom demands.

Combination of two related events. On 15 April 2019, an armed group abducted five Chinese nationals in Niger state. Location coded to Minna (Minna, Niger); the abductees were rescued by the police on 5 May (coded separately); On 9 May 2019, policemen clashed with a Niger militia who abducted 5 Chinese nationals on 15 April (coded separately). Two from the armed group were killed and the abductees were rescued. Location coded to Minna (Minna, Niger).

Combination of two related events. On 17 December 2022, the special forces of the Nigerian Air Force clashed with a Kaduna militia and rescued seven Chinese abductees in Gwaska (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and Kamfanin Doka [coded separately] who were previously abducted in Niger state [coded separately]. The militiamen fled, abandoned their weapons and the abductees; On 17 December 2022, the special forces of the Nigerian Air Force clashed with a Kaduna militia and rescued seven Chinese abductees in Kamfanin Doka (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and Gwaska [coded separately] who were previously abducted in Niger state [coded separately]. The militiamen fled, abandoned their weapons and the abductees.
On 3 January 2023, members of the IMN demonstrated in Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT) over the murder of an Iranian general by the USA. The demonstrators set an American flag ablaze.

On 22 December 2022, a Zamfara militia engaged policemen and a local defense militia who responded to a distress call in an armed clash in Maradun LGA (Zamfara) where the assailants ambushed two Chinese citizens and their police escort. One of the Chinese and 11 of the assailants were killed, an unspecified number of others were wounded, two rifles and cutlasses were recovered by the policemen.

On 21 February 2023, Amotekun operatives in collaboration with local hunters clashed with an unidentified armed group at Ayanma area in Iganna town (Iwajowa, Oyo) following a tip off and foiled an attempt by the group to abduct a Chinese national. One member of the group was killed, four escaped with gunshot wounds and two were arrested. One rifle was recovered and handed over to the police alongside the arrested persons.

On 13 October 2023, the Islamic Movement in Nigeria, for the second time in the week, burnt the American and Israeli flags in Abuja (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory), demonstrating against the 'attack on females and children in Gaza'. They marched from Annur Mosque in Wuse11 along IBB way immediately after the Juma'at Prayer, terminated at the traffic light at Ahamadu Bello Way.

On 31 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a Chinese expatriate near a quarry site in Lokpanta (Nneochi, Abia). The abductee was rescued by a joint security team on 5 June [there are no reports of an armed clash] and the police claimed that no ransom was paid.

On 12 October 2023, the Ajegunle/Araromi community residents protested the demolition of their houses in Makun (Shagamu, Ogun) and the seizure of their land by the government. They displayed placards with various inscriptions claiming ownership of the land. They alleged that the government sold their land to a Chinese company without compensating them.

On 1 January 2024, land owners in Igbesa town (Ado-Odo, Ogun) protested in the town against the encroachment into their land by Chinese companies occupying an area. The protesters claimed that the companies moved beyond their allotted area and used security agencies to intimidate them, policemen were at the venue of the protest but due to the presence of journalists did not disrupt the protest.

On 19 January 2024, the police engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group while raiding a forest along the Ibiono Ibom axis of the Calabar-Itu-Ikot Ekpene, coded to Oko Ita (Ibiono Ibom, Akwa Ibom). The militiamen laid an ambush to abduct the Chinese expatriates working in the area. The police stormed the hideout and engaged them in a shootout. They outgunned the militiamen and arrested ten. They recovered four AK-47 rifles and some locally made pistols from them. There were no fatalities.

On 7 March 2024, an unidentified armed group shot and killed an NSCDC officer at a construction site in Obangede (Okehi, Kogi). The armed group invaded the site and opened fire sporadically on the people. They abducted a Chinese engineer and injured many other people.

On 10 March 2024, an unidentified armed group numbering six abducted a Chinese national from a guest house around Eyenkorin in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) where he was lodged. The police claimed to have arrested three suspects in connection with the abduction. The abductee was rescued on 19 March by operatives of the state police command (there are no further details on ransom payment or a clash).

Traders begin a protest march against some Chinese business men who they accused of undermining and killing their businesses. Speaking during the protest, the national Chairman of the association, Mr. Azubike Nwachukwu , said Nigerian dealers have been operating at a loss since the Chinese business men started retail selling of the leather products at a very cheap price.

On 5 November 2024, a Niger militia attacked and killed ten farmers, including women and a Chinese citizen, in the Wayam community, also spelt as Wyam (Rafi, Niger) and Belu-Belu villages, coded separately. The assailants beheaded six people and went away with their heads. Many people sustained gunshot injuries and were taken to the hospital while others deserted the villages. The militia abducted many others after setting houses and food items on fire. Ten fatalities shared across the two events; five fatalities coded.

On 7 November 2024, an unidentified armed group, dressed in military camouflage, shot and killed a Police Inspector and abducted two Chinese nationals and a Nigerian at a Qaurry Camp in Akankpa LGA, location coded to LGA administrative headquarters, Akamkpa (Akamkpa, Cross River). They took away the police rifle.

Thousands of Muslims, under the auspices of a pro-Iranian Shiite group, Islamic Movement, gather to burn US and Israeli flags and denouncing a US made anti-Islamic film, following the possible AQIM attack in Benghazi and other worldwide protests.

On 11 August 2024, an unidentified armed group abducted two Chinese expatriates in the Kemta/ Abule -Owu area, along Onigbedu Road, coded to Kemta (Obafemi, Ogun). The expatriates left their factory and travelled about one kilometer to visit a friend without security details.

On 22 July 2024, an unidentified armed group killed five people and abducted two Chinese nationals during an attack on a mining site in Zango Daji (Adavi, Kogi). Among the dead were three guards and two workers from the site, all of whom were Nigerians.

properties.actor: Boko Haram - Jamaatu Ahli is-Sunnah lid-Dawati wal-Jihad
properties.notes: Boko Haram gunmen attack a small town market with firearms, killing three Chinese construction workers an a Nigeria aid.

Around 16 March 2025 (as reported), a mob vandalized an SUV transporting three Chinese nationals and their police escort in Manigi (Mashegu, Niger) for failing to stop after hitting a girl in Tashan-Hajiya village. Motorcycle riders chased the SUV to Manigi, where a tire burst due to poor road conditions, and then attacked them. Police rescued the victims from the mob. There were no casualties.
Several hundred protesters gather outside the US embassy in Abuja to denounce perceived corruption the embassy has in its dealings with the Nigerian Government.
Gunmen shot and killed two Chinese construction workers in rural Borno state, motive unknown.
Militant youths in Nigerias volatile Niger Delta have kidnapped two Chinese oil workers.

Over 100 youths working for a Chinese company, Linda Manufacturing Company at Agege protested to Lagos State House of Assembly over the death of their colleague. The protesting workers alleged he was denied medical treatment after he complained of stomach pain.
Employees of a Chinese construction company protest compensation they believe unfair.

Muslims in Borno and Yobe states are holding special prayers called qunut in support of the people of Afghanistan and for the retreat of the Anglo-American forces following US military strikes against the Central Asian country. Accompanying demonstrations were held in Yobe and Borno states.
Nigerians working for a Chinese company protested their employment termination.

A coalition of civil society groups protest at the US Embassy in Lagos against what they termed Amnesty Internationals interference in war against terrorism in the country, describing the interference as a grand ploy to frustrate the countries security agencies.
Unidentified gunmen kidnap two Chinese workers in Agada (Agwada).
Two Chinese nationals are kidnapped in Odeda LGA. The pair was rescued in the following week.
Residents protest an alleged land takeover by a Chinese company.

On 27 October 2020, unknown gunmen abducted a U.S. national at his home in Massalata (Birni N'Konni, Tahoua). American special operations forces liberated the individual taken hostage in a rescue operation on October 31 between Gaidu and Kalmalo (Illela, Sokoto) in Nigeria.
A Chinese miner is attacked and killed and another injured by gunmen in Alogani. The motive for the attack ins not known.

On 20 August 2023, a number of people demonstrated in support of the military junta CNSP in the town of Agadez (Tchirozerine, Agadez). The demonstrators called for the closure of the American military base in Agadez.

On 15 March 2024, the synergy of civil society organizations of Niger staged a demonstration in front of the US embassy in Niamey (Ville de Niamey, Niamey). The organization denounced American interferences in the current transition in Niger and called for the departure of American soldiers deployed in Niger.

properties.actor: JNIM: Group for Support of Islam and Muslims
properties.notes: On 6 June 2021, presumed JNIM militants abducted two Chinese miners at a mining site in MBanga (Kollo, Tillaberi). The militants also seized belongings from workers at the site. The two abductees showed up on 1 February 2022 near the mine of Boungou (Partiaga, Tapoa). It is unclear whether they were released or escaped.

properties.actor: MPLJ: Patriotic Movement for Freedom and Justice
properties.notes: On 1 February 2025, armed militants (likely MPLJ, based on location) kidnapped a Chinese worker in the surroundings of the Agadem oil field (N'Gourti, Diffa).

properties.actor: Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (ISGS)
properties.notes: Nigerien & US troops reportedly killed in ambush by presumed 'ISGS' following attack on village Tongo Tongo: 4 US soldiers & 4 Nigerien soldiers killed; 2 US soldiers & 8 Nigerien soldiers wounded

properties.actor: Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) - Greater Sahara Faction
properties.notes: On 8 June 2019, a U.S. armored vehicle was struck by an IED at a firing range near Ouallam, no casualties were reported, the device was most likely planted by ISGS militants.
Gunmen kidnap a Chinese oil worker.

On 7 May 2022, at the call of AI and several feminist associations, including Women Inc., hundreds of people staged a protest on Dam Square in Amsterdam to denounce the US Supreme Court's plan to overturn abortion rights in the US. A group of 20 to 30 demonstrators headed towards the US consulate, blocking tramway lines and graffitiing streetcars, and resisted police forces as they attempted to arrest a female demonstrator. Two people were arrested.

On 30 June 2022, around 30 people staged a protest in Volkel against the alleged presence of American nuclear weapons at the military airbase in Volkel and the future deployment of F35 aircrafts there.

Property destruction: On 16 June 2024, FPL militants destroyed the Niger - Benin grude pipeline west of Tesker (Tesker, Zinder). In a statement, its leader Mahmoud Sallah claimed responsibility of the attack and asked the Chinese oil company WAPCO to cancel the $400 million loan granted to the junta, otherwise, all oil installations will be paralyzed.
