On 11 April 2018, civil society members staged a protest demonstration outside the National Press Club over the death of a youth in an accident involving the US military attache.

On 23 February 2018, dozens of women staged a protest demonstration on the China Pakistan Economic Corridor route at Sheenbar Nagir, Gilgit district, to demand an end to electricity cuts in their area.

The resident of Digri under the banner of the Ulema Action Committee staged a mammoth protest demonstration against the pastor of a church in US who plans to desecrate the Holy Quran to protest against the 9/11 incident and operating of a local wine den in the city on 10 Sep 2010.
On 15 May 2018, students with Islami Jamiat-e-Talaba Pakistan staged a protest demonstration outside the US consolate in Lahore - Data Gunj Buksh (Punjab) against the United State and Israel.
Locals in Shawal, NWA protested against drone strikes by the US Military near Miranshah on 14 Sep 2010. They also recovered dead bodies from the debris.

On 3 February 2010, 4 schoolgirls, 3 US soldiers, an FC soldier and at least 2 other people were killed in a suicide bomb blast carried out by an Uzbek TTP militant near a school in Koto, while 124 others were injured, including 2 US soldiers and 70 schoolgirls. The attack allegedly targeted the schoolgirls and not the American personnel. The Koto Girls High School was devastated in the explosion. The U.S. embassy released a statement saying the US soldiers were working to train FC forces in the area.
Anjuman Hussaini took out protest rallies against the US and Israel aggressions in Palestinie on 17 Sep 2010 in Larkana.

Thousands of people belonging to different walks of life staged a protest rally for repatriation of Dr Aafia Siddiqui in Karachi on 23 Sep 2010. The Protesters started marching from Karachi Press Club to the US Consulate where they staged sit-in. The police broke up this peaceful protest with batons.
Activists of the Balochistan chapter of JI held a demonstration to protest against the conviction of Dr. Aafia Siddiqui in the U.S.

On 26 March 2018, dozens of farmers and land owners staged a protest demonstration near the Karna Sher Khan interchange just outside the village of Rashakai, Nowshera district, against the construction of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.

On 15 April 2018, landowners from around Nowshera staged a protest demonstration in the town against Chief Minister Pervez Khattak for allegedly taking their land for a mega city project under the China Pakistan Economic Corridor.
On 15 October 2018, after a US consulate vehicle hit and injured a motorcyclist in Karachi town (Sindh), passers-by encircled the car in protest.

On 11 August 2018, a suicide bombing attack, claimed by the BLA, targeted a civilian bus transporting Chinese engineers to a mining project in the Dalbandin area of Balochistan Province. The bomber was killed; 6 people, including 3 Chinese, the bus driver, and 2 paramilitary soldiers (Frontier Constabulary), were wounded. This is reportedly the first time a Baloch separatist group has claimed a suicide attack.

On Sep 28, relatives of Pakistanis who have been in Chinese jails for many years staged a protest outside of the Press Club in Peshawar city (KP) to demand action from PM Imran Khan and the Chief Justice to obtain their relatives' freedom.

On 25 January 2019, Civil Progressive Alliance along with civil rights activists and civil society members staged a protest outside Karachi Press Club in Saddar town (Karachi, Sindh), against the arrest of a noted American journalist Marzieh Hashemi by the US administration.

On 2 October 2018, a large number of residents staged a protest march in Muzaffarabad town (AJK) against Pakistan and China for looting their resources, mostly in reference to plans to construct a hydropower plant on the Neelum River.

On 23 November 2018, BLA members opened fired at police forces during an attempted attack at the Chinese Consulate in Karachi-Clifton town (Karachi, Sindh). Two police officials, 3 alleged BLA attackers and 2 civilians were killed during the clash while one police personnel was injured.

On 29 January 2019, residents of Dodial, Shahta and adjoining areas supported by JI youth wing staged a protest rally in Dodial area near Mansehra city (Mansehra, KP), against a Chinese company, demanding the construction of an underpass to link areas detached by the Hazara Motorway project

On 20 March 2019, people affected by the Suki Kanari Hydropower Project staged a protest in Shangria area of Kaghan valley (populated place in Kaghan valley coded) (Balakot, Manshera, KP), demanding market price for their land acquired by the district administration for the hydropower project under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor Project.
On 16 May 2019, MWM workers and leaders protested in different parts of the Karachi (Karachi, Sindh) against the US policy towards Iran.

On 5 February 2018, unidentified armed men opened fire at a vehicle with two Chinese nationals and employees of a shipping company near Zamzama Park in Clifton town (Karachi, Sindh) killing one of the Chinese nationals and injuring a passerby.

On 11 May 2019, three BLA militants fatally shot a security guard and three other hotel employees before exchanging fire with Pakistan Army and Navy personnel during an attack on the Pearl Continental Hotel in Gwadar city (Gwadar, Balochistan) allegedly targeting Chinese citizens. A navy soldier and all three militants were also killed during the exchange and six others including two army captains, two navy soldiers, and two hotel employees were reported injured.

On 23 May 2019, workers of PTI, money changers and locals torched US dollars and protested at Bank Road in Rawalpindi city (Rawalpindi, Punjab) against the government, IMF and the United States over the hike in price of the dollar.

Members of Pasban staged a protest march towards the US consulate in Karachi on Feb 10 against the detention of Dr. Aafia Siddiqui. When they tried to enter the 'red zone', Police Forces interfered and dispersed the group by using teargas and arrested some protesters.

People from right-wing, religious and banned organizations staged a protest in front of the Parliament in Islamabad, Punjab on March 27 calling on Pakistan not to reopen its Afghan border to NATO and US supplies.
A rally convoy led by PTI leader Imran Khan against the US drone attacks departure on Oct 6 from Islamabad to Dera Ismail Khan. The next day the protest march would continue to Tank.

On 22 May 2019, labourers protested in Sahianwala Industrial Estate of Chak One Hundred Fifty-three (variant Sahianwala) town (Faisalabad, Punjab) against a Chinese supervisor for pushing a labourer into a furnace and injuring the labourer.

On 1 September 2019, Aafia Movement Pakistan along with large number of PTI leaders and MPAs, leaders from JI, Pasban Pakistan and MSO, held a protest outside Islamabad Press Club in Islamabad city (Islamabad, Federal Capital Territory) demanding the release of Aafia Siddiqui from prison in America and freedom for people of Kashmir.
siddiqui

On 22 May 2019, relatives and family members of Pakistani nationals who are imprisoned in Chinese prisons, protested outside Peshawar Press Club in Peshawar city (Peshawar, KP) against the federal government for failing to release the prisoners and demanded the government to take immediate steps for release of their family members.

The relatives of the Pakistanis, imprisoned in various jails of China, on 18 Dec 2010 held a protest demonstration outside the Peshawar Press Club to press the government to play its role in getting them released.
On 22 September 2019, locals held a mass protest in Ghanche district (GB) against the federal government's decision of leasing local pasture land to China for mining.

As reported on October 14, employees and scores of labourers of working with a Chinese company who became victims of a highway robbery protested by blocking Patan Road near Rawlpindi city (assumed based on city line) (Rawalpindi, Punjab) demanding arrest of the robbers and recovery of their money and valuables.

On 3 January 2020, Majlis-e-Wahdat Muslimeen held a in Landhi town (Karachi city, Sindh), condemning the killing of General Qassem Soleimani, the head of Iran's elite Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC's) Quds Force, and Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis, deputy commander of the Iraqi Popular Mobilization Forces, in a US air strike at the Baghdad International Airport.

Combination of two related events. On 24 May 2017, two Chinese language teachers were kidnapped by armed men disguised as policemen in Quetta city (Quetta, Balochistan). IS is believed to be responsible for the attack; Security forces killed a dozen Islamic State (ISIS) militants in the Splinji area of Mastung at the end of a three-day raid prompted by intelligence reports that the group were holding two recently kidnapped Chinese nationals.

On 31 January 2020, local leaders held a protest demonstration in Clifton town (Karachi, Sindh), to show solidarity with Palestinians and express anger against the Israeli aggression and the US for their bad designs.
Thousands of protesters gathered in Lahore to demand the hanging of Raymond Davis, an American national who shot and killed two Pakistanis. The protest took place on 1 February 2011.
On 25 February 2011, activists of Tanzeem-e-Islami took out a protest to demonstrate against American drones and American interference in Islamabad.

On 31 January 2020, family members of students staged a protest at the Chakdarra Press Club in Chakdarra town (Lower Dir, KPK), to seek safe return of the students studying in China due to the fear of coronavirus.
Activists of Jamaat AhleSunnat staged a protest against the release of US national Raymond Davis on 17 March 2011 in Hyderabad.
On 12 August 2020, locals took out a massive protest rally at Muzaffarabad city (Muzaffarabad, AJK) against construction of a dam by China.
Protesters in Bannu burnt US flags and Obama effigies to protest against drone attacks on 24 March 2011.
Activists from JUI-F held a protest and torched US flags in a demonstration against Terry Jones, a priest, in Karachi on 25 March 2011.
Religious parties staged country-wide protests against an American evangelical priest, the release of Raymond Davis and drone strikes in Islamabad on 1 Apr 2011.
Tahaffuz-e-Namoos-e-Risalat Mahaz (TNRM) staged a protest demonstrations and sit-in against the desecration of Holy Quran by US pastor Terry Jones in front of the American Consulate on 5 Apr 2011.

Leftist political parties and movements on 10 Apr 2011 held a protest against the US war on terror at the Charing Cross in Lahore. The protesters chanted slogans against the US war on terror, drone attacks, NATO supply and attack on Libya.
On 24 August 2020, people held a massive protest at Muzaffarabad city (Muzaffarabad, AJK) over construction of a dam by Chinese firms on Neelum-Jhelum river.
On 7 September 2020, a massive protest was held by people at Muzaffarabad city (AJK) against the proposed mega dam to be constructed by Chinese companies.

properties.actor: Police Forces of Pakistan (2018-2022) Frontier Corps
properties.notes: On 15 December 2020, police forces of Pakistan defused a bomb at Karachi-Clifton town (Sindh) planted on the car of a Chinese restaurant owner.
On 9 March 2021, BLF militants attacked a Chinese worker at Karachi - Lyari city (Karachi city district, Sindh). No casualties were caused in the incident.
Suspected Taliban militants attacked vehicles of a Chinese oil and gas survey company near Lachi, killing one of its guards.

On 2 April 2021, BLF militants fired rockets at the construction site of a new airport under the China-Pakistan economic corridor project at Gorandani town (Gwadar district, Balochistan). BLF claimed that heavy casualties were inflicted in the attack.
The JUI-F initiated a protest day across various cities of KPK and FATA. They were protesting against the US operation which killed Osama Bin Laden.
4000 protesters in Lahore staged a demonstration against US interference in Pakistan. JUD leaders spoke at the protest rally.
2 people were killed and 10 were injured in a remote control bomb explosion targeting a US consulate convoy in Peshawar. TTP claimed responsibility for the attack.
On 3 April 2021, BLF militants burnt down a mobile tower that belonged to a Chinese company located at Dasht town (Kech district, Balochistan). No casualties were inflicted in the attack.
Protesters in Lahore staged a demonstration against the hostilities of America, India and Israel toward Pakistan.

On 14 June 2021, hundreds of political activists from National Party, members of the civil society, students and fishers took out a protest rally in Gwadar city (Gwadar, Balochistan), against issuing of licence to the Chinese trawlers for fishing.

On 14 July 2021, twelve people, including nine Chinese engineers and three Frontier Corps personnel, were killed and several others injured in a bomb explosion on a bus near Dasu town (Kohistan, KPK). The vehicle was carrying workers to the Dasu Dam.

Property destruction: On 17 February 2021, BLF militants targeted a mobile tower of a Chinese company in Dasht (Kech) tehsil (Kech district, Balochistan). No casualties were inflicted in the incident.

On 28 July 2021, militants attacked two Chinese nationals in Gulbai area in Karachi - Site town (Karachi City, Sindh). Baloch Liberation Front claimed responsibility for the attack. The government claimed the two Chinese nationals were laborers at a factory.

On 8 October 2021, police officials arrested protesters when they tried to move towards American Consulate during a demonstration near Sindh Assembly in Karachi - Saddar town (Karachi City, Sindh), demanding release of Dr. Afia Siddiqui, who was convicted of firing at US troops in Afghanistan while in their custody and has been imprisioned in the US.

On 22 August 2021, hundreds of locals, activists of National Party and Baloch Student Organisation staged a demonstration in Gwadar city (Gwadar, Balochistan), against illegal fishing by Chinese trawlers.
Activists of a social welfare organization stage a protest in Hyderabad for the release of a woman from an American jail.

On 20 August 2021, a suicide bomber detonated his explosives near a vehicle carrying Chinese workers in Gwadar city (Gwadar, Balochistan), killing two Pakistani children playing by the roadside and injuring a Chinese and two other Pakistani nationals. BLA claimed responsibility for the attack. Fatalities coded as 3 including the suicide bomber.
9 rioters and 4 policemen were injured when a protest in Islamabad, against a gay rights party held by the US embassy, became violent.

On 17 January 2022, locals along with activists of JSMM and Sindhi nationalist parties held a protest demonstration in Sann town (Jamshoro, Sindh), against the presence of China on the coast of Sindh and the construction of a naval base.
On 23 February 2022, local women and children held a protest at Saindak town (Chagai district, Balochistan) against a Chinese company over putting strict coronavirus restrictions in the neighborhood.

On 24 April 2022, locals along with activists of JSMM took out a massive protest rally in Sann town (Jamshoro, Sindh), opposing the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) and the issue of enforced disappearances and forced conversion of Hindu girls in the region.

On 26 April 2022, a female suicide bomber targeted a van, killing three Chinese nationals (teachers) and a driver and injuring two (Chinese and a guard) at the University of Karachi in Karachi - Saddar town (Karachi City, Sindh). Balochistan Liberation Army claimed responsibility for the attack. Total fatalities counted as 5 including the suicide bomber.
A protest organized by Almi Muttahida Ulema-o-Mashaikh Council was staged in Peshawar against US interference in Pakistan.
On 12 May 2022, 'Haqq do movement' members held a protest at Gwadar city (Balochistan) where they hailed the suicide attacker who targeted the Chinese nationals at Karachi.

On 22 September 2022, members of the Aafia Movement held a protest demonstration at the press club in Karachi - Saddar town (Karachi City, Sindh), against detention of Dr. Aafia Siddiqui by US authorities.

On 16 May 2022, hundreds of locals held a protest demonstration in Gwadar city (Gwadar, Gilgit Baltistan), against the CTD personnel for arresting two women who are accused of killing Chinese nationals in a planned attack.

On 29 July 2022, members of Kohistan Tahfuz Movement (a local movement), students and residents of Herban-Shatial and Diamer areas held a protest at Shatial Bazaar town (coded as Shatial) (Diamir district, GB) against the Chinese administration and the local authorities managing the Diamir-Bhasha dam site over no jobs for locals in the dam construction and lack of compensation for the land taken for the project.

On 9 November 2022, members of the Aafia Movement held a protest demonstration at the press club in Karachi - Saddar town (Karachi City, Sindh), against detention of Dr. Aafia Siddiqui by the US authorities.

On 28 September 2022, unidentified assailants fired at a doctor, his wife and assistant running a medical clinic and holding dual Chinese and Pakistani citizenship in a targeted attack at Karachi - Saddar town (Karachi City district, Sindh). One person was killed and two others were left injured in the attack.
Different student groups staged a protest in Peshawar against US involvement in the region.

On 8 October 2022, a large number of locals, fishers and activists from Haq Do Tehreek (Give Rights to Gwadar Movement) took out a protest rally in front of Gharibabad Transport in Main Chowk in Pasni town (Gwadar, Balochistan), against Chinese trawlers and demanded basic amenities like medical facilities.

On 18 February 2023, family members, drivers and transporters working with Chinese engineers and other staff at the Dasu Hydropower Project held a protest demonstration in Mansehra city (Mansehra, KPK), demanding their salaries.

On 16 April 2023, workers at the Dasu hydropower project tried to force their way into a Chinese workers camp in Barseen and demonstrated at the Karakoram Highway in Kamila Bazaar in Dasu town (Kohistan, KPK) after an argument with a Chinese worker on the siter over prayer breaks, accusing him of blasphemy. On 17 April 2023, locals staged a protest shouting slogans at the Karakoram Highway outside the police station in Komila locality (Kohistan, KPK) over the registration of the FIR after they accused a Chinese national of blasphemy at Dasu dam site.

On 2 June 2023, activists of Islami Jamiat-e-Talba held a protest demonstration at Jinnah Hospital premises in Karachi - Saddar town (Karachi City, Sindh), demanding the release of a Pakistani national imprisoned in the US on charges of attempted murder and assault of US personnel in Afghanistan.

On 11 June 2023, scores of people held a protest at Balakot tehsil (Mansehra district, KP) to demand the immediate release of a Pakistani national imprisoned in the US on charges of attempted murder and assault of US personnel in Afghanistan.

The students of various schools and members of civil society organisations set up a protest camp in front of the US consulate to express their anger against Nato forces attack in Mohmand Agency. The camp was set up jointly by Rotary Club Peshawar New City (RCPNC) and Pakistan Thinkers Forum (PTF).
Pakistan Peoples Party Shaheed Bhutto took out a large rally led by Chairperson Ghinwa Bhutto against US atrocities here in Larkana on Thursday.

On 10 May 2023, Sindh police shot dead a suspected suicide bomber when he was planning on attacking a Chinese National in Sukkhan area of Karachi - Malir (Karachi City, Sindh). One police official was also injured in the exchange of fire.

Three security personnel and two civilians were killed and eleven others wounded in a remote controlled bomb attack on Chinese engineers in restive district Dera Bugti. The Chinese engineers remained unharmed. No group has claimed responsibility, however, police suspect Baloch militants might be behind the attack.

On 13 November 2023, in David, Chiriqui, people blocked the InterAmerican highway, specifically at the bridge over the Risacua River as part of a demonstration against the mining law under which a concession to explode a copper mine was approved and demanded the repeal of the law as well as an indefinite end to metal mining in the country. The roadblock was suspended later that day allowing normal transit. This is part of ongoing national protests (coded separately).

On 13 November 2023, in Santiago de Veraguas, Veraguas, people blocked the InterAmerican highway as part of a demonstration against the mining law under which a concession to explode a copper mine was approved and demanded the repeal of the law as well as an indefinite end to metal mining in the country. This is part of ongoing national protests (coded separately).

On 14 November 2023, in David, Chiriqui, for the second consecutive day, demonstrators protested against the roadblocks and against the mining law under which a concession to explode a copper mine was approved and demanded the repeal of the law as well as an indefinite end to metal mining in the country. The demonstration started in the Parque de las Madres, on Obadia Avenue, and toured the main roads of the city of David, ending with a rally in front of the facilities of the government of the province of Chiriqui. For the same reason, a group of people blocked the InterAmerican highway at the bridge over the Risacua River. This is part of ongoing national protests (coded separately).

On 23 December 2024, in Panama City, Panama, members of the Single Union of Construction and Associated Workers (SUNTRACS) demonstrated holding anti-Trump banners in front of the National Assembly, to reject the statements made by the elected US President with regards to the United States retaking control of the Panama Canal. The demonstrators firmly rejected the statements, stating that the canal belongs to Panama and demanded that the Panamanian President calls upon the current US ambassador to Panama to formally address the statements. During the demonstration, the Suntracs members burned a US-flag.

On 9 January 2025, in Panama City, Panama, a group from the Canal Area Communities Association (ACAC) staged a small demonstration, carrying banners and shouting slogans, outside the Ascanio Arosemena Training Center. The demonstrators demanded the equitable use of the Canal Zone, complained about the work of the Panama Canal board, and rejected the words of US President-elect Donald Trump regarding the US regaining control of the Panama Canal. The group also complained about the general inequality existing in Panama and critizised the Panama Municipality's decision to reduce the mourning hours dedicated to Martyrs' Day.

On 20 January 2025, in Panama City, Panama, one hundred people, including members of the Single Union of Construction and Associated Workers (Suntracs) demonstrated, holding banners and chanting slogans, in front of the embassy of the United States, to reject the recent statements made by the US President with regards to the US regaining control of the Panama Canal. During the demonstration, a US flag was burned as a symbolic act against the President's statements.

Around 31 January 2025 (as reported), in Panama City, Panama, a group of graduates of the National Institute, who participated in the historical gesture of planting and raising a national flag in the Canal Zone in January 1964, accompanied by civil society groups and students, gathered at the 'Eternal Flame' monument in the neighbourhood of Balboa and in the surrounding of the building of the Panama Canal Administration, to plant flags as a symbolic act to show their dissent for the recent statements of the US President Donald Trump. The demonstrators, chanting slogans, objected the US President's statements, concerning the US regaining control of the Panama Canal.

On 31 January 2025, in Panama City, Panama, members of the Single Union of Construction and Associated Workers (Suntracs) and other teachers' and students' unions blocked different roads in the city to object the statements of President Donald Trump, with regards to the US regaining control of the Panama Canal and also demonstrated against the expected visit of the US Secretary of State to Panama and against the CSS reforms. Participants clashed with police forces deployed for crowd control and threw stones and other objects at the officers. On the other hand, the police fired tear gas and blocked entry and exit to the University of Panama. Among the participants to the demonstration, the Panamanian Association of Teachers (Asoprof) was also present. Two people were arrested after the demonstration.

On 1 February 2025, in Panama City, Panama, a group of demonstrators gathered for a vigil and burned US flags, to show their dissent for the arrival of the US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in visit to Panama. The demonstrators rejected US President Donald Trump's statements concerning the US regaining control of the Panama Canal. They also demonstrated against the reforms to the Social Security Fund (CSS). The Single Union of Construction and Associated Workers (SUNTRACS) was present.

On 12 February 2025, in Panama City, Panama, members of the Single Union of Construction and Associated Workers (Suntracs) and students blocked several streets of the city. On Avenida Balboa, Suntracs members set a barricade in the construction site of the new Children's Hospital and clashed with the police, deployed for crowd control. The rioters damaged the construction site and threw stones and other blunt objects at the officers, to which the police responded by firing tear-gas and pellets. Similar clashes between students and police occurred in front of the University of Panama. The union members and students were demonstrating against the reforms of the Social Security Fund (CSS) and against US President Donald Trump's statements, concerning the US regaining control of the Panama Canal. During the clashes, 16 police officers and five people were injured and over 518 people were arrested. Relatives of the arrested people claim that many of those detained were not actively involved with the demonstration, but were passerby.

Combination of two related events. On 13 June 2022, in Panama City, Panama, a group of university students protested in front of the headquarters of the Chinese embassy in Panama against the ongoing negotiation for a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) between Panama and China; On 16 July 2022, in Panama City, Pueblo Nuevo, Panama, members of the University Student's movement staged a protest at the Chinese embassy against a free-trade agreement between Panama and China.

Around 17 July 2024 (as reported), on the Coast of Paita (Piura), around 150 fishers carried out a demonstration on open sea denouncing the presence of Chinese vessels in prohibited areas of the Peruvian sea, as well as damage on the marine ecosystem and unfair competition.

On 24 July 2024, in Piura (Piura), over 500 fishers from Piura, Sechura, and Paita municipalities, carried out a demonstration by marching through the main streets of the city demanding greater control over Chinese vessels entering the Peruvian sea. They also denounced the damage that international vessels represent for the marine life.

On 2 October 2024, in Atico district (Caraveli, Arequipa), a group of fishers carried out a demonstration by blocking the coastal road, protesting against the ministry of production, arguing the institution had issued regulations (unspecified) that affect the artisanal fishing sector and demanded the correction of those regulations. They also protested against Chinese vessels fishing in the region and demanded the borders between Lomas and Marcoma municipalities to be marked. The demonstration was called by the sector in nearby municipalities with the same demands.

On 11 October 2024, in Paita (Piura), a group of artisanal fishermen protested in the main square, demanding that the government declare a state of emergency for the fishing sector due to an ongoing economic crisis. They are particularly concerned about the shortage of giant squid and the presence of Chinese fishing vessels off the Peruvian coast. The protesters also called for the removal of several ministers, including those of Production, Transport, Defense, and Foreign Trade and Tourism for their inaction to the crisis.

Around 17 October 2024 (as reported), in Piura (Piura), a group of artisanal fishermen gathered outside the regional governor's office to demonstrate demanding the declaration of emergency for the sector due to contamination of the Peruvian sea, oil spills, as well as the presence of Chinese ships. The group denounced the new regulations of the national and regional governments are only benefiting large-scale fishers.

On 3 December 2020, in Guadalupe, Ica, a group of farmers staged a demonstration by blocking the south Pan American highway, in Alamo sector, to demand the elimination of the current Agrarian Law, that would favor a new labor system, and to provide them a better labor regime that would increase their wages and to not exceed the hours worked in a day.

On 30 December 2020, in Cusco city, farmers of Quispicanchi, Canchis and Canas blocked the South Pan American highway with sticks and stones, to support the 2nd national Farmers strike, to reject the decision of the Congress of not approving the substitute text of the new farming labor regime that would eliminate the 27360 Law. Farmers are demanding that the law should establish a decent increase in their daily wages.

On 11 March 2021, in Lima-La Victoria, Lima Province, a group of merchants of Gamarra market staged a demonstration in Gamarra e Hipolito Unanue sector to demand the government to stop imports of clothes for sale from China and Bangladesh. They claim the sale of these products harms the national textile industry.

On 13 August 2019, in Talara, Piura, citizens of El Alto, staged a demonstration against the Chinese company CNPC to demand an increase in wages and to generate more job openings for the cleaning of their lot in which they operate. On 16 August 2019, in Talara, Piura, citizens staged a demonstration against the Chinese company CNPC to demand an increase in wages and to generate more job openings for the cleaning of their lot in which they operate. They burned down offices of the company, that left no one injured.

On 6 September 2023, in Lima - Santiago de Surco (Lima), residents and members of social organizations protested outside the United Stated of America Embassy. The motives behind the protest are unknown.

On 6 February 2020, demonstrators from Anakbayan and LFS disguised as joggers lobbed paint at the US Embassy building in Manila, which also got on a police officer. The demonstrators decried the existing military agreements between the Philippines and the US, particularly the joint military exercises between the two countries. Police officers blocked the demonstrators and pushed them away, and then arrested one of them.

On 1 June 2022, in Chimbote (Ancash), workers of a services providing Chinese company staged a demonstration outside the company offices in La Caleta urbanization to complain about two months of pending salaries and payment of the Compensation for Service Time (CTS).

On 6 March 2020, GABRIELA Youth staged a demonstration in front of the US Embassy in Manila against what they called imperialist domination over the Duterte administration. The demonstrators were also marking International Women's Day.

On 3 September 2020, demonstrators led by LGBT group Bahaghari and women's group GABRIELA staged a demonstration in front of the Department of Justice in Manila (Metro Manila, National Capital Region), to condemn a local court's order for the early release of a US marine convicted of killing a Filipino transgender woman in 2014. The demonstrators also demanded the abrogation of the Visiting Forces Agreement between the United States and the Philippines, which allows US soldiers into the Philippines.

On 11 September 2020, LGBT groups and other organizations such as the Scrap VFA! Movement staged a demonstration at the Commission on Human Rights grounds in Quezon City (Metro Manila, National Capital Region), in order to condemn President Rodrigo Duterte's absolute pardon of a US marine convicted of killing a Filipino transgender woman in 2014. The demonstrators also demanded the abrogation of the Visiting Forces Agreement between the United States and the Philippines, which allows US soldiers into the Philippines.

On 22 February 2020, at least 100 demonstrators from groups like Kilusan Kontra Tsina, Oust Duterte Movement, Bunyog and Confederation against Federalism demanded the resignation of President Rodrigo Duterte during a demonstration at the People Power Monument in Quezon City on the occasion of the EDSA People Power Revolution anniversary, which toppled the late dictator Ferdinand Marcos. The demonstrators decried the president's supposed subservience to China.

On 29 January 2021, demonstrators led by Pamalakaya staged a demonstration in front of the Chinese Consular Office in Makati (Metro Manila, National Capital Region), in order to oppose China's new Coast Guard Law, which allows China's coast guard to fire at foreign vessels that enter maritime areas claimed by China.

On 24 February 2021, demonstrators led by Pamalakaya staged a demonstration at the Baywalk in Manila (Metro Manila, National Capital Region), in order to oppose China's new Coast Guard Law, which allows China's coast guard to fire at foreign vessels that enter maritime areas claimed by China.

On 7 April 2021, demonstrators led by such groups as Pamalakaya staged a demonstration by Manila Bay in Manila (Metro Manila, National Capital Region), in order to condemn the presence of Chinese vessels in Julian Felipe Reef, part of the disputed Spratly Islands, since March.

Non-violent activity: Around 21 April 2021 (week of), the Philippine military conducted military drills near the coast of Pag-asa Island (Kalayaan, Palawan, Mimaropa Region), a disputed area in the Spratly Islands claimed by the Philippines to be within its Exclusive Economic Zone, amid heightened tensions over the continued presence of Chinese vessels near Julian Felipe Reef - also claimed by the Philippines - since March. The Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson called on the Philippines to 'stop' such actions as it asserted sovereignty over the disputed areas; the Philippines responded by filing another diplomatic protest over the spokesperson's remarks, adding to the daily protests that the Philippines has been filing for weeks over the issue.

On 10 May 2021, a drug suspect - reportedly a Chinese national - was shot dead in a vigilante-style attack by unidentified assailants near Dona Soledad Avenue in Paranaque City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region). The slain suspect, who was with a paralegal at the time of the attack, had just been released from jail moments earlier, after being detained on drug charges.

Non-violent activity: On 7 June 2021, the chief of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, accompanied by other top military officials, visited Pag-asa Island, Barangay Pag-Asa (Kalayaan, Palawan, Mimaropa Region) in the disputed Spratly Islands in the South China Sea, following weeks of tension between the Philippines and China over the presence of Chinese maritime vessels in areas claimed by the Philippines as within its EEZ. The Philippine military noted that its visit to Pag-asa Island was not challenged by the Chinese, as was usual. The Philippine military officials were transported by a C-130 military plane.

On 12 June 2021, around 400-500 demonstrators from such groups as Bahaghari, Bayan Muna, Kalikasan, KARAPATAN, Makabayan, Milk Tea Alliance Philippines, Pamalakaya, and SCMP staged a demonstration to mark the 123rd Philippine Independence Day, beginning at the University of the Philippines campus in Diliman, Quezon City and at the Plaza Rajah Sulayman in Manila before converging in front of the Chinese Consulate in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region). The demonstrators called for the ouster of President Rodrigo Duterte and demanded China's withdrawal from the Philippines' EEZ in the West Philippine Sea.

On 12 June 2021, demonstrators led by BAYAN staged a demonstration near the Fountain of Justice in Bacolod City (Negros Occidental, Western Visayas), in order to mark the 123rd Philippine Independence Day. The demonstrators denounced the Philippines' alleged subservience to the US and China.

On 12 June 2021, demonstrators led by BAYAN staged a demonstration in Davao City (Davao del Sur, Davao Region), in order to mark the 123rd Philippine Independence Day. The demonstrators demanded China's withdrawal from the Philippines' EEZ in the West Philippine Sea. The demonstrators attempted to approach the Chinese Consulate in Davao City but were blocked by the police.

On 12 June 2021, demonstrators led by such groups as the League of Filipino Students staged a demonstration in Kawit town (Cavite, Calabarzon), in order to mark the 123rd Philippine Independence Day. The demonstrators lamented the country's 'false liberty' and denounced US and Chinese imperialism.

On 12 June 2021, fisherfolk led by Pamalakaya staged a demonstration in Botolan town (Zambales, Central Luzon), in order to mark the 123rd Philippine Independence Day. The demonstrators demanded China's withdrawal from the Philippines' EEZ in the West Philippine Sea and called on the government to uphold the country's sovereignty.

Around 1 November 2017, in Manila (Metro Manila, National Capital Region), demonstrators camped outside the Presidential Palace to protest against US President Trump's visit to the Philippines to join a summit of East Asian leaders.

On 21 December 2017, a group of Muslim community staged a protest rally at Bonifacio Global City in Makati city (Metro Manila, National Capital Region) to protest against US President Trump's declaration of Jerusalem as Israel's capital.

On 12 July 2021, demonstrators led by such groups as Akbayan and Pamalakaya staged a demonstration in front of the Chinese Embassy in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), in order to protest China's military presence in disputed areas claimed by the Philippines as its EEZ in the South China Sea. The demonstrators were marking the 5th anniversary of the Hague-based Permanent Court of Arbitration's ruling in favor of the Philippines against China's expansive territorial claims in the disputed region.

Arrests: On 18 July 2017, in Pasay city (Metro Manila, National Capital Region), 40 people, including around 30 Chinese nationals, were arrested by the joint PNP-Anti Kidnapping Group and Bureau of Immigration at the Solaire Resort and Casino over charges of kidnapping a Singaporean national.

On 21 May 2022, demonstrators led by such groups as BAYAN, Defend Jobs Philippines and LFS, joined by different sectors such as the youth and labor, staged a demonstration along the United Nations Avenue in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), in order to condemn US militarism and foreign policy as US President Joe Biden began his visit to Asia. The demonstrators attempted to get near the nearby US Embassy, but were dispersed by the police, who claimed that the demonstrators had no permit to rally. Police arrested a few individuals, including a student journalist. The rest of the demonstrators later moved to Plaza Kalaw.

On 24 November 2021, demonstrators led by Pamalakaya staged a protest in front of the Chinese Consulate in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), in order to condemn China for what was said to be its plunder and destruction of natural resources in disputed areas of the South China Sea, following China Coast Guard vessels' use of a water cannon against Philippine supply boats in the South China Sea on 16 November.

Around 7 August 2022 (as reported), demonstrators staged a demonstration in Mendiola, Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) against the visit of US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to the Philippines.

On 11 October 2022, members of Bahaghari staged a demonstration at the Boy Scout Circle in Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), in order to call for justice for a Filipino trans woman killed by a US soldier in Olongapo City eight years prior. The US soldier was freed from detention and allowed to leave the country in 2020 after being granted an absolute pardon by former President Rodrigo Duterte.

On 21 November 2022, demonstrators led by such groups as Bayan Muna, BAYAN, Gabriela Women's Party, ILPS, KABATAAN, KADAMAY, KMU, LFS and Migrante staged a demonstration in Morayta, Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), in order to call for the termination of the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) and other military agreements between the US and the Philippines, on the occasion of US Vice President Kamala Harris's visit to the Philippines. The demonstrators attempted to march toward Mendiola Street but were blocked by the police.

On 14 February 2022, vegetable farmers, led by the League of Associations at La Trinidad Vegetable Trading Post and the Benguet Vegetable Truckers and Traders Association, staged a demonstration at the La Trinidad Trading Post in La Trinidad town (Benguet, Cordillera Administrative Region), in order to condemn the smuggling of vegetables and fruits from China and South Korea, which they claim to be flooding markets in Manila and other key cities and provinces. The demonstrators decried the Department of Agriculture's inaction over the issue.

On 2 February 2023, hundreds of demonstrators led by groups such as BAYAN, GABRIELA and LFS staged a protest outside Camp Aguinaldo, the Philippine military headquarters in Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), in order to protest the expansion of the US military's access to military bases in the Philippines under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), as agreed upon by the Philippine and US governments during US Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin's visit to the Philippines on the same day. The demonstrators condemned US military intervention in the country. Women and LGBT protesters from groups such as GABRIELA and Lakapati also said that heightened US military presence in the country will lead to greater abuse of women and transgender people by US soldiers, as in the past.

Around 15 June 2022 (as reported), fisherfolk belonging to Pamalakaya staged a demonstration in front of the Department of Agriculture headquarters in Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), in order to denounce the government's importation of 38,000 metric tons of fish from China.

On 11 April 2023, almost 50 students staged a lightning demonstration in front of the United States Embassy in Manila City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to call for the abolition of the Balikatan Exercises, joint military drills of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and United States (US) Armed Forces. The protesters opposed the Visiting Forces Agreement and other military agreements between the US and the Philippines. They also expressed concern that the Philippines might be caught in the crossfire amid the increasing tension between the US and China over Taiwan. Police arrested 2 students after the rally. Police reported that the arrested students were charged with vandalism for throwing paint at the US Embassy's seal and resisting arrest.

On 21 January 2023, amid Lunar New Year celebrations, climate campaigners staged a 'protest dragon dance' at the Chinatown area in Binondo, Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), in order to call on the Chinese government to address the climate crisis and to transition to renewable energy.

On 12 June 2023, on the 125th anniversary of Philippine Independence, groups such as Anakbayan Davao, BAYAN, and KADAMAY, staged a rally at the Freedom Park in Davao City (Davao del Sur, Davao Region) to express their concerns on sovereignty issues, such as the shift in the Philippine government's alliance from China to the United States under President Ferdinand 'Bongbong' Marcos Jr.'s administration and the establishment of 4 new Enhanced Defense Cooperation Arrangement (EDCA) sites in the country for the use of the US military, which the protesters claimed could lead to increased human rights violations. The protesters demanded an independent foreign policy to assert the country's ownership of the West Philippine Sea and protect Filipino fishers.

On 5 June 2023, Bagong Silangan Youth members and other protesters staged a demonstration led by Kalipunan ng Kilusang Masa at Boy Scout Circle in Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to commemorate the 34th Anniversary of the Tiananmen Square Massacre in China and encourage Filipinos to draw lessons from the 1989 Tiananmen Square incident and demand accountability from the government.

On 12 June 2023, on the 125th anniversary of Philippine Independence, groups such as Anakbayan Davao, BAYAN, and KADAMAY, staged a rally at the Freedom Park in Davao City (Davao del Sur, Davao Region) to express their concerns on sovereignty issues, such as the shift in the Philippine government's alliance from China to the United States under President Ferdinand 'Bongbong' Marcos Jr.'s administration and the establishment of 4 new Enhanced Defense Cooperation Arrangement (EDCA) sites in the country for the use of the US military, which the protesters claimed could lead to increased human rights violations. The protesters demanded an independent foreign policy to assert the country's ownership of the West Philippine Sea and protect Filipino fishers.

On 11 August 2023, members of Socialista Pilipinas staged a demonstration in front of the Chinese Embassy in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to denounce the China Coast Guard's recent actions against Philippine vessels in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea). The China Coast Guard (CCG) ships had fired a water cannon against the Philippine Coast Guard's (PCG) vessels and Philippine indigenous boats at Ayungin Shoal in the West Philippine Sea on 5 August.

Around 9 November 2023 (as reported), youth groups staged a lightning rally in front of the United States (US) Embassy in Manila City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to oppose the Kamandag military exercises of the Philippines and US military, joined by the South Korea and Japan military. The demonstrators scuffled with the police guarding the embassy.

Around 10 May 2018 (as reported), youth groups staged a protest in front of the Chinese Embassy in Manila City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to denounce the militarization of the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) and the conflict in the Philippines between the United States and China.

On 11 September 2023, youth and student activists staged a protest in front of the United States (US) Embassy in Manila City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to urge the end of the US wars of aggression and its ongoing intervention in the Philippines.

On 6 November 2023, the Association of Masinloc Fishermen and their families staged a demonstration and released a buoy effigy at San Salvador Island in Barangay San Salvador (Masinloc, Zambales, Central Luzon) to protest against what they described as the 'aggression' and 'harassment' of China in Scarborough Shoal (Bajo de Masinloc) and show concerns about being denied access to the shoal by China. The protest was also joined by their barangay councilor, their incoming barangay chairperson.

On 4 February 2024, members of BAYAN and other groups staged a protest near the United States (US) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to commemorate the 125th anniversary of the Philippine-American War in 1899 and oppose the expansion of US military bases in the Philippines under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Arrangement (EDCA) between the US and the Philippines. They also protested against US involvement in the ongoing conflict in Palestine.

On 19 October 2016, about 1000 demonstrators (including members of indigenous peoples' alliance SANDUGO, BAYAN, and the Alliance of Health Workers) gathered outside the US Embassy in Manila (Metro Manila, National Capital Region) to call for an end of the presence of US troops in the Philippines. During the demonstration, a police van rammed into the demonstrators, after demonstrators surrounded the vehicle and hitting it with wooden batons. Several youths also splattered red paint and spray-painted slogans on the embassy wall. Police fired tear gas, fired water cannon, and used batons to hit demonstrators. At least 53 demonstrators were wounded and 31 were arrested. At least 3 demonstrators were hospitalized.

On 6 February 2024, Pamalakaya members staged a protest in front of the Chinese Embassy in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to express concerns about China's actions in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 9 April 2024, demonstrators from BAYAN and other groups staged a protest at the Chinese Consulate in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to denounce China's actions in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) and call for an end to the presence of foreign troops in Philippine territory and the militarization of the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea). The protesters trampled an effigy of Chinese President Xi Jinping.

On 10 April 2024, around 1,000 protesters from Alyansa Bantay Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (Alliance for Peace and Democracy Watch) and other groups staged a protest and marched from Morayta Street to Mendiola Bridge in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to show support for President Ferdinand 'Bongbong' Marcos Jr.'s actions regarding the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea), call for unity among Filipinos in supporting the Marcos administration, and denounce China's actions in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea). The protesters released doves as a symbol of peace and lit candles and torches.

On 19 April 2024, Alyansa Bantay Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (Alliance for Peace and Democracy Watch) members staged a protest in front of the Chinese Consulate in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to express their concerns over the actions of the Chinese Coast Guard in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) and call on China to adhere to the decisions of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The group opposed the 'gentlemen's agreement' between former President Rodrigo Duterte and Chinese President Xing Jinping on keeping the status quo in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 28 April 2024, around 1,000 members of Alyansa Bantay Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (Alliance for Peace and Democracy Watch) and other youth groups staged a protest from Morayta to Mendiola in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to show support for President Ferdinand 'Bongbong' Marcos Jr.'s actions regarding the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) and denounce China's actions in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 5 May 2024, demonstrators staged a protest near the United States (US) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to oppose the Balikatan Exercises, joint military drills between the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the US, and express their concern about the actions of China in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 17 June 2024, hundreds of Alyansa Bantay Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (Alliance for Peace and Democracy Watch) members staged a protest from Espana Boulevard to Morayta in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to show support for President Ferdinand 'Bongbong' Marcos Jr.'s actions regarding the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) and denounce China's actions in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 31 May 2024, fishers staged a protest in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to coincide with National Fisherfolk Day and to oppose the government's coastal reclamation projects and China's fishing ban and activities affecting the marine habitat in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 4 June 2024, Alyansa Bantay Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (Alliance for Peace and Democracy Watch) members staged a protest in front of the Chinese Consulate in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to denounce China's fishing ban in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 11 June 2024, about 500 members of Akbayan Party, Akbayan Youth, Atin Ito Coalition, Catholic Christian leaders, farmers and fishers group Pambansang Katipunan ng mga Samahan sa Kanayunan (PKSK), farmers group Pambansang Kilusan ng mga Samahang Magsasaka (PAKISAMA), fishers group New Masinloc Fishermen Association, and the Mabayo Agri Aqua Association in Bataan, Philippine Rural Reconstruction Movement (PRRM), and Student Council Alliance of the Philippines (SCAP) staged a protest in front of the Chinese Consulate in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to urge the Chinese government to stop what the protesters described as 'aggressive' actions in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 12 June 2024, on the 126th anniversary of Philippine Independence, Bunyog (Pagkakaisa) members staged a protest in front of the Chinese Consulate in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to urge the Chinese government to stop what the protesters described as 'aggressive' actions in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) and call for the resignation of Vice President Sara Duterte following her lack of reaction on issues about China's actions.

On 30 July 2024, about 2 dozen demonstrators staged a protest outside the military headquarters in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to condemn the United States-Philippines meetings as actions that could escalate tensions over the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) dispute. Demonstrators burned a mock US flag.

On 11 July 2024, Alyansa Bantay Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (Alliance for Peace and Democracy Watch) members staged a protest at the Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to condemn China's actions in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 12 July 2024, fishers staged a fluvial protest led by Pamalakaya on the waters of Subic (coded at Coast of Subic, Zambales, Central Luzon) to urge China to comply with the 2016 arbitral ruling that invalidated most of China's claims in the South China Sea (West Philippine Sea) and to mark the 8th anniversary of the ruling.

On 5 October 2024, dozens of members of BAYAN, SCMP, KABATAAN, and other groups protested near the United States (US) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to condemn what they described as genocide by Israel against Palestinians, and to denounce the US's military support for Israel and the bombings by Israel in Lebanon and Syria. Police blocked the protesters from reaching the embassy. The protest was part of the Global Day of Action for Palestine.

On 7 October 2024, demonstrators protested and lit candles at the Boy Scout Center in Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to express solidarity with Palestine and to mark the first anniversary of the Al-Aqsa Flood. They also criticized the United States' support for the Israeli occupation and compared it to the Philippine government's actions against its people.

On 17 October 2024, an American was shot and abducted by suspected ASG or BIFF members in Barangay Poblacion (Sibuco, Zamboanga del Norte, Zamboanga Peninsula). A resident said the assailants introduced themselves as police officers. Police said the assailants shot him in the leg before dragging him into a speedboat and then fled by sea. The motive for the abduction was unclear.

On 11 October 2024, members of the League of Filipino Students, the University of the Philippines Cinema (UP Cinema), and other progressive groups protested at the Oblation Plaza at the University of the Philippines Diliman (UPD) in Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to commemorate the 10th anniversary of the killing of a Filipino transgender woman by a US marine and to call for justice for the transgender woman.

On 20 January 2025, members of BAYAN, KARAPATAN, and other progressive groups staged a protest at the United States (US) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to protest against President-elect Donald Trump and condemn his presidency, which they described as 'the biggest threat to world peace, justice, and democracy.'

On 11 March 2025, members of the Filipinos Do Not Yield Movement staged a protest in front of the Chinese Embassy in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to denounce China's claims over Palawan Island and the actions of the China Coast Guard in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 19 March 2025, Akbayan Citizens' Action Party members staged a protest in front of the Chinese Consular Office in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to urge China to leave the Philippines' Exclusive Economic Zone and condemn China's actions in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

On 20 January 2017, hundreds of protesters, including GABRIELA, staged a protest led by BAYAN at the US embassy in Manila City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to denounce Donald Trump ahead of his inauguration as president of the United States, accusing him of sexism, racism, and xenophobia. Protesters burned an American flag and reiterated their long-time demands for US troops to leave the Philippines and the termination of what they called 'unequal' military agreements.

A large crowd of protesters of a Left-wing feminist group marched in Manila on March 8 on the occasion of the International Women's Day and burnt the US flag with President Donald Trump's face printed on it.

On 17 May 2017, a local group called Karapatan held a protest rally at the U.S. embassy in Manila against joint military drills between the United States and the Philippines. They demanded that the Philippine government should terminate one-sided agreements with the United States, including the Visiting Forces Agreement and the Enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement. Bagong Alyansang Makabayan or Bayan attended the protest.

Various groups, led by BAYAN: New Patriotic Alliance, held a Black Friday protest on June 2 in Quezon City, Manila against the declaration of martial law in Mindanao, the attack at the Resorts World Manila casino in Pasay City and US President Donald Trump for falsely calling the casino attack a 'terrorist attack'. They also called for the resumption of the peace talks between government and the National Democratic Front of the Philippines (NDFP).

The environmental group Kalikasan People's Network for the Environment (Kalikasan PNE) staged a demonstration outside the Chinese Consulate in Manila on January 31, to protest the continuous construction of military bases in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea).

The leftist group Bayan staged a demonstration outside the United States embassy in Manila on June 12, as the country celebrated its 119th Independence Day, to denounced what they described as US 'intervention' in the Philippines' affairs. Some activists clashed with the police.

Militant group BAYAN: New Patriotic Alliance staged a protest near the United States embassy on Roxas Boulevard in Manila on July 3, against the American role in the war against the Islamic State-linked Maute group in Marawi City.

At least 30 members of a militant group staged a protest rally in front of one the venues of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Cebu City, Cebu in April 5, to oppose any moves for the Philippines to join hands with 'imperialist nations' like the United States and China.

Activists, led by BAYAN: New Patriotic Alliance, staged an anti-China protest at Makati City, Manila on Independence Day on June 12. They called for an end to China's aggressiveness in the disputed waters, demanding that it respect Philippine sovereignty.
The League of Filipino Students protested in front of the City Hall in Davao City, Davao del Sur on 27 April to protest the alleged torture of a Filipino national by the US government.

Protestors associated with Bayan and other activist groups demonstrated in front of the Chinese consulate in Manila, Metro Manila on February 10. They were protesting against China's supposed militarization of the South China Sea.
Indigenous people held a rally in front of the Chinese Consulate in Manila, Metro Manila on March 13, against Chinese-funded mega dam projects in the ancestral territories of indigenous people.

On 12 June 2016, Independence Day, 16 members of the Kalayaan Atin Ito (Freedom This is Ours) group including an American volunteer from Sea Access by International Law (SAIL) were blocked and sprayed with water by Chinese Coast Guard ships as they were trying to sail to the Scarborough shoal. The group is protesting China's occupation in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) Shoal.
Protesters from Pamakalaya organized a demonstration in front of the Chinese consulate in Makati, Metro Manila on 18 May. They criticized China for its actions in the disputed South China Sea.

People staged anti-President Duterte protests as Independent Day celebrations were held at Kawit town, Cavite province on June 12. They criticized the government for allegedly being subservient to the Chinese government. A Bayan member was arrested for disturbing public order.
The League of Filipino Students held a demonstration against United States' presence in the Philippines in front of the US embassy in Manila, Metro Manila on July 4.

Protesters held an Independence Day demonstration in front of the Chinese embassy at Makati City, Metro Manila on June 12. They criticized the government for allegedly being subservient to the Chinese government.

Progressive groups led by the Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) staged a protest on 4 Feb 2016 at the US embassy in Manila, Metro Manila demonstrating against the atrocities committed during the Philippine-American War and subsequent colonial dominance.

Several youth organizations staged a protest in front of the US Embassy in Manila, Metro Manila on 12 June 2016 (Philippine Independence Day) against inter-country treaties such as the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA).

Hundreds of protesters staged a demonstration at the US Embassy in Manila, Metro Manila on July 27, 2016 condemning the visit of US Secretary of State John Kerry and protesting the final ruling affirming the constitutionality of the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA).

On 22 June 2016, around 100 fishers staged a protest organized by the People Power Volunteers for Reform (PPVR), National Youth Movement for the West Philippines Sea, among others, in Masinloc, Zambales, to oppose China's occupation in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) Panatag Shoal.
Youth groups staged a protest on 19 Feb 2016 at the Chinese Consulate in Makati City, Metro Manila demonstrating against China's missile deployment in Paracel Islands, South China Sea.

On 12 July 2016, a protest led by fisherfolk organization National Force of Fisherfolk Movement in the Philippines (Pamalakaya), Bayan Muna, and attended by fishers was held outside the Chinese Embassy in Makati City, Metro Manila, denouncing China's claims over the Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea.

Protesters rallied in the streets of Manila, Metro Manila on November 20, 2018, the day of Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to the Philippines. They denounced China's supposed militarization of the South China Sea.
Two drug suspects from China were killed during a joint police-PDEA raid at Barangay Amaya I, Tanza town, Cavite province on February 3, 2019.

A small crowd of protesters associated with Bayan Muna held a rally in front of the Chinese Embassy at Makati City, Metro Manila on March 4, 2019. They criticized the Chinese government for its actions in the South China Sea and its infrastructure contracts with the Philippines.

Protesters, many of whom were from the Dumagat tribe, held a demonstration in front of the Chinese Consulate in Makati City, Metro Manila on March 14, 2018 to protest China's role in dam construction.

Members of BAYAN, Gabriela, and Kabataan Partylist held a demonstration in front of the US Embassy at Manila, Metro Manila on June 12, 2019, which is Independence Day. They criticized the US government for trying to re-establish its military bases in the Philippines.

On 9 April 2019, hundreds of protesters, including senatorial candidates, BAYAN, the Dumagat ethnic group, P1NAS, and other groups held a demonstration in front of the Chinese consulate in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to denounce President Rodrigo Duterte's foreign policy strategy with China and protest against China's invasion of the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea) and other parts of the Philippine waters.
Akbayan held a demonstration at the Chinese Consulate in Pasay City, Metro Manila on April 25, 2019 in order to protest China's actions in the contested West China Sea.

On 12 July 2019, in Makati City, Metro Manila, protesters staged a protest at the Chinese consulate opposing China's intrusion in the West Philippine Sea. A PINAS co-convenor and former Bayan Muna Congressman joined them.

On 6 August 2019, in Lagawe, Ifugao, a journalist for Northern Dispatch and paralegal volunteer for the Ifugao Peasant Movement (IPM) was shot and wounded by unidentified gunmen in front of his house. The Cordillera Human Rights Alliance (CHRA) reported that the 54th IB were seen frequenting the victim's house for weeks before the shooting. The victim was an American national.

On 20 July 2019, in Makati City, Metro Manila, protesters from Bayan-Southern Tagalog region, including farmers' group Kapisanan ng Magsasaka sa Timog Katagalugan (Kasama-TK), staged a protest at the Chinese Embassy opposing China's intrusion in the West Philippine Sea.

On 10 January 2020, different groups such as BAYAN, Bayan Muna, and Migrante demonstrated outside the Department of Foreign Affairs in Pasay against the escalation of US military activity in the Middle East after the US assassination of Iranian general Qassem Soleimani. The demonstrators also rejected the possibility of sending Filipino troops to the Middle East to assist the US military. The demonstrators were heckled by the Philippine Foreign Secretary.

Assumed on 27 Jul 2019, in Muntinlupa City, Metro Manila, a Chinese couple were abducted and tortured by unidentified assailants (some of whom were Chinese). The abductions occurred due to the victims reporting to Chinese authorities of a firm's illegal online gambling activities in the Philippines. One of the captives escaped.

On 30 November 2019, striking workers and allied organizations such as Kilusang Mayo Uno, Anakbayan as well as other allied sectors such as students, held a demonstration in front of the Chinese Consulate in Makati in order to demand the rights and welfare of workers, as well as to assert national sovereignty, on the occasion of Bonifacio Day, which commemorates a working-class Philippine revolutionary hero. China and the Philippines have long been caught in a territorial dispute over islands in the South China Sea.

Around 27 February 2025 (week of), over 200 people from Enga convoying in 10 vehicles, who were relatives of an Engan teacher who was murdered during the week, were attacked by the public in Tari (Tari-Pori, Hela), after they had mistakenly thought the relatives from Enga were retaliating against them. The man's relatives from Enga had convoyed up to Tari to collect the body whilst dressed up in their traditional mourning attire and covered in mud to show their sorrow. Upon arriving the public thought, they were being attacked and started throwing stones at the Engans and in the process looted a store owned by Chinese nationals, however there was no report of casualties.

On 28 July 2024, more than 60 settlers from Finschhafen, Yamap, and Kumalu residing at Kilolo alluvial mine site and a group from East Sepik attacked Wido Mining Limited company workers at the Kilolo alluvial mine site in Wau Urban, Morobe. One Chinese national was chopped to death and two others were critically wounded. The settlers also burned machinery. They were unhappy about foreigners engaging in alluvial mining in the area. Police arrested 20 suspects.

On 30 May 2020, activists affiliated to the Coalition Against Racism gathered in Warsaw, protesting against police violence against civilians, especially those of Afro-Americans origins. The protest was sparked by the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.

On 19 July 2021, activists, including representatives of various unions of tenants, gathered for a rally near the embassy of the US in Warsaw, criticizing the decision of the US administration to lift the coronavirus-related moratorium on rents, which affects mainly the low-income tenants.

On 13 October 2023, Palestinian and Polish activists gathered for a march in Krakow, protesting against violence committed by Israel against Palestine, allegedly in accordance with the US imperialism.

On 22 December 2023, activists gathered for a rally near the US consulate in Poznan, protesting against the ongoing violence perpetrated by Israel in Gaza (with the US military and financial support) and calling for peace in Palestine.
On 15 May 2024, activists gathered for a march toward the Embassy of the US in Warsaw, declaring their solidarity with Palestine and protesting against violence perpetrated in Gaza by Israel.

On 3 March 2025, activists, including Poles and Ukrainians, gathered for a rally in front of the US embassy in Warsaw, demanding preservation of the US assistance to Ukraine and criticizing the US president's remarks towards his Ukrainian counterpart. Members of the KOD and Democratic Action movements also participated.

properties.actor: Police Forces of Papua New Guinea (2019-)
properties.notes: On 7 January 2021, a policeman and two other assailants killed a Chinese businessman at his store in Dande village (Western). Police asserted that the assailants were paid to kill the victim as nothing was stolen. The motive for the attack is unknown.

On 22 January 2022, activists gathered for a rally in Warsaw, protesting against a planned participation of the president at the opening ceremony of the 2022 Olympics in China due to violations of human rights in the country.

On 9 November 2024, at the call of PUSP - Unitary Platform for Solidarity with Palestine (PUSP - Plataforma Unitaria de Solidariedade com a Palestina), dozens of people protested near the Port of Lisboa in Lisboa (Lisboa) against the docking of a Nysted Maersk ship, accused of transporting US military material to Israel. Protesters called on the Portuguese government to revoke the ship's docking authorization and prohibit vessels carrying arms to Israel from transiting through Portuguese waters.

On 7 March 2025, members of the Ukrainian community in Portugal held a protest outside the US Embassy in Lisboa (Lisboa) against the Trump administration's decision to pause military support for Ukraine, condemning its recent shift in foreign policy regarding Russia.

On 9 March 2025, around a dozen people gathered outside a Tesla showroom in Lisboa (Lisboa) to protest against Tesla owner Elon Musk, criticizing his role in the Trump Administration in the United States. The demonstration was part of a series of coordinated protests held in over 50 cities worldwide in recent days.
On 3 December 2022, a dozen Chinese citizens carried out a demonstration in Lisbon (Lisbon), repudiating the coronavirus pandemic measures that are being taken in China.

Around 15 March 2021 (month of), the North Korean Coastal Patrol fired warning shots with rubber bullets at a Chinese fishing boat that was fishing illegally in North Korean waters near Haeju off the coast of South Hwanghae Province (coded at Coast of Haeju). On 24 November 2021, hundreds of demonstrators calling for the removal of Prime Minister Sogavare and angered by tensions between the Malaita provincial government and the national government, turned violent when hundreds of rioters set fire to a hut in the parliament precinct, attacked police officers causing serious injury to one police officer, and destroyed the Kukum Traffic Police Station in Honiara (Guadalcanal). Two groups of demonstrators first attempted to storm Parliament, one from the town council area of Vavaya Ridge Road, the other group from the foothills of Parliament from Point Cruz. The latter group was bolstered by a number of newly arrived demonstrators from Malaita carrying two flags - the Malaita Provincial flag and the Israeli flag, and were able to push through the fenced area into the parliament precinct. There, they set fire to a leaf hut and also threw stones at the small police contingent inside the parliament precinct, severely injuring one female police officer. Eventually, special forces police arrived and used tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse the rioters away from the parliament precinct. The demonstrators then moved to the Kukum commercial area, where they set fire to the Kukum Traffic Police Station which had 10 police officers inside, although none were injured. Many of the demonstrators were from Malaita and were particularly inflamed by the national government's decision in 2019 to end diplomatic ties with Taiwan in favour of the People's Republic of China. Displacement: Around 27 November 2021 (from 24 - 27 November), hundreds of Chinese residents were left homeless as a result of riots that torched and looted the Chinatown district in Honiara (Guadalcanal). As of 27 November 2021, only six buildings in the Chinatown area remain standing.

Initial reports indicate that about 11 people, including two police officers and the attackers, have been killed. Al Shabaab has claimed responsibility for the attack. On 23 November 2021, an unknown armed group targeted a US military base in Kharab Eljir airbase in Al Hasakeh countryside with five rockets, two of those fell on Jafal town as well which is near the airbase. Casualties unknown.
On 2 December 2021, an unidentified armed group detonated an IED against 2 US military trucks in the area of Al-Malikeyyeh in Al Hasakeh governorate. Casualties unknown.
