On 23 May 2024, Russian warplanes conducted airstrikes targeting Kabani axis in Lattakia countryside, killing a Turkistan Islamic Party-backed Jaafar bin Abi Talib Brigade Chinese member. 1 fatality.

Over 500 Muslims gathered in front of the US Embassy in Bangkok to protest a controversial American film, which is deemed insulting to Islam. The demonstrators expressed their anger over the movie called 'Innocence of Muslims,' which mocks the Prophet Mohammad. They demanded the US oversee the matter and stop the dissemination of the film.

On 22 July 2024, QSD forces detained an Uzbek child and a Chinese woman from the foreigners section in Hole Camp in the countryside of Al-Hasakeh on allegations of contacting IS members outside the camp.

On 15 July 2024, Syrian regime forces arrested a Chinese tourist while he was leaving the city of As-Sweida to the city of Dara and handed him over to the Chinese embassy in the city of Damascus then deported him outside the country on allegations of conducting suspected activities.

On 15 November 2022, members of People's Party and People Stop APEC2022 marched along Yaowarat Road (Bangkok - Samphanthawong) and staged a demonstration at Lan Khon Mueang Town Square in front of Bangkok City Hall in Bangkok - Phra Nakhon (coded Bangkok - Phra Nakhon) to protest against the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit 2022 which took place in Thailand on 16-18 November 2022. During the march, demonstrators stopped at the embassies of Canada, Australia, France, New Zealand, and the United States. Some protesters dressed as characters from Chinese folklore to protest against the One China policy. The protesters also called for the resignation of the military-led government and the restoration of democracy as well as human rights in Thailand.

On 24 May 2023, members of People's Center Protecting the Institution (PCPI) gathered in front of the US embassy in Bangkok - Pathum Wan to demand the US not interfere in Thailand's politics and protest against an amendment of the lese majeste law. The protesters also submitted a letter to the ambassador of the United States to Thailand.

On 3 July 2023, about 100 members of People's Center Protecting the Institution (PCPI) gathered and held placards outside the US Consulate General in tambon Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai (Chiang Mai) to submit a letter to the ambassador of the US to Thailand, demanding the US not interfere in Thailand's politics.

On 5 May 2024, members of Chiangmai for Palestine and Socialist Thai staged a protest outside the US Consulate General in tambon Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai (Chiang Mai) condemning Israel's ongoing actions in Palestine and calling for an end to what they term as genocide. With placards and chants of 'Stop genocide' and 'Free Palestine,' the protesters highlighted the 11 months of Israeli actions, accusing the United States of contributing both financially and militarily to the conflict.

On 30 June 2024, members of Chiangmai for Palestine and Socialist Thai staged a protest outside the US Consulate General in tambon Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai (Chiang Mai), demanding the United States stop its military and financial support to Israel, which they argue perpetuates violence against Palestinians, including children.

On 9 August 2024, members of People's Center Protecting the Institution (PCPI) and Dhamma Team staged a protest in front of the US embassy in Bangkok - Pathum Wan and submitted a letter to the US Ambassador, demanding that the US apologize for its response to the Thai Constitutional Court's decision to dissolve the Move Forward Party. The groups criticized the US for allegedly interfering in Thailand's internal affairs, following a statement from the US State Department expressing concern over the court's ruling.

On 14 March 2025, over 700 Thai residents in Mae Ai district staged a protest in Tha Ton, Mae Ai (Chiang Mai) against large-scale gold mining across the border in Myanmar's eastern Shan State, citing severe environmental damage to the Kok River. The mining, conducted by four Chinese companies under the control of the United Wa State Army, has intensified since 2023 and now operates using toxic chemicals like cyanide.

On 19 December 2013, the anti-government demonstrators marched through downtown Bangkok and gathered outside the US embassy in Pathum Wan district (PW, Bangkok) to demonstrate against Washington's support of the Feb 2 general election. More than 15,000 people joined the march, which started from the Democracy Monument then headed to Bangkok's business district of Siam, Ratchaprasong, Asoke and Pratunam. The group was largely affiliated with the PDRC and the NSPRT and their aim was to invite the public to their upcoming rally to call for the ousting of Prime Minister Yingluck Shinawatra.

On 5 January 2017, around 50 Myanmar citizens of Kachin ethnicity gathered at the Myanmar General Consulate in tambon Chang Phueak, Mueang Chiang Mai district of Chiang Mai, Thailand, to protest and demand an end to all attacks against ethnic minorities carried out by the government, to demand the government to facilitate operations of aid organizations, and to demand the Chinese government allow Myanmar citizens to seek refuge in the country.

On 8 January 2017, around 80 villagers gathered in Chiang Khong (Chiang Rai), Thailand, as a Chinese survey boat entered the area on Mekong river. The protesters opposed the project commissioned by the Chinese government to improve the water channel which would also include the blasting of rapids. Coded was Wiang.

On 27 November 2015, a Buddhist monk led more than 70 protesters to demonstrate in front of the US Embassy in Bangkok - Pathum Wan, Thailand, to protest the US ambassador's criticism of Thailand's lese majeste law.

On 28 April 2017, more than 30 villagers rallied in Mueang Kan village, tambon Rim Khong, Chiang Khong district of Chiang Rai, Thailand, to protest against a Chinese vessel that was conducting an exploration for the blasting of Khong river rapids.

Dozens of protesters gathered in front of the Chinese embassy to submit a petition calling on China to disclose the whereabouts and legal status of hundreds of human rights attorneys and activists detained in a crackdown in Beijing lasst month.
Environment activists in Chiang Khong district, Chiang Rai protested China's reefs blasting in the Mekong river on 8 January 2017.

On 28 January 2015, representatives from the Network to Protect Thai People's Interests and Dignity protested in front of the US Embassy in kwaeng Lumpini, Pathum Wan district of Bangkok, Thailand, demanding the US to stop any form of interference with Thailand's domestic affairs.

On 4 June 2019, a group of Thai students and Chinese refugees gathered in front of the Chinese Embassy in kwaeng Din Daeng, Din Daeng district, Bangkok, Thailand, in the remembrance of the Tiananmen massacre in 1989.

On 13 October 2015, a group of protesters demonstrated in front of the US Embassy in kwaeng Lumpini, Pathum Wan district of Bangkok, Thailand, reading a report on the impact on the local community and human rights violations caused by the petroleum drilling of an American company in Nakhon Ratchasima province.

On 3 April 2010, more than 20 activists, including students, demonstrated in front of the Chinese Consulate in tambon Phra Sing, Mueang Chiang Mai district of Chiang Mai, Thailand, to protest against the construction of several dams in China that would negatively impact the Mekong river.

On 17 September 2020, around 25 members of the Coordination Centre of Vocational Students and People Protecting the Institution demonstrated in front of Thai Summit tower in kwaeng Bang Kapi, Huai Khwang district (Bangkok), belonging to the leader of the Progressive Movement who was the leader of the dissolved Future Forward party, claiming he is behind the student protests and demanding his banishment from Thailand. The protesters then rallied to the US Embassy in kwaeng Lumpini, Pathum Wan district (Bangkok) (coded as Bangkok-Pathum Wan), to demand the end of the US' involvement in Thailand politics, following the release of the images showing the student protest leaders meeting with the American ambassador.

On 13 July 2015, representatives from the Muslim Students for Humanity group gathered and filed a petition at the Chinese Embassy in kwaeng Din Daeng, Din Daeng district of Bangkok, Thailand, protesting against forced repatriation of Uyghur Muslims and demanding humane treatment of Uyghur-ethnic Muslims in China.

On 4 June 2018, around 10 students demonstrated in front of the Chinese Embassy in Bangkok in kwaeng Din Daeng, Din Daeng district, Thailand, to commemorate 29th anniversary of the Tiananmen massacre.

On 1 October 2020, the Chinese National Day, around 20 student protesters rallied near the Chinese Embassy in kwaeng Huai Khwang, Huai Khwang district (Bangkok), denouncing the human rights abuses by the Chinese government, as well as the One China policy, in solidarity with pro-democracy movements in Taiwan and Hong Kong.

On 9 October 2020, at least 7 members of the Anti One China TH group protested in front of the Chinese Embassy in kwaeng Din Daeng, Din Daeng district (Bangkok), demanding the release of 12 Hong Kong youth activists.

On 27 October 2020, more than 100 villagers demonstrated at Sakon Nakhon Provincial Hall in tambon That Choeng Chum (Mueang Sakon Nakhon district, Sakon Nakhon), opposing a Chinese company which filed a request for an authorization for a mine exploration.

On 20 August 2021, Thalufah and People's Party protesters held a rally towards the embassy of China at kwaeng Din Daeng, Din Daeng district (Bangkok) (coded as Bangkok - Din Daeng) to submit a letter to the Chinese government regarding the Chinese-made Sinovac vaccines which fail to help contain the spread of the coronavirus.

On 08 February 2020, in Princes Town, a man and a woman were killed and another man injured as two gunmen dressed as Muslims entered their property and opened fire. Another woman who was present had received death threats and her husband was murdered recently, police think the killers mistook her for the other woman. The man who was killed was a US citizen.

Around 3 July 2023 (as reported), in Caroni, Tunapuna Piarco, a person was killed and human remains were found in the trunk of a burnt vehicle on South Bank Road. The victim was thought to be a US citizen who had gone missing over the week, as his relatives stated that he had rented the car were the human remains were found. The motivation and the perpetrators of the attack are unknown. 1 fatality.

On 28 March 2024, in Penal, Penal-Debe, two masked men, armed with cutlasses, stabbed to death a US woman at her house, off the Penal Rock Road. The attackers fled the scene in a vehicle. Motivation unknown. 1 fatality.
On 1 June 2020, in Port of Spain, just over a dozen people gathered at the US Embassy for a Black Lives Matter protest against police violence and racism in the United States.

On 9 February 2023, citizens organized a protest in front of the Municipal Theater in Tunis (El Omrane, Tunis) and called for the end of US blockade against the country and the resumption of relations.

On 18 October 2023, 20000 citizens, including middle and high school students organized a protest in front of the Municipal Theater on Habib Bourguiba street and in front of the United States of America's Embassy in Tunis (El Omrane, Tunis) and denounced the Israeli attacks on the Palestinian people in Gaza. They also showed their support to the Palestinian people.

On 18 February 2025, dozens of citizens, unionists and activists, under the invitation of the URT, carried out a march in Bizerte (Bizerte Nord, Bizerte) to express their rejection of the American and Israeli project to relocate Palestinians to Egypt and Jordan. They also called for the criminalization of normalization with the Israeli state and showed their support to the Palestinian people following the Israeli military campaign in Gaza.
Representatives of civil society and national organisations in Sidi Bouzid, on Monday, staged a rally to support the Syrian people, condemning last Friday's US strike on a military airbase in Homs.
Tunisians protested to denounce the US decision to recognize Jerusalem as Israels capital.
On 15 May 2018, people gathered in front of the U.S. embassy in Tunis to protest against the Israeli violence and killing of Palestinian protesters on the border with the Gaza Strip.

On 5 February 2020, associations and labour groups held a national protest march in Tunis, against the Israeli-Palestinian peace plan presented by the US administration and calling for the criminalization of any normalization with Israel.

On 13 February 2022, in Barataria, San Juan-Laventille, one armed man excited a vehicle on the passenger's side, exchanged some words and opened fire on a Chinese national while he was about to enter his own vehicle. The armed man then returned to the other vehicle and fled the scene. Motivations of the attack are unknown. 1 fatality.

On 11 August 2022, in Bon Accord, Tobago, residents clashed with police forces and Chinese employees of a construction company during an eviction attempt against families on Compston Trace Extension. The police tried to execute the eviction of an area where the authorities are planing a project to expand the local airport, in which the Chinese citizens are working as constructors. The eviction was stopped following the mob's action.

150 Militia (Hizb ut-Tahrir) activists - adherents to a strict, conservative interpretation of the Quran, and advocates for the establishment of an Islamic Caliphate - protested against the official visit of the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Christine Lagarde. Protesters urged the state to reject all cooperation with European and North American economic partners, advocating an 'Islamic economy.'

On 4 September 2021, dozens of Tunisians Workers Party (PTT) members held a protest sit-in in front of the Municipal Theatre in Tunis (El Omrane, Tunis) to denounce the visit of a US parliamentary delegation to meet the President, considering it to be an interference in Tunisian affairs.

On 11 December 2022, in Wallerfield, Tunapuna Piarco, unidentified armed men in a vehicle shot and killed a Chinese businesswoman and injured her Chinese co-worker in a drive-by attack on Antigua Road. Motivation and perpetrators of the attack are unknown. 1 fatality, 1 injured.

On 30 July 2022, members of the Tunisian Human Rights League and civil society activists organized a protest in front of the United States embassy in Tunis (El Omrane, Tunis) and denounced American interference in Tunisian affairs.

Tunisian police fired teargas and rubber bullets into the air today to disperse a protest over a US-made film depicting the Prophet Mohammad near the US Embassy in the capital Tunis. Around 200 protesters threw rocks at the police, burnt US flags and chanted slogans.

Interception: On 31 August 2022, Taiwanese soldiers fired live ammunition over Kinmen County islets Dadan, Erdan, and Shiyu (coded to Lieyu Township), at three unidentified drones reportedly belonging to civilians operating from mainland China. All three drones flew to Xiamen after being shot at. Previously, Taiwanese forces only used warning flares to deter unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) incursions. The Ministry of National Defense (MND) on 28 August 2022 implemented a four-step plan to deter unwanted drone activity which would include 'firing warning flares, reporting the incursion, expelling the drone and ultimately shooting it down.' The policy change was announced after detailed video footage taken by a private Chinese UAV of personnel at a Taiwanese lookout post went viral. On 1 September 2022, Taiwanese soldiers shot down a Chinese civilian-operated drone for the first time over Kinmen, Shiyu (Lieyu township).

They marched towards the Bank of China (Taipei City - Xinyi). Hong Kong, Tibet and Uyghur ethnic group rights advocates, including Taiwan East Turkistan Association, Taiwan Tibetan Welfare Association, Hong Kong Outlanders, and Human Rights Network for Tibet and Taiwan, also joined the rally. They urged the authorities to fight against the Chinese government's 'dictatorship' and defend human rights.

On 29 December 2020, people with the East Turkmenistan National Awakening Movement and members of the East Turkistan Government in Exile protested in Washington DC (District of Columbia) against the China-Turkey Extradition Treaty.

On 10 March 2020, about 15 Tibetan monks staged a demonstration at Monument Square in Portland (Maine), coinciding with Tibetan National Uprising Day, and calling for an end to the Chinese occupation of Tibet.

On 10 March 2020, Tibetan residents of Salt Lake City (Utah), took part in a march through the city for Tibetan National Uprising Day to call for an end to the Chinese occupation of Tibet. They carried images of the Dalai Lama, the spiritual leader of Tibet.

On 27 July 2020, nurses with National Nurses United protested at Chinese Hospital in San Francisco (California) against racism and raising awareness for the importance of having a strong union contract to help end systemic oppression.

Security measures: On 18 February 2020, the State Department of the Government of the United States, located in Washington DC - Northwest (District of Columbia), classified five Chinese outlets as foreign missions in the US territory, claiming the Chinese state controlled them. This measure imposed new obligations for the companies: it became mandatory to disclose a list of employees' names, addresses, and ages working in the newspapers, and to ask for the State Department's Office permission to lease or buy real estate. The US government's actions prompted reactions from China, which expelled three Wall Street Journal reporters in the country. Later, in March, the State Department urged the outlets to reduce their number of Chinese employees by 40%. The outlets affected by these measures are Xinhua News Agency, China Global Television Network, China Radio International, China Daily Distribution Corporation, and Hai Tian Development USA.
On 19 January 2020, between 50-75 protesters marched from Astor Place to Time Squares in New York - Manhattan (New York) rallying against China's crackdown on Hong Kong protesters.

On 12 February 2021, an unreported number of people rallied outside the Chinese Consulate in San Francisco (California) against the firing of Namibian mineworkers who refused reduced healthcare benefits by the Chinese National Nuclear Corporation amid the coronavirus. Demonstrators also rallied against the 'imperialist encirclement of China' by the United States. Members of the Freedom Socialist Party and Laborers' International Union Local 261 attended.

On 20 February 2021, over 400 Burmese people rallied outside the Chinese Consulate in San Francisco (California) against the military coup in Myanmar earlier in February and the Chinese Communist Party.

On 27 September 2020, over 200 people, organized by NY Chinese Democracy Force, Christians from Church of Rock, and Global Alliance for Hong Kong rallied in Flushing New York - Queens (New York) calling to terminate the Chinese Communist Party as they claim it is the largest terrorist organization in the world.

On 10 March 2021, around 400-500 Tibetans and supporters marched through New York - Manhattan (New York) against China's occupation of Tibet marking the 62nd anniversary of the Tibetan National Uprising. People chanted, 'China lies, people die!' and 'Shame on Chinese Government'.
On 22 March 2021, people took part in a Uyghur Freedom rally in New York - Manhattan (New York) against China's actions against the Uyghur people, calling for their freedom.

On 30 March 2021, around 50 Uighurs and supporters including members of the Uyghur American Association protested outside the Chinese Embassy in Washington DC - Northwest (District of Columbia) against human rights abuses in Beijing and to call on the United States to take action against China on the issue.

On 24 July 2020, around 100 gathered held a protest in Houston (Texas), outside the Chinese consulate, after the US government ordered the building closed, calling it a hub for spying on American companies and researchers. Protesters chanted 'take back China' and denounced the ruling Chinese Communist Party.
On 28 April 2021, people rallied outside the Chinese Consulate in Los Angeles - Central (California) with calls of 'Free Mengzhu.'

On 23 June 2021, people rallied at the Golden Gate Bridge near San Francisco (California) against Beijing hosting the 2022 Winter Olympics. Members of Bay Area Friends of Tibet attended and rallied against what they claim are China's human rights violations.
On 15 July 2021, people gathered outside Penn Station in New York - Manhattan (New York) against colonialism and imperialist policies by the US and China towards Trinidad and Tobago, Cuba, and Haiti.

On 13 August 2021, people rallied outside the Chinese consulate in San Francisco (California) calling for the rehiring of the Miners Union of Namibia Rossing Branch by the Chinese government, which is the majority owner of the mine.

On 1 October 2021, a group of people, including members of DC4HK, gathered in front of the White House in Washington DC - National Mall (District of Columbia) as part of a 'Rally for Resistance against CCP Dictatorship' to demonstrate against China taking 'political prisoners' in Hong Kong.

Around 12 November 2021 (as reported), Uyghur people rallied outside the White House in Washington DC - National Mall (District of Columbia) against the 'genocide Olympics' in China. Demonstrators also called for East Turkmenistan to be recognized as an occupied country.

On 14 November 2021, Hong Kongers, Tibetans, and Uyghurs gathered outside the White House in Washington DC - National Mall (District of Columbia) to protest against human rights abuses they said were committed by the Chinese government and to urge President Biden to hold China accountable.

On 20 November 2021, members of the Yale Students for Uyghur Freedom, including students of Uyghur origin, gathered outside the Yale Bowl at Yale University in New Haven (Connecticut) to protest ongoing human rights violations by the Chinese government against Uyghurs in China. People also demanded that the university investigate the university's possible contributions to these human rights violations.

On 3 February 2022, dozens of people, including Tibetans, Uyghurs, and Hong Kongers held a march across the Golden Gate Bridge, ending at the Chinese Consulate in San Francisco (California) to protest the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics and to demand a boycott over the 'human rights record' of the Chinese government. The San Francisco Regional Tibetan Youth Congress (SFRTYC), the International Tibet Network, Santa Barbara Friends of Tibet, Tibetan Association of Northern California, Students for Hong Kong, Students for a Free Tibet, and Uyghur SF Bay Area participated.

On 30 January 2022, people gathered outside the Target Center in Minneapolis (Minnesota) to protest China's human rights record ahead of the Winter Olympics, to call for a boycott of the Olympics, to oppose China's treatment of the Uyghur Muslim minority group, and China's occupation of Tibet.

On 3 February 2022, a group of people demonstrated outside of the Chinese Consulate in Los Angeles - Central (California) to call for a boycott of the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics and to denounce the Chinese Government's treatment of Uyghurs.

On 12 February 2022, dozens of people organized by Students for a Free Tibet gathered outside NBC Sports headquarters in Stamford (Connecticut) to protest NBC's coverage of the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics and China's human rights violations, including in Xinjiang Province.

On 14 March 2020, a man attacked a 6-year-old child, his parent, and a Sam's Club employee who tried to intervene, with a knife in a Sam's Club in Midland (Texas), believing the customers were Chinese though they were in fact Burmese. The man yelled 'Get out of America!' as he attacked them. A Texas Assistant Attorney later stated that the man attacked the customers because of their race and because he blamed them for the coronavirus pandemic. The man later pled guilty to three federal hate crimes.

On 10 March 2022, dozens of people, including members of the Tibetan community, held a pro-Ukraine march in Burlington (Vermont) to protest China's control of Tibet and in solidarity with people in Ukraine amid Russia's invasion which began on 24 February 2022.

On 14 April 2022, about 30 students and supporters marched from Trousdale Parkway to the USC Village and returned to rally outside of the Ronald Tutor Campus Center at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles - South (California) to demand USC release a statement in recognition of the oppression of the Uyghur people by the Chinese government and to demand that the university call it a genocide. The protest was organized by the Muslim Student Union and Delta Phi Epsilon, and was attended by Uyghurs.

On 14 May 2022, more than 100 Taiwanese-Americans rallied outside of City Hall in San Francisco (California) against what they say is China's intent to stop Taiwanese officials from being approved to become observers at the upcoming World Health Assembly meeting.

On 5 July 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of the White House in Washington DC - National Mall (District of Columbia) to call on the US government to take action against China to end the Uyghur genocide and 'occupation in East Turkistan' as well as to commemorate the anniversary of the 2009 Urumchi Massacre. The East Turkistan National Awakening Movement and East Turkistan Government in Exile participated in the protest.

On 10 July 2022, hundreds, many of Chinese descent, and adherents of Falun Gong, marched in Chinatown in New York - Manhattan (New York) to protest against the government of China's treatment of Falun Gong practitioners in what they claim is 'crimes against humanity.'

On 18 July 2022, nearly 200 Falun Gong adherents held a vigil and rally outside of the Chinese Consulate in Los Angeles - Central (California) in protest of 'persecution' of the group by the Chinese government. Chinese-Americans participated in the event.

On 20 August 2022, hundreds of Falun Gong adherents marched in San Francisco (California) to protest against 'persecution' of the group by the Chinese government, and to celebrate the milestone of 400 million people who have 'quit' the CCP, according to the group. Chinese-Americans and the San Francisco chapter of Tuidang participated.

On 1 October 2022, a group of people held a rally at the University of California in Berkeley (California) to protest against a scheduled event featuring the Consulate General of China, and to protest against the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) which they say is responsible for human rights abuses in China and around the world. The San Francisco Regional Tibetan Youth Congress participated.

On 3 November 2022, a group of Falun Gong adherents and supporters, including members of the Chinese community, rallied outside of the Chinese Consulate in San Francisco (California) to demand an end to the Chinese government's 'persecution' of Falun Gong practitioners.

On 29 November 2022, several dozen students gathered on Purdue University's campus in West Lafayette (Indiana) in solidarity with anti-lockdown demonstrations in China. One student approached and began to harass the group, waving a cigarette around and taking photos and videos of them. A demonstrator attempted to take the phone away from the student and was punched in the face. Police were called when the student got into a fight with one of the demonstrators and they separated but did not detain the student. The student does not appear to be a counter-demonstrator.
On 29 November 2022, around 150-200 demonstrators gathered outside the Chinese consulate in Chicago - Central (Illinois) in solidarity with anti-lockdown demonstrations in China.

On 27 November 2022, about 100 people, including members of the Chinese community, gathered outside the Chinese Consulate General in San Francisco (California) to demonstrate support for anti-lockdown demonstrations in China and to honor the 10 people who died in a fire in Urumqi, the capital of China's Xinjiang region. During the protest, a masked demonstrator graffitied a wall of the Chinese Consulate.

On 29 November 2022, about 50 to more than a hundred protesters including students, faculty, and members of the Chinese community rallied at Harvard University in Cambridge (Massachusetts) to demonstrate solidarity with anti-lockdown demonstrations in China. Some protesters also opposed government censorship in China.

On 28 November 2022, some 200 protesters, including Chinese Americans and students, gathered at Columbia University Low Library in New York - Manhattan (New York) in solidarity with anti-lockdown demonstrations in China. Protesters also held a vigil for the ten people killed in an apartment fire in Urumqi, China. During the demonstration, a man approached a 21-year-old woman who was protesting in solidarity with anti-lockdown demonstrations in China, repeatedly punched her in the head and rendered her unconscious in an unprovoked attack. The victim was taken to the hospital.

On 29 November 2022, about 400 protesters rallied opposite the Consulate General of China in New York - Manhattan (New York) to demonstrate solidarity with anti-lockdown demonstrations in China. Protesters also opposed government censorship in China.

On 28 November 2022, over a hundred people gathered at the Duke Chapel on the Duke University campus in Durham (North Carolina) to demonstrate solidarity with the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China as well as to honor the victims of the Urumqi apartment fire in China. Members of the Chinese-American student community as well as international students from China participated in the demonstration.

On 4 December 2022, dozens rallied in Washington Square Park in New York - Manhattan (New York) to demonstrate solidarity with the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China and demand that the Chinese government release detained demonstrators. Members of Chinese, Hong Kong, and Tibetan communities organized the rally.

On 28 November 2022, an unreported number of people rallied on the Johns Hopkins University campus in Baltimore (Maryland) in support of the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China. Students and members of the Chinese community participated in the demonstration.

On 3 December 2022, more than 80 protesters including students, Muslims, and members of the Chinese and Uyghur communities held a march in Harvard Square and a vigil at Widener Library in Cambridge (Massachusetts) to demonstrate against the Chinese policy towards Uyghurs and 'other populations living in occupied territories' and in support of anti-lockdown demonstrations in China.

On 6 December 2022, almost 200 people gathered in front of the Chinese consulate at West Erie and North Clark Street in Chicago - Central (Illinois) to demonstrate in favor of the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China.

On 4 December 2022, more than 100 demonstrators including Chinese students gathered on the campus of University of Chicago in Chicago - South Side (Illinois) to mourn the victims of an apartment fire in Xinjiang, China, to demand more rights from the Chinese government, to support anti-lockdown demonstrations in China, and to call for the release of a protestor that's been imprisoned since October.

On 2 December 2022, a man in Quincy (Massachusetts) told an Asian man to 'Go back to China' several times, before hitting the man with his car, driving him on the car's hood for about 50 yards, then striking the man again as he stood up and pushing him into a ditch. The victim suffered a broken shoulder, an injured leg, and a concussion. Police said the interaction between the two began after the driver 'exchanged words' with pedestrians about how fast he was driving. Police are investigating the attack as a hate crime.

On 2 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated on the Pennsylvania State University campus in State College (Pennsylvania) in support of the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China and to call for the Chinese Communist Party to relinquish power. Chinese students and members of the Chinese community participated in the demonstration which was organized by Penn State Students for Hong Kong.

On 4 December 2022, about 200 people demonstrated in Freedom Plaza in Washington DC - Northwest (District of Columbia) in support of the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China and to call for the Chinese Communist Party to relinquish power. International Chinese students were present. Additionally, members of the Uighur and Tibetan ethnic communities were present alongside other Chinese ethnic minorities.

On 28 November 2022, over 100 people rallied in Kogan Plaza on the George Washington University campus in Washington DC - Northwest (District of Columbia) to call for the end of Chinese Communist Party rule of China, to support anti-lockdown demonstrations in China, and to honor the victims of the Urumqi fire. Students and members of the Chinese, Uyghur, Hong Kong, Taiwanese, and Ukrainian diasporas participated in the protest.

On 18 December 2022, a few dozen people gathered outside the Washington Commanders and New York Giants football game in Landover (Maryland), to demonstrate in favor of the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China and in solidarity with 'white paper' student protesters in China, who are also demonstrating against censorship. Afterwards, demonstrators entered the stadium, where they held blank pieces of paper in front of their faces to symbolize anti-censorship views.

On 10 December 2022, protestors, including the group Chicago Solidarity with Hong Kong, demonstrated in Chicago - Central (Illinois) in honor of International Human Rights Day and the victims of humans rights abuses by China in Hong Kong and Tibet. Demonstrators marched past multiple consulates, ending at the Chinese Consulate of Chicago.

On 13 December 2022, about a dozen protesters including students and members of the Chinese community rallied in Harvard Square's Pit in Cambridge (Massachusetts) to demonstrate in favor of the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China as well as against the state's censorship.

On 21 January 2023, members of Falun Gong and the Chinese community marched in Flushing in New York - Queens (New York) as part of the 2023 Chinese New Year parade to demonstrate against the Chinese Communist Party as they claim it is 'a virus that's contaminated the entire world.'

properties.actor: Military Forces of the United States (2021-)
properties.notes: Interception: On 4 February 2023, the United States government shot down an unmanned aircraft, which it says is a Chinese surveillance craft, nearby in US territorial waters six miles off the coast, near Myrtle Beach (South Carolina). The balloon had initially entered US airspace in Alaska before flying over Canada and then back into the United States, where it was downed by an F-22 fighter firing a missile just off the South Carolina coast. Gen Glen VanHerck, the head of Norad, said the aircraft may use a balloon to stay afloat, and also said that Norad had tuned its radar system, making it more sensitive to small aircraft like the one that was shot down. The Chinese government described the balloon as a 'civilian unmanned airship,' but US officials claimed that the balloon had multiple antennas for receiving and transmitting information, including geo-location data.

properties.actor: Military Forces of the United States (2021-)
properties.notes: Interception: On 10 February 2023, the United States government shot down an unmanned aircraft nearby Deadhorse (Alaska). The aircraft was shot down by F-22s firing a sidewinder missile. The US had previously shot down what it claims is a Chinese surveillance balloon near South Carolina a week prior, but did not immediately claim that this object was also operated by China. A US official said the aircraft was shot down to ensure the safety of flights in the area.

On 5 February 2023, dozens of people rallied in Lafayette Square in Washington DC - National Mall (District of Columbia) in opposition to the treatment and surveillance of Uyghurs by China as well as to commemorate the anniversary of the Ghulja Massacre. The rally was organized by the East Turkestan Government in Exile and the East Turkestan National Movement.

On 13 February 2023, a 43 year-old male entered Berkey Hall on Michigan State University's (MSU) East Lansing campus (Michigan) and fired shots both outside and inside a classroom. He then went inside the MSU Union building and fired shots there before leaving. About 4 hours later, the suspect was found several miles away from the campus having committed suicide while being chased by police. There were 8 victims total - 3 were killed and 5 were hospitalized in critical condition. All victims were MSU students, two of whom were Chinese exchange students. The motive for the shooting remains unknown, though police said the shooter left a note detailing a list of other targets, including a warehouse he had previously worked for and businesses where he had had issues with employees, though he has no known ties to MSU. Police said his note suggests 'he felt slighted' by some of the people or businesses on the list and also claimed that he was a member of 20 individuals who would participate in his plans, though the existence of such a group has not been confirmed. 4 fatalities.

properties.actor: Military Forces of the United States (2021-)
properties.notes: Interception: On 13 February 2023, the United States government shot down an unmanned aircraft over Lake Huron (Coded as Oscoda (Michigan). A US official said the object was octagonal in structure and was traveling at about 20,000 feet. The US had previously shot down what it claims is a Chinese surveillance balloon near South Carolina a week prior, as well as an unmanned aircraft over Alaska and Canada's Yukon territory during the two preceding days.

On 25 February 2023, more than 60 protesters and members of the Chinese community and Women's Rights in China rallied at the ChangLe Association Inc. service station in New York - Manhattan (New York) to demonstrate against the organization as they claim it surveils 'dissidents' of Chinese descent in the area. Congressman Mike Gallagher (R) participated in the rally.

On 10 March 2023, an unreported number of people rallied outside of the Chinese Embassy in Washington DC - Northwest (District of Columbia) in opposition to 'cultural genocide' by China in Tibet and to call for independence for Tibet. Rep. Mike Gallagher (R) and members of the International Campaign for Tibet participated in the rally, which was held in honor of Tibetan Uprising Day.

On 10 March 2023, hundreds of demonstrators rallied in front of City Hall in San Francisco (California) to protest the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)'s treatment of Tibetans in commemoration of the anniversary of the 1959 Tibetan uprising. Those present included members of the Tibetan Association of Northern California, the San Francisco Regional Tibetan Youth Congress, as well as Hong Kong organizations.

On 4 April 2023, pro-Taiwan demonstrators gathered outside a hotel in downtown Los Angeles - Central (California) in support of Taiwanese independence and of a visit by Taiwanese President Tsai Ing-wen. A smaller group of counter-demonstrators demonstrated in the name of 'One China.'

On 22 April 2023, hundreds of people protested in Big Rapids (Michigan) at the proposed site of a battery plant. Those present included Michigan Republican Party chairperson Kristina Karamo, Rep. John Moolenaar (R), and State Sen. Lana Theis (R). Demonstrators were concerned about the company's ties to China and the possible negative environmental impact.

On 12 May 2023, members of Falun Gong and the Chinese community held a march as part of World Falun Dafa Day in New York - Manhattan (New York) to demonstrate against the Communist Party of China and its religious prosecutions.

On 23 May 2023, a perpetrator came up to a man and a woman of Asian descent, used anti-Chinese slur, pulled the man out and beat him as the couple were getting into an Uber in New York - Manhattan (New York) in an unprovoked attack. The male victim suffered minor injuries. Police are investigating the incident as a hate crime.

Property destruction: On 14 September 2023, a 76-year-old man allegedly vandalized the Wing Luke Museum of the AsianPacific American Experience in Chinatown in Seattle (Washington) by breaking multiple windows with a sledgehammer while saying 'hateful things about Chinese people.' Police said he said 'the Chinese ruined my life' to them upon his arrest. The 76-year-old man is being charged with property destruction and anti-Asian hate crime offenses.

On 2 October 2023, about 200 demonstrators rallied in Manteno (Illinois) to protest the planned arrival of a Chinese battery manufacturing plant due to concerns over safety of the community and the company's affiliation with the Chinese Communist Party. Those present included members of the Illinois Freedom Caucus, Manteno Mayor Tim Nugent, State Rep. Don Caulkins (R), State Rep. Chris Miller (R), State Rep. Blane Wilhour (R), and State Rep. Brad Halbrook (R).

On 9 October 2023, an individual drove a vehicle into the lobby of the Consulate General of the People's Republic of China in San Francisco (California) and yelled 'where is CCP?' apparently referring to the Chinese Communist Party. A spokesperson for the Consulate said the crash caused serious damage and represented a major threat to safety. The individual then fought with the police. Police shot and killed the individual. It is unclear if the individual was armed, and police did not initially elaborate on why he was killed or whether he was a US or Chinese national.

On 15 October 2023, Falun Gong practitioners gathered in Chinatown in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to celebrate Chinese people who have left the Chinese Communist Party and condemn what they describe as 'forced organ harvesting' and China's 'undemocratic regime.' 35 Chinese people who have quit the CCP were present at the event. Pennsylvania State Representative Sharif Street (D) spoke at the rally.

On 15 October 2023, Falun Gong adherents marched in New York - Brooklyn (New York) to protest against the government of China's treatment of Falun Gong practitioners and the Communist Party of China's policies.

On 16 October 2023, people gathered outside the White House in Washington DC - National Mall (District of Columbia) to call for China to stop repatriating North Korean defectors and to call for the support of the international community. South Korean lawmaker Tae Young-ho (People's Power) and members of North Korea Freedom Coalition were present.

On 15 November 2023, dozens of people from the Emergency Committee on the Forced Repatriation of North Korean Escapees, a South Korean group visiting the United States, gathered in front of the White House in Washington DC - National Mall (District of Columbia) to call for China to stop repatriating North Korean escapees to North Korea. The group later held a press conference in front of the Chinese embassy.

On 14 November 2023, about 50 people gathered in front of the UN Headquarters in New York - Manhattan (New York) to call for China to stop repatriating North Korean escapees to North Korea. Among the participating groups were members of The Korean American Association of New York, the New York Advisory Council for Democratic and Peaceful Unification, and the Northeastern American Branch of the Korean Veterans Association.

On 15 November 2023, hundreds of demonstrators marched to the Moscone Center in San Francisco (California) to denounce Chinese President Xi Jinping as he attended the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' conference. The demonstration included the Tibetan National Congress, the New Federal State of China, and Chinese, Uyghur, Tibetan, and Hong Kong nationals demanding human rights and that China end its 'forced education' and censorship in Tibet, its arrest of Chinese political prisoners, and its policies on Taiwan, Xinxiang, and Hong Kong. The march was met by Chinese nationals and Chinese-American counter-demonstrators showing support for President Xi. There were several incidents of pushing and shoving but no casualties or arrests.

On 16 November 2023, members of the Vietnamese community demonstrated at the Moscone Center in San Francisco (California) to denounce Chinese President Xi Jinping and Vietnamese President Vo Van Thuong as they attended the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' conference. They were organized by the United Vietnamese American Community of Northern California.

Property destruction: On 7 December 2023, an unknown assailant smashed the front glass door and broke into the WaterCreek Nails and Spa in Salt Lake City (Utah) and sprayed painted 'fuck China' in the store (though the store's owners are Vietnamese). The nail salon has incurred a reported $15,000 in damages and the police are investigating this incident as a hate crime.

On 10 February 2024, people and members of the Tibetan community gathered at the Town Hall in Belleville (New Jersey) to honor the Lunar Year and to demonstrate solidarity with the people of Tibet. Some participants also stood against Chinese communist 'oppression.' Mayor Michael Melham participated in the demonstration.

On 20 April 2024, roughly 35 local residents, Harvard students, and members of Falun Gong, the Tibetan and Taiwanese communities rallied in front of the Kennedy School on campus in Cambridge (Massachusetts) outside of the Chinese Ambassador to the United States' speech condemning China for what they called 'colonial boarding schools' in Tibet, as well as Chinese policy on Tibet, Hong Kong, East Turkestan, and Taiwan. Six protesters disrupted the Ambassador's address. Students for a Free Tibet and Coalition of Students Resisting China organized the rally. Security forces escorted the protesters out but it was not immediately clear if they were physically removed or if they complied with orders to leave.

On 21 April 2024, more than a dozen protesters, members of the Chinese community, and Falun Gong practitioners rallied in Flushing in New York - Queens (New York) to call for an end to China's persecution of Falun Gong and in support of the Tuidang movement which encourages the Chinese community to withdraw from the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) organizations. State Assembly District Leader Martha Flores Vazquez (D) joined the rally.

On 10 May 2024, thousands of Falun Gong members and Chinese Americans marched on World Falun Dafa Day in New York - Manhattan (New York) to support Falun Gong ideology and to demand an end to persecution in China.

On 2 June 2024, members of the Falun Gong, Doctors Against Forced Organ Harvesting, and professors gathered outside of the American Transplant Congress meeting in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for an end to forced organ harvesting and 'genocide' in China, and an end to persecution of the Falun Gong. Delaware State Representative Mike Ramone (R) was present at the event.
On 20 July 2023, Falun Gong members gathered in Washington DC - National Mall (District of Columbia) to call for an end to persecution of Falun Gong in China.

On 11 July 2024, thousands of people, including members of the Falun Gong, US Commission in International Religious Freedom, Alliance Defending Freedom, Christian Freedom International, Friends of Falun Gong, Tuidang Center, World Organization to Investigate the Persecution of Falun Gong, and Victims of Communism, gathered in Washington DC - National Mall (District of Columbia) to call for an end to persecution of Falun Gong practitioners in China. Representative Pat Ryan (D) spoke at the event.

On 21 August 2024, protesters gathered outside of a Senate campaign rally for Mike Rogers (R) in Green Charter Township (Michigan) to support creating an electric vehicle factory in the area because they claim it will create jobs. Another group of counter-protesters opposed the creation of the electric vehicle factory saying that it would benefit China more than local workers and would negatively impact the environment. Representative John Moolenaar (R) also participated in the rally against the factory.

On 2 September 2024, Falun Gong members and members of Doctors Against Forced Organ Harvesting gathered in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for an end to persecution of Falun Gong in China and an end to forced organ harvesting.

On 14 September 2024, several members of the Falun Gong marched in the Chinese Mid-Autumn Festival parade in New York - Brooklyn (New York) to demonstrate against the Chinese Communist Party and to demand more people quit it. The parade was organized by the Global Service Center for Quitting the CCP. During the march, an Asian American man attacked several members of Falun Gong. The man spat on a woman, repeatedly punched another woman from behind, briefly left, and then returned to hit the second woman on the neck and back.

On 14 September 2024, more than 50 Burmese Americans gathered outside of the Chinese Embassy in Washington DC - Northwest (District of Columbia) to call for China to withdraw support for Myanmar's military junta and 'sham' elections.

On 9 October 2024, a group of protesters, including Chinese-Americans, gathered outside of the Chinese ambassador's house in Washington DC - Northwest (District of Columbia) to protest against persecution by the Chinese government. Demonstrators protest daily.

On 10 November 2024, Burmese protesters gathered outside of the Chinese Embassy in Washington DC - Northwest (District of Columbia) to protest against the Burmese military leader's visit to China. Demonstrators say that the visit amounts to formal recognition of the military council.

On 20 January 2025, dozens of Proud Boys affiliates marched in Washington DC - Northwest (District of Columbia) in support of President Donald Trump, to demand the release of 'political prisoners' referring to people who were detained inside due to their participation in the 6 January 2021 Capitol Riot, and to promote their group. Affiliates also chanted 'Fuck Joe Biden.' Proud Boys briefly joined a group of Chinese American demonstrators who they passed, chanting together to demand an end to the Chinese Communist Party. Counter-protesters also confronted marchers to condemn them.

On 1 February 2025, members of Falun Gong marched in the Chinese New Year's parade in Flushing in New York - Queens (New York) to demonstrate against the Chinese Communist Party and to support Falun Gong.

On 10 March 2025, members of the Tibetan community gathered in Madison (Wisconsin) to mark the 66th anniversary of the Tibetan National Uprising and to call upon China to 'stop cultural genocide in Tibet', call for peace and the protection of religious rights in Tibet. The protest was attended by Madison Mayor Satya Rhodes-Conway (D).

On 19 August 2024, people, including Korean groups, gathered outside the Chinese Consulate General in Los Angeles - Central (California) to protest against the Chinese government repatriating North Korean defectors. Demonstrators gathered outside the consulate for three days.

On 21 December 2024, in Maracay (Aragua), several members of the Los Jardineros gang abducted a Chinese local business owner for ransom, as he was driving in his private vehicle down Bermudez Avenue. He would be liberated the day after, following an armed clash between these suspects and CICPC police forces in San Diego (Carabobo), where the kidnapers shot the victim in the leg (coded separately). There were no casualties.
On 21 May 2019, a group of teachers protested outside the Chinese Embassy in Baruta, Caracas and presented a document that details the violations to their labor rights by the regime.

On 23 March 2023, in Ciudad Guayana (Bolivar), a group of workers of the Venezuelan subsidiary of the China Railway No. 10 Engineering Group (CREG Venezuela), protested to demand payment of owed stipends, and answers from the company's upper management. The protesters argue that they are owed over six weeks of pay. The protest was staged inside the plant.

On 22 March 2024, in Caracas - Libertador (Distrito Capital), three unidentified crime group suspects abducted a Chinese woman from her home in the 23 de Enero neighborhood, and held her for a 50,000 USD ransom. Her husband paid the fee and she was liberated shortly after. All three kidnappers were arrested a few days later.

On 15 July 2020, in Valencia, Carabobo state, a group of workers from three companies protested to reject the import of Chinese tires. Protesters informed that this import is putting at risk the national production.

Around 17 December 2020 (as reported), in Valencia (Carabobo state), workers from the rubber industry held a protest to call for authorities to reactive the sector in the state and to demand Chinese producers to pay taxes on their rubber exports to Venezuela. Protesters reported that the importation of Chinese rubbers, exempted from taxes, has created unfair competition in the market and left most of the country's manufacturing companies paralyzed.

Combination of two related events. On 14 March 2018, in Hanoi, activists held an unauthorized ceremony commemorating the 1988 naval clash with China. There was a brief brawl between activists and a few others believed to be government supporters at the ceremony. The police did not interfere; On 14 March 2018, in Hanoi, a man was beaten at a police station when seeking the release of another activist who had been detained for attending an unauthorized commemoration of the 1988 naval clash with China. The activist lost two of his teeth due to the beating.

Farmers marched to the parliament in Maseru, demonstrating against the regulations that force them to sell their wool and mohair to a Chinese broker. . several thousand farmers in the mountain kingdom of lesotho marched to parliament on friday to protest against regulations forcing them to sell their wool and mohair to a chinese broker. wool and mohair are key exports for farmers in lesotho, but the government of the small southern africa nation signed a monopoly deal last year with a chinese broker who is accused of failing to pay for goods. the protest won the support of some members of prime minister thomas thabane s all basotho convention party, most opposition parties and prince seeiso bereng seeiso, the king s brother. about 30,000 farmers in lesotho, which is entirely surrounded by south africa, rely on wool and mohair exports. we will not sell our wool and mohair to the chinese, we would rather burn it, mokoenihi thinyane, chairman of the national wool and mohair growers association, told protesters in the capital maseru. the day before the march, the government suspended the monopoly deal for three months to allow farmers to sell globally. spokesman for the opposition parties selibe mochoboroane said we will fight this war by legal means and if we don t win, we will resort to other means.

On 5 May 2016, more than 300 villagers staged a protest against the Chinese Wanbao mining company because it had failed to follow recommendations made by an investigative committee report. hundreds of myanmar villagers rallied against a controversial chinese backed copper mine, activists said, reigniting a contentious issue that could pose an early challenge to aung san suu kyi s new government. the letpadaung mine in the central town of monywa has for years been dogged by complaints of land grabbing, environmental damage and brutal police crackdowns on protesters. growing numbers of villagers have gathered over the past four days in the first major anti mine demonstration since suu kyi s civilian administration took power this year, ending decades of military domination. today we demanded our rights by showing up with over 200 local protesters, said khin lae, a protest leader. no one was hurt today. yesterday there were some clashes between protesters and the police, she added. winbao, the chinese firm that jointly runs the mine with a major myanmar military conglomerate, said this year it aimed to start production in may after years of construction. another protest organiser, amar cho, said the demonstrations have swelled since wednesday, as have the number of police dispatched to control the crowds.

More that 60 demonstrators protest against the increase in rhino poaching during the bail application of three Chinese nationals accused of poaching. zoo park was fittingly the venue for namibia s first anti rhino poaching protest, bringing together more than 60 demonstrators fighting the cause of the threatened species yesterday. now that it looks as if the eyes of the poachers are turning towards namibia, we want to send them a strong message that we have zero tolerance for poachers, and that they will be caught and sent to jail, high school pupil nita pallett said during the protest. at yesterday s protest, weeks told the namibian that it was vital that the public took a stand during the bail hearing of the chinese to ensure that a zero tolerance policy would be enforced before the situation ends up like in south africa , where rhino poaching has reached unprecedented and uncontrollable levels. weeks also said that the protest was aimed at creating awareness not only among the public but also among lawmakers, who should amend legislation to ensure that current laws to protect wildlife, which are too lenient , are tightened.

Miners and villagers killed Chinese manager by hitting him with a trolley during a riot over demands for new minimum wage. Manager's colleague and another person injured in riot.
