09/11/1998: Three Chinese nationals were kidnapped on Sitangkai, a remote southern island in the Philippines. The families of the kidnapped were about to board their family van when three armed men entered their compound and dragged them outside to a waiting dark blue vehicle. No group claimed responsibility, but Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) was suspected of the attack.

09/26/1999: Around a dozen Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) boats attacked and attempted to hijack the M.V. Yugi,  a Chinese cargo vessel carrying fertilizer, along the northeastern coast of Sri Lanka. The ship, which sustained some damage from rocket-propelled grenades, was rescued quickly by four Navy gunboats after by police officials. One perpetrator was believed to have died during the exchange of fire with the Navy.

05/25/2000: A Chinese delegation member was killed and two others injured when their car came under automatic weapon fire from unknown attackers in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. The Chinese delegation was helping to investigate an arson incident that occurred earlier in the May 2000. In addition to the two Chinese delegates who were killed and injured, respectively, their Kyrgyz driver was also injured.

05/09/2001: One person was killed and three more were wounded when the vehicle a group of workers with the Bureau of Geophysics Prospects (BGP), a Chinese company, was traveling in was hit by a rocket in Sunny Shoran, Sibi district, Pakistan. The group was surveying for oil as subcontractors for the British Premier Oil company. No group claimed responsibility for the attack. The Pakistani driver, Bacha Khan, was killed, while the two guards and the Chinese engineer, Pong Weixing, were going to survive their injuries.  China halted work in the area because of the attack. Although the specific motive was unknown, sources note that oil and gas surveyers are often targeted by local tribes.

08/12/2001: Four people, three Chinese and a Filipino businessman, were kidnapped by former members of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) while they were trying to secure the release of a man previously taken captive, in Datu Paglas village, North Cotabato Province, Philippines. Two were killed and one was unhurt after a rescue operation by Filipino soldiers on August 19, 2001. Two of the Chinese men were killed in the course of the rescue operation and one was successfully rescued. The Filipino businessman was not accounted for in reports. The kidnapping victims were Zang Zong Yee, Wang Shung Li, Zho Zhing, all Chinese; and Filipino Edwin Lim. It was not known which persons were killed in the rescue.

11/27/2001: Palestinian gunmen fired upon an Israeli car near Sinjil, West Bank, West Bank and Gaza Strip. Loyan Zehn, a worker from China and the only person in the car, was injured in the attack. He continued driving and succeeded in reaching authorities and receiving medical attention. No group claimed responsibility for the incident.

12/20/2001: Two Chinese nationals were killed and a third wounded in Irkutsk, Russia. The attack was described as a "contract-hit" by local news agencies. Reports stated that the surviving Chinese national, who received multiple gunshot wounds, was rushed to the hospital. He managed to scribble a telephone number and several clues on the floor of the vehicle before he was taken to the hospital. The attack was described as a "contract-hit" by local news organizations.
06/29/2002: A Chinese diplomat was assassinated and his driver was killed in Bishkek, the capital city of Kyrgyzstan. The two men who were contracted for the murder were apprehended.

02/10/2003: At around 11:30PM local time, an armed gang of four men stormed the residence of the Chinese Ambassador to Guinea-Bissau at his residence in the capital, Bissau, along with two other Chinese Embassy staff. The Diplomats, including the Ambassador were stabbed in a violent knife attack and beaten with iron bars. They were then taken to the Chinese Embassy at around 3:30AM local time and forced to remove cash from the Embassy safe. The armed gang were about to leave with the cash and valuables from the Ambassador's residence at around 4AM on 02/11/2003 when a special Police intervention squad arrived at the Embassy. In the ensuing gunfight, one kidnapper was killed; the other three escaped and were not captured. Guinea-Bissau's Internal Administration Minister stated that political motives could not be ruled out.

03/20/2003: A Chinese fishing vessel was bombed and sunk, killing 14 fishermen on board and injuring one, off the Eastern Coast of Sri Lanka in a rocket attack by suspected Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels. Nine other fisherman, including a Sri Lanka national, were rescued by another vessel nearby. The rebels denied the accusation.

05/03/2004: Unknown perpetrators used a car bomb to kill three Chinese nationals, and injured 11 others riding in a bus en route to the port city of Gwadar, Pakistan, approximately 300 miles west of Karachi on the border with Iran.as 12 engineers from the China Engineering Harbour Company traveled in a van to work at Gwadar, an Arabian Sea coastal town near the Iranian border some 480 kilometers (300 miles) west of Karachi, Pakistan..

06/10/2004: Eleven Chinese construction workers were shot dead when unidentified gunmen launched a night-time raid on their compound in north-eastern Afghanistan. Sixteen people were also injured in the attack. Up to 20 unknown, armed men stormed the site south of Kunduz and opened fire in what the Chinese embassy said was a terrorist attack. Muslim Militants were suspected in the attack.

07/27/2004: A rocket launched by suspected Taliban fighters hit the road directly in front of the Chinese Embassy in Kabul, Afghanistan. There were no casualties, but the rocket did cause some damage. A 60 centimeter-wide crater was left in the road, and the Embassy gate and wall, as well as a housing unit, had slight damage. The rocket also landed near the house of Afghanistan’s Minister of Health, so the intended target was unclear.

10/09/2007: Two Chinese engineers working on the Gomalzam dam project in South Waziristan were kidnapped by Afghan immigrants in a region known to contain many Al-Qaida affiliated fighters. The Gomalzam Dam is a 203 million dollar project that has between 70 and 80 Chinese engineers working on it. During the resolution of the hostage crisis, a tribal chieftan agreed to separately guard both the kidnapped and the kidnappers. The kidnappers had been holed up in a cave surrounded by Pakistani security forces. Though Afghan immigrants conducted the kidnapping, it is believed that foreign elements were behind it.

02/15/2006: Gunmen on motorcycles fatally shot three Chinese engineers and their Pakistani driver as they were driving home from work in the town of Hub, Balochistan Province, Pakistan. Balochistan Liberation Army claimed responsibility for the attack, stating that the Chinese were aiding the Pakistani government in exploiting Balochistan's natural resources. The attack came just four days before President Pervez Musharraf left for China on a five-day official visit to strengthen the links between the allies. The Balochistan Liberation Army spokesman said that the Chinese were aiding the Pakistani government in exploiting Balochistan's natural resources.

04/13/2006: More than a dozen youths attacked Chinese construction workers in Chita, Russian Federation, in an apparently racially-motivated assault. No group claimed responsibility for the attack. This was part of a series of attacks on foreigners in Russia around this time.

08/21/2006: A blast at a crowded market in Moscow, Russia killed ten people and wounded dozens. Authorities believed the attack could have been motivated by race, as at least six of the ten killed were of Asian ethnicity. Two men were detained for questioning, but no one claimed responsibility for the attack.

01/05/2007: Five Chinese telecommunications workers were kidnapped by gunmen from their residence in Rumauakunde Emouha, Nigeria. They were held for 13 days before their release by an unidentified group.

01/25/2007: Seven employees of a Chinese oil company were abducted as gunmen stormed the local offices in the southern Nigerian state of Bayelsa. Militants were behind the attack, but no specific group has claimed responsibility for the attack. To attack Chinese business.

04/24/2007: Over 200 gunmen of the Ogaden National Liberation Front (ONLF) attacked a Chinese-run oil field in Abole, Ethiopia. Seventy-four people were killed including nine Chinese and 65 Ethiopians, in a raid claimed by the ONLF separatist rebel group on their website. The exploration facility of the Zhongyuan Petroleum Exploration Bureau of the China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation was completely destroyed. Seven Chinese workers were also kidnapped and then released unharmed five days later on April 29, 2007.
06/13/2007: Three Chinese civilians were kidnapped by an unknown number of unknown perpetrators carrying unspecified weapons in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. No claim of responsibility was reported.

properties.actor: Movement of Niger People for Justice (MNJ)
properties.notes: 07/06/2007: A Chinese executive, Zhang Guohua, was kidnapped in Niger's north region of Agadez by Tuareg tribesmen. The Movement of Niger People for Justice claimed responsibility for the attack. It said that the kidnapping was in response to the company's policy of employing people from the capital rather than locals, according to the Chinese embassy.

07/08/2007: Three Chinese workers were killed and one wounded in an attack near Peshawar, Pakistan. No claim of responsibility was reported. Authorities believe the attack may be related to the Lal Masjid Mosque confrontation.

07/20/2007: A suicide bomber of unknown affiliation targeted a convoy of Chinese workers in the town of Hub, Pakistan, killing 30 Pakistanis but no Chinese nationals. No claim of responsibility was issued for the suicide bomb attack.

02/25/2008: A group of unidentified gunmen, dressed in uniforms similar to those worn by Burmese drug traffickers, attacked a Chinese patrol boat on the Mekong River near the Lao-Burmese border, 10 km from Chiang Rai's Chiang Saen district. The attackers boarded the patrol boat and shot and stabbed the officers in a span of five minutes. Three Chinese police officers were injured. No group actually claimed responsibility for the incident. It is likely that the perpetrators were trying to protect a drugs shipment on the river as the Chinese officers had received a tip-off on a drug delivery. Although no group claimed responsibility for this attack, the perpetrators are suspected of being involved in the rampant drug trafficking that occurs in this area.

4/7/2008: On Monday, five suspected Nezavisimost-88 (Independence-88) skinheads attacked three Chinese nationals on Miklukho-Maklai Street in Moscow, Moscow, Russia. Two members of the group nicknamed Sokol and Vandal have been arrested for the attack. The victims were hit and stabbed while the skinheads shouted nationalist slogans at them.

4/9/2008: Ten perpetrators, believed to be affiliated with the Islamic insurgency in Algeria, attacked Chinese workers in Souk El Had, Algeria. One member of the Algerian municipal guard was killed defending the workers. Additionally, one of the assailants was wounded in the incident. To protest the presence of foreigners in Algeria.

12/13/2008: On Saturday night, Peter Go, a cashier of Perlas Trading in Barangay Walled, Jolo, was abducted by four suspected Abu Sayyaf militants. Go was closing his electronics store late when four armed men accosted him, disarmed his security guard and took Go away in a van. Chief Inspector Usman Pingay, the Jolo police chief, said Go's real name is Xili Wu, from the Chinese province of Fujian. Police pursued the  kidnappers but lost them in Indanan. Police suspected the group behind the kidnapping was led by Commander Albader Parad. No group claimed responsibility. It is unknown the length of detainment and the outcome of the kidnapping. Commander Albader Parad of the ASG is suspected as being involved in the kidnapping.

12/24/2008: On Wednesday, in Malakand, North-West Frontier, Pakistan, assailants assaulted and wounded one security guard and one driver,  then fired upon and wounded one Chinese engineer. There was no damage reported and no group claimed responsibility. The specific motive for the attack is unknown.

properties.actor: Movement for the Emancipation of the Niger Delta (MEND)
properties.notes: 07/07/2009: On Tuesday, off the coast of the Bakassi peninsula in Cameroon, five unidentified Chinese nationals were abducted while on a trawler. According to unconfirmed reports, the five victims worked in the fisheries sector of the peninsula. The status of the hostages is unknown. No group claimed responsibility for the attack however the Movement for the Emancipation of the Niger Delta (MEND) was believed to be responsible. Jomo Gbomo, a spokesman for MEND said he was unaware of the incident. Neither the Cameroon government nor the Chinese embassy could confirm the incident.

8/6/2009: An explosive device was discovered by workers at a construction site in Lakhdaria, Bouira province, Algeria. Security forces safely defused the device. The construction site was operated by CITIC-CRCC, a Chinese company that was responsible for building a portion of the east-west highway. No group claimed responsibility and the specific motive was unknown; however, this was the second bomb to placed at a CITIC-CRCC site in less than a month. The town of Lakhdaria was placed under tight security following the incident and sources indicated that a larger attack was expected. Specific motive is unknown; however, sources indicate that the incident may have been follow-up on threats that groups directed towards the Chinese in the past.

01/16/2010: On Saturday, in an unspecified location of the Faryab province, Afghanistan, two Chinese engineers, two Afghan drivers and two guards were kidnapped by the Taliban. On 1/19/2010 the four Afghans were released after negotiations by tribal elders and the Taliban. The two Chinese engineers were still in militant custody. No casualties were reported. The two Chinese engineers were still in militant custody.

02/08/2010: On Monday morning around 0700, in Cotabato City, unidentified gunmen shot dead a Chinese-Filipino businessman who was running for councilor of Cotabato City in the May elections. Joseph Kwan Datuwata, 42, had just left his home in Rosary Heights 10 with his two children when their vehicle was flagged down by three armed men. The gunmen shot Cuan in the head and chest with a .45 caliber pistol, killing him instantly. His two children were also injured in the attack. No group has claimed responsibility.

05/02/2010: On Sunday, in Athens, Greece, a bomb exploded at a branch of the Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation bank, damaging the bank but causing no casualties. The home-made bomb was comprised of gas canisters and fuel. No group claimed responsibility, but it was widely believed that anarchists were responsible.

05/16/2010: On Sunday, in Habban, Shabwah, Yemen, armed tribesmen kidnapped two Chinese engineers, their two Yemeni drivers, and two Yemeni soldiers. On 05/19/2010 the assailants released all of the victims. No group claimed responsibility, but it was believed that Aqmur or Laqmush tribesmen kidnapped them in response to the killing of a member of this tribe in a clash with the personnel of a checkpoint.

07/06/2010: On Tuesday, in Gawadar, Balochistan, Pakistan, unidentified militants fired rockets from a boat seaside at the Gawadar Port and the Gawadar Pearl Continental Hotel targeting Chinese engineers. The engineers had arrived in Gwadar recently and were reportedly working on an oil refinery. Official sources believe that they were the targets of the attack. The hotel’s elevator was destroyed in the attack. No casualties were reported and no group claimed responsibility. Police officials suspected that the target of the attack were the Chinese engineers. The specific motive for the attack is unknown.

08/16/2010: On Monday afternoon around 1700, on Magallanes Street, in Cotabato City, Maguindanao, Philippines, five unidentified armed men wearing military uniforms kidnapped a Chinese businessman, identified as Nelson Tay, owner of New Asian Marketing from his store. The men barged inside his store and disarmed a security guard and then took Tay into a van outside the store and sped off, leaving behind the security guard who reported the matter to the police. On 08/19/2010 Nestor Tay was freed. The release of Tay came a day after Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) rebels joined the search for the kidnapped trader. “Tay was freed because of the pressure exerted by the MILF to the kidnappers,” said Von Al-Haq, the MILF spokesman. It was unknown if a ransom was demanded. No group claimed responsibility.

09/05/2010: On Sunday, in the Qaisar district of Faryab, Afghanistan, a vehicle carrying construction company workers was intercepted by armed assailants. They forced a Chinese engineer that was aboard out of the vehicle and took him hostage while letting the other 11 Afghans go. No group claimed responsibility but the Taliban is suspected responsible. The status of the hostage remains unknown and there was no damage reported in the attack to property.

properties.actor: Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda (FLEC)
properties.notes: 11/08/2010: On Monday, in an unknown area of Cabinda, Angola, unidentified militants attacked a military convoy transporting a group of Chinese mine workers by unknown means, killing two Angolan soldiers. No damage was reported and the militant group Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda claimed responsibility for the attack.

11/26/2010: On Friday, in an unknown location in Janub Kurdufan, Sudan, unidentified militants abducted a Chinese national oil field worker from an oil facility worksite by unknown means. No casualties were reported and the hostage was released on 11/27/2010. No group claimed responsibility for the attack.

11/4/2011: Four members of New People's Army (NPA) attacked a road repair project site in Bansalan, Davao del Sur province, Philippines. The assailants poured gasoline on and set fire to four large pieces of machinery belonging to the Chinese firm Qingjian Group; the Qingjian Group was part of the ongoing project to pave portions of the Davao del Sur-North Cotabato highway. The NPA has stated that it would attack corporations that were responsible for environmental destruction and worker abuse.

01/29/2012: Assailants attacked 47 Chinese construction workers in South Kordofan, Sudan. Seventeen workers escaped, one was shot and killed, and 29 were kidnapped in the attack. The group's president, Malik Agar, met with the Chinese ambassador to Ethiopia, demanding extra Red Cross humanitarian aid in the country. The hostages were released on February 7, 2012. No group claimed responsibility, but sources attributed the incident to members of the Sudan People's Liberation Movement: North. Fourteen of the 29 Chinese workers who were taken hostage in this attack were freed on 01/30/2012. The fate of the remaining 15 hostages is unknown. The specific motive is unknown; however, sources noted that the assailants demanded extra Red Cross humanitarian aid in Sudan in exchange for the hostages.

01/31/2012: Twenty-five Chinese workers were abducted from a bus on their way to a cement factory in Arish city, North Sinai governorate, Egypt. The hostages were released 15 hours later with no injuries. Bedouin tribesman claimed responsibility for the incident and demanded the release of five relatives who were jailed for a suspected role in terrorist incidents in South Sinai between the years 2004 and 2006.

03/02/2012: A roadside bomb detonated and injured two employees of China International Water and Electric Corporation in Pigcawayan, North Cotabato, Philippines. No group claimed responsibility for the incident.

03/30/2012: Assailants set fire to equipment at a construction site in Dolo town, Davao del Sur province, Philippines. The equipment was owned by CNQC-Quingjian Group of Companies. There were no casualties reported in the attack, and the assailants claimed to be members of the New People's Army (NPA).

06/04/2012: Assailants kidnapped Yuan Kai Lin, vice president of operations for Li-Lo Mineral Traders, and a companion in Kabasalan city, Zamboanga Sibugay province, Philippines. The companion was released on August 26, 2012, and Yuan Kai Lin was rescued in a raid on September 20, 2012; neither abductee was injured during the incident. No group claimed responsibility, but sources attributed the incident to Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG).

04/07/2013: Assailants set fire to mining equipment in Napaod town, Camarines Norte province, Philippines. There were no reported casualties; however two dump trucks and two payloaders were destroyed in the attack. The National Democratic Front-Bicol (NDF-Bicol) claimed responsibility, stating that the incident was retaliation against foreign mining firms that abuse the environment and put civilian lives at risk. Additionally, authorities suspect that the New People's Army (NPA) was behind the attack.

05/21/2013: Assailants attempted to detonate an explosive device hidden on the road near a van carrying Chinese workers escorted by Rangers in Karachi city, Sindh province, Pakistan. No one was injured in the blast because the device did not fully detonate. No group claimed responsibility for the incident.

09/30/2013: Assailants launched a mortar shell that landed near the compound of the Chinese Embassy in Mazzeh neighborhood, Damascus city, Damascus governorate, Syria. At least one person was injured while the embassy and several nearby vehicles were damaged in the blast. No group claimed responsibility for the incident. The specific motive is unknown; however, sources speculated that the attack, which targeted the Chinese embassy, is part of a larger spike in mortar strikes against embassies of countries supportive of the Assad regime.

10/31/2013: Assailants attacked an oil tower in the Al-Ahdab oilfield, Wasit governorate, Iraq. The number of injuries and damage is unknown; however, the assailants stole the cell phones and weapons of the oil field guards. No group claimed responsibility for the incident.

04/02/2014: Assailants kidnapped a Chinese tourist and a Filipino worker from the Singhamata Reef Resort resort in Semporna town, Sabah state, Malaysia. The kidnappers took the victims to the Philippines and demanded a ransom of $11,562,045.00 for the Chinese victim. Both victims were released unharmed on May 30, 2014. No group claimed responsibility for the incident; however, sources attributed it to the Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG).

04/05/2014: Assailants attacked the Philastron mining firm in Tagmamarkay village, Agusan del Norte province, Philippines. No one was injured in the attack, but several pieces of construction equipment were damaged. No group claimed responsibility for the incident; however, sources attributed the incident to the New People's Army (NPA)'s Northeastern Mindanao Regional Command. The specific motive is unknown; however, an army spokesperson stated that the attack was the result of an extortion attempt by the New People's Army (NPA).

04/18/2014: Assailants opened fire on Kanar oil field near Baleela area in West Kordofan state, Sudan. Five people, including two guards and three assailants, were killed and eight workers, including three foreign workers, were abducted in the attack. The three foreign workers were released on May 1, 2014; however, the fate of the remaining five workers is unknown. The Sudanese People's Front claimed responsibility for the incident and stated that it was carried out in retaliation to the government's alleged refusal to employ residents of West Kordofan state in the oil industry.

05/06/2014: Five assailants abducted Yang Zai Lin from Pulau Baik, Sabah state, Malaysia. Lin, a Chinese national and manager at a local fish farm, was released on July 10, 2014. No group claimed responsibility for the incident; however, sources attributed the kidnapping to the Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG).

05/17/2014: Assailants opened fire on Sinohydro, a Chinese construction camp, near Waza town, Extreme-North region, Cameroon. At least one soldier was killed, one Chinese worker was wounded, and 10 others were abducted in the attack; the hostages were released on October 11, 2014. This was one of two attacks carried out by Boko Haram in Waza town on April 17, 2014. No group claimed responsibility for the incident; however, sources attributed the attack to Boko Haram.

05/19/2014: Assailants abducted a Chinese national in Daraban town, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan. The hostages was freed on October 22, 2015. Jaish al-Hadeed claimed responsibility for the attack. Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) also claimed responsibility for the incident, stating that the abduction was carried out in order to exchange the hostage for TTP members. The group later denied involvement. However, authorities questioned the veracity of the claim made by TTP.

05/20/2014: Assailants abducted three Chinese engineers at a construction site in Benghazi city, Benghazi district, Libya. One engineer was killed and the remaining two were released the same day. No group claimed responsibility for the incident.

05/22/2014: Assailants abducted two Chinese civilians, Dina Lim Iraham and Yahong Lim Tan, at a karaoke bar in Isabela city, Basilan province, Philippines. One hostafe was released in 2015 and the second hostage was released on May 3, 2016. No group claimed responsibility for the incident; however, sources attributed the abduction to the Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG).

06/16/2014: Assailants opened fire on a truck being escorted by a security convoy near Muxungue town, Sofala province, Mozambique. No one was killed or injured in the attack, but the truck was damaged. This was one of two coordinated attacks on convoys on the same road on the same day. No group claimed responsibility; however, sources attributed the incident to the Mozambique National Resistance Movement (MNR).

08/24/2014: Assailants abducted three China Machinery Engineering Corporation (CMEC) engineers while they were grocery shopping in Silopi town, Sirnak province, Turkey. The hostages were released on October 10, 2014. This was one of two attacks by the same group targeting the power plant and its employees on the same day. No group claimed responsibility; however, sources attributed the incidents to the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK).

09/11/2014: Assailants abducted Li Pei Zhei, a Chinese national, from his business in Zamboanga Sibugay province, Philippines. Zhei was released on November 5, 2014 after an unspecified ransom was paid. No group claimed responsibility; however, sources attributed the kidnapping to Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG). The specific motive is unknown; however, sources noted that the Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) released Li Pei Zhei in exchange for a ransom.

02/15/2015: Assailants abducted Hadja Dingkim Yap from her residence in Chinese Pier village, Jolo town, Sulu province, Philippines. Yap was released on March 18, 2015. No group claimed responsibility for the incident; however, sources attributed the abduction to the Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG). The specific motive is unknown; however, sources stated that the Abu Sayyaf Group (ASG) demanded a ransom in exchange for the victim.

02/19/2015: Assailants set fire to mining equipment in Patungcaleo village, Ilocos Sur province, Philippines. The equipment was damaged in the attack. The assailants identified themselves as members of the New People's Army (NPA).

04/26/2015: An assailant threw an explosive device targeting Chinese trains at a Pakistan Railways workshop near Garhi Shahu, Lahore city, Punjab province, Pakistan. The device failed to detonate, and no one was injured. No group claimed responsibility for the incident.

07/26/2015: A suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at the front gate of the Jazeera Palace Hotel in Mogadishu city, Banaadir region, Somalia. At least 18 people, including an employee of the Chinese Embassy, were killed and 41 others were injured in the blast. Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility and stated that the attack was carried out in retaliation for military operations in Somalia.

01/12/2016: Assailants threw an incendiary device at the residence of a Chinese family on Ebor Street in Belfast, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom. There were no reported casualties as the device failed to catch fire. No group claimed responsibility for the attack.

02/18/2016: An assailant armed with a hatchet attacked Zhang Yue, an 18-year-old Chinese exchange student, in Nashville, Indiana, United States. Yue was injured in the assault. Authorities arrested Dana Ericson, who confessed to the attack, self-identified as a white supremacist, and indicated that his goal was ethnic cleansing. In court Ericson stated that he was "trying to start a revolution."

08/18/2016: Assailants kidnapped a Chinese worker, Daniel Wu, in Posadas, Misiones, Argentina. Wu escaped unharmed later the same day. No group claimed responsibility for the incident; however, sources suspected that the Paraguayan People's Army (EPP) was involved.

08/30/2016: A suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at the front gate of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China (MOFA) Embassy in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Aside from the death of the bomber, at least three other people were wounded in the blast. No group claimed responsibility; however, sources attributed the attack to the Turkestan Islamic Party. The specific motive is unknown; however, sources noted that the attack occurred on the eve of Kyrgyzstan's 25th anniversary of the country's independence.

09/00/2016: Sometime between September 1, 2016 and September 30, 2016, a roadside bomb detonated targeting Chinese engineers in Hub, Balochistan, Pakistan. Two engineers were killed in the blast. No group claimed responsibility for the incident.

11/21/2016: Assailants attacked and took control of an Ecsa Ecuacorriente mining camp in Morona Santiago, Ecuador. The assailants relinquished control of the mining camp the following day. At least seven police officers were injured in the assault. Shuar extremists claimed responsibility for the incident and stated that the attack was carried out in response to military operations evicting Shuar civilians in order to open up the land for mining activities.

11/26/2016: Assailants opened fire on a Coal Geophysical Company vehicle in Kulanchi neighborhood, Pasni, Balochistan, Pakistan. At least two employees were killed and the driver was abducted in the assault. The hostage was released unharmed later the same day. The Baloch Liberation Front (BLF) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) separately claimed responsibility for the attack.

On 19 January 2026, an IS suicide bomber detonated himself inside a Chinese restaurant, known as the 'Chinese Noodle' restaurant, in Gulforoshi Alley in the Shahr-e Naw area of PD4, Kabul city (coded to Kabul - PD4). One Chinese Muslim national and six Afghan civilians were killed, and 13-20 others were wounded, many in critical condition, including four women and one child. Kabul's Emergency Hospital confirmed that 20 casualties were brought to the facility, seven of whom were dead upon arrival. The Taliban claimed the explosion was caused by a gas cylinder. However, residents and eyewitnesses described the blast as extremely powerful, shattering windows of nearby shops and homes. The restaurant was jointly run by a Chinese Muslim man, his wife, and an Afghan partner, and primarily served members of the Chinese Muslim community. Islamic State claimed responsibility for the attack, claiming it targeted Chinese nationals and their Taliban guards. IS claimed a total of 25 killed and wounded and said Chinese nationals were targeted due to alleged abuses against Uyghur Muslims. Some unverified reports claimed that a senior Chinese intelligence official may have been among the casualties. Total fatalities coded as 8 (including the suicide bomber) based on the lowest estimate.

On 12 July 2025, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), a large group marched from the intersection of Callao and Corrientes Avenues to Mayo Square to repudiate Israel's actions in Gaza, which they described as genocide. Protesters also condemned the annexation of the West Bank by Israel, its military actions against Iran, Syria, and Lebanon, and Argentina's political alignment with the United States, including the plan to relocate its embassy to Jerusalem. The Argentine Committee of Solidarity organized the march in support of the Palestinian People.

On 7 August 2025, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), hundreds of members of unions and various social organizations, students, retirees, Catholics, among others, after attending a mass, marched from the Saint Cajetan parish to Mayo Square, where members of Territories in Struggle and of various organizations from other nearby points also arrived from the Obelisk, to demonstrate against hunger, especially in poor neighborhoods due to the lack of food in community kitchens, the economic policies of President Javier Milei, the opening of imports, the labor reform promoted by the Minister of Deregulation, which they consider precarious, and the agreement between the National Government and the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The demonstrators also criticized the United States ambassador for statements they considered interfering, the violence and persecution against migrants, the dismantling of the Garrahan Hospital, the National Scientific and Technical Research Council (CONICET), National Roads, and the National Institute of Agricultural Technology (INTA), rejected policies that cut labor rights, demanded free wage negotiations, and denounced the judicial persecution of former president Cristina Fernandez, convicted and under house arrest for the 'Vialidad Case.' The mobilization, in the context of the feast of San Cayetano, included members of CTA-A, CTA, ATE, CATT, UOM, UOCRA, UPCN, UEJN, FOL, MLS, UATRE, UTEP, CCC, Barrios de Pie, FPDS, Evita Movement, a national deputy, and members of Patria Grande Front, La Campora, Not One Less (Argentina), PCR, Priests of Villas and Popular Neighborhoods of Argentina, 'Front for Sovereignty, Decent Work and Fair Wages,' Federation of Oil Workers, Movement for the Right to the Future, Maritime, Port and Naval Industry Federation of the Argentine Republic, Union of Newspaper and Magazine Vendors, Union of Leather Workers of the Argentine Republic (SOCRA), Association of Tax and Public Revenue Employees (AEFIP), Truck Drivers Union of the Province of Buenos Aires, Airline Pilots Association (APLA), among others.

On 27 August 2025, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), relatives of people killed by state force abuses participated in the 11th National March Against 'Gatillo Facil' (easy trigger). Participants remembered the victims and demanded an end to deaths caused by state abuses. The demonstrators also denounced femicides and transfemicides, expressed solidarity with the Palestinian people, and condemned Israel's actions in Gaza with the complicity of the United States. In addition, they supported Garrahan Hospital workers and their fight for wage and budget improvements. Similar protests took place in other cities.

On 30 August 2025, in San Carlos de Bariloche (Rio Negro), members of various groups gathered in the Civic Center to demand an end to the genocide in Gaza perpetrated by Israel and expressed support for the 'Global Sumud' flotila that will depart from Barcelona to Gaza. Demonstrators repudiated the possible visit of Israel's prime minister to Argentina and the support he receives from President Javier Milei and Donald Trump in the United States.

Participants repudiated the stance of President Javier Milei's government toward U.S. influence.

On 5 November 2025, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), retirees demonstrated in front of the National Congress to demand better pensions, free provision of medicine, and other social benefits. They also repudiated President Javier Milei's economic policies and his alignment with United States interventionism.

On 29 November 2025, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), thousands marched from the National Congress to May Square in solidarity with the Palestinian people and in opposition to attempts to release individuals convicted of crimes against humanity. Participants also repudiated what they claim is 'colonialism promoted by US President Donald Trump'; the presence of Israeli troops in Palestine, Syria, and Lebanon; and demanded severing diplomatic relations with Israel, as well as sanctions and boycotts. Members of the 'Memory, Truth, and Justice Gathering' and the Committee in Solidarity with the Palestinian People joined the mobilization.

On 3 January 2026, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 14 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), members and workers members of left-wing groups led by MST, FIT, and the International Socialist League (LIS) marched to the United States embassy to protest the US military operation that led to the detention of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. The demonstrators described the operation as an 'imperialist aggression' and a 'violation' of South American sovereignty.

On 3 January 2026, in Santa Rosa (La Pampa), members of various social organizations protested in front of the National University of La Pampa (UNLPAM) to repudiate the United States military operation that led to the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. The demonstrators claimed support for self-determination and the sovereignty of peoples. The Popular Movement of La Pampa for Human Rights called the mobilization, and a local councilor from the Patria Grande Front participated.

On 7 February 2026, in Santa Rosa (La Pampa), more than 50 individuals protested in San Martin square during the 'Second Anti-Fascist and Anti-Racist Pride March' against policies of President Javier Milei's government, its alignment with the United States, the national government's intervention in the port of Ushuaia, the facilitation of US access to Patagonian territory, the persecution of journalists, forest burning, and the reform of the Glacier Law, among other measures. The demonstrators also repudiated repression and defended migrants' rights. Memorias Maricas Pampeanas, the Network of Self-Organized Lesbian Identities (RILA), Pampa Trans, Familias Transformadas, and Frente Orgullo Pampeano, among others, supported the mobilization.

On 7 February 2026, in Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Buenos Aires), thousands participated in the 'Second Federal Anti-Fascist and Anti-Racist LGBTI+ Pride March,' which moved from Congress Square to Mayo Square to reclaim rights, oppose the labor reform and socioeconomic policies promoted by President Javier Milei, and demand historical reparation for older travestis and trans people. The demonstrators also opposed policies of President Trump (USA), the invasion of Venezuela, and the genocide in Palestine. The Homosexual Community of Argentina (CHA), 100% Diversity and Rights, Abosex Lawyers for Sexual Rights, and the Gender Secretariats at the national and Buenos Aires City levels supported the mobilization, among others.

On 9 March 2026, in Buenos Aires - Comuna 1 (Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires), thousands of women from social, feminist, union, and political organizations marched from Congress Square to May Square in commemoration of 8 March, International Working Women's Day. During the mobilization, they denounced machista violence, femicides, and the failure to implement public policies on sexual and reproductive health, as well as attacks on comprehensive sexual education, the labor reform, and the modification of the Glaciers Law promoted by the national government. They also spoke out against the attack by the United States and Israel on Iran, denounced labor precarization, and expressed support for the implementation of the university funding law. A group of participants diverted the march in front of the house of former President Cristina Fernandez to express support following her corruption conviction. Participants included members of the LGBTQ+ community, ATE, students, CTERA, UTE, Pan y Rosas, FIT, CTA, CGT, MST, supporters of the PJ, members of the collective Not One [Woman] Less, the Unified Union of Education Workers of Buenos Aires (SUTEBA), retirees, Mothers of Victims of Human Trafficking, Las Rojas, a national deputy (FIT) and a city legislator (PTS), university professors, workers from Garrahan Hospital, among others.

On 9 March 2026, in San Luis (San Luis), hundreds of women, members of sexual diversity groups, social organizations, unions, feminist collectives, and student groups mobilized from Pringles Square through the city center in the framework of International Working Women's Day to denounce setbacks in gender policies, hunger, and the advance of fascist and racist discourses. During the mobilization, in front of the Cathedral Church, participants burned effigies of Donald Trump, president of the United States, and Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli prime minister.

On 9 March 2026, in Villa Mercedes (San Luis), women gathered at the intersection of General Paz and Tucuman streets in the framework of International Working Women's Day, where they burned effigies of United States president Donald Trump, as well as Argentine president Javier Milei and other political figures, to repudiate their political actions. Participants also opposed the labor reform and the austerity policies of President Milei. They also remembered victims of violence and demanded justice for them.

On 25 April 2025, supporters of a man who has been detained by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and is facing deportation, protested in front of the US Embassy in Yerevan, Armenia, calling the US government to release him.

On 28 March 2026, about 20 demonstrators staged a No Kings protest at the Daniel K. Inouye Industrial Park, Tafuna (Western), to express concerns over democracy and leadership in the United States. Protesters displayed signs like 'Buy Books, Not Bombs,' 'No New Wars,' 'No Kings Since 1776,' 'Protect Our Democracy,' 'Healthcare, Not Warfare,' 'No Crowns, No Thrones, No Kings,' and 'We the People, No Kings.'

On 11 April 2025, about 50 activists from NSW university groups and student representative councils protested outside the Tesla Sydney offices in Alexandria, Sydney - Eastern, New South Wales denouncing Elon Musk's role in the Trump administration and accusing him of supporting authoritarian policies. Participants destroyed a cardboard model of a Tesla Cybertruck and displayed signs with slogans critical of Musk.

On 12 May 2025, members of the Palestinian community held a press conference outside the US consulate in Perth - Inner South, Western Australia, displaying photos of victims in Gaza. The Friends of Palestine WA secretary and a Greens senator attended.

On 24 May 2025, dozens of activists, including a Palestinian activist and a Tamil refugee activist, protested in Melbourne - Central, Victoria, calling on the government to 'cut ties with Trump's America.' Members of Free Palestine Melbourne, Students for Palestine, and the VS attended. The protest was part of a national day of action led by Students for Palestine, opposing Trump's far-right agenda, which includes undermining the rights of workers, trans people, Black people, and migrants, as well as mass deportations and detaining Palestine solidarity activists.

On 29 May 2025, people protested outside the United States consulate in Perth - Central, Western Australia, to mark 600 days of what they described as Israel's genocide in Gaza and to condemn Western governments' ongoing support.

On 22 June 2025, hundreds of people marched along St Kilda Rd to the US Consulate in Melbourne - Central, Victoria, against the Israeli attack on Gaza and Iran and the USA's participation in the conflict. They waved Palestinian flags. An Iranian activist who is also a member of Students for Palestine attended the event.

On 4 July 2025, people, including the Independent and Peaceful Australia Network chair, protested outside the United States Chamber of Commerce in Brisbane - Central, Queensland, against AUKUS. They opposed Australia's perceived military involvement with the USA in the Middle East, claiming the government is complicit in Israeli actions in Gaza and supports the USA's attack on Iran. They waved Palestinian flags.

On 8 August 2025, more than 250 people, including former students of the 8888 generation from Melbourne, Sydney, and Canberra, former members of the All Burma Students' Democratic Front (ABSDF), supporters, and Myanmar activists living in Australia, protested in front of the Myanmar Embassy in Canberra, Australian Capital Territory, to mark the 37th anniversary of the 8888 Uprising. They marched to the Chinese Embassy and submitted a petition urging the Chinese government to refrain from interfering in Myanmar's internal affairs and to stop supplying military weapons and aircraft to Min Aung Hlaing and the military junta. The event was organized by a group supporting the National Unity Government (NUG) and the Committee Representing the Pyidaungsu Hluttaw (CRPH).

On 12 September 2025, a group of people, including members of Jews for Palestine WA, protested at the US Consulate in Perth - Central (Western Australia). They voiced support for Palestine and condemned the US role in allowing Israel's war on Gaza. They also demanded that the Australian government end the arms trade with Israel and called for sanctions.

On 20 September 2025, a group of Latin American Solidarity activists, including members of the Socialist Alliance, a member of the Guatemala Human Rights Committee, and a member of the Association for Human Rights in Bolivia, peacefully protested at the Town Hall Square in Sydney - Eastern (New South Wales). They voiced several demands, including opposing the US military deployment in the Caribbean, the US intervention in Venezuela and Latin America, and calling on the federal Labor government to oppose the US military threats toward Venezuela.

On 25 October 2025, about 50 people protested in Melbourne - Central, Victoria, calling on the ALP to condemn United States attacks on boats in Venezuela, Colombia, and other Latin American countries. The action was organized by the Venezuela Solidarity Campaign (VSC). Members of the Latin American Solidarity Network, Australia-Cuba Friendship Society, Colombian and Filipino communities, Campaign for International Cooperation and Disarmament, Maritime Union of Australia (affiliated with CFMEU), Bendigo Trades Hall Council, SA, and the Communist Party of Australia attended the event.

On 23 November 2025, people protested in Melbourne - Central, Victoria, to criticize the United States' pressure on Latin America, particularly Venezuela and Colombia, through the deployment of warships, planes, and soldiers to the Caribbean. A Colombian-Australian and members of the Latin American Solidarity Network, SA, Australia-Cuba Friendship Society, Red Spark, and Red Ant attended the event.

On 10 December 2025, people protested at Sydney Town Hall in Sydney - Eastern to express support for Venezuela, in response to the perceived threats by Trump and his administration to attack Venezuela. Members of the Red Spark, SA, CPA, Socialist Alternative/NSW Socialists, Solidarity, and the Australia-Venezuela Solidarity Network attended the event.

On 31 December 2025, 4 people, including a member of Daylesford for Palestine, marched with a placard reading, 'I'm sleep walking into an AI (American Israel state) Surveillance State,' during the Daylesford New Year's Eve Parade. They waved a Palestinian flag.

On 4 January 2026, about 250-500 people, including SA and Palestine Action Group members, protested at Sydney Town Hall in Sydney - Eastern, New South Wales, against US intervention in Venezuela. About 40 pro-Trump supporters attempted to disrupt the protest. Police arrested three people, including an activist for wearing a shirt with the phrase 'globalize the intifada' and another counter-protester.

On 4 January 2026, about 200 people protested in Brisbane, Queensland, against US intervention in Venezuela. The Red Spark and the Latin American Solidarity Network organized the event. Another group of people counter-protested.

On 5 January 2026, up to 150 people protested in Adelaide, South Australia, against US intervention in Venezuela. Members of the CPA, Spirit of Eureka, SA, and the Australia-Cuba Friendship Society, along with representatives of the Latin American community, attended the event.

On 18 February 2026, CPA members and other demonstrators staged a protest, led by Australia Cuba Friendship Society (ACFS), outside the United States (U.S.) consulate in Perth - Central, Western Australia, to denounce the ongoing U.S. blockade and sanctions on Cuba.

On 28 February 2026, about 100 people called for an end to the United States blockade of Cuba and Venezuela at Sydney Town Hall in Sydney - Eastern, New South Wales. The protest demanded the US release Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and that the Australian government reaffirm Cuba and Venezuela's sovereignty and right to self-determination. The protest was supported by the Australia-Cuba Friendship Society (ACFS), the Australia Venezuela Solidarity Network (AVSN), SA, Red Spark, and Spirit of Eureka.

On 6 March 2026, around 20 members of the Democratic Solidarity of Iranians group protested outside the United States Consulate in North Sydney, Sydney - North, New South Wales, demanding an end to the war. They chanted 'No war on Iran,' 'Down with Trump,' and 'Stop the US-Israel war on Iran.' The event was organized by Iranian exiles and anti-war groups. Another group, waving US, Australian, and Israeli flags, stood nearby in support of the attack.

On 21 March 2026, activists, including a NSW Greens MP, a MUA (affiliated with CFMEU) Sydney branch secretary, and a Progressive International (PI) member, protested outside the City Town Hall in Sydney - Eastern to demand Australia pressure the United States to end its blockade of Cuba. They chanted 'Cuba si! Yankee no!' and 'Unblock Cuba!' The rally was part of an international day of action and was co-sponsored by the Australia-Cuba Friendship Society (ACFS), CPA, Red Spark, SA, Solidarity, and Spirit of Eureka.

On 29 March 2026, about 500 people marched from Belmore Park to Victoria Park in Sydney - Eastern, New South Wales, calling for peace, justice, and refugee rights. They opposed war, condemned Trump's 'destructive, pro-war and racist agenda,' criticized what they described as Israel's 'genocide' in Gaza and the US-Israel war on Iran, called on ALP to withdraw from the AUKUS military alliance, and stated that migrants and refugees should be welcomed. Members of the Jewish Council of Australia, NSW Ecumenical Council, Refugee Action Coalition Sydney, World Beyond War Aotearoa New Zealand, ASU, Sydney Student Representative Council, Sydney Trade Union Choir, MUA (affiliated with CFMEU), Australia, National Tertiary Education Union, IEU, and NSW Teachers Federation attended the event.

On 24 January 2026, people staged a protest marching from the European Union headquarters to the US Embassy in Wien - Alsergrund (Wien) demanding respect for Latin America and the Caribbean as a 'Zone of Peace', calling for an end to the blockade of Venezuelan oil by the United States. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026.

On 8 January 2026, under the motto 'Hands-off-Venezuela', around 300 people staged a protest in front of the Venezuelan Embassy in Wien - Inner City (Wien) to condemn the United States' military intervention in Venezuela. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 7 March 2026, under the motto 'Hands off Iran', between 500 and 600 people staged a protest in Wien - Inner City (Wien), opposing the military conflict involving Iran, the US and Israel, calling for an end to the war. The event was part of a wider protest movement that emerged after the joint Israeli and US military strikes on Iran on 28 February 2026.

On 28 March 2026, under the motto 'No Tyrants, No Kings, No Trump', around 300 people staged a protest at Karls Square in Wien - Inner City (Wien) against the US President Donald Trump and his policies and in solidarity with protests in the United States, criticizing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), while demanding the release of files related to Jeffrey Epstein. The event was part of a broader internationally coordinated protest movement originating in the United States.

On 3 April 2025, in the afternoon, at the call of the joint union front (CGSLB, ABVV), around 50 employees protested outside the BNP Paribas Fortis headquarters in Liege (Wallonie) against the planned outsourcing of the Client Service Center to the American company Accenture. The unions condemned the sale of staff and activities, raised concerns about client data confidentiality, and criticized Accenture's abandonment of diversity policies under U.S. political pressure.

On 22 July 2025, in the evening, between 300 and 400 people marched with drums, Palestinian flags, and keffiyehs through Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to support Palestine and raise awareness about the ongoing violence in Gaza. The march began at De Beurs and passed through the squares of Sint-Gorikplein, Sint-Katelijneplein, and Vismarkt before returning to De Beurs, briefly disrupting bus traffic on Antoine Dansaert Street. The protesters chanted slogans such as 'free Palestine,' 'boycott Israel boycott USA,' and 'solidarity with the Palestinian people.'

On 14 June 2025, in the afternoon, around 100 members and supporters of Democrats Abroad demonstrated in front of the US Embassy in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels). They protested against US President Donald Trump, denouncing his alleged attacks on democracy, the constitution, and the rule of law, including the military mobilization in Los Angeles to suppress critics of current immigration policies. The demonstration coincided with similar protests in 1,500 cities worldwide, as part of a global protest movement called 'No Kings', which took place on the day of a military parade on Donald Trump's 79th birthday.

On 18 September 2025, in the afternoon, around 50 activists, including members of Sensoa, 11.11.11, International Planned Parenthood, and Belgian federal parliamentarians Sophie Merckx (PVDA) and Sarah Schlitz (Ecolo), held a protest in front of the US Embassy in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) against the planned destruction of US-supplied contraceptives stored in Belgium. The demonstrators denounced the decision of President Donald Trump to destroy the contraceptives and called on Belgian authorities to prevent the destruction.

On 27 September 2025, in the afternoon, more than 150 peace activists demonstrated at the entrance of the Kleine-Brogel airbase in Kleine-Brogel (Vlaanderen) to demand the removal of American nuclear bombs stored at the military site and to call on the Belgian government to ban nuclear weapons from its territory.

On 18 October 2025, in the afternoon, around 100 American Democratic Party members and supporters, including representatives from Democrats Abroad Belgium, held a demonstration outside the United States Embassy in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest President Donald Trump's government and policies. Participants condemned Trump and the Republican Party for undermining human rights and constitutional protections, denouncing ICE enforcement practices. The event was part of a global protest movement called 'No Kings,' condemning President Donald Trump's administration for authoritarian practices and corruption.

On 20 December 2025, a hundred protesters, among them members of the Congolese diaspora, at the call of Congolese organization Free Congo, gathered at the American Embassy in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest against an agreement between the US, Congo and Rwanda. Protesters said the agreement will not bring peace or economic development for the Congolese people, but will only serve to divide the spoils of rare minerals in Congo between the parties.

On 4 January 2026, 300-400 people, among them Venezuelan diaspora members, at the call of Intal and the NGO Peace, as well as PTB and PS party representatives, gathered at the US consulate in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population. Participants called the military operation a grave violation of international law.

On 20 January 2026, around 40 people gathered at Martyrs' square in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest against Trump and the American president's policies. Protesters denounced the erosion of democracy and the rule of law, and expressed their solidarity with the victims of immigration policies in the US. Protesters also specifically honored the Renee Good, who was shot by ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) agents in Minneapolis on 7 January 2026.

On 29 January 2026, Greenpeace activists placed an inflatable statue of Putin and Trump on an LNG-gas tanker in front of the European Council building in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest against the European dependency on US gas. Protesters welcomed the recent move by the EU to ban the import of Russian gas, but feared it would lead to increased dependency on US gas. Greenpeace said the EU should focus on reducing its gas consumption, stop new gas negotiations with the US and break existing contracts early.

On 23 January 2026, in the evening, at the call of Arlon's anti-fascist group, protesters gathered at the US Air Force Band concert in Arlon (Wallonie) to protest the policies of US President Donald Trump's government. Protesters held placards with 'Leave Greenland Alone' and 'Stop US fascism'.

On 7 February 2026, between 100 and 200 protesters, at the call of several Cuban solidarity organizations, gathered in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest against the American blockade of Cuba. Protesters claimed the new measures by the Trump administration would place a further increased burden on Cuban people. Speakers and protesters called for the end of the blockade, sending humanitarian aid and oil to Cuba and maintaining the Belgium embassy in Havanna.

On 10 February 2026, protesters gathered in front of the EU Commission and EU External Action Service in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to call for the release of the Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026.

On 5 March 2026, in the evening, at the call of Pax Christi, Intal, Act for Peace (Agir pour la paix), Attac Brussels, National Coordination of Action for Peace and Democracy (Coordination Nationale d'Action pour la Paix et la Democratie - CNAPD), Christian Worker Movement (Mouvement Ouvrier Chretien - MOC), Peace (Vrede), Vredesactie, ABVV-FGTB, and the youth of ABVV-FGTB and ACV-CSC unions, protesters gathered on the Schumanplein in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest against the American-Israeli war on Iran. Protesters denounced this war as against international law, and for sanctions on Iran to be lifted and refugees and asylum seekers to be received and taken care of. Protesters reaffirmed they did not support the Islamic regime in Iran, but said 'Democracy cannot be brought with bombs'. The protest was joined by MEP Marc Botenga (PTB) and Brussels MP Kalvin Soiresse (Ecolo).

On 19 March 2026, at 4 am, 15 Greenpeace activists from Austria, Belgium, Germany, Croatia, France and Poland, gathered on Schuman Square in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to protest against the EU's relationship with Trump. Greenpeace called on EU leaders to become more independent from Trump's policies, to stop the cutting of protective measures of the climate, public health and privacy, and to denounce the Trump administration's breaches of international law. All 15 activists were arrested.

On 21 March 2026, at the call of Platform 21/3 and Jong Groen, the youth department of the political party Groen, several hundred people marched from Sint-Baafsplein to Het Zuid in Gent (Vlaanderen) to protest against racism and fascism on the occasion of the International Day against Racism. Protesters also denounced the official name of the square where the march ended, Woodrow Wilson square, as they said that the American president had racist policies and reversed progressive policies around equality.

On 11 April 2026, at 12 pm, around 100 protesters, including from the Cuban solidarity group Cubanismo, gathered in front of the US embassy in Brussels - Ville de Bruxelles (Brussels) to demand the lifting of the American embargo on Cuba. Protesters denounced the grave humanitarian costs of the embargo and said the future of Cuba should be in the hands of the Cuban people.

On 30 April 2025, following a call from the national coordination of citizen watch associations, several thousands of residents including members of government (prime minister), students, religious and traditional leaders gathered and demonstrated peacefully in the city of Ouagadougou (Kadiogo, Centre), to express their support for the government and the AES authorities (Alliance of Sahel States: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger). The protestors condemned comments made on 15 April 2025 by US General Michael Langley, head of the US military command for Africa (AFRICOM), who said that the country's mining resources were poorly managed and that the military junta benefited more than the Burkinabe people.

On 1 May 2025, following a call from the national coordination of citizen watch associations, residents gathered and demonstrated peacefully in the town of Samorogouan (Kenedougou, Hauts-Bassins), to express their support for the government and the president. The protestors condemned comments made on 15 April 2025 by US General Michael Langley, head of the US military command for Africa (AFRICOM), who said that the country's mining resources were poorly managed and that the military junta benefited more than the Burkinabe people.

On 3 May 2025, following a call from the national coordination of citizen watch associations, several residents gathered and demonstrated peacefully in the village of Cinkanse (Koulpelogo, Centre-Est), to express their support for the president. The protestors condemned comments made on 15 April 2025 by US General Michael Langley, head of the US military command for Africa (AFRICOM), who said that the country's mining resources were poorly managed and that the military junta benefited more than the Burkinabe people. They launched a fundraising campaign that raised 86,000 CFA which were handed over to the local authorities.

On 17 May 2025, following a call from the national coordination of citizen watch associations, residents gathered and demonstrated peacefully in the town of Tougouri (Namentenga, Centre-Nord), to express their support for the president. The protestors condemned comments made on 15 April 2025 by US General Michael Langley, head of the US military command for Africa (AFRICOM), who said that the country's mining resources were poorly managed and that the military junta benefited more than the Burkinabe people.

On 17 January 2026, protesters gathered at the Thomas Sankara memorial in Ouagadougou (Ouagadougou, Kadiogo, Centre) to denounce the US military intervention in Venezuela and call for the liberation of the Venezuelan President and his wife, currently detained in the United States.

On 7 April 2025, students of United International University, Presidency University, University of Information Technology and Sciences, and Bangladesh Navy College staged protest rallies opposite to US Embassy in Dhaka - Gulshan (Gulshan), against the aggression of Israel military forces in Palestine, and expressed solidarity with the people of Palestine.

Around 2 May 2025 (as reported), the National Revolutionary Council held a protest march around Dhaka area, demanding an end to the genocide in Gaza and the establishment of an independent Palestine. The march protested US President Donald Trump's occupation of Gaza and called for an end to ethnic cleansing.

On 21 September 2025, members of RWPB staged a protest rally in front of National Press Club, Dhaka - Paltan (Paltan), demanding cancellation of all deals signed with the United States, accusing government of signing the deals in secrecy while compromising national security.

On 4 January 2026, members of the Ganatantantrik Jukta Front (Democratic United Front), including representation from National Freedom Fighter Council (JMC), SPB (Marxist), CPB, BJSD, RWPB, Bhashani Janashakti Party, Democratic Revolutionary Party, held protest rallies in front of National Press Club, Dhaka - Paltan (Paltan), demanding immediate release of the president of Venezuela, and against the aggression of US forces to detain him.

On 8 January 2026, poets, artists, writers, teachers, cultural activists and student leaders, under the banner of 'Democratic Cultural Unity', staged a protest rally in front of National Museum, Dhaka - Shahbagh (Shahbagh), against the US military aggression in Venezuela and the abduction of the president of Venezuela.

On 13 March 2026, members of Network for People's Action (social organization) staged a sit-in protest in front of Parliament in Dhaka - Sher e Bangla Nagar (Sher-e-bangla Nagar), with 4-point demands including a review of the interim government's trade agreement with the United States and suspending it.

On 16 March 2026, members of 'Voice of Palestine - Bangladesh' (civil society organization) staged a human chain protest in front of National Press Club, Dhaka - Paltan (Paltan), demanding withdrawal of the United States' military bases from the Middle East and Asia, and against the military aggression of US and Israeli forces in Iran.

On 6 April 2026, members of Jukta Front (GJF) staged a protest rally in front of National Press Club, Dhaka - Paltan (Paltan), demanding from government to take immediate steps to scrap the trade deal signed with United States during the interim government.

On 10 April 2026, members of BSU, BYU, and Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi (cultural org.) staged a protest rally in front of National Museum, Dhaka - Shahbagh (Shahbagh), demanding scrapping of trade deals signed with the United States.

On 5 January 2026, a protest was held Sofia in opposition to the United States operation in Venezuela and the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro. About 50 participants gathered near the Simon Bolivar monument to condemn the action as a violation of international law and to express solidarity with Venezuela.

On 27 January 2026, citizens protested in front of the national assembly building in Sofia against Bulgaria's participation in the Peace Council, a body meant to deal with the conflict in Gaza under the patronage of the United States. The protest was organized by the informal group Solidarity with Palestine, and participants submitted an open letter with over 770 signatures demanding that Bulgaria halt efforts to legitimize the council.

On 2 March 2026, a protest organized by the Revival (Vazrazhdane) party took place in front of the Council of Ministers building in Sofia as party supporters and citizens called for American military aircraft to leave the country, as it can present a target for Iran, and voiced opposition to Bulgaria's involvement in military conflicts.
