On 5 September 2025, in La Paz (La Paz), dozens of university students carried out a demonstration outside a local university and marched towards the embassies of the United States and Argentina, rejecting what they called the ongoing genocide that Israel is perpetrating in Palestine. They also voiced their support to a group of ships that sailed days earlier from Spain to Palestine with humanitarian aid. Outside the embassies, the group questioned the support of the Argentinian and US governments to Israel, argued that the ongoing conflict is not a war, but a genocide and urged freedom for Palestine.

On 1 August 2025, in Belo Horizonte (Minas Gerais), demonstrators and social movements such as the UNE, the Brazil Popular Front, and the Fearless People Front gathered in front of the headquarters of the Federation of Industries of the State of Minas Gerais (FIEMG) to demonstrate against the US tariffs imposed on Brazil by the US government. Students burned a doll with the face of President Donald Trump and displayed a banner with the words 'Sovereignty is the people in power'. The act was part of a national agenda of demonstrations (coded separately).

On 1 August 2025, in Rio de Janeiro - Central Zone (Rio de Janeiro), demonstrators and social movements such as the CUT, the Brazil Popular Front and the Fearless People Front gathered in front of the US Consulate, in the Centro neighborhood, to demonstrate against the US tariffs imposed on Brazil by the US government. The act was part of a national agenda of demonstrations (coded separately).

On 1 August 2025, in Brasilia (Distrito Federal), around 100 people gathered in front of the United States embassy to demonstrate against the sanctions imposed by President Donald Trump against the Brazilian government. Members of the PT and CUT parties, FEPAL, and CSB were present in the demonstration, which was organized by social movements like FBP, UNE, and FPSM.

On 1 August 2025, in Manaus - South Zone (Amazonas), a group of people gathered in the centre of the city to demonstrate against the sanctions imposed by President Donald Trump against the Brazilian government. Members of the PT and CUT parties, FEPAL, and CSB were present in the demonstration, which was organized by social movements like FBP, UNE, and FPSM.

On 1 August 2025, in Porto Alegre (Rio Grande do Sul), hundreds of people protested in the city center to oppose the 50% tariffs imposed by U.S. President Donald Trump on Brazilian products exported to the United States and to defend Brazilian sovereignty.

On 1 August 2025, in Curitiba (Parana), at the call of UNE, people protested to oppose the 50% tariffs imposed by U.S. President Donald Trump on Brazilian products exported to the United States and to defend Brazilian sovereignty.

On 19 August 2025, in Brasilia (Distrito Federal), hundreds of protesters, including students organisations and labour unions demonstrated in front of the US Embassy against Israel's actions in Palestine and to call for the severing of diplomatic and commercial relations between the Brazilian government and Israel.

On 19 August 2025, in Porto Alegre (Rio Grande do Sul), dozens of protesters gathered in front of the United States Consulate to protest against the economic tariffs imposed to Brazilian products by the President of the United States, Donald Trump.

On 7 September 2025, in Florianopolis (Santa Catarina), a group opposed to the amnesty project that would favor those involved in the 8 January 2023 attempted coup (coded separately) staged a protest at the entrance of the Hercilio Luz bridge. Demonstrators defended national sovereignty and expressed criticism of the tariffs imposed by Donald Trump, demanded the taxation of the super-rich, and other issues. This was part of the annual Cry of the Excluded demonstrations.

On 7 September 2025, in Manaus - South Zone (Amazonas), anti-Bolsonaro protesters gathered in the city center to demonstrate against the amnesty for those convicted of the 8 January riots (coded separately). The protesters criticized economic measures by the United States and displayed signs demanding 'no amnesty.' This was part of the annual Cry of the Excluded demonstrations.

On 5 January 2026, in Sao Paulo - South Zone (Sao Paulo), protesters gathered in front of the U.S. Consulate, in the Chacara Santo Antonio neighborhood, to protest against the US intervention and attack in Venezuela, which captured President Nicolas Maduro. The act was also attended by representatives from the social movements UNE, MST and CUT. There were other protests in several Brazilian cities (coded separately).

On 3 January 2026, in Brasilia (Distrito Federal), around 100 people gathered in front of Venezuela's Embassy, next to Simon Bolivar's statue, in a demonstration against Venezuela's bombing by the United States and the kidnapping of Nicolas Maduro that took place earlier in the day. The demonstrators spoke against US's imperialism and for Venezuela's sovereignty and right to self-determination.

On 8 January 2026, in Natal (Rio Grande do Norte), at the call of PT, protesters gathered in the Tirol neighbourhood to defend national sovereignty and oppose the U.S. President Donald Trump. The protest was part of a nationwide mobilization to mark three years of the 8 January 2023 attempted coup (coded separately).

On 28 January 2026, in Rio de Janeiro - Central Zone (Rio de Janeiro), protesters and popular movements gathered in the Cinelandia neighborhood to protest for the freedom of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and First Lady and Congresswoman Cilia Flores and denounce US military intervention in Venezuelan territory. The demonstration was part of a national agenda (coded separately).
On 28 January 2026, in Brasilia (Distrito Federal), protesters demonstrated in front of the US Embassy to denounce what they called imperialist intervention against Venezuela's sovereignty.

On 28 January 2026, in Porto Alegre (Rio Grande do Sul), protesters gathered at Esquina Democratica and marched to Palacio Piratini in a demonstration organized by the Committee in Solidarity with the Venezuelan People to denounce perceived US intervention in Venezuela and defend Latin American sovereignty, marking the 12th anniversary of CELAC. Participants included political parties, labor unions, student groups, and social movements, and the march later joined a vigil against femicide at the palace (coded separately).

On 29 March 2026, in Sao Paulo - Central Zone (Sao Paulo), protesters gathered on Oswaldo Cruz Square, on Paulista Avenue, to protest against U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran, Lebanon, and Palestine. Participants also accused the two nations of practicing 'imperialism and Zionism' against the three Middle Eastern countries. The event was held in observance of Palestinian Land Day, which is celebrated annually on 30 March.

On 28 March 2026, in Rio de Janeiro - Central Zone (Rio de Janeiro), more than 200 participants gathered in downtown Rio de Janeiro for a demonstration against 'Operation Kagaar' and in support of the Communist Party of India. The act was organized by the International Anti-Imperialist League (LAI) as part of a day of mobilization for its National Conference, which took place immediately following the demonstration. Participants also burned photos of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump.

On 27 June 2025, in Sao Paulo - South Zone (Sao Paulo), demonstrators, members of the PT party and the MST movement gathered in front of the US Consulate in Sao Paulo to protest against Israel's attacks on Palestine and the wars promoted by Israel and the United States. The demonstrators also demanded action from the Brazilian government, with placards and slogans calling on President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (PT) to break off trade and diplomatic relations with Israel.
On 17 July 2025, in Sao Jose dos Campos (Sao Paulo), workers protested in front of the Embraer's headquarters against the 50% tariffs imposed by the US President Donald Trump on Brazilian goods.

On 18 July 2025, in Sao Paulo - Central Zone (Sao Paulo), around 120 workers protested in the Mercado neighborhood, at the 25 de Marco street market, to denounce the 50% tariffs imposed by U.S. President Donald Trump on Brazilian goods, as well as the American government's criticism of the sale of falsified products in the street market. The protest was called by the Sao Paulo Retail Workers' Union (SECSP) and the Trade Union Center (UGT).

On 25 July 2025, in Sao Paulo - Central Zone (Sao Paulo), representatives of social movements, political parties, jurists, universities, trade unions, and civil society organizations gathered at the University of Sao Paulo (USP) Law School, in Largo Sao Francisco, to hold an act in defense of national sovereignty. A manifesto was presented criticizing attempts to interfere with Brazilian democracy, citing, among other things, the tariffs imposed on Brazil by US President Donald Trump.

On 27 March 2025, dozens of protesters staged a rally of 'Elbows up Canada' in front of the U.S. Embassy on Sussex Drive in Ottawa (Ontario) to protest against the U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his recent suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state, and in support of Canadian sovereignty.

On 5 April 2025, several hundred people rallied in front of the Stablex factory in Blainville (Quebec) to protest against Bill 93, which authorizes the expropriation of land owned by the City of Blainville for the expansion of the Stablex hazardous waste landfill. They demanded that the toxic waste coming from the USA stop being deposited in their area. Blainville Mayor Liza Poulin, MNA Virginie Dufour (LPC), MNA Christine Labrie (QS), and MNA Catherine Gentilcore (PQ) attended the rally.

On 29 March 2025, about two dozen demonstrators rallied outside a Tesla showroom in Vancouver (British Columbia) to demonstrate against Elon Musk and in solidarity with the LGBTQ+ community. They also supported Canadian sovereignty in response to U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs and threats. Counter-demonstrators also gathered in support of Elon Musk. Demonstrators also waved 'Trump 2024,' and wore MAGA gear. This demonstration was part of a global day of action called 'Tesla Takedown.'

On 30 March 2025, about 150 Canadian and American protesters staged a rally of 'The Hands Across the Border' on the International Falls Bridge, which connects Ontario - Canada, and Minnesota, USA at the riverfront in Fort Frances (Ontario) to protest against the U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his recent suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state, and in support of Canadian sovereignty. The rally aimed to highlight the strong ties between Canadians and Americans and to reject Trump's divisive approach.

On 31 March 2025, a handful of members from Unifor Local 195 picketed at the Titan Tool and Die in Windsor (Ontario) to protest against the potential removal of equipment from the plant to a Titan factory in Michigan, USA. They wanted the company to honor their commitment to their workers.

On 7 April 2025, protesters, including CLC, CUPE Local 1393 and UAW Local 251 members, staged a rally at the riverfront in Windsor (Ontario) during the first week of shutdown at the Windsor Assembly Plant due to U.S. tariffs. They protested against President Donald Trump's 25% tariffs on the Canadian auto industry.

On 5 April 2025, hundreds of Canadian and American protesters staged a 'Hands Off' rally near the U.S. Embassy in Ottawa (Ontario) to protest against the U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his recent suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state, and in support of Canadian sovereignty. The rally aimed to highlight the strong ties between Canadians and Americans and to reject Trump's divisive approach. They also protested against Elon Musk's role in U.S. government policy. Indivisible Ottawa, a chapter of the U.S.-based Indivisible movement organized the rally.

On 6 April 2025, hundreds of protesters staged a 'Hands Off' rally at the Mount Royal Park in Montreal - Center East (Quebec) to protest against the U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his recent suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state, and in support of Canadian sovereignty. The rally aimed to highlight the strong ties between Canadians and Americans and to reject Trump's divisive approach. They also protested against Elon Musk's role in U.S. government policy.

On 16 April 2025, students staged a rally at Ecole secondaire des Patriotes de Saint-Eustache in Saint-Eustache (Quebec) to protest against the U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his recent suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state, and in support of Canadian sovereignty. The rally aimed to highlight the strong ties between Canadians and Americans and to reject Trump's divisive approach. They also protested against Elon Musk's role in U.S. government policy.

On 12 April 2025, dozens of protesters staged a rally outside the Tesla dealership on Wonderland Road in London (Ontario) against Elon Musk, to call for a boycott of Tesla, due to his support of Donald Trump and his controversial statements. They also supported Canadian sovereignty in response to U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs and threats.

On 26 April 2025, more than 1000 people, including Unifor members, staged a rally at the Festival Plaza on the Windsor waterfront, along the Detroit River in Windsor (Ontario) to protest against President Donald Trump's 25% tariffs on the Canadian auto industry. They called for a strong government response to defend Canadian jobs and counter U.S. tariffs. NDP leader Jagmeet Singh attended the rally. Workers from sectors such as automotive, lumber, and healthcare were represented.

On 1 May 2025, union members and student groups held a rally and picketed in St. John's (Newfoundland and Labrador) to celebrate the workers' movement and to demand improvements in workplaces. A key concern highlighted was the impact of the international trade war and U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs, with the demand for pushback against employers attempting to roll back collective agreements due to these tariffs and to continue making gains at the bargaining table. Members of the Newfoundland and Labrador Federation of Labour and Unifor were present at the rally.

On 26 April 2025, hundreds of people staged an 'elbows up' rally in Sault Ste. Marie (Ontario) to protest against the U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his recent suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state, and in support of Canadian sovereignty.

On 10 May 2025, dozens of people from Vermont, including Canadian and Americans, staged a rally at the Jean Talon market in Montreal - Center East (Quebec) to protest against U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policies and political rhetoric, particularly his tariffs against Canada and his suggestion that Canada should become the 51st U.S. state. Demonstrators also showed support for Canadian sovereignty.

On 15 June 2025, several hundred people, including Revolutionary Communist Party's members, staged a rally outside Calgary City Hall in Calgary (Alberta) to protest against the G7 summit. Some protesters protested against the U.S. President Donald Trump's comments about Canada becoming the 51st state, in support of Canadian sovereignty, and climate change policy. People also demonstrated in support of labor rights, pro-Palestinian rights, and Indigenous rights. People also demonstrated in solidarity with Kashmiri, Ethiopian, Palestinian and Ukrainian peoples.

On 14 June 2025, nearly 2000 people staged a march from York Street to the American embassy in Ottawa (Ontario) to protest against President Donald Trump's immigration policies and his planned military parade in Washington D.C. Organizers in Ottawa used the slogans 'No Tyrants' and 'No Crowns' instead of 'No Kings' and 'No Clowns', respectively, acknowledging the Canadian head of state. The protests coincided with President Donald Trump's visit to the G7 leaders' summit, held in Kananaskis, near Calgary.

On 22 June 2025, hundreds of people, including members of the Iranian, Palestinian, and Jewish communities, held a rally of 'Hands Off Iran' outside the U.S. Consulate in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to protest against the Israel-Iran war and to demand a ceasefire. Members of the Iranian Canadian Congress, the Palestinian Youth Movement, CUPE Ontario, and the Canadian Arab Federation were present. Around 50 counter-protesters staged a rally at the same location waving Israeli flags and the lion and sun flag (associated with Iran's former monarchy).

On 5 July 2025, about 40 people held a rally in Dieppe Park in Windsor (Ontario) to oppose U.S. President Donald Trump's ongoing tariff threats and his rhetoric about making Canada the 51st state. Participants expressed their discontent with his policies and the 'division that he incites', advocating for unity between the two countries and in support of Canadian sovereignty. This was the third iteration of the cross-border 'Elbows Up United Rally'.

On 29 July 2025, nearly 100 people, members of the Peace Alliance Winnipeg, held a rally outside the Winnipeg Art Gallery in Winnipeg (Manitoba) to oppose the appearance of U.S. Ambassador to Canada. Pro-Palestinian demonstrators carried signs of support for Palestine, Cuba, transgender rights, in support of Canadian sovereignty, and Canada against US policies. Some demonstrators also condemned Prime Minister Carney for 'being on Trump's side.'

On 16 August 2025, more than 400 people held a rally of friendship and solidarity between Canada and the U.S. at the Quebec-Vermont border near Frelighsburg, Quebec, and Berkshire, Vermont (coded to Frelighsburg) (Quebec) in support of Canadian sovereignty, to show resistance to what organizers called U.S. President Donald Trump's oppressive policies, such as ongoing tariff threats and his rhetoric about making Canada the 51st state. The event was organized by Mothers on the front lines of the Eastern Townships and Vermont Indivisible. A few dozen gathered on the U.S. side.

On 22 August 2025, between 50 to 100 people staged a rally at the Alberta legislature grounds in Edmonton (Alberta) to protest against an American singer, Sam Feucht's concert and to stand up to Feucht's anti-LGBTQ+ views. The protest was organized by a local initiative called Let Us Protest.

On 7 October 2025, thousands of students rallied at McGill University in Montreal - Center East (Quebec) in solidarity with Palestine, for a 'Free Palestine,' to demonstrate against Israel's 'genocide' in Palestine, and to call for divestment from Israel. Demonstrators smashed a window of the university's Redpath Library and set an Israeli flag on fire. Students also held a pro-Palestinian campus demonstration at Concordia University. Demonstrators held anti-Trump signs that read 'Trump Wanted For War Crimes.' Hundreds of demonstrators also rallied at Victoria Square and held anti-Trump signs that read 'Trump Wanted For War Crimes.' In the evening, demonstrators also marched from Place-des-Arts towards McGill University. A small group of counter-demonstrators, including Jewish students, rallied outside in support of Israel with some, holding Quebec flags.

On 4 October 2025, hundreds of Unifor Local 707 workers rallied at Stellantis Brampton Assembly Plant in Brampton (Ontario) to demonstrate against U.S. tariffs, to demand protection for auto industry jobs in Brampton, and to demand stronger protections for Canadian workers. Unifor Ontario's Regional Director, the National President of Unifor, Stellantis' Brampton Assembly Plant's Chairperson, the Vice-Chair of the Stellantis Master Bargaining Committee, and Unifor's Local 1285 President spoke at the rally.

On 10 October 2025, dozens of steelworkers and union leaders, including the CEO of Zekelman Industries, rallied in Windsor (Ontario) to call for protection of Canadian steel jobs and to demand that tariffs on U.S. steel be raised.

On 18 October 2025, dozens of demonstrators, including lawyers, gathered at Place du Canada in downtown Montreal - Center East (Quebec) for a 'No Tyrants' demonstration to show opposition to Donald Trump, support for migrants, and to call for protections for healthcare, environmental, and educational programs, and in support of Canadian sovereignty. Nationwide demonstrations were held in solidarity with the United State's No Kings 2 day of action and were organized by a coalition of organizations led by the 50501 movement, including the Quebec chapter of Democrats Abroad and Indivisible Quebec.

On 18 November 2025, pro-Palestinian demonstrators rallied outside the US Consulate in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) in solidarity with Palestine, to demand an arms embargo on Israel, and to demonstrate against the United Nations' approval of a US plan authorizing an international stabilization force in Gaza. A snowplow drove slowly through a group of demonstrators, and police have stated that they believe there was 'no criminal intention' when they interviewed the driver; however, Mayor Olivia Chow has ordered the transportation department to open an investigation.

On 3 January 2026, hundreds of demonstrators gathered outside the U.S. Consulate in downtown Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario), to demonstrate against US intervention in Venezuela. Demonstrators called for the US to keep its 'hands off Venezuela', clear messages from the Canadian government, and respect for international law. A separate demonstration in support of the US' actions also took place at Yonge-Dundas square (coded separately).

On 4 January 2026, more than 100 demonstrators gathered outside the U.S. Embassy in Ottawa (Ontario) to demonstrate against US intervention in Venezuela. Demonstrators called for the US to keep its 'hands off Venezuela.' Members of the Communist Party of Canada attended the event. A handful of counter-demonstrators, including Venezuelan Canadians, were also present to demonstrate their support for US intervention in Venezuela.

On 5 January 2026, around 50 demonstrators gathered outside City Hall in Regina (Saskatchewan), to demonstrate against US intervention in Venezuela. Demonstrators, including members of the Mexican and Chilean community, called for the US not to attack the South American nation. The Regina Peace Council organized the event.

On 11 January 2026, roughly two-dozen demonstrators held an 'Ice Out for Good' rally outside the U.S. Consulate in Vancouver (British Columbia) to show solidarity with anti-ICE demonstrators in the United States.

On 17 January 2026, dozens of Nunavummiut, including Inuit community members, held a rally in Iqaluit (Nunavut) to show solidarity with Greenland and to protest against threats of annexation by the United States.
On 17 January 2026, protesters gathered in front of the US consulate in Vancouver (British Columbia) to demonstrate against US intervention in Venezuela.

On 27 January 2026, dozens of people held a rally outside the U.S. Consulate in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario), to honor the memory of a 37-year-old man killed by a U.S. Border Patrol officer in Minneapolis. The Organizers said there were at least 150 people in attendance, while the police estimated there were about 60.

On 1 February 2026, nearly 200 people gathered in front of the United States Consulate at 1134 Ste-Catherine St. W. and, marched across Peel St. to the northwestern corner of Dorchester Square in Montreal - Center East (Quebec) to protest against the actions of U.S Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Canada's 'complicity' in these operations and to support anti-ICE demonstrators in Minneapolis.

On 31 January 2026, dozens of people cycled for 4 km and gathered in front of the American consulate in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to protest against the actions of U.S Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and to commemorate a man who was shot dead by ICE agents on January 24 in Minneapolis.

On 31 January 2026, local residents held a rally in front of the U.S. consulate in Winnipeg (Manitoba) to show solidarity with Greenland, in support of Canadian sovereignty, and to protest against threats of annexation by the United States.

On 15 February 2026, roughly 100 demonstrators gathered outside the U.S. consulate near Portage Avenue and Main Street in Winnipeg (Manitoba) for a 'Canadians Against I.C.E. Brutality' protest opposing the actions of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and expressing support for anti-ICE demonstrators in Minneapolis.

On 28 February 2026, demonstrators, including members of the Iranian community, gathered at the U.S. consulate in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario), to demonstrate against US intervention in Iran. Counter-demonstrators called for an end to the war, demonstrated against the current Iranian regime, and in support of regime change in Iran.
On 1 March 2026, around 40 demonstrators gathered outside the U.S. consulate in Winnipeg (Manitoba) to demonstrate against US intervention in Iran. Peace Alliance Winnipeg organized the rally.

On 7 March 2026, a small group of demonstrators held a rally near the United States Consulate in downtown Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) to demonstrate against US and Israel intervention in Iran and to mourn Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's death. The rally was organized by Canadian Defenders For Human Rights and was endorsed by the Iranian Canadian Congress, Al-Quds Toronto, and Palestinian Youth Movement. A group of counter demonstrators including members of the Iranian community gathered at the same place to call for regime change in Iran.

On 10 March 2026, two individuals fired shots at the U.S. Consulate in Toronto - Old Toronto (Ontario) with a handgun, causing very minor damage to the building. This attack took place around 4:30am according to police. The building was occupied with embassy staff at the time of shooting. The police claim that bulletproof windows and doors were not damaged by gunfire during the incident. Photos appeared to show bullet impacts on exterior walls and steps. Police are investigating the incident as a 'national security incident.'

On 28 March 2026, hundreds of people gathered in downtown Vancouver (British Columbia) for the No Kings 3 demonstration (No Tyrants), to oppose Donald Trump and the ongoing conflict in the Middle East while expressing support for migrants. They also called on three Vancouver-based companies linked to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to immediately cancel their contracts and urged all levels of government in Canada to prohibit ICE from carrying out enforcement activities on Canadian soil.

On 8 April 2026, demonstrators holding Palestinian and Lebanese flags held a rally outside the American embassy in Ottawa (Ontario) to protest against the U.S. and Israeli-led wars in Iran and Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon. The Palestinian Youth Movement organized the rally.

On 2 August 2025, youths clashed (means unspecified) with Chinese investors in Akoupe-Zeudji (Abidjian, Abidjan, Abidjan), during a land stripping operation carried out by the investors. The youths, claiming ownership of the land, objected to the work being carried out by Chinese investors and clashes ensued resulting in the death of 1 person, and the serious injury of several others.

On 27 April 2025, Shark militia abducted and tortured a driver for the US Embassy in Bangui (Arrondissement 1, Bangui, Bangui). The victim was intercepted near a shop in the city center and taken to Camp de Roux, where he was tortured before being released in critical condition.

On 29 March 2025, in the morning, at the call of the Campax Swiss citizens' movement, around 20 people demonstrated outside a Tesla dealership in Zurich (Zurich) to protest against Elon Musk, owner of Tesla and X. The event was part of a global campaign organized by the Tesla Takedown movement, which sought to target Tesla's CEO Elon Musk and his company and criticize his policies within the Trump administration in the U.S.

On 17 May 2025, in the evening, between 700 and 800 pro-Palestinian activists gathered in central Basel (Basel-Stadt) to demonstrate against Israel's participation in the 2025 Eurovision Song Contest. The unauthorized demonstration escalated when rioters burned Israeli and U.S. flags, lit green smoke bombs, and marched with a banner reading 'United for Palestine'. Police blocked their route through the city center, using pepper spray and rubber bullets after firecrackers were thrown at officers. Three police officers were hospitalized, and 400 participants were subjected to identity checks. Tensions also rose when two men carrying Israeli flags entered the crowd and were escorted away by police.

On 14 June 2025, 3,000 people, including members of the Fribourg Solidarity with Palestine Collective (Collectif Solidarite Palestine Fribourg), marched in Fribourg (Fribourg) to protest gender inequality, anti-trans laws, low wages, Israeli actions in Gaza, and the roles of Donald Trump and Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis, accused of undermining diversity and supporting oppression.

On 17 January 2026, at 2pm, at the call of dozens of associations, collectives including antiracist collective Outrage, unions and political parties including Solidarity and EAG, close to 200 people, including local elected officials, protested in Geneva (Geneve) against U.S. imperial aggression and demonstrated solidarity with the people of Venezuela. Protesters also demanded for U.S. President Donald Trump to be banned from Switzerland and for Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife to be freed. Light tension arose between protesters supporting Maduro and those against him. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026.

On 18 January 2026, around 600 people blocked the road in direction of Davos (Graubunden), as part of their protest march against the World Economic Forum (WEF) that gathered world leaders, including U.S. President Donald Trump, in Davos on 17 and 18 January 2026. The police intervened to disperse the crowd and allow traffic to resume. Protesters marched to Davos where a protest was organized by PS/SP.

On 19 January 2026, at the call of Movement for Socialism, several thousand people gathered in Zurich (Zurich) to demonstrate against the World Economic Forum (WEF) and, more specifically, against U.S. President Donald Trump's appearance at the WEF meeting in Davos. Activists set off firecrackers, smoke devices, and fireworks, sprayed graffiti, and damaged property along the route. They threw paint at building facades, smashed shop windows near Bahnhofstrasse and Uraniastrasse, and broke windows at a tram stop. Some demonstrators also built barricades and set fire to rubbish containers, while also throwing stones at police officers. The latter fired rubber bullets and sprayed tear gas.

On 2 March 2026, at the call of Solidarity, Feminist Strike (Greve Feministe) and other left-wing organizations, around 100 people gathered in front of Cornarvin in Geneva (Geneve) to protest against the war in Iran, following the American and Israeli strikes on Iran. Protesters demanded peace based on justice and auto determination. The event was part of a wave of demonstrations worldwide following the American-Israeli strikes on Iran and the death of the Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

On 10 April 2026, around 100 people walked from the train station square to the American embassy in Bern (Bern) to protest against the war in the Middle East. Protesters called the demonstration an 'Anti-Imperialist Spontaneous Demonstration Hands off Lebanon', and held a banner reading 'Hands off Libanon, Iran, Palastina, Venezuela'. The cantonal police blocked the access to the embassy.

On 23 April 2025, in Santiago (Metropolitana), around 50 members of the Pehuenmapu Pehuenche and Mapuche Indigenous communities and other unspecified socioenvironmental organizations gathered on Ciudadania Square outside the Moneda presidential palace to protest against the Rucalhue hydroelectric project on the Biobio River (developed by China International Water & Electric Corp., a Chinese state-owned enterprise). Protesters, who delivered a letter to the Moneda, claimed that the project had been greenlighted without prior Indigenous consultation, and also stated that the government of President Boric had failed to measure up to its pro-environmental pledges. The Rucalhue hydroelectric project suffered an arson attack on 20 April (coded separately) and protesters also repudiated allegations of links between the attack and Indigenous communities. Protesters also demanded the liberation of Mapuche prisoners. Protesters gathered outside the Chinese embassy in Providencia on the same day (coded separately).

On 6 October 2025, in Coquimbo (Coquimbo), around 20 artisanal fishers demonstrated at the Coquimbo Cove and set tires on fire to demonstrate the impact of foreign vessels, particularly Chinese fishers, on local squid (jibia) fishing. The demonstrators called for stricter control over international fishing operations near Chile's northern coast. There were no casualties.

On 7 October 2025, in La Serena (Coquimbo), members of the local Palestinian community gathered near the junction between Balmaceda Street and Francisco de Aguirre Avenue and marched through the city to protest against the massacre in Gaza. Protesters deployed puppets to represent the almost 20,000 children killed in Gaza and expressed horror at two years of genocide. Protesters denounced the collusion of economic and imperialist powers, including the United States, members of NATO and the European Union, with Israel in order to destroy the Palestinian people.

On 7 October 2025, in Valparaiso (Valparaiso), artisanal fishers, including members of the Union of Independent Workers and Fishers of the Sudamericana Dock (SIPSA), marched via Sotomayor Square to the offices of the Regional Presidential Delegation and erected incendiary barricades to demonstrate against the alleged overfishing of cuttlefish in the region by a fleet of around 50 Chinese vessels. Demonstrators claimed that the fleet had been in place for over a year and were both threatening the sustainability of marine resources and fishers' source of revenue. Demonstrators also gathered on La Polvora Way and in the Porvenir Bajo and Playa Ancha neighborhoods. Police intervened in an unspecified manner to restore traffic in the city center. There were no casualties.

On 7 October 2025, in Caldera (Atacama), fishers blocked Highway 5 for two hours to protest against the alleged exploitation of national fish stocks by fleets of Chinese vessels. Protesters demanded greater supervision of foreign vessels.

On 6 October 2025, in San Antonio (Valparaiso), artisanal fishers, including members of the Artisanal Fishing Federation of the Southern Fifth Region, erected incendiary barricades on Barros Luco Avenue to express solidarity with northern colleagues, who were concerned about alleged overfishing of cuttlefish by a fleet of Chinese vessels. Demonstrators demanded that the Navy investigate the fleet. There were no casualties.

On 3 January 2026, in Santiago - Providencia (Metropolitana), around 30 people gathered in front of the United States Embassy on Avenida Andres Bello to protest against the US military intervention in Venezuela and the attack carried out in Caracas that led to the capture of President Nicolas Maduro. Protesters held upside-down American flags, Venezuelan flags, and called the action US imperialism and a violation of Venezuelan sovereignty.

On 24 February 2026, in Punta Arenas (Magallanes), on the fiftieth anniversary of the proclamation of the 1976 Cuban constitution, a dozen individuals, including supporters of the Communist Party and the Communist Youth, gathered at the junction between Colon and Bories Streets to express their opposition to the United States' blockade of Cuba. Protesters sought to express their support and solidarity with the Cuban people.

On 11 March 2026, in Valparaiso (Valparaiso), on the day of President Kast's inauguration, between around 50 and 150 individuals, including members of the Valparaiso Antiimperialist Coordinator, gathered on Victoria Square to mobilize against the presence of the United States Deputy Secretary of State, that of Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, and that of the Argentinian, Panamanian, Ecuadorian and Bolivian Presidents, as well as the King of Spain. Demonstrators also mobilized against President Kast's regressive agenda, as well as his alignment with the United States following its attack on Iran, blockade on Cuba, and its support for genocide in Gaza. Demonstrators subsequently marched along Pedro Montt Street towards the National Congress building until they were halted by security barriers in the Italia Park area. Demonstrators set fire to an effigy of US President Trump, erected a barricade near the junction between Pedro Montt Avenue and General Cruz Street, and threw stones at police. Police dispersed the demonstrators using water cannons and made one arrest.

On 1 April 2025, around 20 representatives of the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong, including lawmakers, chanted slogans and held placards outside the Consulate General of the United States, Hong Kong and Macau in Hong Kong - Central and Western to demand that the United States government put an end to sanctions against China.

On 22 October 2025, four activists and members of the Ocean Ancestors Collective staged a maritime protest at the Rarotonga Port (located on the Coast of Avarua, Southern) to oppose deep-sea mining in the Cook Islands and the Pacific region. The protesters were on kayaks and paddled alongside a United States-owned vessel that returned from a deep-sea research expedition.

On 7 October 2025, in Bogota - Teusaquillo (Bogota, D.C.), participants marched along El Dorado Avenue and gathered near the U.S. Embassy as part of a series of demonstrations organized by several pro-Palestinian groups. Some attendees burned Israeli and U.S. flags and condemned what they described as a genocide against the Palestinian population by Israel. This was part of a series of demonstrations that concluded at Bolivar Square. Approximately 4.500 people took part across 3 events. There were no casualties.

On 7 October 2025, in Medellin - Southeast (Antioquia), dozens of people marched through the El Poblado sector as part of a Pro-Palestinian demonstration. During the march, participants burned the flags of Israel and the United States, as well as images of their presidents, and held banners with messages in support of the Palestinian people. Hours later, some demonstrators clashed with public order officials from the city's Security Secretariat and with other citizens present in the area. Videos shared on social media show a local councilman from the Democratic Center party carrying a baseball bat and threatening some demonstrators, as well as municipal officials beating a human rights observer. According to local authorities, 10 city officials were injured. Members of the UNDMO intervened to disperse the crowd. There were no fatalities.

On 24 October 2025, in Bogota - La Candelaria (Bogota, D.C.), large groups of demonstrators, including members of the CUT labor union, gathered at various locations of the city and marched to the Bolivar Square to express their support for the government (PH) amid the diplomatic tensions between the governments of the United States and Colombia. During the protest, a group of hooded rioters suspected of carrying bladed weapons, attacked the demonstrators on a street near Bolivar Square, but the situation was contained by the security forces. Palestinian flags were seen during the marches. President Petro (PH) attended the event at Bolivar Square and delivered a speech.

On 7 January 2026, in Bogota - La Candelaria (Bogota, D.C.), approximately 3,500 demonstrators, including PH party supporters, members of CUT, university students, and government officials (PH), marched to Bolivar Square in support of national unity, democracy, and the government (PH) amid rising tensions between the governments of the United States and Colombia, and against the US intervention in Venezuela. President Petro (PH) gave a speech during the demonstration. M-19 and Palestinian flags were seen during the event. Similar marches took place in several other cities that day (coded separately).

On 7 January 2026, in Medellin - Central East (Antioquia), approximately 3,000 PH supporters marched from Bicentenario Park to the La Alpujarra sector in support of national unity, democracy, and the government (PH) amid rising tensions between the governments of the United States and Colombia. During the demonstration, some participants set fire to a US flag and an image of Donald Trump. Palestinian flags were also seen during the event. Similar marches took place in several other cities that day (coded separately). There were no casualties.

On 3 January 2026, in Bogota - Teusaquillo (Bogota, D.C.), around 50 people protested outside the U.S. Embassy on 26th Street to condemn the military intervention by U.S. forces in Venezuela earlier that day and the capture of Nicolas Maduro. The demonstrators protested what they described as the beginning of a military invasion and an attack on the country's sovereignty.

On 3 January 2026, in Bucaramanga (Santander), Colombian and Venezuelan demonstrators gathered outside the Venezuelan consulate to condemn the capture of Nicolas Maduro following a U.S. military operation in Caracas earlier that day.

On 5 January 2026, in Santiago de Cali - Comuna 2 (Valle del Cauca), a group of demonstrators gathered near the Municipal Administrative Center (CAM) in support of Nicolas Maduro following his capture by U.S. forces during a military operation in Caracas on 3 January. Demonstrators also condemned the intervention by U.S. forces in Venezuela and displayed messages opposing the United States.

On 15 January 2026, in Arauca (Arauca), a group of demonstrators, including members of the Guardia Indigena, social movements, and labor unions, and an official of the Arauca Department government (PLC), gathered on the Colombian side of the Jose Antonio Paez International Bridge in support of national unity and democracy amid rising tensions between the governments of the United States and Colombia, and against the US intervention in Venezuela.

On 18 February 2026, in Bogota - Teusaquillo (Bogota, D.C.), more than 200 sugarcane, panela, and palm oil workers and members of the CUT, CTC, and CGT unions demonstrated by blocking all entrances to the Ministry of Mines and Energy at the Central Administrative Offices. The workers came from the departments of Valle del Cauca and Meta. They denounced labor insecurity due to imports from the United States and changes in biofuel policies limiting their output. Protesters blocked Avenida Calle 26 near the National University.

On 9 October 2025, in Habana, La Habana, a group of citizens, accompanied by representatives of the Government and workers of the Electric Union (UNE), held a protest in front of the US Embassy to condemn the Israeli occupation of the Palestinian territories and the Palestinian genocide and to blame the US for their support to Israel. Governmental authorities claim that more than 100,000 citizens took part in the protest, whereas independent media estimate that about 32,000 people attended the event.

On 3 January 2026, in Habana, La Habana, a group of citizens, including university students, ministry workers, and Government officials took part in a protest organized by the Cuban Government in support of the Venezuelan people and against the United States. Protesters condemned the US' apprehension of the Venezuelan President, Nicolas Maduro, and called for respect for the states' national sovereignty.

On 27 January 2026, in Habana, La Habana, thousands of citizens held a march, organized by the Government, in occasion of the anniversary of the birth of Jose Julian Marti Perez, founder of the Cuban Revolutionary Party. The march was also an anti-imperialist protest against the US military operation in Venezuela as well as against the US threats against Cuba.

On 16 January 2026, in Habana, La Habana, a group of citizens, including students and workers, held a protest to commemorate the death of 32 Cuban soldiers killed during the US military intervention in Venezuela. The protest was organized by the Government of Cuba.

On 5 January 2026, protesters organized by the Cyprus Peace Council, AKEL, the Communist Initiative of Cyprus and PEO, rallied in Nicosia to protest the U.S. military operation in Venezuela, seizing President Nicolas Maduro. The protesters carried banners with anti-imperialist slogans and slogans in support of International Law. They held speeches.

On 8 March 2026, on International Women's Day, members of POGO and PEO rallied and marched in Nicosia, carrying banners and placards, protesting for women's rights. The leader of AKEL held a speech. They protested for peace and the removal of the British bases from the island, expressed their solidarity with women in war-afflicted countries and protested the regression of women's rights in the United States.

On 11 June 2025, 8 activists affiliated with Greenpeace gathered in Cestlice and occupied a local Tesla store, protesting against ongoing attacks of E. Musk and D. Trump towards environmentally-oriented NGOs.

On 26 June 2025, activists, including members of the Communist party, gathered for a rally in Prague in front of the US embassy, criticizing what they describe as an imperialist aggression in the near East, especially against the civilians in Palestine.

On 25 November 2025, several dozen activists gathered for a rally in front of the US embassy in Prague, condemning the current ceasefire proposal of the US president for Ukraine and demanding higher support to Kyiv instead.
On 30 January 2026, several dozen activists gathered for a rally in Prague, protesting against normalisation of violence in politics, both in the Czech Republic and in the United States.
On 2 March 2026, activists gathered in front of the US embassy in Prague, condemning the recent attack against Iran as an unprovoked escalation of tensions and a looming another war.

On 29 March 2025, at the call of the activist group Neuen Generation (New Generation), around 35 people gathered in front of the Tesla Store in Berlin - Reinickendorf (Berlin) for a protest. The event was part of a global campaign organized by the Tesla Takedown movement, which sought to target Tesla's CEO Elon Musk and his company and criticize his policies within the Trump administration in the U.S.

On 5 April 2025, at the call of Campact, FFF, the alliance Turn off the tap on Tesla (Tesla den Hahn abdrehen), between 250 and hundreds of people staged a protest in front of a Tesla showroom in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) against Elon Musk and his company Tesla, accusing Musk of undermining democratic structures. The event was part of a global campaign organized by the Tesla Takedown movement, which sought to target Tesla's CEO Elon Musk and his company and criticize his policies within the Trump administration in the U.S.

On 5 April 2025, dozens of US citizens gathered in Frankfurt am Main (Hessen) to protest against the Trump administration, demanding the resignation of US President Trump and calling for action from the Republican Party.

On 12 April 2025, around 15 people, including members of FFF, Parents for Future, and the 'Resistance-Collective' ('Widerstands-Kollektiv'), gathered near a Tesla dealership on Weimarische Street in Erfurt (Thuringen) to protest against Tesla and Elon Musk. The event was part of the global protest movement known as Tesla Takedown, which targeted Tesla CEO Elon Musk and his company and criticized his role within the Trump administration in the United States.

On 14 June 2025, at the call of Democrats Abroad, around 200 people gathered in Frankfurt am Main (Hessen) to protest under the slogan 'No Kings' against the Trump administration. The demonstrators marched from Opernplatz through Fresgass and Rathenauplatz before returning to Opernplatz for further rallies, denouncing what they described as increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption by Trump and his allies.

On 27 July 2025, in the morning, around 50 people, including members of the Catholic Women's Association of Germany (Katholische Frauengemeinschaft Deutschlands - KFD), Representatives of the Family Association of Catholics (Familienbund der Katholiken), the Greens and the Maria 2.0 reform movement (Reformbewegung Maria 2.0), staged a protest in Munster (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against the awarding of the Josef-Pieper Award to a US Bishop, some carrying rainbow flags and placards. The protest criticized Barron for his political closeness to US President Donald Trump and his exclusionary attitudes toward various social groups.

On 11 October 2025, 17 pro-Palestinian activists staged a protest on the Main River in Frankfurt am Main (Hessen) using three boats, waving Palestinian flags and calling for solidarity with people in Gaza while criticizing Donald Trump's peace plan as 'colonialism in a new form'.
On 21 November 2025, in the evening, antifascists staged a protest in Connewitz district in Leipzig (Sachsen) in solidarity with antifascists on trial and against the planned Antifa ban in the USA.

On 9 December 2025, approximately 40 individuals gathered in front of the US embassy in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) in solidarity with Mumia Abu-Jamal, an African-American journalist jailed in the US for murder who has been imprisoned for 44 years without substantial evidence against him. During the event, speeches addressed issues including mass incarceration in the US, racism and classism in relation to the death penalty.

On 4 January 2026, between 350 and 400 people, supported by a broad alliance including International Youth (Internationale Jugend), the Peace Forum (Friedensforum), Red Alliance (Roter Bund), KKE, SDAJ, DKP, MLPD, REBELL, the Federation of Class-Struggle Organizations (Foderation Klassenkampferischer Organisationen - FKO), Communist Workers' Youth (Kommunistische Arbeiterjugend - KA), Dusseldorf Appeal Against War (Dusseldorf Appell gegen Krieg), Young Struggle and other peace groups staged a protest marching through the Oberbilk district to the US consulate in Dusseldorf (Nordhrein-Westfalen). The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 3 January 2026, in the evening, around 300 people staged a protest, marching from the main railway station through Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte (Hamburg), carrying anti-US slogans and a Venezuelan flag. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 4 February 2026, around 250 people, including members of the Kurdish community, the Left, Left Youth Solid, The Greens, MLPD and RKP Wurzburg, staged a protest in Schweinfurt (Bayern) against the attacks on Rojava, condemning the Syrian and Turkish government, while criticizing the USA and the German federal government. The event was part of a wider demonstration movement against the clashes between Kurdish militias and the Syrian armed forces in the Kurdish-controlled areas of Syria.
On 5 March 2026, students staged a protest at Georg-Schramm Square in Eberswalde (Brandenburg) against the war in Iran, criticizing the roles of the USA and Israel.

On 8 March 2026, at the call of the Islamic Religious Community of Hessen (Islamische Religionsgemeinde Hessen), under the motto 'For peace and international law - Stop the illegal war of the USA and Israel against Iran', around 800 people staged a protest in Frankfurt am Main (Hessen) against Israeli and US military strikes on Iran, featuring pro-Iran and anti-Israel slogans and portraits of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei. At the same time, around 450 people gathered for a counter-protest in support of the attacks, with police keeping the two groups separated. Minor physical confrontations occurred between counter-protesters and police, although the report does not specify the nature of the confrontations. The event was part of a wider protest movement that emerged after the joint Israeli and US military strikes on Iran on 28 February 2026.

On 21 March 2026, at around 1 pm, at the call of the BSW, under the motto 'No to war against Iran! Peace instead of war inflation!', hundreds of people, including members of the Iranian diaspora, students, retirees and activists, gathered at Potsdamer Square in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), opposing US and Israeli attacks on Iran while warning against possible German involvement in military escalation, highlighting the social and economic impact of the war on German households. Participants promoted peace and protection of civilians in Iran. The event was part of a wider protest movement that emerged after the joint Israeli and US military strikes on Iran on 28 February 2026.

On 28 March 2026, under the motto 'No Kings', several hundred people protested at Bebel Square in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin) against US President Donald Trump and his policies, criticizing 'attacks on democracy', US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), while demanding the release of files related to Jeffrey Epstein. The event was part of a broader internationally coordinated protest movement originating in the United States.

On 11 April 2026, in the afternoon, around 600 people staged a protest at two locations near the U.S. Embassy and the Holocaust Memorial in Berlin - Mitte (Berlin), demanding democracy and human rights in Iran and the end of the current Iranian regime. The protests included slogans such as 'Freedom for Iran' and 'Democracy for Iran', with participants showing support for opposition figures like Reza Pahlavi.

On 27 March 2025, five people demonstrated in Christiania, Copenhagen, to oppose the Danish government's proposal to allow permanent US military bases on Danish soil and to express their dissatisfaction with US President Donald Trump's policies.

On 29 March 2025, hundreds of people demonstrated in Aarhus, Midtjylland, to protest against the administration of US President Trump and their statements about gaining control over Greenland, including the possible annexation of Greenland by the United States. Greenland residents and students participated in the event, among others.

On 1 April 2025, around 15 people demonstrated during Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's visit to Aalborg, Nordjylland, to oppose the permanent establishment of US military bases on Danish soil and to call for prioritizing welfare over military spending.

On 8 April 2025, activists from the Workers' Communist Party (APK) in Odense, Syddanmark, to oppose the Danish government's proposal to allow the permanent presence of US military bases on Danish soil. The demonstration took place in connection with parliamentary hearings on the matter.

On 6 April 2025, people demonstrated in front of the US embassy in Osterbro, Copenhagen, to protest against the administration of US President Trump and their statements about gaining control over Greenland, including the possible annexation of Greenland by the United States.

On 11 April 2025, around 50 people demonstrated outside the Danish Parliament in Copenhagen to oppose the Danish government's proposal to allow the permanent presence of US military bases on Danish soil. The demonstration took place in connection with parliamentary hearings on the matter. Members of the parliament Trine Pertou Mach (the Red-Green Alliance), activists from the Youth of the Socialist People's Party (SFU), the Global Action (GA) and NOAH movement participated in the event, among others.

On 9 April 2025, people staged a protest performance in Copenhagen to oppose the Danish government's proposal to allow the permanent presence of US military bases on Danish soil. The demonstration took place in connection with the upcoming parliamentary hearings on the matter.

On 1 May 2025, people demonstrated in Aarhus, Midtjylland, to mark Labor Day and in support of workers' rights. Among other things, the activists opposed militarization and Denmark's base agreement with the United States. Activists from the Communist Party (KP) and the Public Resistance movement (Almen Modstand) participated in the event, among others.

On 10 June 2025, people demonstrated in Copenhagen to oppose the Danish government's proposal to allow the permanent presence of US military bases on Danish soil. Activists from the Time for Peace - Active Against War movement participated in the event, among others.

On 11 June 2025, people demonstrated outside of the Danish Parliament in Copenhagen to oppose the Danish government's proposal to allow the permanent presence of US military bases on Danish soil. The demonstration took place in connection with the final parliamentary hearings on the matter.

On 14 June 2025, American community members, demonstrated in Copenhagen to protest a military parade in the United States coinciding with President Donald Trump's birthday and to show solidarity with protests taking place in U.S. cities. The event was organized by the Democrats Abroad.

On 4 July 2025, around 40 people demonstrated during the American Independence Day celebration in Aalborg, Nordjylland, to oppose US President Donald Trump, his policies, and what they referred to as American imperialism. American community members, activists from the Red-Green Alliance (EL) and the Socialist People's Party (SF) participated in the event, among others.

On 6 August 2025, around 50 peace activists demonstrated in Norrebro, Copenhagen, calling for a ban on nuclear weapons and commemorating the victims of the atomic bomb in Hiroshima and Nagasaki. The activists also showed their opposition to the US military bases on Danish soil.

On 18 October 2025, members of the American community demonstrated in Copenhagen to oppose the US President Donald Trump and show solidarity with the nationwide 'No Kings' protests in the United States. The event was organized by the Democrats Abroad.

On 4 January 2026, around 300 to 400 people demonstrated outside the US Embassy in Copenhagen to oppose the US military intervention in Venezuela and the arrest of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.

On 17 January 2026, hundreds of people demonstrated in Aalborg, Nordjylland, to oppose US claims over Greenland and to defend Greenlandic sovereignty, following renewed statements by the US President Donald Trump regarding control over the island. Among those present was city council member Nuuradiin S. Hussein (S). The event was organized by the National Organization for Greenlanders in Denmark (Uagut), the Danish Association for International Cooperation and the Inuit Umbrella Association.

On 14 January 2026, people demonstrated outside the United States Embassy in Copenhagen to oppose US claims over Greenland and to defend Greenlandic sovereignty, following renewed statements by the US President Donald Trump regarding control over the island.

On 24 January 2026, people demonstrated in Vejle, Syddanmark, to oppose US claims over Greenland and to defend Greenlandic sovereignty, following renewed statements by the US President Donald Trump regarding control over the island. The Red-Green Alliance Party was among the organizers.

On 31 January 2026, thousands of demonstrators, including combat veterans, took part in the 'NoWords' demonstration outside the US Embassy in Copenhagen to protest the US President Donald Trump's statements on European NATO soldiers and to honor Danish soldiers killed in action in Iraq and Afghanistan.

On 8 February 2026, people demonstrated outside the Embassy of the United States in Copenhagen to express solidarity with Venezuela and called for the release of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores. The activists also opposed US sanctions against Latin American countries.

On 22 February 2026, around 50 people demonstrated outside Karup Air Base in Karup, Midtjylland, to oppose the new defense agreement between Denmark and the United States allowing US soldiers to be stationed in Denmark and to call for the cancellation of the agreement.

On 30 May 2025, a peaceful protest took place in Kakanda (Lubudi, Lualaba). The protest was staged by civil society and included representatives of 27 local communities impact by the activities of mining company 'Boss Mining'. The protest was staged to denounce the 'illegal exploitation' of the mines by Chinese and Lebanese citizens with the support of the army which is blocking the activities of Boss Mining. The protesters demanded for the resumption of activities of Boss Mining, which protesters said was the legal exploitant and contributed to local development and employment.

On 1 July 2025, a protest took place in Fungurume (Lubudi, Lualaba), to demand the freeing of 3 agents of Tenke Fungurume Mining (TFM), who were arrested on 3 June 2025. Community leaders say they were arrested by two Chinese leaders of TFM assisted by Congolese police without any official warrant.

On 11 July 2025, over 150 residents led by civil society groups protested against illegal mining at the COMIDE mining site in Lubudi (Lubudi, Lualaba). FARDC forces violently intervened (means unspecified), causing 1 civilian to be injured and hospitalized. Protesters denounced illegal Chinese and Lebanese operators working the site, accusing military personnel of enabling their presence. The extent of injuries is not known.

On 23 December 2025, at the call of M23, tens of thousands of people demonstrated in Bukavu (Bukavu, Sud-Kivu) to support M23 and to denounce the withdrawal of M23 from Uvira under American pressure. Several sources indicated that the demonstrators were forced by M23. On the same day, Wazalendo carried out a raid on the city to dissuade residents from responding to M23's call, killing 1 civilian (coded separately).

On 16 April 2026, artisanal miners staged a protest in Kisankala (Luilu, Lubudi, Lualaba) to show their opposition to the expansion of mining activities by a Chinese company on the Kisanfu-Kisankala road.

On 24 April 2026, police arrested several Alternative 2028 members who were staging a sit-in in front of the U.S. embassy in Kinshasa - Gombe (Kinshasa, Kinshasa).
