Around 6 June 2025 (as reported), in Guayaquil - Tarqui (Guayas), four people were killed and their bodies were found tied up inside a cistern in the Nueva Frontera cooperative, Nueva Prosperina neighbourhoods. The victims died from asphyxiation. Two of whom were merchants and one was a female Chinese national. The victims had been kidnapped between 29 May and 5 June (coded separately). The police arrested between five and seven suspects and identified them as members of the Los Igualitos gang. The motivations are unknown. 4 fatalities.

Around 9 September 2025 (as reported), in Guayaquil - Tarqui (Guayas), a Chinese man was killed and his body was found in an advanced state of decomposition inside a house in the Paraiso del Rio 2 area, Mucho Lote 2 sector. Police seized five cell phones, a laptop, three grenades, a pistol, two rifles, and 281 ammunition rounds. It is unknown whether the Chinese man was a kidnapping victim or a member of an armed group. The number of perpetrators, authorship and motivations are unknown. 1 fatality.
On 3 January 2026, in Quito - Eugenio Espejo (Pichincha), political and social groups held a protest at Abraham Lincoln square to protest against the US military intervention in Venezuela.

On 14 October 2025, students of the American University in Cairo (AUC) protested inside the university campus in Cairo - New Cairo 2 (New Cairo 1, Cairo) against hosting former U.S. ambassador to Israel Daniel Kurtzer, who was invited to take part in a lecture on Washington's role in the Middle East. They chanted slogans against Israel and the normalization of relations with the country.
On 8 February 2026, workers at the Chinese electronics company OPPO protested in 10th of Ramadan City (10th of Ramadan 1, Sharqia) over low wages.

On 12 April 2025, at the call of the Palestinian House of Aragon (Casa Palestina de Aragon), dozens of people protested outside the US embassy in Madrid - Salamanca (Madrid) to denounce the US 'complicity' in Israel's 'massacre' in Palestine and to call for unity among peoples.

On 1 May 2025, on the occasion of Labor Day and International Workers' Day, at the call of UGT and CCOO, around 300 people held a protest in Ceuta (Ceuta) to demand better working conditions, focusing mainly on a reduced workweek, the renewal of collective bargaining agreements and the protection of the residence compensation amid the costs and difficulties of living in Ceuta. Protesters also expressed solidarity with Ukraine and Palestine and criticized Trump's tariff policies and the rise of far-right politics in Europe, demanding a stronger Europe.

On 1 May 2025, on the occasion of Labor Day and International Workers' Day, at the call of UGT and CCOO, thousands of people, including local PSOE elected officials, marched from O Infernino to Plaza de Armas in Ferrol (Galicia) to demand improved working conditions. Protesters called for the introduction of a 37.5-hour workweek, fair pensions, higher wages, and increased workload in the shipbuilding sector, while expressing solidarity with Palestine and rejecting the war in Gaza, as well as denouncing tariffs imposed by US President Donald Trump.

On 1 May 2025, on the occasion of Labor Day and International Workers' Day, at the call of UGT, CCOO and USO, hundreds of people, including an elected deputy of Podemos, held a protest in Murcia (Murcia) to demand better working conditions with a reduced workweek. Moroccan workers, who also took part in the demonstration, advocated for easier driver's license recognition, while others defended sex workers' rights. Other motives included the opposition to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Donald Trump's new term, and energy concerns amid the recent general blackout in the Iberian Peninsula.

On 12 July 2025, at the call of the Stop The War Movement, more than 1,000 people, including members of the PSOE in Madrid, More Madrid, and SMR, protested in Plaza de Callao in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) to support the Palestinian people and demand a definitive ceasefire. Protesters denounced what they described as an ongoing genocide in Gaza and held Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and former US President Trump responsible for the escalation. They called for international accountability, an end to the war, and solidarity from all sectors of society.

On 19 July 2025, at the call of Alicante Understands (Alicante Entiende), Diversity (Diversitat) and We Understand LGBTI (Entendemos LGTBI), between 15,000 and more than 20,000 people, including LGBTQ+ activists, protested in Alicante (Valencia) to denounce a recent homophobic attack against a 20-year-old. Protesters condemned the rise in anti-LGBTQ+ violence, called for stronger protections and education on diversity, and criticized right-wing parties in local institutions for undermining LGBTQ+ rights. The genocide in Gaza and the LGBTI regression in Hungary and Trump's policies were also denounced.

On 18 September 2025, at the call of the Global Movement to Gaza Platform and Marches for Palestine (Marxes per Palestina), around 250 people, including lawyers, staged a pot-banging protest outside the US consulate in Palma de Mallorca (Islas Baleares) in support of Palestine and the Sumud Flotilla, demanding the end of the 'genocide' in Gaza and urging sanctions and boycotts against Israel.

On 18 October 2025, 300 people protested in Madrid - Centro (Madrid) to condemn US President Donald Trump's attacks on democracy, migrants living in the US, and the US Constitution. The event was part of a global protest movement called 'No Kings,' condemning President Donald Trump's administration for authoritarian practices and corruption.

On 17 December 2025, in the evening, activists protested outside the US Consulate in Las Palmas de Gran Canarias (Canarias) to oppose the escalating US aggression toward Venezuela, arguing the military intervention violates international law. Protesters rejected the Nobel Peace Prize awarded to Maria Corina Machado, accusing her of supporting foreign intervention.

On 3 January 2026, at the call of by the Bolivarian Assembly of Catalonia (L'Assemblea Bolivariana de Catalunya), around 400 people, including members of the CUP, gathered in front of the US Consulate in Barcelona - Sarria - Sant Gervasi (Cataluna) to condemn the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026. Protesters burned two US flags. At the beginning, there was a brief verbal clash with some Venezuelans in favor of the military intervention against Maduro.

On 3 January 2026, two groups of people gathered in Vigo (Galicia). One group, called by Galician-Bolivarian Association Hugo Chavez (Asociacion Galego-Bolivariana Hugo Chavez - Agabo), BNG, CIG, Unitary Central of Workers (Central Unitaria de Traballadoras - CUT), Sea of Lights (Mar de Lumes), Landlord Movement (Movemento Arrendista), PCG (PCE), PCRG, Podemos Galicia, and UPG, of around 400 people, including BNG leaders such as a BNG MP and a BNG City Councilor, protested against the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026. The other group of around 30 people, mainly Venezuelans, called by the Venezuelan Federation of Galicia, supported the capture and celebrated their freedom. No physical clashes between the two groups were reported.

On 4 January 2026, at noon, at the call of various organizations and left-wing parties, including SMR, 1,000 people, including Podemos Secretary General Ione Belarra, PCE general secretary, an SMR deputy and IU spokesperson in Congress, protested outside the US Embassy in Madrid - Salamanca (Madrid) in support of international law and to condemn the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026. Protesters called on the Spanish Government and Europe to sever ties with the Trump Administration.

On 3 January 2026, in the afternoon, at the call of Soldepaz, 200 people, including representatives from CCOO, UGT, Podemos, We Are Asturias and the Unitary and Autonomous Union of Teaching Workers of Asturias (Sindicato Unitario y Autonomo de Trabajadores de la Ensenanza de Asturias - SUATEA), gathered in Gijon (Asturias), opposing the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026.

On 4 January 2026, in the morning, at the call of Interpueblos, CGT, IU, Antifascists, the Assembly Against War (Asamblea Contra la Guerra), and PCPE, a little over 100 people protested in Santander (Cantabria), opposing the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026.

On 4 January 2026, in the afternoon, at the call of IU, around 200 people protested in Logrono (La Rioja), opposing the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026. A group of 20 Venezuelans celebrated the liberation and counter-protested against the IU protest. The two groups exchanged shouts, insults, and profanities. One pro-Maduro protester also confronted journalists, reproaching them for gathering statements from the Venezuelans.

On 4 January 2026, around 12:30 pm, at the call of the Wings platform (plataforma Hegoak), people, including the Venezuelan Consul in Bilbao, CCOO Euskadi general secretary, political representatives from parties such as EH Bildu such as the head of Policy and International Relations, regional MPs, and the spokesperson for the municipal group in the Bilbao City Council, protested in Bilbao (Pais Vasco) to condemn the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026. At the start of the protest, a minor incident occurred when a Venezuelan man, opposed to the Nicolas Maduro regime, approached the demonstration and chanted slogans denouncing the situation in his country.

On 4 January 2026, hundreds of people, including Committees of Solidarity Among Peoples and for Peace (Comites de Solidaridad entre los Pueblos y por la Paz - CosPaz), protested in Leon (Castilla y Leon) to condemn the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026.

On 3 January 2026, a pro-Maduro group from the Bolivarian Platform (Platforma Bolivariana) gathered in front of the Venezuelan Consulate in Santa Cruz de Tenerife (Canarias) to express their discontent with signs reading 'Canary Islands with Venezuela' and condemn what they consider a 'massacre' following a the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026. Other protesters supported the capture and argued that the US action seeks to hold Maduro accountable for alleged drug trafficking and corruption offenses.

On 3 January 2026, two groups of people gathered in Plaza de Espana in Zaragoza (Aragon). One group, mainly Spaniards, condemned the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026. The other group, mainly Venezuelans, supported the capture and celebrated their freedom.

On 10 January 2026, at noon, at the call of the Galician-Bolivarian Association Hugo Chavez (Asociacion Galego-Bolivariana Hugo Chavez - Agabo), more than 1,000 people, including a Member of Parliament (BNG), the BNG's International Relations Coordinator, and the IU National Coordinator, demonstrated in Santiago de Compostela (Galicia) against US imperialism and for peace and sovereignty in Venezuela. The demonstration came after the US military intervention in Venezuela on 3 January 2026, which culminated in the capture of President Nicolas Maduro.
On 2 March 2026, at the call of the BDS, people protested in front of the US consulate in Valencia (Valencia) to condemn the US-Israeli military attack on Iran and calling for an end to the war.

On 21 March 2026, at the call of Defend Cuba (Defensem Cuba), around 100 people staged a protest outside the US consulate in Barcelona - Sarria - Sant Gervasi (Cataluna) against US policies toward Cuba and to demand an end to the US blockade on Cuba.

On 28 March 2026, at the call of Democrats Abroad, around 200 people, including American citizens, staged a protest in Plaza Sant Jaume in Barcelona - Ciutat Vella (Cataluna) against US President Donald Trump and his unlawful policies, notably against migrants, and to demand the defense of democracy and civil rights. The event was part of the international protest against Trump movement labeled 'No Kings Day'.

On 28 March 2026, at the call of the Coordinator for Peace of the Region of Murcia (Coordinadora por la Paz de la Region de Murcia), around 700 people marched in Murcia (Murcia) against the US-Israeli war against Iran, and to demand peace, a ceasefire, diplomatic solutions, the closure of US military bases in Spain, and the severing of diplomatic relations with Israel.
On 30 August 2025, an unidentified armed group abducted 3 Chinese nationals near Debre Birhan (Debre Berhan town, North Shewa, Amhara). Further information not available.

properties.actor: OLF-OLA: Oromo Liberation Army-Oromo Liberation Front
properties.notes: Around 15 September 2025 (month of), the OLF-OLA abducted 2 - 4 employees of a Chinese government company (all Ethiopians) in Laas Dheere (location coded to Shinile, in Shinille, Sitti, Somali). The armed group released them after receiving a ransom of 4 million birr. Suspected individuals involved in the alleged kidnapping were arrested, and the bank account where the four million birr was paid to release the hostages, and a person using the account number was arrested in Dire Dawa.

On 19 April 2025, more than 30 demonstrators, including American community members, gathered in Helsinki to protest against US President Donald Trump and his policies. The event was organized by the Americans Abroad.

On 11 June 2025, Greenpeace activists staged a protest performance and displayed a large banner reading 'Time to Resist' on the Central Station tower in Helsinki. The action was part of Greenpeace's global Time to Resist campaign, aimed to highlight perceived growing crackdowns on activism around the world, including in the United States and Romania.

On 18 October 2025, around 70 people, mostly members of the American community in Finland, demonstrated in Helsinki, to oppose the US President Donald Trump and show solidarity with the nationwide 'No Kings' protests in the United States. The event was organized by the Democrats Abroad.

On 6 January 2026, people demonstrated in Helsinki to oppose imperialism and military interventions, criticizing the US military intervention in Venezuela as well as Finland's arms purchases and defence agreements with the United States and Israel.
On 7 March 2026, people demonstrated in Helsinki to oppose the US-Israeli offensive in Iran and the policies of the US President Donald Trump.

On 28 March 2026, demonstrators, mostly members of the American community in Finland, demonstrated in Helsinki to oppose the US President Donald Trump and show solidarity with the nationwide 'No Kings' protests in the United States. The event was organized by the Democrats Abroad.

On 29 March 2025, a small group of people gathered outside a Tesla charging station in Beauvais (Hauts-de-France) to protest against Tesla and its owner Elon Musk. Participants denounced what they described as Musk's 'anti-democratic actions' and the spread of far-right ideologies through his companies and political influence. The event was part of a global campaign organized by the Tesla Takedown movement, which sought to target Tesla's CEO Elon Musk and his company and criticize his policies within the Trump administration in the U.S.

On 3 April 2025, in the morning, around 100 people gathered at the Vieux-Port in Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) as part of the global 'Stand Up for Science' mobilization. The protest was in response to budget cuts and censorship, particularly under the policies of US President Donald Trump, and aimed to demand greater funding and support for public research and academic freedom. Participants expressed solidarity with researchers, especially those in the United States, arguing they were facing significant challenges in their work due to political decisions.

On 10 April 2025, Vencorex employees, CGT affiliates, National Deputy Elisa Martin (LFI/NFP), and Mayor Christophe Ferrari (independent) gathered outside the Vencorex factory in Le Pont-de-Claix (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against the Commercial Court's decision to sell the factory to Chinese company Wanhua instead of handing it to a workers' cooperative. The protesters expressed fears of downsizing and their frustration over the lack of state support for the workers.

On 5 April 2025, people, including around 100 United States citizens, gathered in Nice (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest United States President Donald Trump's policies. The demonstrators expressed opposition to issues including tariffs, human rights violations, and threats to data privacy and democracy. The rally was organized by Democrats Abroad.

On 7 April 2025, at the call of the Hands Off movement and the Collective 13 Women's Rights (Collectif 13 Droit des Femmes), around 20 women gathered outside the U.S. consulate in Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest against U.S. President Donald Trump. The protesters expressed solidarity with American women facing attacks on their rights and denounced the global repercussions of Trump's policies.

On 5 April 2025, people, including around 200 US nationals, gathered at Republique Square in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against US President Donald Trump and Elon Musk. Protesters denounced attacks on democracy, human rights, and international partnerships, and held banners reading 'Resist the Tyrant', 'Feminists for Freedom, Not Fascism', and 'Save Democracy'. The demonstration was part of a broader transatlantic mobilization called by Democrats Abroad.

On 26 April 2025, at the call of AFPS, around 80 people demonstrated in Brest (Bretagne) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people, condemn the Israeli airstrikes on Gaza, and protest against US President Donald Trump's plans to buy the Gaza Strip.

On 1 May 2025, at 9:30 am, on the occasion of Labor and International Workers' Day, between 550 (according to police) and 1,100 people (unions), including CGT, SUD, and FSU affiliates, gathered for at a parking lot then a square in Foix (Occitanie) condemning Trump for attacking democracy, abortion rights, education and development aid and to demand better working conditions.

On 5 June 2025, at the call of the association Freedom in Tibet (Liberte au Tibet), around 15 people demonstrated in Colmar (Grand Est) to remember the Tiananmen Square massacre and demand that local elected officials form a support group in support of the independence of Tibet. The protesters also criticized Chinese authorities, labeling the Chinese state totalitarian.
On 14 June 2025, several dozen people gathered in Montpellier (Occitanie) to protest against Donald Trump and his administration. The event was part of the global 'No Kings' demonstration day.

On 22 June 2025, around 400 people, including Iranian nationals, refugees, and members of the Iranian community, gathered on Chatelet Square in Paris (Ile-de-France) to condemn the recent Israeli airstrikes on Iranian military and economic assets and U.S. President Donald Trump's decision to strike Iran's nuclear facilities. The protesters called for the protection of Iranian civilians.

On 25 August 2025, on the occasion of the Independence Day of Ukraine, around 100 people gathered in front of the city hall in Amiens (Hauts-de-France) to express solidarity with Ukraine. The commemoration took place against the backdrop of renewed concerns for peace following the 2025 Russia-United States Summit on 15 August 2025.

On 3 November 2025, at the call of the association Mouv'Enfants, people staged a protest in front of the BHV in Paris (Ile-de-France) to denounce Shein for selling child-pornographic dolls on its platform and to urge the department store to cut ties with the Chinese retailer, condemning what they called a 'culture of impunity'. Protesters held banners reading 'Shein is involved in child exploitation'.

On 4 January 2026, at 11am, at the call of PS, PCF, and LE, around 50 people, including Senator Olivier Jacquin (PS), gathered at Place Stanislas in Nancy (Grand Est) to denounce the military intervention the United States carried out in Venezuela and to support the Venezuelan civilian population. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 3 January 2026, in the evening, at the call of LFI, PCF and civil society organizations including the International Collective for peace in Venezuela (Collectif international pour la paix au Venezuela), RP, NPA, The Aftermath, the coalition War Against War (Guerre a la guerre), comprising Attac, SLT, the Paris Suburb Antifascist Action (Action Antifasciste Paris Banlieue), the Paris Suburb Feminist Assembly (Assemblee Feministe Paris Banlieue), and other organizations, as well as pro-Palestinian collectives, over 1,000 people, including LFI leader Jean-Luc Melanchon, LFI national deputies Mathilde Panot and Sophia Chikirou, PCF national secretary Fabien Roussel and other party representatives, elected officials, locals and nationals from South America including Columbia, gathered at Place de la Republique in Paris (Ile-de-France) to protest against the United States' military intervention in Venezuela and to denounce French President Emmanuel Macron's alleged supportive stance toward the event. Protesters raised Venezuelan, Columbian and Palestinian flags, as well as flags of French left political parties. Three protesters, including two who were hooded and masked, climbed on top of the statue of Place de la Republique and burnt a US flag. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 3 January 2026, between 80 and 100 people, including PCF, LFI, JC affiliates, and students from UNEF, Coordination-UEG, and Young Struggle, gathered at Place Felix Poulat in Grenoble (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against the United States' military intervention in Venezuela, chanting a popular pro-revolution South American chant. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 3 January 2026, around 30 people, including PCF affiliates, gathered at Place de la Reunion in Mulhouse (Grand Est) to denounce the military intervention the United States carried out in Venezuela. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 3 January 2026, at the call of EHKS, 120 people (according to organizers), gathered at Place du Reduit in Bayonne (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to protest against the United States' military intervention in Venezuela. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 3 January 2026, in the evening, at the call of LFI, PCF, local CGT and antimilitarist organizations, a few hundred people, including RP and War Against War (Guerre a la guerre), gathered at the prefecture of Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to protest against the United States' military intervention in Venezuela. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 5 January 2026, in the evening, at the call CGT, FSU, SUD, PCF, du JC, NPA, LFI, LO, Alternatiba, and AFPS, around 80 people, including national deputy Emmanuel Duplessy (Generation.s), gathered in front of the prefecture in Orleans (Centre-Val de Loire) to demonstrate. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 7 January 2026, at the call of PCF, LFI, Attac, CGT, FSU, SUD, MP and POI, between 30 and 40 people gathered in De la Liberation in Dijon (Bourgogne-Franche-Comte) to demonstrate. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 11 January 2026, at 6pm, at the call of DA, around 50 people, including French nationals and US nationals residing in France, held a night vigil outside the Consulate of the United States in Strasbourg (Grand Est), to pay tribute to and denounce the killing of Renee Nicole Good by a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent in Minneapolis on 7 January 2026. Protesters demonstrated solidarity with the wave of indignation that swept across the United States following the violent event, and also warned of the potential rise of fascism in France if left unchecked.

On 10 January 2026, at the call of different organizations, including CGT, LFI, PCF, UTOPAX, and ECOVIPAD, a few hundred people, including LFI leader Jean-Luc Melenchon, National Assembly Members Abdelkader Lahmar, Anais Belouassa-Cherifi, Idir Boumertit and Raphael Arnault (all LFI), protested at Place Bellecour in Lyon (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to condemn the United States' military intervention in Venezuela. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 9 January 2026, at the call of a local collective supporting the Palestinian people, around 40 people gathered in Privas (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against US 'imperialism' and 'colonialism', as well as to show solidarity with the Venezuelan people. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 17 January 2026, at 3pm, at the call of the local French association for Palestine (Poitiers-Palestine) and the local South-American collective of Poitiers (Collectif latino-americain de Poitiers - Colap), around 80 people, including a municipal councilor (Generation.s), as wel as LDH, LFI and POI affiliates, protested in Poitiers (Nouvelle-Aquitaine), to denounce the genocide in Gaza and show solidarity with both the Palestinian and Venezuelan people. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026.

On 28 January 2026, at 6:30pm, at the call of French and American associations fighting the far-right and authoritarianism in the world, including La Digue (The Barrier) association, 300 people, including American and Colombian nationals, protested in front of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Paris (Ile-de-France) against U.S. President Donald Trump's policies. Protesters also denounced the violent methods used by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) federal law enforcement agency.

On 3 February 2026, at the call of French social, political and trade union organizations, along with Latin American solidarity groups, people, including members of the Venezuelan community, gathered in La Republique Square in Paris (Ile-de-France) to demand the release of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife, as well as the respect of sovereignty and to condemned US imperialism. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population.

On 31 January 2026, around 70 people, including members of the US diaspora, gathered in Lille (Hauts-de-France) to protest against the US President Donald Trump administration's migration policies and ICE practices.

On 7 February 2026, at the call of the citizen movement Nou Bouke, several hundred people, including members of the anti-imperialist collectives and the Haitian diaspora, marched in Paris (Ile-de-France) to denounce alleged U.S. interference in Haiti and protest against Alix Didier Fils-Aime, the interim President of Haiti. Participants called for national sovereignty, an end to corruption, and international solidarity against imperialism.

On 2 March 2026, around 100 people, including members of the association Azadi Iranian Women (Asadi Femmes Iraniennes), AFPS, anti-imperialist and antimilitary collectives, the mayor of Brest Francois Cuillandre (PS) and National Deputy Pierre-Yves Cadalen (LFI), gathered in Liberty square in Brest (Bretagne) to express their support to the Iranian people following the American and Israeli strikes on Iran, expressing their opposition to forceful regime change and outlining the humanitarian impact of the current war. The event was part of a wave of demonstrations worldwide following the American-Israeli strikes on Iran and the death of the Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

On 7 March 2026, around 20 people and members of the collective Solidarity Palestine (Collectif Solidarite Palestine) gathered on Francois de Menthon square in Annecy (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to protest against the joint US-Israeli military offensive on Iran. Participants denounced American imperialism.

On 28 March 2026, at the call of DA, around 50 of the group's members, including American citizens residing in France, gathered in Aix-en-Provence (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) as part of the 'No Kings' Day, to protest against the authoritarianism of the Trump administration. This event coincided with a massive wave of protests that swept across the US that same day, for the same motives.

On 29 March 2025, at the call of Tesla Takedown global campaign and Action Network, protestors gathered outside the Tesla Center on Cliftonhall Road in Edinburgh (Scotland) calling for a boycott of Elon Musk's company. Protesters hold signs that read 'Save democracy, boycott Tesla' and 'Honk if you hate Elon'. The event was part of a global campaign organized by the Tesla Takedown movement, which sought to target Tesla's CEO Elon Musk and his company and criticize his policies within the Trump administration in the U.S.

On 29 March 2025, at the call of Tesla Takedown global campaign and Progressive Politics NI, dozens of protestors gathered outside a Tesla Center on Boucher Road in Belfast - South (Northern Ireland) calling for a boycott of Elon Musk's company. The event was part of a global campaign organized by the Tesla Takedown movement, which sought to target Tesla's CEO Elon Musk and his company and criticize his policies within the Trump administration in the U.S.

On 5 April 2025, at the call of more than 150 groups, including civil rights groups and trade unions, hundreds of people, including Americans living in the UK, gathered in Trafalgar Square in London - Westminster (England) as part of global demonstrations 'hands off' against Donald Trump's administration and his policies. Protesters chanted 'Hands off Ukraine' and 'Hands off the UK' and held banners that read 'No to Maga hate' and 'Dump Trump'.

On 5 April 2025, between 40-50 protesters gathered outside a Tesla Showroom on Loughborough Road in Nottingham (England) for 'Nottingham Against Elon' protest, calling for a boycott of Elon Musk's company. The event was part of a global campaign organized by the Tesla Takedown movement, which sought to target Tesla's CEO Elon Musk and his company and criticize his policies within the Trump administration in the U.S.

On 14 June 2025, at the call of Democrats Abroad, protesters gathered outside the US Embassy in London - Kensington and Chelsea (England) under the banner of No Kings Protests against Donald Trump's policies and actions during his second presidency. The event was part of a global protest movement called 'No Kings', which took place on the day of a military parade on Donald Trump's 79th birthday.

On 23 June 2025, several hundred people gathered at the top of Buchanan Street in Glasgow (Scotland) to protest the bombing of Iranian nuclear facilities by US forces. Demonstrators waved Iranian, Lebanese, and Palestinian flags and held signs reading 'Cut war, not welfare' and 'Starmer has blood on his hands'.

On 26 July 2025, at the call of the Stop Trump Coalition, hundreds of people gathered at the Union Terrace in the city center in Aberdeen (Scotland) in opposition to US President Donald Trump's visit to Scotland, which coincided with his private golf trip at Turnberry. Protesters voiced their disapproval of Trump's rhetoric and policies, particularly his stances on immigration, abortion rights, climate change, and foreign affairs, and Gaza. Activists from a wide array of groups, including trade unions, climate justice campaigners, and pro-Palestine groups, addressed the crowd.

On 28 July 2025, in the early afternoon, around 100 protesters gathered outside the White Horse Inn near Trump's Menie Estate golf course in the village of Balmedie (Scotland) to demonstrate against the visit of US President Donald Trump and primarily in opposition to his environmental legacy, political rhetoric, and recent remarks on Gaza. Demonstrators waved Palestinian flags and held signs and placards.

On 13 August 2025, pro-Palestine protesters gathered outside the Carnell Estate resort near Kilmarnock (Scotland) against U.S. Vice President JD Vance and his support of 'Israel's genocide in Gaza' as he was entering the resort for his family vacation. Protesters waved Palestinian flags, banged pots and pans, and chanted pro-Palestine slogans.

On 16 September 2025, at the call of the Stop Trump Coalition, around 70 demonstrators gathered outside Windsor Castle in Windsor (England) to oppose Donald Trump's second state visit to the UK. Protesters carried placards and chanted 'Trump out' and 'say it loud, say it clear: Donald Trump not welcome here'. Demonstrators also projected an image of Trump, Epstein, and Prince Andrew on the Windsor Castle.

On 17 September 2025, at the call of the Stop Trump Coalition, around 5,000 demonstrators marched from Portland Place to Parliament Square in London - Westminster (England) to oppose Donald Trump's second state visit to the UK. Protesters carried placards with slogans such as 'No to racism, no to Trump' and 'Stop Trump, stop fascism.' Participants expressed concerns about Trump's global influence, linking him to the rise of far-right movements in Britain and Europe. Independent MPs Zarah Sultana and Jeremy Corbyn also addressed the crowd.

On 5 January 2026, anti-war protesters gathered outside the US Embassy in London - Wandsworth (England) to condemn the United States' military action in Venezuela following the raid by US Special forces and capturing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on charges of narco-terrorism. Participants labeled the military intervention as illegal and expressed opposition to the US President's announcement that the United States would oversee the administration and infrastructure of Venezuela during a transition period.

On 9 January 2026, at the call of Your Party, around 30 people, including trade unionists, students, peace activists, and community campaigners, gathered outside Reading Train Station in Reading (England) to protest US military intervention in Venezuela and the subsequent arrest of President Nicolas Maduro. Protesters called upon the UK government and local Reading Members of Parliament to publicly condemn the intervention. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026

On 10 January 2026, at the call of Stop the War Scotland with support from the Scottish Trades Union Congress, the Scottish Venezuela Solidarity Campaign, and the Scottish Cuba Solidarity Campaign, demonstrators gathered outside the United States consulate on Regent Terrace in Edinburgh (Scotland) to protest the arrest and detention of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and the First Lady. Protesters condemned the detention as an act of military aggression and kidnapping that violated international law and Venezuelan sovereignty. The event was part of a wider mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026.

On 17 January 2026, hundreds of demonstrators gathered at Royal Mint Court in Tower Hill area in London - Tower Hamlets (England) to protest the proposed construction of a Chinese 'mega-embassy' at the site. Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch, former leader Iain Duncan Smith, and MPs from the Liberal Democrat and Reform UK also attended the protest. Protesters carried flags and banners, chanted slogans against the development, citing significant security concerns and the potential for increased surveillance of British officials.

On 29 January 2026, more than a hundred members of the Kurdish group living in the UK and their supporters held a flash protest and marched through the city center in Norwich (England) to protest against the Syrian Transitional Government (STG) and escalating military attacks on Rojava, the Kurdish-led autonomous region in north-east Syria, by Syrian government troops. Demonstrators waved Kurdish and Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) flags and criticized the role of United Kingdom and the United States foreign policy under Donald Trump in the region.

On 26 January 2026, at the call of SUTR, hundreds of people gathered on Trafalgar Square in London - Westminster (England) to demonstrate in solidarity with activists in Minneapolis and to protest against the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and to commemorate Alex Pretti, a US health worker who was killed by ICE agents on 24 January 2026.

On 3 February 2026, at the call of the International Antifascist organization of London, demonstrators held a march in London (England) to mark one month since the 3 January 2026 detention of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and First Lady Cilia Flores by United States forces and to demand the immediate release of the presidential couple, arguing that their capture on drug and weapons charges violated international immunity agreements. Protesters called for the UK government to cease diplomatic and military support for Israel and demanded the restitution of Venezuelan gold held in the Bank of England.

On 30 August 2025, at the call of the Venezuelan Embassy in London and in collaboration with the Anti-Fascist International and the Revolutionary Communist Group, demonstrators gathered under the banner 'Venezuela is not a threat; Venezuela is hope' in Notting Hill in London - Kensington and Chelsea (England) against the deployment of United States warships in the Caribbean earlier that month. Protesters condemned 'gunboat diplomacy' and US military aggression aimed at destabilizing the region.

On 14 February 2026, at the call of the Gaza Genocide Emergency Committee, pro-Palestine and anti-war protesters held a march from McLennan Arch to the city center in Glasgow (Scotland) to protest against Donald Trump's proposed policies regarding Gaza. Participants carried Palestinian flags and placards with slogans such as 'Stop Arming Israel' and 'Cut War, Not Welfare'.

On 2 March 2026, anti-war activists, including members of the PBP and the Iranian diaspora, held an emergency 'Stop Bombing Iran' rally at the City Hall in Belfast - South (Northern Ireland), to condemn the military strikes led by the United States and Israel against Iran, which reportedly caused civilian casualties. Participants criticized the involvement of Western leaders such as Donald Trump, Benjamin Netanyahu, and Keir Starmer, accusing them of 'warmongering' and undermining Iranian self-determination through aerial bombardment.

On 6 March 2026, at the call of the SUTR, anti-war campaigners held a 'Hand Off Iran' rally at Guildhall Square in Portsmouth (England) to condemn the recent series of US-Israel aerial bombardments and the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. On 7 March 2026, in the aftenoon, at the call of the CND, StWC, PSC, Muslim Association of Britain, Palestinian Forum in Britain, and Friends of Al-Aqsa in London, between 5,000 and 6,000 people held a march from Millbank to the US Embassy in London - Wandsworth (England) for the Hands off Iran rally to demand an end to US and Israeli military strikes against Iran following the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader. On 7 March 2026, anti-war activists marched to the US consulate in Edinburgh (Scotland) to demonstrate against the US and Israeli air strikes on Iran. Protesters carried placards denouncing the legality of the war and calling for an end to the arming of Israel.

On 7 March 2026, demonstrators marched through the city center and gathered at Writer's Square in Belfast - South (Northern Ireland) to mark the International Women's Day rally. Participants, including representatives from Women's Aid, Global Women's Strike, Youth Action, and Surviving Economic Abuse. The rally featured a speech by former Irish President Mary Robinson, who condemned 'attacks on truth' by the United States administration and highlighted an epidemic of violence against women and girls.

On 21 March 2026, at the call of the Stop The War Coalition, hundreds of protesters marched in Belfast (Northern Ireland) to protest the joint US-Israeli military operation on Iran, the occupation of Palestine by Israel, and Israeli military attacks on Lebanon. On 21 March 2026, at the call of the Stop The War Coalition, protesters gathered in Cardiff (Wales) to protest the joint US-Israeli military operation on Iran, the occupation of Palestine by Israel, and Israeli military attacks on Lebanon. On 22 March 2026, at the call of Stop the War Scotland, Ayrshire Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament and Ayrshire Global Justice, around 40 people protested at Glasgow Prestwick Airport in Glasgow (Scotland), against the US military's use of the airport facilities. Protesters gathered at the airport train station before entering the airport terminal, where they handed a letter to staff calling for all military flights to be stopped. Protesters also called for an end to the war in Iran. A woman was arrested during the protest.

On 28 March 2026, at the call of the Together Alliance and Stand Up To Racism, between 50,000 (according to the police) and 500,000 of people (according to the organizers) marched in London - Westminster (England) as part of the Together Alliance march, a march against the far-right. Participants held banners against anti-racism, Donald Trump, and reading 'refugees welcome'. Protesters marched from Park Lane to Whitehall, where speakers delivered speeches, and to Trafalgar Park, where multiple musicians and artists performed. Labour MPs Diane Abbott and Dawn Butler, leader of the Green Party Zack Polanski, and the General Secretary of the National Education Union participated in the march. A separate protest at the call of the Palestine Coalition and the Stop the War Coalition took place in London on the same day (coded separately), with both groups merging in Whitehall (London-Westminster). 25 people were arrested across both marches, including 18 Palestine Action supporters.

On 4 April 2026, at the call of Lakenheath Alliance for Peace, more than a hundred people gathered at a peace encampment outside of the airbase in Lakenheath (England), to protest against the use of the airbase by US military forces. Protesters erected a blockade outside of the airbase's main gate. The encampment was formed after a US fighter jet had taken off from the Lakenheath airbase and was later shot down in Iran. The encampment lasted for six days, ending on 6 April. Police intervened and arrested seven people, including two on suspicion of obstructing a public highway, and others on suspicion of supporting Palestine Action.

On 7 April 2026, at the call of the Islamic Human Rights Commission (IHRC), dozens of pro-Iranian protesters gathered outside Downing Street in London - Westminster (England) to protest against US President Donald Trump, hours after he had issued new threats against Iran. Protesters carried flags and denounced the US and Israeli military operations in Iran. Protesters also chanted 'Allahu Akbar'.

On 11 April 2026, hundreds of residents marched in Glasgow's city center (Scotland) to protest against Scottish airports being used by US military forces as part of their ongoing military intervention in Iran. Protesters marched from Glasgow Green to Clyde Street. Several anti-war and trade union organizations participated in the protest. Protesters held anti-Trump signs and denounced the bombings in Lebanon and the Middle East more broadly, and the UK Government's decision to allow the use of UK air bases by US forces.

On 7 July 2025, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a Chinese and a Ghanaian men at an illegal mining site in Subri-Nkwanta (Sefwi Bibiani-Ahwiaso Bekwai, Western North) while they were returning from their mining site with gold concentrate. The attackers escaped with the gold. The motive remains unclear with police suspecting a robbery while community members believe the attack might be linked to rival illegal mining groups.

On 31 December 2025, residents gathered in Aboso (Prestea-Huni Valley, Western) to denounce the handover of a gangway illegal mining (galamsey) site to Chinese operators, citing environmental destruction and livelihood losses. Police fired warning shots to disperse the crowd, fatally shooting 2 people. Police later released a statement describing the incident as an act of self-defense in response to a hostile and armed crowd who had shot at the police. 2 fatalities.

On 21 January 2026, for the second consecutive day, members of the group 'Arise Ghana' protested outside the US Embassy in Accra (Accra, Greater Accra) to demand that the US authorities take action on their request for the former finance minister to return to Ghana and face allegations of corruption. The protest was announced to last for 2 weeks.

Around 9 April 2026, some youths rioted at a Chinese owned illegal mining site at Tigarikrom (Wassa Amenfi East, Western) to denounce the death of a young man who was beat by security forces on the night of 8 April (coded separately). The demonstrators set two excavators ablaze and seized another one.

On 1 May 2025, during a nationwide 24-hour strike, workers participated in a very massive rally in Eleusis at the call of GSEE and ADEDY to mark International Labor Day and to protest for their rights with the main slogan 'May Day is not a holiday, it is a day of strike'. This was followed by a strong march to the military airport of Eleusis. The protesters objected to its use 'for the criminal plans of NATO and the United States'.

On 18 May 2025, the Central Committee of KKE and affiliated groups, including the Hellenic Committee for International Disarmament and Peace (EEDYE), PAME, OGE, rallied outside the Ministry of Defence, Athens - North Athens, where the 42nd Marathon Peace March with the slogan 'against the imperialist plans of USA-NATO-EU and Greece's involvement in them' would terminate. University and school students also participated in the rally.

On 13 June 2025, the Communist Party of Greece (KKE) held a rally in Lamia to commemorate the 80th anniversary since the death of Aris Velouchiotis and the 'Antifascist Victory of the Peoples'. The General Secretary of KKE held a speech and called for an 'end to the war of imperialists', referring to Israel and the United States, and for a renewed 'struggle of the people', also expressing solidarity with the Palestinian people.

On 22 June 2025, demonstrators marched at the call of KNE and rallied outside the United States embassy in Athens - Central Athens carrying a giant banner reading 'Alert! Greece out of the war. Shut down the United States - NATO bases in our country'. The demonstrators shouted slogans against NATO and against Israel and they held speeches. Similar demonstrations were called across the country.

On 23 June 2025, thousands rallied at Syntagma square, Athens - Central Athens, at the call of PAME to demonstrate against the United States strikes on Iran. The were joined by labor unions, civil society, migrant and political organizations, carrying banners and chanting slogans, demanding Greece's disengagement from 'military operations and the imperialist war'. A large number of members representing the central committee of the Communist Party were present, headed by the general secretary of KKE. Students unfurled a banner outside parliament. The Alliance Stop The War rallied on a central avenue and joined the rest of the demonstrators in a march to the United States embassy. They demanded an end to the strikes against Iran and chanted solidarity slogans with Palestine. Just before the end of the demonstration an Iranian protester heading the march with the Iranian flag broke down in tears. Throughout the demonstration, police had lined up their forces without preventing people from reaching parliament and the rally sites. They were also helpful in regulating traffic.

On 6 August 2025, on the occasion of the 80th anniversary since the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki on 6 and 9 August, members of the Thessaloniki Committee for International Disarmament and Peace (EDYETH) rallied in central Thessaloniki and held a speech before marching to the port. The protesters shouted slogans against the United States and NATO and expressed their solidarity with the Palestinian people.

On 10 August 2025, there was a mass rally in Ioannina during a nationwide 'Day of Action' in solidarity with the Palestinian people at the call of March to Gaza Greece, BDS Greece and the Palestinian Community in Greece, with the main slogan 'Stop the genocide - No cooperation between Greece and Israel - Not in our land - Not in out name', protesting against the government of Benjamin Netanyahu and the Israeli army, also objecting to the leisure program of IDF soldiers in Greece on the Crown Iris cruise ship. They accused the Greek government of being complicit to the genocide and of using the anti-racism law to silence the solidarity protesters. The protesters then marched in the city chanting anti-imperialist and anti-American slogans. There was a strong M-L KKE bloc.

On 24 August 2025, there was a mass rally followed by a march in central Thessaloniki, organized by labor groups, at the call of March to Gaza Greece, PAME and the Palestinian Community in Greece, to protest in solidarity with the Palestinian people and against Israel's latest escalation in Gaza. The march was headed by a large Palestinian flag and a banner reading 'Solidarity with Palestine'. The protesters were carrying fake corpses symbolizing dead children, which they placed on a red cloth outside the US consulate to protest the killing of children and civilians in Gaza.

On 7 October 2025, thousands, including leftist organizations and anarchists, participated in a demonstration in central Athens in solidarity with Palestine. Strong police forces - with particular presence outside the US embassy - observed the demonstrators, who were waving Palestinian flags. Various collectives, likely far-left, marched to the Israeli embassy in north Athens and clashed with riot police. A group of rioters hurled flares and petrol bombs at police, who responded with tear gas and stun grenades. Traffic was disrupted. There were 19 detentions.

On 17 November 2025, marking the 52nd anniversary of the 1973 Polytechnic uprising, at 5 pm, between 15,000 and 23,000 people, including members of the KKE, students of the youth organization of PASOK, marched through the streets with the US embassy as the final destination in Athens - Central Athens (Attica) to honor the victims and oppose authoritarianism. Protesters showed their solidarity with the relatives of the victims of the Tempe rail crash and with Palestine, carrying Palestinian flags. Public transport disruptions remained in effect across the capital, with temporary changes to bus and trolley routes and heightened police presence. Police officers conducted 1,072 checks, making 47 detentions and 13 arrests.

On 3 January 2026, organizations of the extra-parliamentary left rallied in Thessaloniki to protest the U.S. military operation in Venezuela, seizing President Nicolas Maduro. The protesters carried banners with anti-American and anti-imperialist slogans. They shouted slogans and burned American flags. KKE supporters protested separately outside the United States consulate.

On 24 February 2026, protesters backed by KKE rallied in Chania, following the arrival of the USS Gerald R. Ford, the world's largest aircraft carrier, which had docked the previous day at the American naval base at Souda Bay on Crete, as part of a major buildup of American forces in the Middle East. The protesters held up individual placards with letters spelling out 'Killers' in English.

On 1 March 2026, about 1,300 members of the extra-parliamentary left and labor groups, students and other groups affiliated to KKE, marched to the United States and Israeli embassies in Athens to protest against the war and imperialism and particularly against NATO and the United States. The protesters, who carried banners and shouted slogans, demanded Greece disengage from the war, and the closure of the NATO base in Souda, saying instead of the bases acting as a deterrence, Greece had become a target.
On 11 March 2026, a pro-Cuba rally at Syntagma square and march to the United States embassy, Athens - Central Athens, blocked traffic. The general secretary of KKE held a speech.

On 12 March 2026, several thousand demonstrators, members of leftist political parties, organizations and collectives, rallied in Athens - Central Athens and marched to the United States embassy to protest against the ongoing US and Israeli attacks on Iran. The leader of Popular Unity, a controversial left populist and former minister during the SYRIZA government, marched carrying a massive, framed portrait of the late Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

On 27 March 2026, thousands of workers affiliated to PAME, students, members of OGE, participated in an anti-war march to the United States embassy, Athens - Central Athens (Attica, Attica, Kendrikou Tomea Athinon), shouting slogans and carrying banners, demanding Greece disengage from the Trump - Netanyahu war. They also protested for salary increases.

On 28 March 2026, on the International Day of Action against War and Racism, labor groups, student collectives, migrant communities and leftist collectives, rallied at Syntagma square in Athens - Central Athens (Attica, Attica, Kendrikou Tomea Athinon), and marched to the United States embassy, using smoke flares and shouting slogans, calling for Greece's disengagement from the war in the Middle East. They also called for an end to the use of Greek military bases and an end to military spending instead of using the state's resources for social spending, particularly for health and education. They also unfurled banners demanding justice for the dead migrants of the Pylos and Chios tragedies.

On 17 January 2026, around 5000 people demonstrated in Nuuk to oppose US claims over Greenland and to defend Greenlandic sovereignty, following renewed statements by the US President Donald Trump regarding control over the island. Government officials and members of various parties, including the Prime Minister Mute B. Egede (IA) and the Premier Jens-Frederik Nielsen (D), participated in the event, among others.

On 31 January 2026, combat veterans demonstrated outside the United States Consulate in Nuuk to protest the US President Donald Trump's statements on European NATO soldiers and to honor Danish soldiers killed in action in Iraq and Afghanistan.

On 10 April 2025, around 100 workers at the American Beverage Industrial Unit protested and blocked the company's entrance (means unspecified) in the Kagbelen district of Conakry (Conakry, Conakry) to demand salary increases, better living conditions and the dismissal of certain supervisors. The protest took place amid an indefinite strike called by the company's employers.

Around 29 May 2025 (as reported), women protested and blocked the road (means unspecified) to dump trucks transporting materials for a bridge construction project in Kassognah (Maneah, Koyah, Kindia). The women felt their previous requests had been ignored and demanded the Chinese construction company to build an embankment on the land next to the new bridge to use that space to construct a public market.

On 14 July 2025, young people marched from the Martyr's Square to the prefecture town hall and to the Bafing River bridge in Siguiri (Siguiri-Centre, Siguiri, Kankan) to denounce the proliferation of Chinese mining companies, the exploitation of gold resources as well as the pollution of the region's waterways, notably the Tinkisso river.

On 4 October 2025, workers of a Chinese company protested at the company base in Niaya Forita (Sandeniah, Faranah, Faranah) to demand the payment of their September salaries. Soldiers began shooting to disperse the crowd, 1 man was shot in the head and died. According to local sources, another person was shot while in his sick bed (no further details). 1 fatality coded.
On 15 November 2025, an unidentified armed group attacked Seke Mansalah in Doko commune (Doko, Siguiri, Kankan) and killed 2 people, including a Chinese national. Motive unknown.

On 28 November 2025, youths demonstrated and 'attacked' (no further details) Chinese nationals in Siguiri (Siguiri-Centre, Siguiri, Siguiri), accusing Chinese operators of contributing to massive degradation through artisanal mining and the use of heavy machinery while also denouncing the ongoing fuel crisis. They also burned a pickup truck belonging to Chinese nationals and threw stones at law enforcement (likely police and gendarmerie forces responsible for the order in the city). 7 people were arrested, including 3 students. 1 Chinese national was slightly injured in the knee.

On 14 January 2026, demonstrators clashed (means unspecified) with security forces (likely police and gendarmerie forces responsible for the order in the city) in Siguiri (Siguiri-Centre, Siguiri, Kankan) during a demonstration to denounce the arrest of a young opinion leader earlier that day known for his commitment against environmental degradation in the prefecture. At least 1 vehicle was burned and security forces used crowd control measures (no further details). In the Kourouni district, some stormed a storage site for Poclain equipment belonging to Chinese nationals and set ablaze 2 Poclain machines and 1 vehicle while another was set ablaze in the Sainte-Alexi district. Stones were thrown at the present workers. 1 Chinese national was injured.

On 27 March 2025, members of environmental group Prutehi Guahan (formerly Prutehi LItekyan: Save Ritidian) staged a protest outside Andersen Air Force Base and Marine Corps Base Camp Blaz in Yigo (Yigo) to oppose the military activities of the United States (US) and the visit of the US Defense Secretary to Guam. One of the protesters' slogans displayed was 'Stop Funding Genocide and Ecocide.'

On 14 June 2025, dozens of residents, teachers, labor union leaders, members of Indivisible, and other groups staged a protest, called No Kings, at the Micronesia Mall in Dededo (Dededo) to condemn what they described as the 'authoritarian' leadership of United States President Donald Trump administration and their use of military forces against civilians and to call for the protection of democracy and civil rights.

On 5 March 2026, activists held banners during a public hearing inside the Guam Congress Building in Hagatna (Hagatna) to oppose the Draft 2025 Programmatic Agreement and the 2008 Programmatic Agreement, which guide how the United States military handles historic and cultural sites in Guam during construction projects.

On 20 May 2025, in Linden, Upper Demerara-Berbice, for the second consecutive day, truck drivers held a protest against foreign nationals taking over their jobs in the trucking sector, particularly Chinese workers, and against what they consider concessions given to them by the government. Protesters blocked the road from Linden to Mabura with their trucks. They also gathered in Wisroc and Soesdyke Junction areas.

On 7 January 2026, in Georgetown, Demerara-Mahaica, a handful of protesters gathered near the U.S. Embassy to demonstrate against the abduction of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and the fatalities that occurred during the recent U.S. intervention in Venezuela. The protesters held signs and denounced U.S. imperialism, expressed solidarity with the victims and warned against potential interventions to obtain Guyanese oil reserves.

On 9 July 2025, in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, a small group of people held a protest in front of the United States Embassy to denounce the cancellation of the Temporary Protected Status (TPS), which they claimed would affect over 75,000 Hondurans residing legally in the U.S. The protest was organized by the National Front of Popular Resistance Party and included the placement of a coffin symbolizing the 'criminalization of migration and the death of human dignity.' Participants also expressed solidarity with the people of Gaza and criticized U.S. foreign policy. The protest was peaceful and lasted a few hours.

Around 30 July 2025 (as reported), in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, four members of the National Front of Popular Resistance (FNRP) protested in front of the United States Embassy to denounce the mistreatment and discrimination of migrants in the United States. Protesters carried a coffin symbolizing migrants who have died, and condemned policies such as the elimination of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) and the establishment of detention centers. The protesters announced they would continue weekly protests against actions they consider harmful to migrant rights.

On 4 December 2025, in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, members of the Coordinated Council of Indigenous Popular Organizations (COPING) protested outside the United States Embassy to reject the presidential pardon granted by U.S. President to former Honduran president, who had been sentenced to 45 years in prison for drug trafficking. Protesters marched with signs reading messages such as 'The pardon to JOH does not erase the narco-state' and accused the US President of contradicting his stated anti-narcotics stance.

On 16 December 2025, in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, supporters of the Liberty and Refoundation Party (LIBRE) protested outside the National Institute for Professional Training (INFOP) where the Electoral Logistics Center (CLE) is located, despite having been previously removed by the National Police. Protesters returned to demand the annulment of the 30 November elections and denounce alleged fraud, following calls to mobilize by the party coordinator and President. Protesters displayed banners and slogans rejecting U.S. interference and accusing electoral officials of misconduct. The protest delayed the start of the special vote recount process.

On 4 January 2026, in Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazan, a group of citizens, lead by the National Front of Popular Resistance (FNRP), protested in front of the U.S. embassy to demand the release of Venezuela's president, Nicolas Maduro, and that of his wife, as well as a stop to the U.S military attacks against the country. They also described the detention of the president and his wife as kidnapping. The protesters voiced that the incident goes against international and constitutional principles of national autonomy and sovereignty.

On 26 February 2026, in San Pedro Sula, Cortes, at least four armed individuals shot and killed a Chinese man at his business location on Junior Avenue in the Las Flores neighborhood after getting off the vehicle in which they were traveling. They then fled the scene. According to witnesses, this was a targeted attack as the businessman was the only one on site at the time of the incident and he had been watched by the perpetrators prior to the attack. The motivation of the attack is unknown, although the hypothesis of extorsion, a widespread practice by criminal groups affecting business owners, has not be discarded by the authorities. 1 fatality.

On 26 February 2026, in Petion Ville - Centre Ville (Ouest), Ouest, scores of political militants from the opposition held a sit-in protest in front of the Organization of American States (OEA) headquarters to decry the interference of the US embassy in Haitian politics. During the protest, the mayor ordered the police to arrest a leader of the political opposition taking part in the mobilization over accusations that he was intimidating and disrupting scholar activities. It was not clarified if he was eventually arrested.

On 10 March 2026, in Tabarre - Chateau Blond, Ouest, scores of residents held a sit-in protest in front of the US Embassy to decry the US diplomatic representation decision to demolish the houses located in the vicinity of the embassy.

On 24 May 2025, in Delmas - Musseau, Ouest, dozens of Haitians living with HIV marched to the prime minister's office to protest a critical shortage of HIV medication following the Trump administration's drastic cuts to USAID funding, affecting 90% of Haiti-related contracts. Activists warned the country faces a deadly health crisis that would affect over 150,000 people living with HIV, and likely many more not officially counted. Experts also say the medication shortage, in a context of rampant poverty and gang violence, could lead to a spike in new infections, drug resistance, and preventable deaths, especially as many cannot afford the nutrition needed to support their immune systems. A similar protest was carried out on 18 May (coded separately).

On 6 May 2025, a few hundred people protested from Ferenciek Square to Szechenyi Square in Budapest - V, demanding free elections, opposing the Chinese facial recognition system, the anti-Pride law, and the undercutting of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences' assets. The protest was organized by independent Member of Parliament Akos Hadhazy, and a Momentum member was also present at the event.

On 9 August 2025, members of the group Legio Hungaria staged a flashmob outside the CATL battery plant in Debrecen (Debreceni, Hajdu-Bihar). The action followed allegations that a Chinese manager at the factory raped a 16-year-old Hungarian girl. Demonstrators held banners and called for 'remigration', demanding the expulsion of all migrants regardless of legal status. The group framed the incident as proof of the dangers of foreign workers in Hungary.

On 7 January 2026, 60-70 protesters gathered in front of the US Embassy in Budapest - V (District 5) for a 'peace demonstration' organized by former MP, protesting what they called American aggression following the US military's reported capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on 3 January. Organizers described the action as American imperialism aimed at controlling Venezuelan oil fields.

On 4 April 2025, hundreds of online app motorbike taxi drivers protested at the US Embassy in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They condemned Israel and voiced support for Palestine in the Israel-Palestine war. They also urged the US to stop its support for Israel.

On 11 April 2025, dozens of a humanitarian organization members, the Aqsa Working Group (AWG), protested in front of the US Embassy in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They showed support for Palestine in the Palestine-Israel conflict. They also urged Arab countries to impose arms and economic and cultural embargo on Israel.

On 21 April 2025, hundreds of people, mostly women, peacefully protested in front of the Immigration building in Batam city (Riau Islands province). They demanded deportation for a Chinese citizen, who they claimed had assaulted a woman in Batam.

On 4 May 2025, thousands of Muslims from the Koran Lover Community, including members of the FPI organization, peacefully protested in front of the US embassy on South Medan Merdeka Road, Gambir district, Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They demanded the US stop supporting Israel in Gaza. They voiced support for Palestine and condemned Israel in the Israel-Palestine war.

On 20 June 2025, members of the Labour Party and the Coalition of Trade Unions (KSP-PB) protested in front of the US Embassy in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They expressed support for Palestine and condemned Israel during the Israel-Palestine war. They also urged the US not to get involved in the conflict between Iran and Israel.

On 27 July 2025, hundreds of people peacefully rallied from the US embassy to the Hotel Indonesia roundabout in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They voiced support for Palestine and condemned Israel in the Israel-Palestine war. They voiced concerns regarding the hunger crisis in Gaza.

On 7 September 2025, thousands of people from the Indonesian Youth Alliance (Aliansi Pemuda Indonesia/API) peacefully protested in front of the US embassy in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They supported Palestine and condemned Israel in the Israel-Palestine war.

On 7 October 2025, hundreds of people from the Global Peace Convoy Indonesia (GPCI), including students, Muslims, laborers, online app taxi drivers, and humanitarian activists, peacefully protested in front of the US Embassy in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They voiced support for Palestine and condemned Israel during the Israel-Palestine war. They also criticized the US support for Israel.

On 12 October 2025, thousands of people peacefully protested in front of the Horse Statue in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They voiced support for Palestine and condemned Israel in the Israel-Palestine war. They also staged another protest in front of the US embassy in the same city.

On 26 October 2025, a group of people from the Hearts of Palestine (HOPE) movement, including artists and musicians, peacefully protested in front of the US Embassy in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They voiced support for Palestine and condemned Israel in the Israel-Palestine war. They also criticized the US support for Israel.

On 2 December 2025, thousands of Muslims from the Alumni 212 movement peacefully protested at the National Monument area in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They voiced support for Palestine in the Palestine-Israel war and the flood victims in Sumatra. Hundreds of people also staged a similar protest in front of the US embassy in the same city.

On 6 January 2026, a group of people, including Muslim students from the HMI organization, a group of pro-Palestine activists from the Free Palestine Network (FPN), and laborers, peacefully protested in front of the US embassy in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They criticized the arrest of the Venezuelan president by the US government, claiming it violated international law. They also demanded that the US government stop military operations in Venezuela.

On 14 January 2026, a group of online app motorbike taxi drivers from the Indonesian Online Motorbike Taxi Association (Perhimpunan Ojek Online Indonesia/O2) and workers from the Jakarta Individual Other Service Provider (Penyedia Jasa Lainnya Perorangan DKI Jakarta/PJLP) protested in front of the city's hall, the National Monument area, and in front of the US Embassy building in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central). They voiced several demands, including urging the government to improve the workers' welfare, and criticized the US military operation in Venezuela and the kidnapping of the Venezuelan president on 3 January 2026.

On 26 January 2026, a group of people peacefully protested in front of the US Embassy in Central Jakarta city (Jakarta province) (coded as Jakarta - Central).
