On 23 June 2025, about 150 people, including workers, residents, and representatives of PaP and USB, took to the streets of Napoli (Campania) to protest the Israeli, Italian, and US governments, the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the war in Iran. Protesters aimed at reaching Repubblica Square, where the US consulate is located, but were blocked by a police cordon. Therefore, demonstrators marched on the seafront before returning to Sannazzaro Square. Here, at the conclusion of the demonstration, they set on fire pictures of both Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and US President Donald Trump.

On 23 June 2025, at around 6:30 pm, about 100 pro-Palestinian activists, students, workers, and representatives of USB and Changing Course gathered outside the US consulate on Turati Street in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to protest the Israeli and US governments, the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the bombing of Iran. Protesters displayed banners and also criticized the Italian government, the EU, and NATO.

On 23 June 2025, pro-Palestinian activists, workers, and representatives of USB gathered outside the US consulate on Vittorio Veneto Street in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest the Israeli and US governments, the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the bombing of Iran.

On 14 July 2025, around 200 pro-Palestine activists, students, workers, and residents gathered in Bologna (Emilia-Romagna) in solidarity with UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, recently sanctioned by the United States government after denouncing the situation in Gaza and accusing all governments, companies, and institutions that fail to take a stand of complicity in the massacre of civilians. Demonstrators also protested the Israeli and US governments and the killing of Palestinian civilians. Representatives of the Bologna For Palestine Committee (Comitato Bologna per la Palestina), Changing Course, the Communist Refoundation Party, USB, and PaP participated in the demonstration. Several city councilors and some representatives of the PD also attended the event.

On 9 August 2025, thousands of people, including residents, political representatives, pro-Palestine activists, and No Bridge Network activists, marched in Messina (Sicilia) to protest the recently approved Messina Strait Bridge project. Demonstrators also denounced the Israeli government and the killing of Palestinian civilians, criticized the state of disarray of existing Italian infrastructures, and argued that the bridge would reinforce Sicily's role as a NATO and US military outpost. Representatives of the PD, the No Bridge Assembly, and the No Bridge Network participated in the protest.

On 13 September 2025, more than 2,500 residents and pro-Palestine activists took to the streets in Vicenza (Veneto) to protest wars and the presence of US military bases on Italian soil. Demonstrators also protested the Israeli, US, and Italian governments, the Italy-USA Friendship Festival, and the killing of Palestinian civilians.

On 9 October 2025, in the evening, about 300 residents and pro-Palestine activists gathered in Cesena (Emilia-Romagna) to protest the Israeli government, the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the peace deal brokered by US President Donald Trump. Demonstrators stressed that there cannot be real and lasting peace without justice and demanded the end of the Israeli occupation of Palestinian lands. Representatives of the association Cesena's Committee for Palestine (Comitato Cesenate per la Palestina), AVS, PD, health workers, Legambiente, and members of the association Stop Rearm Europe participated in the demonstration.

On 21 October 2025, at the call of GPI, several hundred people staged a protest march from the US Consulate to Porta Venezia in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to denounce what participants called a 'sham truce', asserting that Israel's actions amounted to 'genocide.' Demonstrators demanded an end to US arms supplies and insisted that no weapons should depart from Italian ports, framing this as necessary for peace.

On 22 October 2025, students of the Pitagora High School occupied their school and cleaned it up, painting walls and reorganizing classrooms, in the Toiano neighborhood of Pozzuoli (Campania) as a form of demonstration against the Israeli government, the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the peace deal between Hamas and the Israeli government brokered by US President Donald Trump. At the time of reporting, on 24 October 2025, the occupation was ongoing.

On 3 January 2026, in the afternoon, about 200 residents, workers, and activists gathered outside the US Embassy on Donegani Square in Milano - Municipio 3 (Lombardia) to demonstrate against the US administration and the military strikes in Caracas. The event was held as part of a wave of demonstrations opposing the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population. Representatives of CGIL, ANPI, ARCI, M5S (including the MEP Gaetano Pedulla), PaP, PRC, USB, Changing Course, SI, AVS, students, and pro-Palestine activists participated in the demonstration.

On 5 January 2026, at 5:30 pm, a large group of people, including residents, workers, and students, gathered in Barberini Square in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to demonstrate against the US administration and the military strikes in Caracas. The event was held as part of a wave of demonstrations opposing the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population. Representatives of CGIL, Anpi, Even Numbers Network (Rete Numeri Pari), Italian Network for Peace and Disarmament, Stop Re-Arm Europe, No Muzzles (#No Bavaglio), Let's Lose Balance (Sbilanciamoci), PaP, OSA, Changing Course, Communist Network (Rete dei Comunisti), USB and PRC participated in the demonstration.

On 9 January 2026, around 40 people gathered on San Francesco Square in Piacenza (Emilia-Romagna) to condemn the US military intervention in Venezuela and what they described as US pressure or threats regarding Greenland, framing the demonstration as a political denunciation of US foreign and military policy. The event was part of a wider national mobilization opposing US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and aimed to demonstrate solidarity with the civilian population. In the same square, members of the Venezuelan community staged a counterdemonstration, celebrating Maduro's capture and describing him as a 'narco-dictator' responsible for repression and for the country's collapse.

On 9 January 2026, people, including PRC and AVS affiliates, gathered outside the Prefecture in Cremona (Lombardia) to protest against the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026. Demonstrators also condemned what they described as the silence and complicity of the Italian government and European institutions, arguing that they failed to respond to the US move, which they portrayed as driven by oil interests.

On 8 January 2026, over 200 people, including CGIL, EMERGENCY, and ANPI affiliates, gathered outside the city hall in Mestre (Veneto) to demonstrate against the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026, and to call for peace and respect for international law.

On 27 January 2026, in the morning, students occupied the 'Virgilio' High School in Milano - Municipio 3 (Lombardia) to protest the Italian government, accusing it of implementing repressive policies. Demonstrators also protested the focus on defense and rearmament projects both at the national and European levels, the US and Israeli governments, the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the US military intervention in Caracas.

On 6 February 2026, students gathered outside the Politecnico in Milano - Municipio 3 (Lombardia), while the city hosted the Olympic torch relay ahead of the opening ceremony of the 2026 Winter Olympics at San Siro, to demonstrate against United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) presence in Milano as part of Olympic security.

On 31 January 2026, hundreds of residents and activists gathered in XXV Aprile Square in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to protest the presence of United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents at the 2026 Milan-Cortina Winter Olympics. Representatives of the PD, M5S, Young Democrats, Milan's Sentinels (Sentinelli di Milano), AVS, CGIL, ANPI, ARCI, Action, and members of the Civic Pact Association (Patto Civico) were present. Demonstrators also protested the US administration and President Donald Trump.

On 14 February 2026, in the morning, about 100 students and activists took to the streets in Empoli (Toscana) to protest the presence of United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents at the Milan-Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics. Demonstrators also protested the so-called Security Decree, police repression, and the Italian government.

On 23 February 2026, people, including anarchists and anti-globalization activists, gathered outside the US Consulate in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to protest a supposed visit by US President Donald Trump, which, according to critics, never actually took place. Demonstrators also expressed solidarity with migrants and criticized immigration detention centers (CPRs), United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and Italy-Albania agreements on migrants.

On 28 February 2026, dozens of pacifist activists and residents gathered outside the US Embassy in Roma - City Center (Lazio) to protest the joint US and Israel offensive, 'Operation Epic Fury,' against Iran. Protesters expressed their solidarity with the civilians in Iran and condemned the bombing of Iran's major cities. Members of the Iranian community in Italy and representatives of a group called The People's Mujaheddin (Mujaheddin del Popolo) participated in the demonstration.

On 2 March 2026, in the afternoon, about 500 residents, workers, members of CGIL, ANPI, and ARCI gathered near the US Consulate in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to protest the joint US and Israel offensive, 'Operation Epic Fury,' against Iran. Members of the Iranian community in Italy gathered in front of the first group for a counter demonstration as they protested the Iranian government and thanked the US Administration for their support to the people of Iran.

On 6 March 2026, people, including PRC affiliates, gathered outside the US military base Camp Darby in Pisa (Toscana) to demonstrate against a government resolution that allowed full access to American military bases in Italy.

On 7 March 2026, at 3 pm, at the call of the Palestinian Association in Italy (Associazione palestinesi in Italia), pro-Palestinian activists staged a march from La Scala Square to the US Consulate in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to demonstrate against what they called the 'imperialist war' led by the US and Israel in the Middle East.

On 9 March 2026, thousands of students marched from Cairoli Street to Porta Venezia in Milano - Municipio 1 (Lombardia) to protest patriarchy, sexism, and violence against women, and to demand gender equality in every aspect of life, from equal pay to women's rights and bodily autonomy. They also demonstrated against a law proposal they considered lacking and ineffective, namely the DDL Bongiorno, which aims to regulate issues related to sexual violence and consent. Activists burned an effigy of Donald Trump wearing an Israeli pin. The event was held as part of a nationwide demonstration on International Women's Day.

On 14 March 2026, at the call of the Let's Remain Human Network (Rete Restiamo Umani) and Catania in Solidarity with the Palestinian People (Catanesi Solidali con il Popolo Palestiniane), residents and activists took to the streets in Catania (Sicilia) to protest the Israeli and US governments, the killing of Palestinian civilians, wars, and the presence of US military bases in Sicily.

On 14 March 2026, at 3 pm, at the call of USB, about 20,000 residents, students, activists, workers, representatives of PaP, CR, and OSA protested from Repubblica Square to San Giovanni Square in Roma - City Center (Lazio) against the government's proposed reform of the Italian judiciary. Demonstrators also protested the Italian, US, and Israeli governments, the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the US military attacks in Iran and Venezuela. In Esquilino Square, demonstrators set fire to the photos of Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Italian Justice Minister Carlo Nordio, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and US President Donald Trump.

On 14 March 2026, hundreds of residents and activists took to the streets in Vicenza (Veneto) and gathered at the Camp Del Din US military base to protest wars, including the US-Israeli joint operation (Operation Fury) in Iran, militarization, and the growing international war escalation.

On 15 March 2026, in the morning, residents and activists gathered in front of the NAS Sigonella military base in Lentini (Sicilia) to protest all wars. Demonstrators criticized the US operation (Operation Fury) in Iran, the US government, and the presence of US military bases in Sicily.

On 28 March 2026, about 100 residents and activists gathered outside the municipality in Firenze (Toscana) to partake in the Italian leg of the international No Kings demonstration against the Trump administration, the joint US-Israeli joint operation in Iran (Operation Epic Fury), and imperialism. Demonstrators also protested the Israeli government, the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the government of Iran. Representatives of associations such as Women's March Florence, US Citizens Against War (Stati Unitensi contro la guerra), and Good Trouble Firenze participated in the demonstration.

On 28 March 2026, residents, pacifist and pro-Palestine activists, and representatives of the No MUOS took to the streets in Niscemi (Sicilia) to protest the presence of US military infrastructure used to coordinate military operations, namely the Mobile User Objective System (MUOS) and the Naval Radio Transmitter Facility (NRTF) station, on Sicilian soil. Demonstrators also protested imperialism, militarism, wars, the US and Israeli governments, the killing of Palestinian civilians, and the US-Israeli joint military operation (Operation Epic Fury) in Iran.

On 4 April 2026, in the morning, a little more than 100 people marched through the Capodichino district of Napoli (Campania) against NATO, against Italy's participation in wars and against the militarization of territories. Protesters waved Palestinian, Iranian and peace flags and marched to the US base located in the district.

On 17 March 2026, in Kingston, Kingston, more than 150 people, described as Jamaicans citizens, held a march around National Heroies Circle, the so-called gratitude walk, carrying Cuban and Jamaican flags and wearing white t-shirts in support of the Cuban national government amid increasing pressure on the regime by the US Trump-led administration. Protesters also supported Cuban doctors and medical professionals who worked under the Cuban medical program. The march was joined by the former People's National Party general secretary, a lecturer from the University of the West Indies, and an attorney.

On 18 May 2025, people protested in front of Shinjuku station in Tokyo - Shinjuku, to call on the Chinese government to enact a law against animal cruelty.
On 24 May 2025, people marched in Kyoto, Kyoto against the Trump administration's exclusion of immigrants and oppression of students. They waved a Palestinian flag.

On 8 June 2025, about 100 people, including Rakhine people in Japan and members of the Kachin, Chin, Karenni, Karen, Shan, Mon, Pa-Oh, and Palaung ethnic groups, marched in Tokyo opposing the Chinese government's interference in Myanmar's affairs and its approach to relations with the country. They expressed concern about nuclear contamination spreading to surrounding and cross-border regions and called for an immediate halt to the attacks. Members of the Japan Confederation of A- and H-Bomb Sufferers Organizations and Hiroshima Congress against A-and-H Bombs (affiliated with Gensuikyo) and international tourists, including a person from Finland, attended. Around 8 December 2025 (as reported), residents, mainly fishermen, marched while carrying twigs at the Mnarani beach landing site (Kilifi North, Kilifi) against the ownership and use of the pier, following a dispute between a local and a Chinese investor. On 13 March 2026, Kitale-Morpus road construction workers protested the CICO Chinese company site office in Makutano (West Pokot, West Pokot) against delayed pay, harassment, and poor working conditions. The group demanded that the company management address their grievances.

On 5 October 2024, road construction workers of the Long Hai company gathered near the town of Balykchy in Issyk-Kul region in protest of unpaid wages since December 2023 calling for the country's government to ensure that the Chinese contractor company provides owed pay in full.

On 3 January 2026, people demonstrated in Oslo to oppose the US military intervention in Venezuela and the arrest of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. Activists from the Socialist Youth (SU), and the Communist Party of Norway (NKP) participated in the event, among others.

On 5 January 2026, people demonstrated in Bergen, Vestland, to oppose the US military intervention in Venezuela and the arrest of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. Activists from the Struggle Committee (KK), Bergen4Palestine, and the Peace and Justice Party (FOR) participated in the event, among others.

On 7 January 2026, more than 50 people demonstrated in Trondheim, Trondelag, to oppose the US military intervention in Venezuela and arrest of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. Activists from the Struggle Committee (KK) and the Communist Party of Norway (NKP) participated in the event, among others.

On 9 January 2026, people demonstrated in Oslo to oppose the US military intervention in Venezuela and the arrest of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. The event was organized by the Red Youth (RU) activists, among others, and activists from the Struggle Committee (KK) participated in the event.

On 3 February 2026, activists demonstrated in Oslo to oppose NATO military bases in Norway and to call for the country's withdrawal from the military alliance. The activists also showed their solidarity with Venezuela in connection with the US military intervention in the country. The event was organized by the Red Youth (RU), activists from the Struggle Committee participated, among others.

On 21 February 2026, demonstrators gathered in Bergen, Vestland, to oppose the presence of US military forces in Norway and to call on the government to terminate the defense cooperation agreement allowing American bases on Norwegian soil.

On 28 February 2026, around 100 people gathered in Oslo to oppose the US-Israeli offensive in Iran and what they perceived as American imperialism. Activists from the Struggle Committee and the Peace and Justice Party (FOR) participated in the event, among others.

On 1 March 2026, people demonstrated in Bergen, Vestland, to oppose the US-Israeli offensive in Iran and what they perceived as American imperialism. Activists from the Struggle Committee, Bergen4Palestine, and the Peace and Justice Party (FOR) participated in the event, among others.

On 7 March 2026, more than 100 people demonstrated in Oslo to oppose the United States' blockade of Cuba and to express solidarity with the people of Cuba. Activists from the Struggle Committee participated in the event, among others.

On 8 March 2026, an improvised explosive device detonated outside the United States Embassy in Oslo, damaging the entrance area and nearby property. No injuries were reported. On 11 March, three Norwegian citizens of Iraqi origin were arrested and charged with a terrorism related offense in connection with the attack. As of 13 March, four individuals, all family members, remained suspects in the case. The incident is reportedly linked to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

On 12 March 2026, people demonstrated outside the Parliament of Norway in Oslo to oppose the US-Israeli offensive in Iran and what they perceived as American imperialism. Activists from the Struggle Committee, participated in the event, among others.

On 28 March 2026, demonstrators, mostly members of the American community in Norway, demonstrated in Stavanger, Rogaland, to oppose the US President Donald Trump and show solidarity with the nationwide 'No Kings' protests in the United States. The event was organized by the Democrats Abroad.

On 16 March 2026, more than 100 people participated in a pride march in Wellington (Wellington). They demanded protections for transgender people, pushed back against imported American 'culture war' narratives, and emphasized that Pride should continue as a protest for queer rights.

On 11 April 2025, women from Jamaat-i-Islami staged a protest rally in Peshawar city (Peshawar, KPK) against Israeli airstrikes in Gaza. Protesters carried symbolic coffins and bloodstained shrouds, chanting anti-Israel slogans, and condemned U.S. President Donald Trump's proposed evacuation plan for Gaza and expressed support for Hamas. Members of the traders' community staged a separate protest at Khyber market against Israeli strikes in Gaza and atrocities against Palestinians.

On 14 June 2025, a large number of members of MWM staged a protest in Gilgit-Baltistan province (coded as Gilgit city, GB), against the aggression of Israel military forces on Iran. Protesters also raised slogans against United States for supporting Israel.

On 28 June 2025, members of the Pakistan Kissan Rabita Committee (PKRC), Labour Education Foundation (LEF), Tameer-e-Nau Women Workers Organisation, Joint Action Committee, and allied groups held a protest in front of the US Consulate in Lahore - Data Gunj Buksh town (Lahore, Punjab), demanding major reforms in the global economic and financial system such as cancellation of 'illegitimate and unsustainable' debts, urgent delivery of climate finance in the form of public, grants-based funds instead of loans, and for the establishment of democratic, multilateral frameworks under the United Nations to address both debt and international tax injustice.

On 3 October 2025, activists of the Markazi Muslim League staged a protest outside the press club in Karachi - Saddar town (Karachi City, Sindh), against the Trump administration's proposed plan for peace in the Middle East and the Israeli attack on the Global Sumud Flotilla and the arrest of over 150 activists.

On 9 October 2025, a clash took place between TLP activists and the police at the TLP headquarters in Multan road in Lahore city (Lahore, Punjab) when police personnel launched a crackdown to arrest the TLP chief after the group announced plans for an anti-Israel demonstration outside the US embassy. TLP activists, attacked the police with stones and iron rods, damaging shops and vehicles. Police responded with tear-gas shelling and baton charge. The activists claimed two of its members were killed and 50 injured, while police confirmed one death and reported at least seven demonstrators and 12 officers wounded. A number of activists were arrested.

On 3 October 2025, JUI-F and Jamaat-e-Islami members and activists held a protest in Dera Ismail Khan city (D.I. Khan District, KPK) rejecting the Trump peace plan and supporting the 'liberation of Al-Quds', following Israel's arrest of Global Sumud Flotilla particpants, including Pakistanis.

On 4 January 2026, members of NTUF, HBWWF, and several allied organizations staged a protest in front of the Karachi Press Club in Karachi - Saddar town (Karachi city, Sindh) condemning the United States attack on Venezuela and abduction of the Venezuelan president and his wife expressing solodiarity with the Venezuelan people.

On 12 January 2026, AWP members staged a protest and raised slogans at the Daulatpur Safan Press Club in Daulatpur town (Shaheed Benazirabad, Sindh) condemning the United States attack on Venezuela and abduction of the Venezuelan president and his wife, and demanded their release. The protest was held as a part of a nationwide series of protests.

On 11 January 2026, scores of students, progressive political workers, trade unionists, Katchi Abadi residents (slum dwellers) and intellectuals, under the banner of AWP and Women Democratic Front (WDF), staged a protest at the Press Club in Karachi - Saddar city (Karachi City, Sindh) condemning the United States attack on Venezuela and abduction of the Venezuelan president and his wife. The protest was held as a part of a nationwide series of protests.

On 10 January 2026, members of Awami Tehreek, Sindhyani Tehreek, and other allied groups, led by the central general secretary, staged a protest at the Hyderabad Press Club in Hyderabad city (Sindh), against the American abduction of Venezuela's president.

On 23 January 2026, a large number of members of the Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) staged a protest outside the Khoja Jamia Masjid Kharadar in Karachi - Saddar town (Karachi City, Sindh), against the government's decision to join the 'Board of Peace,' announced by U.S. President Donald Trump, describing it as inconsistent with support for the Palestinian cause and potentially affecting national sovereignty.

On 2 March 2026, locals staged protests in various parts of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (coded to Muzaffarabad city, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Pakistan) against the United States and Israel over the military strikes on Iran and the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader. Internet services were suspended in the entire AJK area.

On 1 March 2026, hundreds of protestors marched towards the U.S. Consulate General in Peshawar city (Peshawar, KPK) against the assassination of Iran's Supreme Leader in coordinated US-Israeli air strikes on 28 February. Police used tear gas to disperse the protesters.

On 6 March 2026, Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) members held a protest rally and marched through Quetta city (Quetta, Balochistan) against the assassination of Iran's supreme leader by the United States and Israel. The protesters held banners and placards, denouncing US and Israeli aggression.

On 1 March 2026, locals staged a demonstration at the American consulate in Karachi - Saddar town (Karachi City, Sindh), against the killing of the Iran Supreme leader. The demonstrators pushed past barriers and entered the consulate's outer perimeter, they fired, hurled stones at security personnel and damaged parts of the surrounding property, and set fire to a section of the consulate. Police, paramilitary rangers and US marines responded with tear gas and baton charged to disperse the demonstrators. 10 demonstrators were killed and 62 were injured (including police personnel). Total 10 fatalities.

On 1 March 2026, hundreds of activists of MWM, a large number of women, children, members of the Imamia Students Organization, and Tehreek-i-Bedari Ummat-i-Mustafa (Muslim group) and other organizations staged a demonstration outside the US Consulate and took out a rally in Lahore - Data Gunj Buksh town (Lahore, Punjab), against the killing of the Iran Supreme leader and US-Israel attacks on Iran. The demonstrators vandalised, set fire to security bunkers and pelted stones. The police responded by firing tear gas to disperse the demonstrators.

On 1 March 2026, thousands of activists of various religious organizations (MWM), a large number of men, women and children took out a rally and blocked the road at Serena chowk in Islamabad city (Islamabad, FCT), against the killing of the Iran Supreme leader and the US-Israel attacks on Iran. A clash took place between demonstrators and the police, as the demonstrators were heading towards the American Consulate. The demonstrators fired at the police personnel, torched a police check post and snatched cameras from the photographers. Police personnel, rangers and armed forces resorted to firing and shelling to disperse them. 3 people were killed, over 60 injured and 15 were arrested. Total 3 fatalities.

On 11 March 2026, members of the Imamia Students Organisation (ISO) held a protest demonstration in Hyderabad city (Hyderabad, Sindh), against the United States and Israel for their 'anti-Islam agenda' and their ongoing attacks on Iran and Palestine.

On 6 March 2026, Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) supporters staged a protest rally in Shinkiari district (Mansehra, KPK) against United States and Israeli strikes on Iran. Protesters marched through local roads and bazaars carrying banners and chanting slogans in support of Iran.

On 3 April 2025, in Panama City, Panama, teachers and other labor unions held a march in the city center, demanding the repeal of the reforms to the Social Security Fund (CSS). The protesters also expressed their opposition to the opening of the First Quantum mine, defended national sovereignty in response to the threats from President Donald Trump, and voiced support for human rights and freedom of expression. In addition to the march, the teachers held a national strike. The Panamanian Association of Teachers (ASOPROF) and the Single Union of Construction and Associated Workers (SUNTRACS) were present.

On 23 April 2025, in Panama City, Panama, hundreds of teachers, students, and labor union members held a demonstration with flags and banners in front of the Carmen Church against the reforms to the Social Security Fund (CSS). Some demonstrators clashed with the police, who used tear gas to disperse them. A group of students of the University of Panama also blocked the Transistmica Highway and threw stones at the police, who also responded firing tear gas. The demonstrators also opposed the memorandum of understanding between the United States and Panama, and rejected the Indio River Reservoir project, among other claims. The Panamanian Association of Teachers (Asoprof) was present, along with members of several other teachers' organizations. Mobilizations on the same claims were held in other provinces of the country on that day as part of a labor strike (coded separately).

On 6 June 2025, in the Bocas del Toro province, banana workers set up roadblocks and kidnapped a female U.S. tourist during a demonstration by the SITRAIBANA against reforms to the Social Security Fund (CSS), in the Alto de Gabo sector. Police forces rescued the woman on the same day. She was not harmed.

On 20 December 2025, in Panama City, Panama, a group of students, members of the Single Union of Construction and Associated Workers (Suntracs), members of the People United for Life Alliance, and members of the National Front for the Defense of Economic and Social Rights (Frenadeso) held a protest in front of the United States Embassy in occasion of the anniversary of the US invasion of Panama, occurred on 20 December 1989. The protesters, shouting slogans, condemned the US threatening an invasion in Venezuela.

On 7 January 2026, in Panama City, Panama, a group of students of the University of Panama held a march in the city center, chanting slogans, to protest against the recent US military intervention in Venezuela and against the capture of the Venezuelan President. The protesters were heading to the US Embassy, although they were intercepted by the police who blocked their path. No violent altercation between the two parties occurred.

On 25 June 2025, in Asuncion (Asuncion), members of the Palestinian Articulation in Paraguay protested in front of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs against the actions of Israel in Gaza, which they consider to be genocide. The demonstrators denounced the complicity of President Santiago Pena's government with the actions of the United States and Israel.

On 3 January 2026, in Asuncion (Asuncion), members of social and political organizations, including the Paraguayan Communist Party, protested in the city's microcenter to repudiate the United States military operation that led to the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. The demonstrators argued that the action constitutes an aggression against the sovereignty of a Latin American country and violates international law.

On 2 October 2024, in Puerto de Lomas district (Caraveli, Arequipa), a group of fishers carried out a demonstration by blocking the Panamericana Sur road, protesting against the ministry of production, arguing the institution had issued regulations (unspecified) that affect the artisanal fishing sector and demanded the correction of those regulations. They also protested against Chinese vessels fishing in the region and demanded the borders between Lomas and Marcoma municipalities to be marked. The demonstration was called by the sector in nearby municipalities with the same demands.

On 16 November 2024, members of BAYAN, People Rising for Climate Justice - Philippines, AKAP Ka Manila Bay (a network of church people, fishers, youth and representatives of the academe), and other groups staged a protest led by YACAP in front of the United States (US) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to call for climate justice and coincide with the global day of action for climate justice and peace.

On 28 March 2025, LFS members staged a protest in front of the United States (US) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to oppose the visit of the US Defense Secretary to the Philippines.

On 9 April 2025, members of BAYAN and other groups staged a protest near the United States (US) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to condemn the growing presence and intervention of US military forces in the Philippines.

On 20 April 2025, BAYAN members staged a protest in front of Camp Aguinaldo in Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to oppose the Balikatan Exercises (joint military drills between the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the United States), saying that they are costly, disruptive to affected communities, and endanger national security.

On 24 April 2025, Akbayan Citizens' Action Party members staged a protest in front of the Chinese Consular Office in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to call for the release of three Palawan residents who were detained by Chinese authorities on accusations of espionage.

On 26 April 2025, members of Anakbayan Southern Mindanao Region (SMR), GABRIELA Youth Davao, and KABATAAN SMR staged a protest at Freedom Park, Davao City (Davao del Sur, Davao Region) to oppose the Balikatan Exercises (joint military drills between the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the United States) and the expansion of Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) bases in the country.

On 12 June 2025, on the 127th anniversary of Philippine Independence, over 2,000 members of BAYAN and other groups staged a protest along T.M. Kalaw Avenue, Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to oppose the United States military intervention in the country, call for the conviction of Vice President Sara Duterte pertaining to the impeachment proceedings against her, and show solidarity with Palestine.
On 22 June 2025, members of progressive groups staged a protest in Tomas Morato, Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), to condemn the United States for bombing Iran.

On 27 June 2025, members of BMP, PLM, and Sanlakas staged a protest and marched from Osmena Boulevard to Colon Street in Cebu City (Cebu, Central Visayas) to call for peace in the Middle East amid the ongoing conflict between Iran and Israel and show concern about the United States' involvement in the conflict.

On 25 August 2025, members of the Filipinos Do Not Yield Movement staged a lightning rally outside the Chinese Embassy in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to condemn China's actions in the West Philippine Sea (South China Sea), show solidarity with fishers affected by their actions, and assert the Philippines' sovereignty.

On 16 September 2025, demonstrators staged a protest in front of the United States (US) embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to mark the 34th anniversary of the termination of the Military Bases Agreement and oppose the presence of US military bases in the country.

On 7 October 2025, members of KABATAAN, Baguio for Palestine, artist groups, and other groups staged a protest in Baguio City (Benguet, Cordillera Administrative Region) to demand justice for Palestinians and call for an end to what participants described as genocide in Gaza. They also opposed the actions of Israel and the United States in Gaza.

Around 17 October 2025 (as reported), Ateneo de Manila University students staged a protest and marched around their campus in Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to call for the freedom of Palestine and for an end to the military interventions of the United States.

On 22 October 2025, hundreds of members of the Akbayan Citizens' Action Party, the Atin Ito Coalition, and other groups staged a protest in front of the Chinese Consulate in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to demand an end to what they described as China's aggression against Filipino fishers and call for a halt to China's activities and plan to build a nature-reserve in the West Philippine Sea, including Panatag Shoal (Scarborough Shoal).

On 15 November 2025, members of Kalikasan People's Network for the Environment and people's organizations staged a protest along Kalaw Avenue in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to mark the Global Day of Action and call for the end of imperialist war and corruption, as well as to push for climate justice. Protesters showed a tableau of United States President Donald Trump holding President Ferdinand 'Bongbong' Marcos Jr. on a leash.

On 16 December 2025, members of the Filipinos Do Not Yield (FDNY) Movement, the pro-democracy group Alyansa Bantay Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (ABKD), ALAB, and other groups staged a lightning rally outside the Chinese Embassy in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to condemn the Chinese Coast Guard's (CCG) use of water cannons against Filipino fishermen at Escoda Shoal, which injured three fishermen on 12 December 2025 (coded separately). They also called on China to respect Philippine sovereignty and the rights of fishers. An effigy of a CCG was destroyed, and cardboard replicas of the Chinese flag were torn apart by the demonstrators as an act of condemnation.

On 5 January 2026, hundreds of members from ACT Teachers Partylist, GABRIELA, Makabayan, and Philippines-Bolivarian Venezuela Friendship Association staged a protest, led by BAYAN, near the United States (U.S.) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to condemn the U.S. military operation in Venezuela, which included airstrikes and ground operations, and the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife.

On 17 January 2026, demonstrators staged a protest from Kalaw Avenue to the United States (U.S.) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to mark the Global Day of Action in Solidarity with Venezuela and to call for an end to U.S. intervention in Venezuela.

On 28 January 2026, members of the West Philippine Sea (WPS) advocacy group Alyansa ng Bantay sa Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (ABKD), People's Alliance for Democracy and Reforms (PADER), LIPI, and the Filipinos Do Not Yield (FDNY) Movement staged a protest in front of the Chinese Embassy in Makati City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to denounce China's use of water cannons and other actions against Filipino soldiers and fishers in the WPS (South China Sea).

On 12 February 2026, members from LIGA Youth, Filipinos Do Not Yield (FDNY) Movement, pro-democracy group Alyansa Bantay Kapayapaan at Demokrasya (ABKD), Peoples Alliance for Democracy and Reform (PADER), artist youth group Kabataang Artista, Manunulat, at Mananayaw para sa Sining at Kultura, youth group Alyansa ng Kabataan sa Komunidad, civil group Liga ng Magkakapitbahay sa Parola Binondo, Cavite Volunteers and Runners for WPS, civil group Katipunan ng Responsableng Maralita para sa Bayan, BBM Calamba Warriors, and other groups staged a protest in front of the Senate Building in Pasay City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to show support for Senate Resolution No. 37, which denounced what Philippine lawmakers called unacceptable actions and statements by the Chinese Embassy toward Philippine officials. Protesters showed support for the Senate's stance on the West Philippine Sea and condemned what demonstrators viewed as improper conduct by China's ambassador to the Philippines.

On 3 March 2026, members of BAYAN, SANDUGO, YACAP, and multisectoral groups staged a protest near the United States (U.S.) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to condemn the U.S. and Israel's military attacks against Iran and call for peace and justice.

On 2 March 2026, KMU members staged a protest at the Boy Scout Circle, Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), to condemn the United States' (U.S.) and Israel's military attacks against Iran and call for the safe return of overseas Filipino workers (OFW) amid the conflict.

On 4 March 2026, about 60 youth activists and students staged a protest at Igorot Park in Baguio City (Benguet, Cordillera Administrative Region) to condemn the United States' (U.S.) and Israel's military attacks against Iran and to show concern about how the U.S.'s actions may drag the Philippines into the conflict due to the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement, which permitted U.S. military bases in different parts of the Philippines.

On 8 March 2026, members of artist group Panday Sining and other groups staged a demonstration, led by GABRIELA, from Liwasang Bonficio to Kalaw Avenue in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to celebrate International Women's Day, demand accountability over government corruption, and call for the abolition of value-added tax (VAT), protection of women's rights, and higher wages. They also denounced military strikes involving the United States (U.S.) and Israel against Iran. A scuffle broke out between police and demonstrators when the demonstrators attempted to march toward the U.S. Embassy but were blocked by authorities along Kalaw Avenue. A policewoman was sprained during the altercation.

On 6 March 2026, Muslim students at the Mindanao State University staged a protest in Marawi City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to condemn the United States' and Israel's attacks against Iran.

On 23 March 2026, ahead of the 57th anniversary of the NPA, members of groups affiliated with the National Democratic Front of the Philippines (NDFP) staged a lightning rally from Espana Boulevard to Morayta Avenue in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to urge onlookers to join the NPA armed revolution, to give tribute to NPA militants who died, and to condemn the war against Iran, Venezuela, and Cuba, which are under attack by the United States.

On 26 March 2026, members of PARA Commuters Network, transport alliance No to Oil Price Hike Coalition, MANIBELA, PISTON, University of the Philippines (likely students, faculty members, and staff), and other groups staged a protest along Aurora Boulevard in Cubao, Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to mark the start of a two-day nationwide transport strike and call for the reduction of fuel prices to PHP 55, the removal of the Value-Added Tax and excise taxes on fuel, and the repeal of the Oil Deregulation Law. They also opposed what they described as the aggression of the United States and Israel against Iran. Drivers passing through joined the protest along Aurora Boulevard by sounding their horns and revving their engines. Other similar protests also took place in Philcoa and other parts of Quezon City.

On 27 March 2026, around 800 members of MANIBELA, PISTON, and other groups staged a protest from Welcome Rotonda in Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to Mendiola, Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), to mark the second day of their two-day nationwide transport strike. They demanded the removal of Value-Added Tax and excise taxes on fuel, reduction of fuel prices by PHP 55, repeal of the Oil Deregulation Law, wage increases, and the end of the United States' attack against Iran, which they said caused fuel price increases.

On 31 March 2026, BAYAN members, transport drivers, and commuters rallied in Iloilo City (Iloilo, Western Visayas) to protest against the increasing oil prices, to denounce the government's lack of action to calls to repeal the Oil Deregulation Law and implement price controls on fuel products, and to call for an end to the United States' attacks against Iran. A jeepney driver carried a wooden cross while being whipped by people portrayed by President Ferdinand 'Bongbong' Marcos Jr. and United States President Donald Trump, symbolizing the burden they described as being borne by the public. Different protests occurred at different gas stations (Petron, Caltex, and Shell) in Barangay Jaro, and they concluded their protest at Jaro Plaza.

On 29 March 2026, members of AMIHAN, Asian Peasant Coalition, Rural Women Advocates, National Network of Agrarian Reform Advocates-Youth, and other groups staged a 'Run for Land Against US Imperialist War' protest at the University of the Philippines Diliman, Quezon City (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region), to mark International Day of the Landless, to denounce the United States' and Israel's war against Iran, emphasizing how the recent oil price hikes worsened the farmers' situation, and to demand the removal of taxes on fuel and basic commodities.

On 9 April 2026, members of BAYAN and other progressive groups staged a protest at the United States (U.S.) Embassy in Manila (Metropolitan Manila, National Capital Region) to condemn U.S. President Donald Trump's threats against Iran and the West Asia region and to call for the abolishment of the Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA) and the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), a pact between the Philippines and the U.S. They also condemned this year's military exercises (Baliktatan) between the Philippines and U.S. in the country. Youth for Justice and Peace (Y4JP) members gathered at the University of the Philippines Manila to protest the same demands.

Around 8 April 2026 (as reported), local landowners and mining operators of Hella Gate Exploration Limited engaged in a physical altercation at the Alluvial mine site at Taure village (coded to Heavala, Kerema, Gulf) over land use, environmental concerns, and lack of proper consultation with the locals. A Chinese national was injured in the confrontation.

On 4 January 2026, about 15 activists gathered for a rally near the local US military facility in Poznan, declaring solidarity with people in Venezuela and condemning what they describe as the US-led imperialism.

On 22 August 2022, around 200 Chinese citizens demonstrated in front of the US embassy in Lisbon (Lisboa) against what they say is the US intention to create a conflict between China and Taiwan. The protest was summoned by several Chinese organizations in the country.

On 14 June 2025, more than 100 people, including US citizens living in Portugal, protested in Praca dos Restauradores in Lisboa (Lisboa) against US President Donald Trump's policies and the 'authoritarianism' of his administration. Three people also showed up at a counter-protest in Lisboa who wanted to show support for the US president. The event was part of a global protest movement called 'No Kings', which took place on the day of a military parade on Donald Trump's 79th birthday.

On 18 October 2025, at the call of Americans in Portugal United in Protest (AMPT), more than 100 people protested in Lisboa (Lisboa) to condemn US President Donald Trump's attacks on democracy, migrants living in the US, and the US Constitution. The event was part of a global protest movement called 'No Kings,' condemning President Donald Trump's administration for authoritarian practices and corruption.

On 4 January 2026, at 6 pm, at the call of the Portuguese Council for Peace and Cooperation (Conselho Portugues para a Paz e Cooperacao - CPPC), around 1,500 people, including the South American community, mainly composed of Brazilians, and representatives of the PCP and BE, protested in Lisboa (Lisboa), opposing the US military intervention in Venezuela, which resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro and his wife on 3 January 2026.

On 28 March 2026, at the call of Indivisible Porto, around 200 people, including US residents in northern Portugal, staged a protest in Porto (Porto) against US President Donald Trump and his policies, and to demand the protection of democracy, civil rights, and an end to US involvement in war in the Middle East. Participants also condemned Immigration and Customs Enforcement's (ICE) crackdown on migrants living in the US. The event was part of the international protest against Trump movement labeled 'No Kings Day'.

On 14 June 2025, in San Juan, San Juan, hundreds of people, joined by several NGOs and civil organizations from the United Front Against Donald Trump's Immigration Policies, marched from La Fortaleza and Del Cristo streets against massive deportation of immigrants, and against President Trump's immigration policies. Protesters claimed to support immigrants and urged the local authorities to stop the raids and stop supporting the federal government in those deportation processes.

On 13 September 2025, in Guaynabo, Guaynabo, over 100 people protested outside Fort Buchanan in opposition to increased US military presence and exercises on the island.
